Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 2, verse 1–5 (part 1 of 3):

Tafsir of verses 1 to 5

After describing the qualities of the believers, the discussion of the surah immediately turns to the description of the disbelievers. Although these qualities in general apply to all disbelievers, the first to be their true referents were those disbelievers who stood blocking the path of the Islamic call at that time, whether they were the disbelievers of Makkah or those connected with Madinah and its surroundings.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, those who have disbelieved, it is all the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them; they will not believe. Allah has set a seal upon their hearts and upon their hearing, and over their vision is a veil. And for them is a great punishment.﴾ (6-7)

Those who refused to accept these matters, for them it is equal, whether you warn them or do not warn them; in any case they are not going to believe. Allah has placed a seal on their hearts and their hearing, and a covering has fallen over their eyes. They deserve a severe punishment.

Apart from these two groups there was also a third group, the hypocrites (munafiqin), as we have explained in detail. The natural result of the circumstances in which the Prophet ﷺ migrated to Madinah al-Tayyibah was that this group came into existence immediately after the completion of the migration. This group did not exist in Makkah, because there Islam had no power or government behind it, nor was there any strong community whose fear would have led the Quraysh to adopt a hypocritical attitude towards Islam. On the contrary, in Makkah Islam was weak, and the call was surrounded by every kind of danger. Only the sincere ones were those who in that period dared to join the ranks of the Islamic call, who were ready to bear every kind of hardship in its path and were prepared to sacrifice everything for it. But in Yathrib (which from the very first day became known as Madinat al-Rasul), the course of events had suddenly changed. Islam had become a power that every person began to feel, and everyone was compelled to keep some relationship with that power. Especially after the great victory of the Battle of Badr, even the great ones had bowed their necks. Among those who were compelled to adopt the path of hypocrisy were some of the leaders of Yathrib. Their families and tribes had entered Islam, so these leaders too, in order to maintain their former position and for the sake of their particular interests, apparently entered the fold of Islam. Among such people, the name of Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul stood at the head, because shortly before the migration of the Muslims, his people had made a plan to make him king, and in order to put this plan into practice, his people were preparing a garland and a crown for him.

At the beginning of Surat al-Baqarah, the attributes of these hypocrites have been described in detail. Some phrases show that the majority of the references are to these great people who, compelled by circumstances, had placed themselves within the fold of Islam. Yet they were still dreaming of keeping their leadership over the common people. And generally, such arrogant elites, just as they hold opinions about the common people, so these people used to call those who accepted Islam "fools." Accordingly, Allah the Exalted says:

﴿And among the people are those who say, "We believe in Allah and the Last Day," but they are not believers. They deceive Allah and those who believe, but they deceive only themselves and do not perceive it. In their hearts is a disease, so Allah has increased their disease; and for them is a painful punishment because they used to lie. And when it is said to them, "Do not cause corruption on the earth," they say, "We are only reformers." Unquestionably, it is they who are the corrupters, but they do not perceive. And when it is said to them, "Believe as the people have believed," they say, "Should we believe as the fools have believed?" Unquestionably, it is they who are the fools, but they do not know. And when they meet those who believe, they say, "We believe"; but when they are alone with their evil ones, they say, "Indeed, we are with you; we were only mocking." Allah mocks them and prolongs them in their transgression, wandering blindly. Those are the ones who have purchased error in exchange for guidance, so their transaction has not profited them, nor were they guided. Their example is like one who kindled a fire, and when it illuminated what was around him, Allah took away their light and left them in darkness, not seeing. Deaf, dumb, blind, so they will not return. Or like a rainstorm from the sky, in which is darkness, thunder and lightning. They put their fingers in their ears against the thunderclaps, out of fear of death, and Allah is encompassing of the disbelievers. The lightning almost snatches away their sight; every time it lights [the way] for them, they walk therein, and when darkness comes over them, they stand still. And if Allah had willed, He would have taken away their hearing and their sight. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.﴾

While this powerful blow is being struck against the hypocrites whose hearts are diseased, there are indications of their devils. From the context of this surah and the events of the Sirah of the Prophet ﷺ, it is understood that by these are meant the Jews, because in this surah their conduct has been criticized comprehensively. The attitude that the Jews adopted towards the Islamic call can be summarized as follows: among the people of Madinah al-Tayyibah, the Jews were the first group that clashed with the Islamic movement, and this confrontation and conflict had several causes. Compared with the unlettered peoples such as the Aws and Khazraj, they held a distinguished position because they were People of the Book. Although among the Arab polytheists there was little inclination towards the Jews, nevertheless the Book and guidance they possessed made them useful to the Jews. Strife, mischief and division are the field in which the Jews work with greater skill; but when Islam came, all these interests of the Jews were struck. It brought a book that confirmed the earlier scriptures and was a guardian of their teachings. Then Islam also ended the disputes between the Aws and Khazraj, through which the Jews used to spread their web of deceit and obtain material gains. Those who had been at each other's throats among the Aws and Khazraj came into the Islamic ranks and embraced one another, and instead of being called Aws and Khazraj, both became known as the Ansar because of their support of the Muhajirin. And by combining all these elements, Islam produced that unparalleled and new Islamic society whose members were united and in agreement, as though they were all limbs of one body, and whose like was not found in history before it and has not come into existence since then until today.

The Jews considered themselves the chosen and favored people of Allah. Countless messengers and prophets had been sent among them, and they possessed many books. They always expected, and eagerly awaited, that the final Prophet would be sent to them. But when he was sent among the Arabs, they then built the hope that perhaps the new Prophet would keep them outside the circle of his call and would confine his message to the unlettered Arabs. But when they saw that he was first calling the People of the Book to this final Book of Allah, and argued for it on the basis that they were more learned than the Arabs and that it was their duty to respond to this call of truth before even the polytheists, their pride of self led them to disobedience, and they regarded it as an insult to themselves, and they began to consider this new call, contrary to their own religion, as an act of aggression.

Now the Jews fell into intense envy and hatred of the Prophet ﷺ. One reason was that Allah had chosen the Final Prophet for the office of prophethood and gave him a Book, about whose truth the Jews had not the slightest doubt. The second reason was that, together with the emergence of prophethood, he achieved swift success in this new environment. Apart from these causes, this envy, hatred, enmity towards the Islamic movement, and the use of every kind of base weapon against it had another cause as well: the Jews were firmly aware that in the new circumstances they would either have to be completely cut off from this new society, and in that case all their leadership in thought, their trade and their interests in usury would end; or else they would have to be fully absorbed into this new society and be lost. These two options are such that neither of them, at any price, can be swallowed by a Jew.

These were the reasons why the Jews of Madinah adopted the harsh attitude towards the Islamic movement that is detailed in Surat al-Baqarah and other surahs. Here we quote some verses that point to this:

﴿O Children of Israel, remember My favor which I bestowed upon you and fulfill My covenant which I have made with you, and I will fulfill your covenant. And fear none but Me. And believe in what I have sent down, confirming that which is with you, and do not be the first to deny it. And do not exchange My verses for a small price, and fear only Me. And do not mix the truth with falsehood or conceal the truth while you know. And establish prayer and give zakah and bow with those who bow. Do you order righteousness of the people and forget yourselves while you recite the Scripture? Then will you not reason?﴾

In another place, the attitude and conduct that the Children of Israel adopted towards their messenger Musa (peace be upon him) has been described in detail, how they showed ingratitude for Allah's blessings, how they displayed neglect regarding the Book of Allah and the Shariah, and how they repeatedly broke the covenants made with Allah. Having described this in detail, the Holy Qur'an warns the Muslims.

﴿O believers, do you hope that they will believe in your call, while a group of them used to hear the speech of Allah and then distort it after they had understood it, knowingly? When they meet those who believe, they say, "We believe"; but when they are alone with one another, they say, "Do you talk to them of what Allah has disclosed to you so that they may argue with you about it before your Lord?"﴾ (2:72)

﴿And they say, "The Fire will not touch us except for a few days." Say, "Have you taken a covenant from Allah, so that Allah will not break His covenant? Or do you say about Allah that which you do not know?"﴾ (2:80)

﴿And when there came to them a Book from Allah, confirming what they already had, although previously they had been asking for victory over the disbelievers, when there came to them that which they recognized, they disbelieved in it. So the curse of Allah is upon the disbelievers.﴾ (2:89)

﴿And when it is said to them, "Believe in what Allah has sent down," they say, "We believe in what was sent down to us," and they reject what is besides it, while it is the truth confirming what is with them.﴾ (2:91)

﴿And when there came to them a Messenger from Allah confirming what was with them, a party of those given the Scripture threw the Book of Allah behind their backs as if they did not know.﴾ (2:101)

﴿Those who disbelieved among the People of the Book or the polytheists do not wish that any good should be sent down to you from your Lord.﴾ (2:105)

﴿Many among the People of the Book wish they could turn you back to disbelief after you have believed, out of envy from themselves, after the truth has become clear to them.﴾ (2:109)

﴿And they say, "None will enter Paradise unless he be a Jew or a Christian." These are their wishful thinking.﴾ (2:111)

﴿The Jews and the Christians will never be pleased with you until you follow their religion.﴾ (2:120)

This is the Urdu translation of Sayyid Qutb's Fi Zilal al-Quran. The Urdu text itself is the source passage, which I am now translating into English:

This is the living, everlasting miracle of the Qur'an: the quality with which it described these Jews has clung to them until today, and it is a quality that has remained inseparable from every generation of theirs, whether those generations passed before Islam or lived in any era after Islam up to today. The Qur'an addresses them as though the Jews of Yathrib themselves were present in the time of Moses and the prophets after him (peace be upon them), because from the very first day the nature of the Children of Israel has been this same nature. Their attributes are the same, their conduct is the same, and in their dealings with truth and righteousness they have behaved in one and the same manner in every age and every era. This is why, in the course of the discourse, indications are found also to the Israelite generations that came after the people of Moses (peace be upon him). And these living words of the Qur'an today still show the relationship and stance between the Muslim Ummah and the Jews, and tell us that the Jews, in their opposition to the Islamic da'wah and the Muslim Ummah, are adopting today the same conduct they adopted centuries ago, and that this will also be their conduct in the future. These Qur'anic verses held the status of a lasting guidance and warning for the Muslim Ummah at that time, and today too they are telling us that the enemies of Islam will adopt the same policy they practised against our predecessors. Even today their intrigues and deceit are just as they were in Yathrib. In every era they have fought against Islam through various and diverse methods, but the reality of this war has remained one: enmity towards Islam.

In short, in this surah, where the qualities of the Jews are described and the Muslims are warned against their plots, there are also instructions on how to form the Islamic community and how to prepare and train it to bear the responsibilities of trusteeship of the Islamic worldview in this world, since the Children of Israel had for a long time failed to fulfil the responsibilities of this trust, and in the end they had adopted a hostile attitude towards this worldview.

As we have said before, the beginning of the surah opens with mention of the groups who, immediately after the Hijrah, had adopted various attitudes towards the Islamic movement. Among these groups were specific allusions to the devils of the Children of Israel, which were discussed in detail later. The nature of the groups mentioned at the beginning of this surah is such that in every age and every era people have adopted the same kind of conduct against the Islamic da'wah. After this, the topics of the whole surah continue along these parallel lines, in which a unity and harmony are kept in view, from which the particular personality of this surah emerges, although its subject matter shows considerable variety.

After the mention of the three groups of disbelievers and hypocrites, and the allusions to the Jewish devils, the call now goes out to all of mankind to worship only one God and to believe in the Book that Allah has sent down upon His servant. The disbelievers are challenged that if they doubt the truth of the Book, then let them produce a single surah like it; the disbelievers are warned of the Fire, and the believers are given the good news of Gardens. After this, the disbelievers are called to reflection, and their disbelief is refuted in an astonished manner:

"How do you deny Allah? Though you were lifeless, He gave you life; then to Him you will return. It is He who created for you all that is on the earth. Then He turned towards the heaven and fashioned it as seven heavens, and He is Knower of all things." (2:29)

After this indication that all creatures of the earth were created for man, the discourse on the vicegerency (khilafah) of Adam (peace be upon him) on the earth begins.

"And [mention] when your Lord said to the angels, 'Indeed, I will make upon the earth a successive authority.'" After this, the details of the story are related: the confrontation of Adam and Iblis takes place, and finally Adam (peace be upon him) is sent down, and within the earth the "era of Adam's vicegerency" begins, which is in essence the era of faith.

We said, "Go down from it, all of you. And when guidance comes to you from Me, whoever follows My guidance – no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve. But those who disbelieve and deny Our signs – those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally." (2:39)

After this, the longest commentary on the history of the Children of Israel begins, a few sentences of which we have already quoted earlier. Between this commentary and criticism, they are called again and again to adopt the Islamic system of life and to believe in the Book which confirms the scriptures of which they themselves are the bearers. At the same time they are warned of the various shortcomings they committed, how they kept straying from the right path and mixed truth with falsehood. The discussion with the Children of Israel extends to the end of the first part of the Qur'an.

From this entire discussion it becomes well known how the Children of Israel received the religion of Islam, the Prophet (ﷺ) and the Qur'an. First of all they adopted a stance of disbelief. They mixed truth with falsehood; they would advise other people to believe, but forget themselves. They would hear the Word of Allah, understand it well, and then, after giving it false meanings, spread false propaganda. They would first express belief and then declare disbelief, trying to deceive the sincere believers, and when they gathered together they would emphatically tell one another: "Beware! Do not tell the Muslims those secrets concerning the Prophet (ﷺ) which are found in the previous scriptures and which they had concealed." They made efforts to force the believers back into the path of disbelief. They claimed that the true people of guidance were none other than the Jews, just as the Christians believed that only they were the people of guidance on the face of the earth. They became enemies of Gabriel (peace be upon him) merely because, as they claimed, he had abandoned them and delivered the message of God to Muhammad (ﷺ). They would become enraged at every success of the Muslims and wait for their destruction; they constantly tried to create doubt about divine revelation and the commands and orders of the Prophet (ﷺ). At the time of the change of the qiblah, their propaganda knew no bounds. They maintained contact with the hypocrites, always guided them, and openly encouraged the polytheists.

This is why this surah contains the most severe criticism of their role, and the surah reminds them that they adopted this very same conduct towards their own prophet Moses (peace be upon him), and after him they treated the prophets and messengers in the same way. Their attitude remained the same across generations. The Qur'an addresses them in such a way that wherever and in whatever era the Children of Israel may be, they are as though one single group, because they possess one nature and disposition, which never changes.

At the end of this lengthy criticism, the Muslims are disappointed about the faith of the Children of Israel, because their selfish mentality, their opportunism, and their corrupt and wicked nature are an obstacle in the way of their faith. Finally, this discourse concludes with the refutation of their claim that "only they are upon guidance, because they alone are the heirs of Abraham (peace be upon him)." It is shown that the true heirs of Abraham (peace be upon him) are those who follow the Sunnah of Abraham and keep the covenant that Abraham made with his Lord. Therefore the inheritance and succession of Abraham have now, in effect, passed to Muhammad (ﷺ) and the believers, because the Jews strayed from the right path, altered their religion, and no longer remained fit to safeguard the trust of the Islamic worldview or worthy of the office of God's vicegerency on this earth. Thus this responsibility was taken upon the shoulders of Muhammad (ﷺ) and those who believed in him. The emergence of the Muslim Ummah was, in effect, the manifest realisation of the answer to the prayer that Abraham and Ishmael (peace be upon them both) made while raising the foundations of the Ka'bah. They had said:

"Our Lord, and make us Muslims [submitting] to You and from our descendants a Muslim nation [submitting] to You. And show us our rites [of worship] and accept our repentance. Indeed, You are the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful. Our Lord, and raise up in them a messenger from themselves who will recite to them Your verses and teach them the Book and wisdom and purify them. Indeed, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise." (2:128–129)

Now from this point the address and direction of speech of the Qur'an turns towards the Prophet (ﷺ) and the Muslim community gathered around him, and the principles and rules on which this new community was formed, which has risen to carry the task of calling to religion, are explained, and it is stated that this community has a particular temperament and holds a distinct outlook in belief and action.

The description of the characteristics of the Muslim Ummah begins with the change of the qiblah. The direction that the Muslim Ummah has to face is determined. This new qiblah is the Sacred House, which was built by Abraham and Ishmael (peace be upon them both) under specific commands from Allah. Allah had commanded them to build it and to purify it so that there Allah alone would be worshipped. The Prophet (ﷺ) himself desired that the qiblah be changed, but he never expressed this. Allah says:

"We have certainly seen the turning of your face, [O Muhammad], toward the heaven, so We will surely turn you to a qiblah with which you will be pleased. So turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram. And wherever you are, turn your faces toward it." (2:144)

After this, the details of the Islamic system of life are explained, upon which this community is to act. The discussion of the system of life, the form of worship, and the conduct and dealings begins. It is explained that those who give their lives in the path of truth should not be regarded as dead; they are indeed living forever. It is explained that trials such as fear, hunger, loss of wealth, and the destruction of crops and fruits in the way of Allah are not mere torments but tests. And these always come upon those who rise up carrying the call to truth. A warning is given that in the struggle between truth and falsehood, Satan frightens you with poverty and sets you upon indecency and immorality, while Allah's promise to you is that He will forgive you and bless you with His bounty; that Allah is the Protector and Helper of the believers, bringing them out from darkness into light, and that the protectors of the disbelievers are the taghut, who take them out of the light and cast them into darkness. After this, the rulings on lawful and unlawful foods are set out. It is explained what righteousness truly is, and that one should not judge the righteous and the wicked merely by outward appearance. Then the rulings on retribution (qisas) in killing, the rulings on bequest, the rulings on fasting, the rulings on jihad, the rulings on Hajj, and the rulings on marriage and divorce are explained. The detailed structure of Islam's family system is set out. And in the economic system, zakat, the prohibition of riba, and the rulings on dealing and trade are explained.

While discussing all these topics, in the course of the discourse, and according to the appropriateness of the occasion, allusions are also made to the circumstances of the Children of Israel after Moses (peace be upon them), and some aspects of the life of Abraham (peace be upon them) are also described. But after the first part, throughout the rest of the surah the address is permanently turned towards the Islamic community. It is prepared to bear the responsibilities of the Islamic system of life and the establishment of the system of khilafah on earth in accordance with the Shari'ah of Allah, and in this way the Muslim Ummah is distinguished from all other nations, because this Ummah itself holds a particular viewpoint regarding the nature of the relationship and connection between itself, this universe, and the Lord of the universe (who chose this Ummah for this great station).

Arriving at the end of the surah, we see that at the conclusion of the discourse the opening of the surah is repeated. The reality of the believing worldview is clarified. It is explained that the Muslim Ummah believes in all the prophets, and also has faith in all the heavenly scriptures, and it believes in the unseen matters described by the prophets, accepts the teachings of the prophets, and is obedient with heart and soul. It is said:

"The Messenger has believed in what was revealed to him from his Lord, and [so have] the believers. All of them have believed in Allah and His angels and His books and His messengers. [They say], 'We make no distinction between any of His messengers.' And they say, 'We hear and we obey. [We seek] Your forgiveness, our Lord, and to You is the [final] destination.' Allah does not burden a soul beyond that it can bear. It will have [the consequence of] what it has earned, and it will bear [the consequence of] what it has earned. 'Our Lord, do not impose blame upon us if we have forgotten or erred. Our Lord, and lay not upon us a burden like that which You laid upon those before us. Our Lord, and burden us not with that which we have no ability to bear. And pardon us; and forgive us; and have mercy upon us. You are our protector, so give us victory over the disbelieving people.'" (2:285–286)

Likewise, between the beginning and the end there is complete harmony, and all the themes of the surah are gathered between these two descriptions of the characteristics and qualities of the sincere believers.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 2, verse 6:

Lesson 2 at a Glance

1. This portion of verses is the introduction to this great surah. In it, apart from the Jews, we are introduced to all the pressure groups (Pressure Groups) that the Islamic movement had to confront in Madinah. In it there is a brief indication of the Jews. The Qur'an gives the hypocrites the title "shayatin" (devils). This very word reveals most of their qualities, and shows what role they played in opposing the Islamic movement. Although this indication is brief, it is sufficient at the beginning to reveal their reality; later, their role is commented upon in detail.

2. While drawing these characteristics, we also become acquainted with the stylistic features of expression in the Qur'an (Style of expression). In place of the outlines used for depicting scenes, here we find the selection of beautiful words. As soon as these words are read, the actual scenes appear before the eyes. These scenes and these concepts move very swiftly and appear full of the bustle of life.

3. At the very beginning of the surah, in light, easily understood and concise words, a strange portrait is drawn of three kinds of people. Each of these categories is a living and enduring model of a great multitude of individuals and groups. These groups are extremely real and deep, and they come into existence again and again in every time and place. It is a particular aspect of the miraculous nature of the Qur'an that, from the earliest times until today, throughout the longest history of humanity, the whole of humankind appears divided into these three groups.

4. Through these brief words and a few sentences, the true features of these classes are impressed upon the mind in such a clear and complete form that these classes appear living, moving, distinct and identifiable, walking before the eyes with their true features. These spontaneous sentences are so well-proportioned and balanced, and possess such melodious phonetic harmony, that no lengthy discourse and no most detailed exposition can reach even their dust.

5. When the portrayal of these classes is finished, the Qur'an then invites all of humankind to join the first class. It calls them to return to the servitude and slavery of the One God, the one Creator and the one Provider, who has no partner and no equal. After this, those who are skeptical about the prophethood and messengerhood of the Prophet ﷺ and about the revelation of the Qur'an upon him are challenged to produce a surah like it. If they cannot accept this challenge, then they should prepare for a painful and frightening punishment. On the contrary, the believers and those who turn in humility (Muminin and Muniboon) are given the good news that for them there is a never-ending bounty and favour. And a glimpse of the mirror of words is also shown.

6. After this, the mischief-making of the Jews and hypocrites is examined again, those who said that the Qur'an gives parables for small things, and therefore it is not a book revealed by God. They began a wide enterprise of spreading doubts and suspicions, using this matter as a pretext. They were told that these examples are based on profound wisdom, and that a person may be misguided by reading them, as they themselves were, while on the other hand the group of believers becomes even firmer in faith through them. After this, they are rebuked: why do they deny that Creator and Manager, the All-Knowing and All-Seeing, the One who gives life and causes death? For it is He who created the whole universe for humankind, made them His khalifah and self-governing rulers by giving them this vast and wide dominion, and blessed them with countless favours and bounties.

"As for those who have disbelieved, it is equal for them whether you warn them or do not warn them; they will not believe. Allah has set a seal upon their hearts and upon their hearing, and over their eyes is a covering. And for them is a great punishment."

Here the pious (muttaqin) and the disbelievers (kafirin) appear standing in direct opposition to one another. This Book is guidance and a light of insight for the pious, but as for the disbelievers, whether they are warned or not, they remain fixed in the path of disbelief in every condition. The doors of divine guidance that are open in the hearts of the believers, and the connections through which they are at every moment joined to this whole universe, its Creator, its outward and inward aspects, and its world of the unseen and the witnessed, all these doorways of right guidance appear closed for the disbelievers. In this same picture, all the connections between the human being and the Creator of the universe that are established and lasting for the believers appear completely severed.

Allah has set a seal upon their hearts and upon their hearing ("Allah has set a seal upon their hearts and upon their hearing"), by which they are no longer able to attain true guidance and to hear the voice of truth. And over their eyes is a covering ("And over their eyes is a covering"), so they are deprived of seeing the light of guidance. Since they persistently rejected warning and glad tidings through their wrong way of life, Allah, the Exalted, inflicted upon them a severe punishment in this very world for this conduct: a seal was placed upon their hearts, veils fell over their eyes, and their ears became deaf to the call of truth. Thus, for them, preaching and proclamation, and warning them or not warning them, became equal.

This is a harsh, rigid and dark picture, which appears before us depicting the profound darkness and blackness of these people's hearts and minds, and their adoption of a course of persistent blindness and deafness. "And for them there is a great punishment" ("And for them there is a great punishment"), because this is the natural consequence of their hostile and disbelieving conduct: those who do not accept the words of the one who warns, for whom warning and not warning become alike, and of whom Allah in His knowledge is aware that they will remain upon this course until the end, are deserving of this very consequence.

The discourse now moves to the third image and the third scene. This third type is portrayed in these words: "Among the people there are those who say, 'We believe in Allah and the Last Day,' but in reality they are not believers. They try to deceive Allah and those who believe, but in fact they are deceiving only themselves, and they are not aware of it. There is a disease in their hearts, and Allah has increased their disease. And for the lie they tell, there is a painful punishment. When it is said to them, 'Do not cause corruption on the earth,' they say, 'We are only reformers.' Beware! Indeed, it is they who are the corrupters, but they are not aware. And when it is said to them, 'Believe as the others have believed,' they say, 'Shall we believe as the foolish have believed?' Beware! Indeed, it is they who are the foolish, but they do not know. When they meet those who believe, they say, 'We believe.' But when they are alone with their devils (shayatin), they say, 'Indeed, we are with you; we were only mocking them.' Allah mocks them and gives them rope to continue in their transgression, and they wander blindly in their rebellion. These are the ones who have bought misguidance in exchange for guidance, but their trade has not profited them, and they were not rightly guided."

The words above depict the actual situation in Madinah Tayyibah accurately. Yet, even setting aside the limits of time and place, we see such people present in every generation of humankind. In every generation there are prominent hypocrites (munafiqin, the hypocrites), who neither have the courage to fully accept truth and believe, nor the resolve to openly reject it. Alongside this condition, such people also desire a high station and lofty status before the common people. They consider themselves more knowledgeable and wiser than the general masses. Therefore, we regard these verses as principled verses, free from all historical examples, which apply to all those in every age who adopt a hypocritical attitude. In short, the psychological condition depicted in these verses has always existed in the depths of the human soul in every era, exists now, and will continue to exist in the future.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 2, verse 9:

Such people always claim to believe in Allah and the Day of Judgment (and to be servants of Islam). But in reality their hearts are empty of the wealth of faith. They are plainly afflicted with hypocrisy (nifaq). They are cowardly, and they lack the courage to express their true opinion about the believers.

Such people are always caught up in the illusion that they are extremely clever, shrewd and skilled in policy, and that they can deceive these simple-hearted believers under any circumstances. The Qur'an says that such people try to deceive not only the believers but also Allah. ﴿They seek to deceive Allah and those who believe﴾. This verse, and other verses like it, reveal a great truth. It is a magnificent grace and kindness of Allah that its expression is repeated and emphasized again and again in the Noble Qur'an, and in it lies the secret of the bond established between the believing servant and Allah. That is, Allah makes the front of the believers His own front. He makes their affairs and circumstances His own affairs and circumstances. Allah joins them with Himself and takes them under the embrace of His kindness and mercy. He makes their enemy His own enemy, and the plots against them plots against Himself. This is the utmost royal generosity and honour, by which the worth and station of the believers reaches its highest peak, and by which it is confirmed that faith in Allah is the greatest truth in this universe, from which springs the fountains of steadfastness and tranquility in the believing heart. He sees that Allah takes the problems and difficulties of a believer into His own hand of power; his struggle becomes Allah's struggle, his enemy becomes Allah's enemy. Allah takes him into His own front and includes him within His own protection. In comparison with this, what is left of the reality of the plots, deceptions and harassments of humans and of insignificant servants?

The second aspect of this truth is that it contains a fearful warning for those who try to deceive the believers, who plot against them and who seek to harass them. They are being told that their war is not only against the believers, but in reality they are arrayed against that most holy Being who is powerful and firm, and who is the Subduer and Irresistible. By fighting against the friends of Allah, they are in fact fighting against Allah, and through these base activities of theirs they are becoming deserving of the wrath and anger of Allah.

It is the duty of the believers to reflect well upon both aspects of this supreme truth, so that they may attain peace and steadfastness, keep moving correctly toward their destination, and pay no heed to the deceptions of deceivers, the plots of schemers, and the harassment of the wicked. The enemies of the believers too should reflect upon this truth for a moment. They should consider with whom they are at war and whose wrath and anger they are becoming deserving of. They should fear what danger they are taking upon themselves by being free to pursue the believers.

Now we turn again to those who wish, in their own opinion, to deceive the believers, who consider themselves extremely clever and shrewd, and who say, "We have believed in Allah and the Day of Judgment." But observe what a great mockery they fall victim to before the end of the verse.

﴿But they deceive none except themselves, and they do not perceive﴾. That is, they are so heedless that they are deceiving their own selves, and they are not even aware of it. And Allah is aware of all their actions. As for the believers, they are directly under the protection of Allah, and He Himself is protecting them from their base scheming and deception. But these fools are being deceived for nothing, and they are involving themselves in evil and sins, and they think that by adopting the way of hypocrisy they have made a very profitable bargain. And they think they have gained much benefit from it. But in this way they have also escaped the difficult task of openly declaring disbelief within the society of the believers, and they have gathered up the interests of the new society along with the believers. Yet the disbelief that they are concealing in their hearts is leading them towards the pit of destruction. Their hypocrisy is a means of ruin for them, and because of it they are about to reach a most ill-omened end.

But the question is: why do the hypocrites behave this way? Why, by adopting the path of hypocrisy, do they want to deceive the believers? The answer is: "Fi qulubihim maradun" (فِی قُلُوبِھِم مَّرَضٌ), "There is a disease in their hearts." A sickness has taken hold of their hearts; a calamity has fallen upon their minds, and it does not allow them to walk on the straight path of truth. As a result, they become deserving that the law of Allah's creation should increase this sickness further: "Fa-zadahumu Allahu maradan" (فَزَادَھُمُ اللہ ُ مَرَضًا), "Allah increased their sickness." It is evident that one sickness gives birth to another. Misguidance is extremely minor at the beginning, and as soon as its lines and limits advance, its angle widens more and more. This is the law of Allah's creation, which operates everywhere. This law of nature is in effect in human thought and conduct, in all things and all circumstances. They are themselves walking toward a known and recognized end, the end that is destined for all those who want to deceive Allah and the believers. "Wa lahum adhabun alimun bima kanu yakdhibun" (وَ لَہُم عَذَابٌ اَلِیمٌم بِمَا کَانُوا یَکذِبُون), "They lie, and for their lying there is a painful punishment." This is the second of their important attributes, especially of those among them who were leaders and who, before the Prophet's ﷺ migration, held positions of chieftainship befitting their people and tribe, such as Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul. Their particular characteristic was that they harbored deep hatred against the believers, presented justifications for the strife and corruption they spread, and, escaping every kind of punishment and accountability for these deeds, swelled with pride.

Thus these people do not limit themselves to lies and deception; rather, considering the believers to be fools, they further claim, in reverse, that "we are indeed reformers." When they are told, "Do not cause corruption on the earth," they do not give the simple reply, "Brother, when are we causing corruption?" Instead, they respond arrogantly, claiming, "We are indeed the reformers."

In every age and every era, this kind of people has been seen, who in practice are carrying out the worst forms of corruption, while their claim is that they merely want the reform of society. When lofty values are destroyed in a society, such people come to the fore. They are deprived of sincerity and purity of soul. When sincerity is lost and corruption arises in the human self, all high values and the standards of good and bad vanish on their own. Those people in whose hearts sincerity and faith do not remain can never attain awareness of the corruption of thought and action. The standard of good and evil, of reform and corruption, that exists in their minds and hearts keeps inclining toward their carnal desires, and does not incline toward the divine system of life. For this reason, this harsh yet realistic answer is given to their claim.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 2, verses 12–13:

"Beware! Indeed, it is they who are the corrupters, but they do not perceive." ("Beware! Verily, they are the ones who cause corruption, but they are not aware.") Among the characteristics of these people is that they are afflicted with arrogance and pride, consider themselves to be of a higher class (Upper Class) than the common people, and try to maintain a false dignity in the hearts of these people. "And when it is said to them, 'Believe as the people have believed,' they say, 'Shall we believe as the foolish have believed?' Beware! Indeed, it is they who are the foolish, but they do not know." ("And when it is said to them, 'Believe as the people believe,' they said, 'Shall we believe as the foolish believe?' Beware! Verily, they are the fools, but they do not know.")

The truth is that what the hypocrites in Medina were being called to was to believe sincerely and to purify their faith from personal desires, just as the other sincere believers had fully absorbed themselves into Islam by effacing their individuality. They had submitted their heads before Allah, and had opened every window of their hearts for the Prophet ﷺ. Whatever guidance the Prophet ﷺ gave them, they responded to it with sincerity and selflessness. Thus the hypocrites were being invited to believe, as those people did, with sincerity, steadfastness, and a clear and pure heart and mind.

But it is also a reality that these hypocrites were not prepared to bow fully before the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in that sense. They considered themselves to be people of a higher class (Upper Class), and they would say that such a state of submission and contentment was not necessary for them. This is why they would say about the believers, "Shall we, like these fools, wander about in blind obedience?" The Qur'an also refuted this false conceit with such severity, emphasis and decisiveness. "Beware! Indeed, it is they who are the fools, but they do not know."

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah al-Baqarah, verse 14:

The question is: has a fool ever thought of himself as a fool, or has a person who has strayed ever been aware that he has left the straight path? Now the last attribute of the hypocrites is described, in which it is explained that these people are not only afflicted with lying, deceit, belittling the Muslims, and self-aggrandizement, but along with these blameworthy qualities they are also low-minded, base, conspiratorial and cunning. Their condition is that: ﴿When they meet those who believe, they say, "We believe," but when they are alone with their devils, they say, "Indeed, we are with you; we were only mocking."﴾ When they meet the believers, they say that in truth we are with you, and we are merely mocking those people.

Some people regard this humiliation and meanness as strength and wisdom; in their view, deception is the highest degree of acumen and statecraft. Yet in reality this is the final limit of helplessness and baseness. A person of power and strength can never be mean or base of soul. Nor does he need deception, nor does he need to engage in backbiting in private and vent the heart's resentment through taunts and sarcasm. The condition of these hypocrites was that they were shrinking from openly facing the Muslims, and while meeting the believers they were also declaring, on their own part, that they were believers, so that in this way they would remain safe from every kind of harm from the believers, and, thus secure and protected, they would keep stinging the believers with their venom. When these people went to their devils, who (probably) were the Jews, and who would find among such people several individuals who were used to spread disorder and discord in the Islamic ranks, the Jews on their part also served as a support and refuge for such people. Thus these hypocrites, when they met their devils in private, would say: "Indeed, we are with you, and we are merely mocking those people." Their mockery of the believers was that they would profess faith and inner conviction, and they thought: "The believers know nothing of what we really are."

Immediately after clarifying their deceitful speech and cunning conduct, the Qur'an gives them such a sharp rebuke that, if they had any feeling, even mountains would tremble in fear.

Allah mocks them and extends them in their transgression, wandering blindly.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran), Urdu translation, on Surah 2, verse 15:

"Allah mocks them, and He prolongs their rope in their transgression, and they wander on, blind like the blind in their own course."

What a wretched person he is, when the Subduer and the Mighty of the heavens and the earth mocks him! There is no greater misery than this. When a sensitive person reflects on these words and lets his imagination work on the composed image, he stands motionless before a terrifying and trembling scene. This is so dreadful an end that hearts quake and the hairs of the body stand on end. Thus these deceivers are left to their own state: they have no guide, no path appears to them, and they have no goal before them. They remain in this state of bewilderment when the hand of Allah's power seizes them in a severe grip, and they fall into the snare like rats, heedless and careless. This is a terrifying end from Allah, and in comparison to it, the mockery that they carry out according to their own thinking has no value.

Here the reality is being expressed that we have pointed out before: in the battle between kufr and Islam, Allah Himself is the protector and helper of the believers. For the friends and servants of Allah, His patronage is a great treasure of tranquillity of heart; for the bewildered, heedless and cast-out enemies of Allah, it is an indication of an evil end and a terrifying final outcome. They are deceived into thinking that Allah is prolonging their rope, and they wander confused in their transgression and misguidance. They are going blind and sinking deeper into heedlessness, while a terrifying end awaits them.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 2, verse 16:

Now the Qur'an, in its last few words, describes their true state and the loss that is reaching them because of this course of conduct. ﴿These are the ones who have bought misguidance in exchange for guidance, so their trade has not profited, and they were not guided.﴾ ﴿These are the ones who have bought error in exchange for guidance, yet this bargain is not profitable for them, and they are by no means on the right path.﴾ If they had wished, the way of guidance was within their reach. The rivers of guidance had been made to flow over them. It was in their hand, but by their own will they gave up guidance and bought misguidance in its place, just as the fate of a heedless merchant is. Their fate was the same. In that transaction they gained nothing, and guidance too slipped out of their hands.

You have seen that in these verses the Qur'an has portrayed three kinds of people. Of these, this third group occupies a comparatively larger space on the canvas. In its broad outline we see various colours filled in that are not present in the first and second pictures. The reason is that the people shown in the first and second pictures have a path and manner that is fixed in some form. They stand openly upon a particular course. In the first picture there is a character who possesses upright thinking; there is a straight road on which he walks in a perfectly straight line. In the second picture a blind person is shown, bewildered and wandering, groping about in darkness. But the psychological state of the third person is so complex, his heart so diseased and his thinking so disturbed, that he requires a further, final comment. In this picture there are some additional outlines, and colours have been applied to them so that the repugnant and fickle personality of this group may be clearly made out in its features.

Through this detailed discussion, on the one hand, the role that the hypocrites of Madina were playing in harassing the devoted followers of Islam, and in spreading disorder and unrest among them, comes clearly before us. On the other hand, the Islamic community is warned how dangerous a single hypocrite can prove to be for the discipline of the community in every age, and how great the importance and necessity is, within the Islamic community, of exposing these hypocrites and unmasking their conspiracies.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 2, verse 17:

For the sake of further clarification, the Qur'an gives examples, so that the psychology of this group, the fickleness of its temperament, its instability and its somersaults are further identified, and the features of such people stand out clearly before us.

﴿Their example is like that of one who kindled a fire; and when it illuminated what was around him, Allah took away their light and left them in darknesses, not seeing.﴾

"Their example is like that of a man who kindled a fire, and when the surroundings were lit up, Allah took away their power of sight and left them in a state where they could see nothing in the darkness. They are deaf, dumb and blind, and therefore they will not return."

From this it becomes clear that initially their attitude was not such that they turned away from guidance, or stuffed their fingers into their ears, or closed their eyes, nor was it the case that they denied studying this movement, as the disbelievers did. But later they preferred misguidance over guidance, and they made this decision deliberately, after thinking and reflection. They kindled the fire; it also lit up their surroundings, but they derived no benefit from it, although they were seekers of light. When these people, having found the light they were seeking, turned away from it, Allah took away their very sight because of this attitude, and left them in a state where they wander about in darkness, because they turned away from exactly that thing which they were seeking.

Allah has given man the eye, the ear and the tongue precisely so that he may hear speech, see the light, and benefit from the light of guidance. But they did not make use of their ears, and so they were made deaf. They also did not make use of their tongues, and so they were declared dumb. They stopped using their eyes to see, and so they became blind. Clearly, in such circumstances it is not possible for them to return to the truth, turn towards the path of guidance, or see the light of truth.

Now, through another parable, their psychological condition is analysed, through which their inner turmoil, bewilderment, fear and restlessness are expressed. ﴿Or [they are] like a rainstorm from the sky…… Indeed, Allah is over all things competent﴾. Or understand their example thus: heavy rain is falling from the sky, and with it there are dark clouds, thunder and lightning. Hearing the crashing of thunder, they thrust their fingers into their ears for fear of their lives, and Allah encompasses these deniers of the truth on every side. The lightning brings them to such a state that it seems as though it will soon take away their sight. Whenever a little light is perceived by them, they walk on in it for a short distance; and when darkness overtakes them, they stand still. If Allah willed, He would indeed take away their hearing and sight entirely; surely Allah is competent over all things.

How strange a scene this is, in which various pictures of running about, anguish and restlessness, misguidance and straying, fear and terror, lamentation and wailing, bewilderment and confusion, glitter and glare, and cries and shouts are seen moving and flowing. Torrential rain is falling from the sky, and with it there are dark clouds, as well as lightning and the harsh sounds of thunder. Some people are trying to advance in the brightness of that intense lightning. Suddenly there is darkness. The poor wretches stand still, bewildered and perplexed, not knowing where to go; they tremble with fear, and at the crashing of thunder their very lives seem to depart, so they thrust their fingers into their ears because of it.

The whole scene is filled with this bustle: torrential rain, darkness, crashing and flashing, and frightened, troubled travellers who advance a few steps with trepidation and stop as soon as the darkness comes. Through this entire scene the Noble Qur'an wishes to convey the clear impression that the hypocrites are caught up in anguish and restlessness, bewilderment and confusion, misguidance and wandering. On one side they meet the believers; on the other side they also have their own devils. On one side there is acknowledgement of the truth, and after a moment there is denial and rebellion. They are seekers of light and guidance, but in practice they are trapped in darkness and misguidance. This is an extremely tangible parable and scene, yet it holds up a mirror to the most hidden psychological condition of the hypocrites, and it displays their conscious state in embodied form. This is the distinctive and remarkable style of expression of the Qur'an: it describes psychological and confused mental states in such a manner that they appear standing visibly before the eyes.
