Following the description of the three types of people mentioned above, the discourse now turns to calling all of humanity. All of humanity is told to adopt, from among these three portraits, the straight, noble, pure and sincere, active and beneficial, guided and successful portrait, namely the portrait of the muttaqin (the God-fearing). Thus it is said:

﴿O mankind! Worship your Lord, who created you and those before you, that you may become righteous. Who made the earth a bed for you and the sky a canopy, and sent down from the sky water, and brought forth thereby fruits as provision for you. So do not set up rivals to Allah while you know.﴾

Now, this is in effect a call to all people to enter into the worship of the one Lord who has created them, and who also created their forefathers. He is a Lord who alone is the Creator of this universe, so He alone is deserving of being worshipped. Worship of Him has a specific purpose, and it is hoped that by worshipping Allah all people will reach that purpose and attain it. That purpose is ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ﴾ ("that you may become righteous"). You should adopt the pattern of human life that is pleasing, and which is pleasing to Allah. That is, the pattern of life of those who worship Allah and fear Him, who fulfilled the right of Allah's creatorship and lordship properly, and worshipped only one Creator, who is the Creator of you, present and past people, and who arranged the provision of their sustenance through the resources of the heavens and the earth, and in this matter He has no equal and no partner. ﴿الَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ الأرْضَ فِرَاشًا﴾ ("who made the earth a bed for you").

This expression shows that Allah has made human life in the earth extremely easy. He made the earth such that it is a pleasant dwelling for human beings and a safe place of residence like a bed. But since human beings live here for a long period, the pleasantness of the earth and the heavens fades from their consciousness. They forget how well-suited and pleasant Allah has made the climate of this earth for them in order to provide their means of life, and what comforts and means of ease He has supplied for them in this world. If these resources did not exist, their life on this globe would not be so pleasant, easy and peaceful. If even one of the constituent elements of this universe were to disappear, the environment here would change so greatly that the growth of all of humanity would become impossible. Take the example of air alone: if there were even a tiny decrease in the fixed elements of which it is composed, it would become difficult for people to breathe on the earth, even though they are yet to live.

﴿وَالسَّمَاءَ بِنَاءً﴾ ("and the sky a canopy"). That is, the sky is suitable and firm like a roof. Human life on this earth, and its comforts, are closely connected with the sky. The heat of the sky, the attraction of the celestial bodies, and balance, and all the natural connections between the earth and the sky, are conducive to life and are the preface and first brick for sustaining life in this earth. This is why, whenever the Qur'an mentions the power of the Creator of this world, it mentions the greatness of the Provider of humanity, and says that it is the duty of all creation and all humans to worship Him alone. Accordingly, on all such occasions the blessings of Allah are mentioned.

﴿وَأَنْزَلَ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً فَأَخْرَجَ بِهِ مِنَ الثَّمَرَاتِ رِزْقًا لَكُمْ﴾ ("and sent down from the sky water, and brought forth thereby fruits as provision for you"). In the context of the power of Allah Jalla Shanuhu and His bounties, the sending of water from the sky and the bringing forth of various kinds of produce through it is mentioned in several places in the Majid Qur'an. Thus, water descending from the sky is, even from a natural standpoint, the fundamental element for the sustaining of life on this earth. Life on earth, in its various forms and levels, depends upon this water. In the Qur'an: ﴿وَجَعَلنَا مِنَ المَآءِ کُلَّ شَیئٍ حَیٍّ﴾ ("and We made from water every living thing"). Sometimes water irrigates fields in the form of rain; sometimes it flows in the form of sweet rivers and canals; and sometimes it penetrates the veins of the earth and emerges in the form of springs and wells, and is used through instruments in agriculture and farming.

The importance of water in the earth, its role in the sustaining of life here, and the dependence of various things' life upon it, is a self-evident and accepted matter, for which a hint and a reminder are sufficient. The purpose is that Allah, who is our Creator and Provider, and who has bestowed all these blessings upon us, is deserving that we worship Him alone.

Through this method of calling, two important principles of the Islamic conception of life become clear by themselves. The first is that the Creator of this entire universe is one. ﴿الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ وَالَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ﴾ ("who created you and those before you"). That is, this universe is one, there is complete harmony among its units and parts, and it is a helper and support for man and for life.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 2, verse 22:

الَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ الأرْضَ فِرَاشًا وَالسَّمَاءَ بِنَاءً وَأَنْزَلَ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً فَأَخْرَجَ بِهِ مِنَ الثَّمَرَاتِ رِزْقًا لَكُمْ فَلا تَجْعَلُوا لِلَّهِ أَنْدَادًا وَأَنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ

"It is He who made the earth a bed spread out for you, and the sky a canopy, and sent down water from the sky and brought forth by it fruits as provision for you. So do not set up rivals to Allah while you know."

The earth lies spread out like a carpet. The order of its atmosphere is bound within the law of nature, and an arrangement of irrigation has been made through it, so that every kind of produce has been provided upon the surface of the earth to supply the needs of people. For whom is all this? For the human being. And all this is the perfection of the Creator of this universe, who has no partner.

فَلا تَجْعَلُوا لِلَّهِ أَنْدَادًا وَأَنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ "So when you know this, do not make others equal to Allah." You know well that He created you. He created all those who passed before you. You know that it is He who made the earth a bed for you and the sky a canopy. He sent down water from the sky, and in this whole work He had no helper who would lend Him a hand in it, nor was there any rival who would oppose any of His affairs. Therefore, even after this knowledge, associating anyone with Him is an extremely improper conduct.

In order to firmly establish the belief in Tawhid (divine oneness) in minds in a clear and transparent manner, the Qur'an repeatedly negates and refutes the partners of Allah, and these are not always only in the well-known form of idols or persons who are made partners of Allah and worshipped. Rather, at times they also exist in other hidden forms. For example, placing hope in anyone other than Allah, or holding in one's heart fear of anyone other than Allah, is also shirk. Likewise, it is shirk to believe that anyone other than Allah can bring benefit or harm. Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "Andad is shirk, and it is as hidden as the crawling of an ant slowly over a black stone in a dark night." It has many forms, such as: someone saying, "By you, O so-and-so, by Allah, by my life, by your life." Or someone saying, "If it were not for the dog at night, thieves would have robbed us," or someone saying, "If it were not for the duck in the house, thieves would have come." Or someone saying to his friend, "Whatever Allah wills and whatever you will." Or someone saying, "If it were not for Allah and so-and-so." In short, all these statements are shirk. Also, it is mentioned in a noble hadith that a person said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), "Whatever Allah wills and whatever you will." Upon this, he (ﷺ) said, "Do you want to make me a partner of Allah?"

This was the view of the righteous predecessors (Salaf al-Salihin) regarding hidden shirk and the partners of Allah. We should lower our heads into our own collars and reflect upon our own condition. Where is the intense sense of the Salaf regarding shirk, and where are we? How far have we moved away from this great truth of the belief in Tawhid?

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 2, verse 23:

The Jews had doubts about the prophethood of the Prophet (ﷺ). The hypocrites also doubted it, and the polytheists were in the same state. The Holy Qur'an here challenges all of them, and, by placing before them a decisive practical test, invites them to produce a book like this Qur'an.

﴿And if you are in doubt concerning what We have sent down upon Our servant, then produce a surah like it, and call your witnesses other than Allah, if you are truthful.﴾ (23)

"If you have doubt about whether this Book which We have sent down upon Our servant is from Us or not, then bring forth a single surah like it. Call all your supporters, leaving aside Allah, take help from whomever you wish, if you are truthful."

This challenge begins in a particular manner, which is significant in this place. Here Allah, the Exalted, mentions the attribute of servanthood of the Prophet (ﷺ): that We have sent down the Book upon Our servant. If you have doubt about whether it is from Us or not, then bring forth a book like it.

Calling the Prophet (ﷺ) "Our servant" points to several interrelated matters. For instance, by calling him "Our servant," his greatness and elevated station are indicated. The purpose is that servitude and slavehood to Allah is the highest honour that can be given to a human being, and the one in which anyone may take pride. Secondly, by calling the Prophet (ﷺ) His servant and slave, it is indicated that the Divine Being has no partner and no equal. Rather, all people are His servants and slaves, and even the Prophet (ﷺ), despite being a prophet and a recipient of revelation, is the slave and servant of Allah, and he takes pride in this honour.

In this challenge, the point taken into consideration is that at the beginning of the surah there was mention of the letters of the alphabet, and this Book is composed of those letters and words which are within their reach. If they have any doubt about this Book being revealed from Allah, these letters are present with them. They should compose and bring forth a single surah like it, and in this task they should also make use of all their supporters and helpers, so that they may say something in their favour in this regard. As for the Divine Being, He has already given testimony in favour of His servant that he is truthful.

This challenge, which was given to those who doubt the Qur'an, remained in force throughout the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and after him. It stands in the same way even up to our own age. It is an argument to which no one has any answer. To this day there is a clear distinction between the Holy Qur'an and all human writings and literary masterpieces, and it will continue thus until the Day of Resurrection, and this distinction will continue to confirm the command of Allah, the Exalted, until the Day of Resurrection.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 2, verse 24:

"But if you do not do it, and you will never be able to do it, then fear the Fire whose fuel is men and stones, prepared for the disbelievers." (24)

If this challenge is strange, then the certainty that no one will ever be able to accept it until the Day of Resurrection is stranger still. Had the disbelievers been able to produce a book like this, they would not have hesitated for a single moment. The Qur'an's statement, "They will certainly never be able to produce a book like it," and the fact that for centuries the opponents were indeed unable to do so, is itself a manifest miracle in which there is no room for any doubt. This was a general challenge to the opponents. The field was open to them. Had they been able to bring forth any book like it, the miracle of the Qur'an could have been ended forever. But they could not do so, and they will not be able to do so. Although the address was initially to one generation, in reality it was a challenge to all of humanity, and it constitutes the historical verdict on the inimitability (i'jaz) of the Qur'an and its authority (hujjiyyah).

Those who have some taste for human styles of expression, who have some knowledge of human conceptions about this universe and existence, and who know something of the methods and systems that man has devised, and who have some understanding of the psychological and social concepts he has established, will certainly understand well that what the Qur'an says on this subject is an entirely different thing, and bears no relation to those flimsy houses of cards which this poor human being keeps building. Anyone who is in doubt about this is either ignorant, lacks the ability to distinguish the genuine from the counterfeit, or is mixing truth and falsehood for the sake of some personal interest.

This is why a severe warning comes concerning those who were rendered powerless before this challenge, yet still did not accept this manifest truth:

"fear the Fire whose fuel is men and stones, prepared for the disbelievers."

Why are men mentioned together with stones in this? And that too in such a frightful and terrifying form? Because that Fire has been prepared for the disbelievers. These are the disbelievers whose condition was described at the beginning of this surah in these words: "Allah has set a seal upon their hearts and their hearing, and a covering is over their eyes." These are the very people to whom the Qur'an issues this challenge, and who, though they are rendered powerless in accepting it for centuries, still do not accept the call to truth. Therefore, these people are, as it were, stones like stones, although in outward appearance they look like human beings. Now the only thing left to await is that on the Day of Resurrection these stones of that kind and the stones of humanity will be gathered together in Hell.

Here, by mentioning stones, a specific meaning is intended to be impressed upon the mind, namely the terrifying nature of the Fire. Observe how it consumes the stones, and within that Fire observe the condition of those wretched people who will lie buried beneath the stones.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 2, verse 25:

Now, in contrast to that frightening and dreadful scene, look at the other side: how abundant are the bounties and honours awaiting the believers?

﴿And give good tidings to those who believe and do righteous deeds, that for them are gardens beneath which rivers flow. Whenever they are provided with a fruit therefrom as provision, they will say, "This is what we were provided with before," and they will be given it in resemblance. And for them therein are purified spouses, and they will abide therein eternally.﴾ (2:25)

These varied bounties and honours: the gaze travels to them and settles upon the purified spouses among them. These fruits will resemble the fruits of the past, and the people of Paradise will think that they were served with such fruits in the past as well. Or they will be given fruits resembling those fruits, but when they taste them, their amazement will know no bounds, for the flavour will be distinct each time and full of delight. At every step they will have new experiences which will show that they are living in an atmosphere of the satisfaction of Allah. How wonderful is this subtle delight: each time, in an apparently similar form, they are given a new blessing.

This similarity of form and this diversity of taste and reality is a distinguished craftsmanship of Allah Almighty in the creation of the universe, through which this universe appears as a great reality. To clarify this great point, it is appropriate that we ourselves study it. Look: all human beings are one in terms of creation. The head, the body and the other organs are all alike. All are made of flesh, bones and nerves. All have been given two eyes, two ears, one nose and one tongue, and all have been created from that same single living cell. In matter and form they are all alike, yet in morals and capacity there is a difference between one and another like the difference between earth and sky, and despite this outward similarity, this difference is sometimes even greater than that between the heavens and the earth.

When a human being reflects on these subtleties of the Creator's craftsmanship, his mind is bewildered. Consider! What variety there is among the different kinds and species of creatures: different forms and multicoloured characteristics, distinction in capacities and qualities, yet all of these things began from one and the same cell, which in its composition and structure is entirely uniform.

So which dark-hearted person is there who, on seeing these manifest signs and evidences of Allah's power, still does not adopt worship and servitude to Him alone? And who is there who, despite these miraculous proofs and clear demonstrations, associates anyone as a equal with Allah in His Being and attributes? Although these countless signs and these abundant proofs are before his eyes and he continually observes them. Many proofs also exist which are hidden from his sight and observation.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 2, verse 26:

Earlier, at the beginning of the surah, the Qur'an had likened the hypocrites, who were among the Jews and polytheists, to a person who kindles a fire, or to one who is caught in a storm of darkness, thunder and lightning in the sky. Moreover, in the Qur'an revealed in the Meccan period, which was commonly recited in Madinah, several parables had also been stated. For example, those who deny the Lord of the worlds were likened to the spider, and it was said: "Their example is like that of the spider which makes for itself a house, and indeed the weakest of houses is the house of the spider. If only they knew." In another place it was said regarding those whom they call upon, to show the helplessness and impotence of their condition: "Those whom they call upon besides Allah, even if they all gathered together, could not create a fly. And if the fly should snatch away something from them, they could not rescue it from it. Weak are the seeker and the sought." 

These verses show that the hypocrites, among whom were both Jews and polytheists, used to object to such parables, saying that these parables mock the hypocrites. They mention insignificant things such as flies and spiders, and it is obvious that the sacred Being of Allah, may He be glorified, is far above this. This objection is one of the various aspects and stratagems of doubts and confusion spread by the polytheists of Makkah and the hypocrites of Madinah.

Accordingly, these verses refute these doubts and explain what Allah's purpose is in the statement of parables: the disbelievers are warned, so that they may refrain from this deceit, and the believers are reassured that these examples will increase their faith.

﴿Indeed, Allah is not shy to present as an example even a gnat or what is above it.﴾ That is, Allah is not ashamed to give as examples a mosquito or anything even more insignificant. Because just as Allah is the Lord of small things, He is also the Lord of great things. He is the Creator of the mosquito and also the Creator of the elephant. Just as the creation of the elephant is a miracle, so too the creation of the mosquito is a miracle, and the life of both is a hidden secret whose knowledge no one possesses except Allah until today. Moreover, a parable is a mode of expression, and its purpose and aim is only that, with its help, the intended matter is clearly explained and fixed in the mind, not that the thing to which comparison is being made must itself be something magnificent. There is nothing in the coining of parables whose mention is blameworthy. Rather, through the statement of these parables, Allah desires to test hearts and examine souls.

﴿As for those who believe, they know that it is the truth from their Lord.﴾ Those who are ready to accept the truth recognise, on seeing these very parables, that it is the truth which has come from their Lord. By their faith they receive guidance from Allah, may He be glorified, in the manner befitting their station. They also know what wisdom lies hidden in these parables. Their hearts are overflowing with light, their souls are sensitive, and their minds and hearts are open to this guidance. Whatever command comes to them from Allah, whatever word of Allah reaches them, they know well its wisdom and its context.

﴿As for those who disbelieve, they say: "What did Allah intend by this as an example?"﴾ This is the question of one from whose sight the light of Allah and His wisdom are hidden. He does not know the Sunnah of Allah and the plan of Allah. Such a question is asked by those in whose hearts there is no reverence for Allah, and who do not look upon the dealings of Allah with the eyes with which a servant and obedient slave of Allah looks upon them. Such people sometimes say these things by way of objection and displeasure, or they say such things because they do not believe that Allah could speak in such a way.

In response to this conduct of theirs, by way of warning and admonition, they are answered that behind these parables a special plan of Allah is at work. These parables are deciding the destiny of people.

﴿By it He leads many astray, and by it He guides many; and He leads astray by it none but the defiantly disobedient.﴾ This is the law of Allah's creation: He puts human beings to trial and test, and in these trials and tribulations every person adopts a course of conduct in accordance with the demands of his nature and capacity. The course of each person conforms to the way of life that he has chosen for himself. The trial is one and the same, but its effects differ upon people who adopt different systems of life. For example, take affliction and hardship: all people are afflicted, the believer and the defiantly disobedient alike. A righteous person, who holds firm conviction in the mercies and wisdom of Allah, when afflicted, turns to Allah in supplication with greater fear, greater humility and greater submission. But if a defiantly disobedient person is afflicted with hardship, his feet slip, and he moves further away from Allah. He goes out from the ranks of the believers. Similarly, take prosperity and abundance: some people are tested by it. But when a believer receives greater favours and honours, he becomes more alert; he becomes even more sensitive in gratitude to Allah. But when a defiantly disobedient person is given comforts, they ruin him. He becomes afflicted with arrogance and adopts the course of misguidance. In the same way, the outcome of the parables which Allah has stated for people is that ﴿by it He leads many astray﴾, and these are the people who do not accept well the guidance that comes from Allah; ﴿and by it He guides many﴾, and these are the people who know the wisdom of the Lord.

﴿And He leads astray by it none but the defiantly disobedient.﴾ These are the people whose hearts have already become defiantly disobedient. Thus, they depart from the path of guidance and reform, and therefore their recompense is that this misguidance of theirs be further increased.

Just as the opening of this surah described the attributes of the God-conscious (al-muttaqin) in detail, so here the characteristics of the defiantly disobedient (al-fasiqin) are also taken up in some detail. For the address of this entire surah will be directed towards such people. Moreover, mankind in every age remains divided into these very categories, and they are as follows.

﴿Those who break the covenant of Allah after its ratification, and sever what Allah has commanded to be joined, and cause corruption on the earth. It is those who are the losers.﴾ (2:27)

What is the covenant that they break? What is the bond that Allah has commanded to be joined, and which they sever? And what is the nature of the corruption they cause? All these matters are left general in the context, because here the disposition of such people is being described in principle. Their nature is being defined and specified. The purpose is not to narrate a particular incident or specific event, but to clarify a general condition. That is, every covenant that exists between Allah and such people has been broken, and all the human ties that Allah has commanded to be established have been severed by them, and whatever corruption is possible, they continually commit it. Their nature has become corrupted. Therefore they are not bound by any covenant or any tie, and they do not refrain from any corruption. Their example is that of an unripe fruit that has been detached from the tree of life, has rotted and decayed, and life has cast it away. This is why those examples through which believers are guided become a cause of misguidance for such people; the things that are a means of guidance for the God-conscious become a source of straying for these defiant ones.

Such people, who in the form of the hypocrites among the Jews and polytheists were found in Madinah, who were a major obstacle to the call of Islam, and who today, with a slight change of name and title and a very minor difference, remain a heavy stone in the path of the movement, look at the traces of their mischief. ﴿Those who break the covenant of Allah after its firm ratification.﴾ The covenant that is bound between human beings and Allah has many forms and aspects. One is the innate covenant that has been deposited in the nature of every living being. According to it, it is the duty of every living being to recognise its Creator and to worship Him. In human nature there is always a thirst for the belief in God. But sometimes corruption occurs in its sound nature, and as a result a person strays from the straight path and begins to make others equal and partners with Allah. Also, one form of it is the covenant of vicegerency, which was concluded between Allah and Adam (peace be upon him), the account of which will come shortly.

﴿Then, if there comes to you guidance from Me, whoever follows My guidance, there will be no fear upon them, nor will they grieve. And those who disbelieve and deny Our signs, they are the companions of the Fire, wherein they will abide forever.﴾ (2:38–39)

Also, one form of this covenant is that which was made through various prophets with various nations, that they would worship Allah alone, and in their lives would adopt only the system of life and the system of law prescribed by Him. All these are covenants which the defiant people break. And when someone breaks a firm pledge made with Allah, then he pays no regard to any other covenant. Whoever has the audacity to break faith with Allah, after that he shows no respect for any agreement or pledge.

﴿And sever what Allah has commanded to be joined.﴾ Allah has commanded that bonds and relationships of every kind be maintained. He has commanded that kinship be upheld with relatives, He has commanded that the great brotherhood of all humanity be established, and that every human be the brother of another. And, above all of these, in the highest rank, He has commanded that an ideological brotherhood and a brotherhood of faith be established, because no bond or relationship is strong except through faith and ideology. When those ties and relationships that Allah has commanded are broken, then all bonds are broken and all connections come to an end. Disorder becomes widespread on earth and evil and corruption spread.

﴿And cause corruption on the earth.﴾ There are also many forms of spreading corruption on earth. All of them are the result of breaking the covenant of Allah, severing the ties that Allah has commanded to be joined, and disobedience to Allah. And the source of all these corruptions is that a person abandons the system of life that Allah has prescribed for human life and its affairs. The Islamic system of life is the path which is separate from all those other paths that end in evil and corruption. If the affairs of this world were freed from the authority and governance of the Islamic system of life, and this life were removed from the sphere of Allah's Shariah, then it would be impossible for this world to be reformed. Whenever it has happened that this firm bond between human beings and their Lord has not remained, the result has been that the world has been engulfed in a great flood of evil and corruption, human morals have been corrupted, the lives and conditions of people have been ruined, and their livelihood has been destroyed. In short, in such circumstances corruption arises in this earth, in all living creatures upon it, and in all things. And this is that devastation and evil that is produced as a consequence of disobedience to Allah. Therefore, those afflicted with such corruption deserve exactly this: that the things through which believers receive the way of guidance become for them a cause of misguidance.

How can you disbelieve in God when you were dead and He gave you life? Then He will cause you to die, then bring you to life again, and then to Him you will be returned.

Disbelief in Allah in the face of such strong proofs is a vile and reprehensible course of denial, which has no authority or evidence behind it. The Qur'an here presents a reality from which they have no way of escape. They are compelled to accept this reality and its necessary consequences. The Qur'an places before them the caravan of life and its various states and conditions, so that they may reflect upon it.

There is no doubt that human beings were dead, Allah gave them life, and it is Allah who brought them from the state of death to the state of life. This is a clear reality, and apart from the power and creation of Allah, they can offer no other explanation for it. They are alive; there is life in their physical hearts. Who is the creator of this life? Who is it that brought into lifeless matter this additional attribute, the attribute of life? For lifeless matter, which is overcome by death and stillness, is entirely different from the nature and reality of life. The question is: what is the source of this life? The truth is that this is a question which the intellect and the soul always seek a real and satisfying answer to, and it is not possible for anyone to ignore this question. Furthermore, no answer to this question can satisfy a person which does not acknowledge a Creator Being beyond this material world.

In short, this life which flows upon this earth, and whose nature is entirely different from that of inanimate matter, from where did it come? The only satisfying answer is that it came from Allah and is a manifestation of His power. This answer alone is one that can be understood. If someone does not accept this answer, we ask them: then bring forward a satisfying answer.

This is the reality which the Qur'an places before the people on this occasion: ﴿How can you disbelieve in Allah when you were dead and He gave you life?﴾ That is, you were lifeless in the same way as this universe spread around you is lifeless. He created life within you and made you alive. How can anyone deny his Creator? ﴿Then He will cause you to die﴾. This too is a reality that no one can deny, because the death of living, soul-bearing creatures is a daily routine and observed fact. Therefore, after life, death is a reality which imposes itself upon minds, and there is no room for any kind of debate or dispute about it. ﴿Then He will bring you to life again﴾. This was the reality about which they had doubts, and therefore they used to dispute about it; and even today some perverse people doubt it, having returned to the ignorance of centuries ago. But if a person reflects that before this he was nothing, and he was brought into existence, then it is not beyond reason that after death he may be brought to life again. Thus this belief is no wonder that must necessarily be denied.

﴿Then to Him you will be returned.﴾ Just as He created you the first time, so you will return to Him; just as He spread you over the earth, so you will be raised up; just as you were brought out from the state of death into this living state, so you will return to Him, so that He may enforce His command among you and decide your disputes.

This is a brief verse, yet within it Allah has, in a moment, both spread out the entire scroll of life and rolled it up again. A flash occurs, and it is seen that all of humanity is in the power of Allah. Allah first made them alive and spread them over the earth, then death suddenly seized them, then there is the scene of the Day of Resurrection in which all of humanity rises and returns to Allah, exactly in the same manner as He had first brought them to life. In this swift mode of expression the complete power of Allah is clearly visible, and it leaves profound effects upon human perception and consciousness.

This is followed by another dazzling light that completes the first. ﴿He it is Who created for you all that is on the earth. Then He turned to the heaven and made it into seven heavens, and He is Knower of all things﴾. ﴿He it is who created for you whatever is on the earth, then turned to the heaven and fashioned it as seven heavens, and He has knowledge of all things.﴾

Exegetes (mufassirin) and theologians (mutakallimin) have engaged in lengthy debates on God's creation. They discuss priority and posteriority, istiwa' (ascending or settling), taswiyah (fashioning), and other points of kalam (scholastic theology). Yet these scholars forget the reality that before and after are merely human concepts, and have no meaning for God. Nor do they keep in view that istiwa' and taswiyah are human linguistic terms which bring the Infinite Being closer to the limited human imagination. There is nothing more to them than that. The lengthy discussions that Muslim scholars conducted on such Qur'anic expressions were the result of the calamity and disaster that descended upon the Muslim community in the form of Greek philosophy and the theological discussions of the Jews and Christians. These debates arose when that philosophy and those theological discussions had clouded the simple minds of the Arabs and the pure thoughts of the Muslims. It is by no means appropriate for us now to fall needlessly into this same calamity and lose the beauty of the Holy Qur'an in logical and theological dialectics.

Therefore, we should free ourselves from these artificial expressions and terminology and see what is the reality of creating the entire universe for man. What is expressed by this reality? Keeping this in view, what purpose of human existence is established? What are man's duties on this earth? What is man's worth in the sight of God? Moreover, what is the value of man in the Islamic conception of life and the Islamic conception of the universe, and what is man's position in the Islamic system of life?

﴿He it is who created for you all that is in the earth.﴾ Here the word "lakum" (for you) carries profound meaning. It expresses the deep reality that God has created this human being for a great purpose. The purpose of his creation is that he should be God's deputy and vicegerent (khalifah) on earth. Whatever is within the earth should be his possession, and he should be influential in it and have authority over it. Because among the vast and extensive creation of God, he is the supreme creature. He is the first heir to this vast inheritance. Therefore, his role in the circumstances and upheavals of this earth is also of the first order. Just as he is the master of this earth, so he is also the master of its instruments. He is not confined and helpless in the grip of the means of production, as in today's material world, where man has become helpless before those instruments. Nor is he subject to the changes and transformations which those instruments produce in human relations with one another, as in today's materialistic conception of life, where man and his role are regarded as ever more worthless, and he is made a slave of lifeless and unconscious instruments. Whereas he is superior to them and their master. According to the Qur'an, among all values there is none that can be superior to the worth of humanity. Man should not be humiliated and disgraced while something else is exalted and lofty in comparison to him. All aims which result in the degradation of human humanity are contrary to the very purpose of man's existence and are therefore reprehensible, even if they bring countless material benefits. Thus, according to the Islamic conception of life, the nobility of man and his superiority is the first value, which takes precedence over all values. All material values are subordinate to it and come after it in rank.

The blessing which God mentions here, and at whose ingratitude He reproves, is not merely that God has blessed man with all the bounties of the earth. It is also that man is the owner and disposer of all these things, and that man's worth is higher than all the material values over which this earth prevails. The favour mentioned here, beyond the ownership of the universe and the benefit from the earth's treasures, is the blessing of human nobility and the superiority of man.

﴿Then He turned to the heaven and fashioned it as seven heavens.﴾ Here there is no need to inquire into the reality and nature of istiwa' ila al-sama' (turning to the heaven). For us, it is sufficient to know what turning toward the heaven means. Istiwa' ila al-sama' is a manner of expressing the manifestation of divine power, that is, God willed creation and formation. Likewise, there is no need to determine the reality of the seven heavens, their shape, or their boundaries. It is sufficient to grasp the basic and general meaning of the verse. Since the disbelievers denied the Creator and Guardian of the universe, it is stated here that God alone is the Creator of the heavens and the earth. He has subjected all creatures of the earth for the benefit of humans and has established such order and harmony among the heavens that the continuation of life on this globe has become easy and simple.

﴿And He is Knower of all things.﴾ He alone is the Creator of all and the Governor of all, so it is obvious that He also has knowledge of everything. That He manages the entire universe while also having knowledge of the entire universe is a reality which serves as an impetus to faith in the one, unique Creator of this universe. Through it, man turns toward the worship of this one, unique Governor, and in gratitude for the blessing, he performs the worship of his Provider and Benefactor.

Here the introductory discussions of the surah conclude. Throughout this entire discussion, emphasis has been placed on people believing and adopting the path of the believers and the God-fearing.

**Lesson 3 at a glance**

In the Qur'an, stories are related on various occasions. The occasion and context themselves reveal the purpose of narrating that story here, which part of the flow of speech is being addressed, in what form the story is presented, and the style of expression in which it is narrated. Such a style of speech creates harmony in the spiritual, intellectual and artistic atmosphere. On the one hand, the subject of the discourse is fully addressed, and on the other hand, the psychological purposes of narrating the story are also fulfilled, and the effects that are intended to be produced by bringing in the story are achieved.

Some people have the illusion that there is repetition in the Qur'anic stories, because one and the same story is repeated in various forms in several places. But upon deep study, it becomes clear that where some part of a story, or the whole story, is repeated somewhere, it is not narrated in its previous form. Rather, in the two places the extent of the story, the context of the discourse, and the style of expression are entirely different. Wherever a part of a story is repeated, a new point is intended to be made. Therefore, in reality, there is no repetition in the narration of stories in the Qur'an.

Some shallow-minded people also say that some of the events narrated in the Qur'an are fictional, or that alterations have been made in their narration, that is, these stories were brought merely for purposes and the embellishment of speech. But whoever has a sound nature and reads the Qur'an with open eyes readily discovers the truth that at every place a story or part of it is brought in accordance with the subject under discussion. Moreover, the manner of expression and style of narration are also entirely different according to the occasion and circumstances. The Holy Qur'an is a book of da'wah (invitation to faith), a system of life, and also the constitution of a system of life. It is not a book of entertaining tales or history. For this reason, selected stories are also related during the propagation of religion. The style of narration and the extent of the stories are decided in light of the context of the speech and the suitability of the situation. In narrating stories, only the best qualities of graceful expression are observed. For the sake of emphasis, events have nowhere been added. Rather, at every place the events are presented in a completely unique manner, and for impact, reliance is placed only on the power of truth and the beauty of expression.

Qur'anic stories are in reality the account and record of the long and continuous journey of the caravan of faith, and the Qur'an has condensed the long story of the propagation of religion, which was presented to people generation after generation and which people continued to accept. On one hand, these stories present the states of faith of those chosen individuals of humanity who were selected for this task, and on the other hand, they show what the nature of the relationship was between these chosen individuals and the Lord of the worlds. Through these stories we see how this caravan of the people of generosity marches along this long highway. Filling the heart with the light, radiance and purity of the heart, it advances, awakening within the heart the awareness of this precious possession, faith, and its importance in this universe. Distinguishing the faithful conception of life from all other transient conceptions of life, it establishes it in the sensibility and consciousness of humanity. This is why a large part of the Holy Qur'an, which is a book of da'wah, consists of such stories.

Now we should, in the light of these explanations, study the story of Adam, as the context of the speech indicates. Before this, the discussion concerned the life of the human caravan, or rather the existence of this entire universe. Then, while mentioning God's blessings upon man, the earth was mentioned, and it was stated that whatever is in this earth has been created by God for humans. In this connection, the story of the bestowal of the office of caliphate upon Adam (peace be upon him) on this earth begins. God entrusts the authority over the earth to Adam (peace be upon him), but this entrustment is conditional, and a covenant is made with Adam. God also grants Adam (peace be upon him) the necessary measure of knowledge and understanding that was required to bear the burden of the caliphate. Furthermore, since God later made the covenant of the caliphate with the Children of Israel, the story of Adam serves as a prelude to it, because God afterwards removed the Children of Israel from this caliphate, and the mantle of the caliphate was handed over to this Muslim community, which fulfils God's covenant well. Thus this story fully harmonises with its context. Now we should, for a moment, read the circumstances of the beginning of humanity, and see what precious guidance is hidden in their background.

The curtain rises, and first of all we arrive at the stage of the higher realm. Through the brightness of the heights and the light of insight, we are watching the story of the beginning of humanity being staged in this way.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 2, verse 30:

And mention when your Lord said to the angels, "Indeed, I am going to place upon the earth a successive authority (khalifah)." Then consider the moment when your Lord said to the angels that He was going to appoint a khalifah on the earth. From this it becomes clear that it is a special decree of the higher realm that this new creature (man), brought into existence in this universe, should be given all the authorities of this earth. He is left free in this world, and the manifestation of the purpose of this universe's creation, and the aim and objective for which it was brought from non-existence into existence, together with the task of putting these into effect, is entrusted to this human being. And this human being is assigned to the work of analysing and synthesising this earth, changing and developing it, discovering the treasures hidden within it, finding out and seeking out its raw resources, and bringing them under his control. All of this is to be by the command of Allah, and is to be a part of the great mission that Allah Almighty entrusted to this human being.

Furthermore, from the istikhlaf (appointment as khalifah) of Adam it also becomes known that Allah has deposited within this new creation (man) hidden powers and has given him such capacity that through it he can put to use all the hidden forces, all the beneficial treasures and all the raw materials within this earth. Allah Almighty has given him inner and concealed powers through which he can bring into effect that divine will.

Moreover, it also becomes evident from this that there is complete harmony and concord between the laws of nature and the regularities of the physical world that govern this universe, and the laws of the Shariah that apply to this human being and his faculties, so that there is no clash or contradiction between these two sets of laws, and human power and capacities are not shattered by colliding with the laws of nature and the regularities of this great universe.

Furthermore, it also becomes known from this that this is an honour which was bestowed upon the human being, Hadrat Insan, within this universe and over this entire earth. This is the dignity which the merciful Creator of man and the generous Lord chose for him, and how exalted is this station! All these matters are known from this sublime indication of the higher realm: "Indeed, I am going to place a khalifah upon the earth." Especially when today we clearly see, with both physical eyes and insight, that man has done this work in this universe and has fulfilled the cosmic purpose of Allah on this earth for which he was created, and was appointed as His khalifah in this vast dominion.

They said, "Will You place upon it one who will cause corruption therein and shed blood, while we exalt You with praise and sanctify You?" They said, "Will You appoint in it someone who will spread corruption in it and shed blood? While we glorify You with Your praise and sanctify You." From the statement of the angels it becomes known that either they had estimated, from the situation prevailing at that time, what kind of creature was coming, or, in light of the experiences of the creature previously settled on earth, they spoke this word. It is also possible that through their God-given insight they came to know what kind of creature would come; and it is also possible that from the essential requirements of human life on earth they gauged the nature of this creature. Therefore they knew, or at least expected, that this new creature coming would spread corruption on earth and that bloodshed would occur here. They raised this question also because, owing to their pure nature and innocence, they could conceive only of absolute goodness and all-encompassing peace and security. They thought that the sole purpose of this universe's existence and the cause of its creation was that Allah be praised and sanctified, and that this was being fully accomplished by their presence, because these angels continually glorified Allah with His praise and sanctity, and never turned away from His worship and obedience.

But the deep and far-reaching wisdom operating in the structuring and shaping of this earth, and in bringing into play the diversity of life within it, was hidden from their sight. The divine will was that this khalifah of Allah, who would, though occasionally, spread corruption and shed blood, would subdue this earth, develop it, and change its structure, so that Allah's purpose might be fulfilled, and that from this minor and partial evil and corruption there would grow great goods that are general and encompass the whole universe. That is: through perpetual growth in this vast universe of Allah, continuous advancement of civilisation, the eternal process of destruction and construction, constant struggle, unceasing striving, and continual change and transformation, this supreme good and welfare is to be brought into effect.

Then, in answer to their question, the decision was issued by Allah, who knows the unseen and is All-Knowing and All-Aware: "Indeed, I know that which you do not know." [Qur'an 2:30]

Look now, with the eye of insight and amid the most exalted lights, at a gathering of angels in some station of the higher world. In that assembly we see the rank of vicegerency being entrusted to humanity, and we are made aware of the great secret that God has deposited in the being of this human creation. The secret is that God gave man the ability to name concepts so that he could express them, and through these names human beings convey what is in their minds.

What is the reality of names? They are simply various kinds of sounds that a person produces from his mouth, and which indicate the perceptible things and persons that he sees. This is an important faculty that God has given to man to make human life easier on this earth. The true value of this faculty can be grasped only if we suppose, for a moment, that man had no power to name things and to use those names. Now consider what difficulties people would face in understanding one another and in settling their mutual affairs. Suddenly they would be confronted with these problems. If someone wishes to conduct a transaction with another regarding some thing, it becomes necessary to bring that thing forward so that they can reach an understanding about it. If the matter concerns a tree, the tree must be present. If something must be decided about a mountain or a plot of land, all the people must go there. If the matter concerns a human being, that person must be brought forward. Think of it: a storm of difficulties would arise and living would become hard. In short, if God had not revealed to Adam this secret, that every meaning and concept can be expressed through names, our lives would not have advanced even two steps.

As for the angels, what need did they have of this capacity? The nature of their work and their duties did not require them to know the names of everything. Therefore God did not reveal this secret to the angels at that time. When God revealed it to Adam, and these things were presented before the angels, they could not name them. They did not know that by assigning names to various things and persons, they could be conveyed easily through words. So, seeing their failure, they praised God and glorified Him, acknowledged their helplessness and incapacity, and said that their knowledge is limited only to those things that God has given them. In this way God introduced Adam (peace be upon him), and at the end, as the conclusion of the discussion, He guided the angels to the wisdom of God and the vastness of His knowledge: "Did I not tell you that I know the hidden realities of the heavens and the earth? I know what you reveal and what you conceal."
