Allah is reminding them that their condition was such that as soon as their prophet went out of sight, they fell upon the calf. Yet it was in Allah's name alone that the prophet had freed them from the painful punishment of the Pharaohs. Allah, commenting on their attitude, says: ﴿and you were wrongdoers﴾. Who could be a greater wrongdoer than one who abandons the worship of Allah, forgets the will of his prophet, and begins to worship a body like a calf, when it was Allah who freed them from the slavery of those people who regarded the calf of a cow as sacred?

Nevertheless, Allah forgives them. He gives their prophet the Book of guidance, the Tawrat (Torah), in which what was written was a Furqan (criterion) between truth and falsehood, in the hope that these people would abandon misguidance and accept the clear truth.

Even so, there was still a need to purify them with severity, because their corrupted nature could be set right only through the naked sword and the harshest punishment. Their nature demanded that their punishment be both severe and unusual. Accordingly the command came: ﴿And [recall] when Moses said to his people, "O my people, indeed you have wronged yourselves by taking the calf [as a deity], so repent to your Creator and kill yourselves. That is better for you in the sight of your Creator."﴾ "Kill yourselves" means that the guilty should be killed so that it purifies the one who is killed and also purifies the one who kills. From among them, the obedient and honourable should kill. The traditions indicate this to be the meaning of this harsh punishment and severe expiation. Indeed, it was a soul-crushing and heart-rending responsibility, for brother to kill brother, as though one were killing oneself. But this was necessary for the training of their corrupted temperament and cowardly disposition, because their nature inclined toward every evil, and they did not hesitate to commit any reprehensible act. Had they had the ability to refrain from reprehensible matters, they would not have fallen upon the worship of the calf the moment the prophet became absent. This was their remedy, for the ghosts of the kicks do not depart by means of words. It was appropriate for them to pay this heavy ransom so that they might gain some benefit and their corrupted temperament be trained.

But after this punishment, Allah's mercy covers them: ﴿Then He accepted your repentance; indeed, He is the Accepting of repentance, the Most Merciful.﴾ At that time your Creator accepted your repentance, for He is the One who forgives greatly and shows mercy.

But the Children of Israel were still the Children of Israel. They were thick-headed, worldly people, and the unseen world and the Hereafter were hidden from their sight. Therefore all they could think of was to demand to see Allah openly. Those who made this demand were not ordinary people; among them were seventy chosen and distinguished men whom Moses (peace be upon him) had selected from the whole nation at the time of meeting his Lord and had taken with him. The full details of this have already been described in the earlier Meccan verses. In short, before seeing Allah openly, the Children of Israel plainly refused to believe. The Qur'an, by recounting the impudence of the forefathers of the Children of Israel here, wants to show that from ancient times this people has been afflicted with obstinacy and stubbornness, and that their ancient obstinacy is exactly like the obstinacy they now display against the Final Prophet (ﷺ). Just as their forefathers did, these people themselves are demanding miracles, and they are also trying to persuade the simple-hearted believers to make such demands, so that they may test the truthfulness of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 2, verse 55:

Allah's countless signs, His favours repeated again and again, and His pardon and forbearance had no effect at all on their material nature and materialistic disposition. Despite all these blessings, these people were extremely quarrelsome and deceitful, and without a severe punishment and retribution they were by no means ready to accept the truth. This shows that slavery to Pharaoh and his oppressive system had badly distorted the very nature of these unfortunate people.

It should be remembered that when an oppressive and tyrannical system remains imposed upon a people for a long time, that people's sound nature is completely distorted, and all human virtues and good qualities are gradually destroyed in them. Through slavery, the fundamental virtues and essential elements of humanity are lost, and the well-known and base traits and habits of slaves come into being within the nation. It is the habit of such people that when a stick is held over their heads, they become submissive; but as soon as they are freed and gain strength and comfort in the shade of freedom, they go beyond their bounds and begin to rebel like demons. This was the very condition of the Children of Israel, and they remain upon it to this day.

For this reason, they utter such words of disbelief and fall into the deep pit of humiliation and misguidance.

﴿And when you said, "O Moses, we will never believe you until we see Allah openly."﴾ Remember when you said to Moses that you would by no means believe his word unless you saw God with your own eyes, openly (speaking with you).

For this reason, while they were still on the mountain, Allah punished them for their disbelieving attitude: ﴿So the thunderbolt seized you while you were looking on.﴾ At that moment, before your very eyes, a terrible thunderbolt struck you.

Then, after this, Allah's mercy again covers them. They are given a second chance at life so that they may take heed and give thanks to the Lord of Glory.

Here Allah reminds them of this blessing: ﴿Then We raised you up after your death, so that you might give thanks﴾ ("But then We brought you back to life after your death, perhaps you would become grateful for this favor.")

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 2, verse 57:

After this, Allah reminds them of the favours and kindnesses He bestowed upon them in the barren plain of Sinai. They were given the food they needed to eat, for which they did not have to make any special effort; it came to them without toil. Then, by His wisdom and special providence, Allah protected them from the scorching heat of the desert and the sun that burns.

﴿And We shaded you with the clouds and sent down upon you the manna and the quail. Eat of the good things with which We have provided you. And they did not wrong Us, but they were wronging themselves.﴾ "We shaded you with the clouds, provided you with the food of manna and salwa, and told you to eat of the pure things We have bestowed upon you. Yet your forebears' conduct was not a wrong done to Us; they wronged only themselves."

It is related in the narrations that Allah kept a piece of cloud fixed over their heads so that they would be protected from the heat. The climate of the desert is such that without clouds and rain it becomes like a boiling hell, with flames of fire rising from it. But if rain falls in the desert and the sky is overcast, its weather becomes fresh and extremely pleasant, in which both body and soul feel delight. The narrations also state that Allah provided them with manna, which was found on trees and was as sweet as honey. Moreover, Allah created an abundant quantity of quail for their food, and they were found in large numbers near their dwellings. Through these two things Allah arranged for the Children of Israel a delicious food the like of which did not exist in the world. He made the place of their residence pleasant and made these pure things lawful for them. But now, just look at the conduct of this people! Do they now become grateful or not? Do they find guidance or not? The last part of the verse clearly points out that they denied all these blessings and committed injustice, but this injustice was against themselves.

﴿And they did not wrong Us, but they were wronging themselves.﴾ "The conduct of your forebears was not a wrong done to Us; they wronged only themselves."

After this, the long account of the Children of Israel's deviation, their denial of the truth, and their persistence in disobedience continues further.

Some reports make it explicit that the village referred to is Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem). After the exodus from Egypt, Allah commanded the Children of Israel to enter this city. At that time the Amalekites were settled in it, and the Children of Israel were commanded to drive them out. But the Children of Israel refused and said: "O Musa! A mighty people dwells in this city. We cannot enter it until they leave it. If they leave, then we will enter." Concerning this same city they had also said to their Prophet, Musa (peace be upon him): "O Musa! We will never enter this city as long as these people are in it. Go you and your Lord and fight them; we will sit here." So Allah inflicted this punishment upon them: they wandered about for forty years. Their existing generation all died, a new generation came into being, and under the leadership of Yusha' ibn Nun (Joshua son of Nun) they conquered the city and entered it. But even after this long punishment, they did not do as Allah had commanded them: to enter the city bowing down in humility and submission, and to say "Hittah, hittah" (a request for forgiveness). They did not enter in the manner Allah had prescribed, nor did they utter the words Allah had commanded.

Here Allah recounts their historical disobedience and places it before them. Moreover, historically this event came immediately after the subject under discussion, namely the exodus of the Children of Israel, so it is mentioned here as well. This manner of the Qur'an shows that it regards the entire history of the Children of Israel as a single unit, whose beginning, middle and end are all alike, because these people are always seen throughout their history as opponents of truth, rebellious, disobedient, and strayed from the right path.

Whatever the historical details of this event may be, we have no certain knowledge of them. However, the event that the Qur'an presents before them is known to them. They know what is being alluded to here: Allah helped them, and they entered that particular city. Also, Allah's command was that they should enter the city in a state of humility and submission, and ask Allah to forgive their errors. Allah had also promised them that He would forgive their mistakes and grant further bounty and favour to those who do good. But these people, in accordance with their habitual conduct, violated this command as well: ﴿But those who did wrong substituted a word other than that which had been said to them﴾.

Here Allah refers specifically to those who altered the command and advice of Allah. That is, "those who did wrong" (alladhina zalamu): either because it was a group from among the Children of Israel who did this, or in order to establish that all the Children of Israel were wrongdoers and that all of them committed this abhorrent act.

﴿So We sent down upon those who did wrong a punishment from the heaven, because they were defiantly disobeying.﴾ The punishment was for the disobedience they were committing.

The rijz (punishment) means chastisement, and fisq (defiant transgression) means opposing the command and going outside the bounds of truth. Both of these qualities were present among the Children of Israel in full measure, along with other qualities.

Allah, just as He provided shade for the Children of Israel in the scorching heat of the desert and arranged their food in the barren, open wilderness, likewise made a special arrangement for their drinking water. And this arrangement too was made in a miraculous manner, like all the other miracles of Hazrat Musa (peace be upon him). The Qur'an mentions this event here as a favour, and then tells what form of response these people gave to this favour and blessing.

Prophet Musa (peace be upon him) asked for water for his people. He made this request to his Lord, and his Lord granted it. Allah told Musa to strike a particular rock with his staff. He obeyed, and twelve springs gushed forth from the rock. These twelve springs corresponded to the number of the twelve tribes of the Children of Israel, because after the grandsons of Prophet Ya'qub (peace be upon him) the people were divided into twelve tribes. Ya'qub's name was Isra'il, and the people are attributed to him. The grandsons of Ya'qub (peace be upon him) are known as the Asbat, a term mentioned repeatedly in the Holy Qur'an. These were the leaders of the Children of Israel, and they lived according to a tribal system. In a tribal system, a tribe is often attributed to its ancestor. Thus the Holy Qur'an says ﴿Every people knew their drinking place﴾, meaning that each tribe knew the spring allotted to it from the twelve springs. ﴿Eat and drink from the provision of Allah, and do not spread corruption in the earth, causing mischief﴾. At that time they were instructed to eat and drink from the provision of Allah and not to spread corruption in the earth.

The condition of the Children of Israel was that they were in the rocky land of a dry desert, while the sky above rained down fiery flames. Yet Allah brought forth water for them from the rocks, and provided Manna and Salwa, honey and birds for them. However, their corrupt and degraded mentality, base nature and habits did not allow them to reach the lofty station for which they had been brought out of Egypt and placed in this waterless desert. Through Prophet Musa (peace be upon him), Allah had delivered them from the humiliation and disgrace in which they had lived, so that the Holy Land would again come under their authority and they would emerge from that life of humiliation and abasement. It is evident that to attain freedom, liberty, honour and dignity, some sacrifices must be made. The great trust that was being handed over to them also required some measure of gratitude. But the Children of Israel were people who were unwilling to pay any price for it. They could neither endure hardships and trials. Therefore they were not even ready to offer thanks for that exalted station. Nor did they wish to abandon the delightful and comfortable life they had led in Egypt. They could not even give up their familiar foods and drinks for the sake of that lofty rank, and they were in no way willing to reshape their lives to some extent in order to attain honour, nobility, liberty and independence. They wanted only the foods to which they had been accustomed in Egypt, and they were fond of greens, vegetables, wheat, garlic and the like. Here in Medina, the Holy Qur'an, in response to their lengthy and broad claims of piety, tells them: just turn over the pages of your own history and see what deeds they performed.

Sayyid Hazrat Musa (peace be upon him) was deeply displeased on hearing their childish request.

"Do you want to exchange what is better for what is inferior? Go down to a city, and you will get what you ask for." Allah wants you to rise to lofty heights, yet you are sinking lower.

"Go down to a city (or Egypt); there you will find whatever you ask for."

This may have two meanings. The first is that what they are asking for is a very ordinary thing, so there is no need for a long petition or prayer; they may go to any city, where these things are available in large quantity. The second is that they should return to Egypt, from where they had been expelled, and resume their former humiliating, degrading and lowly life of servitude. There, they would find plenty of greens, vegetables, wheat, garlic and onions, and they should abandon the lofty purpose for which they had been chosen. If this second meaning is taken, then it is a form of rebuke and reproach from Hazrat Musa (peace be upon him), intended to shame them.

Although some exegetes have regarded this second meaning as unlikely, I believe that if one reflects on the outcome mentioned afterwards, this meaning is more appropriate. It is said:

"Eventually, humiliation, disgrace, lowliness and misery were imposed upon them, and they were overtaken by the wrath of Allah."

The imposition of perpetual humiliation and disgrace upon them, and their being overtaken by the wrath of Allah, did not occur at this stage historically. These people became humiliated and disgraced in later times, when they fell into many evils, which are mentioned in the final part of this verse:

"This was the consequence of their disbelief in the signs of Allah and their unjust killing of the prophets. This was the consequence of their disobedience and of their transgressing the limits of the Sharia."

The occurrence of these evils took place many generations after the time of Hazrat Musa (peace be upon him). However, since they had here made the demand for greens, vegetables, wheat, garlic and onions, therefore, in keeping with their despicable attitude, it is mentioned here that among other causes, one reason for their humiliation was that they were demanding these things.

Therefore, it is most appropriate to understand Hazrat Musa's (peace be upon him) statement, "Go down to a city," as meaning that he was reminding them of their servile life in Egypt and telling them to be grateful for being freed from that life, and not to chase their base carnal desires, to which they had become accustomed during their humiliating life in Egypt.

The atrocities which the Children of Israel inflicted upon the reforming preachers and prophets who called to the path of guidance, and the continuous savage and merciless conduct they displayed towards them, have no parallel in the history of any other nation. They slaughtered, killed and even sawed in two many prophets and reformers; what a worst and savage act it was that proceeded from them... They presented the worst examples of disbelief and transgression of limits. In savage examples of oppression and injustice, they surpassed all others, and they established a record of insolence and disobedience. In short, in all these fields of wickedness and immorality, they performed those outstanding deeds which were and are their own.

Yet, despite all this, they continued to make long and broad, grand claims. Their constant claim has been that only they can be called rightly guided, that only they are the people pleasing to Allah, that only they deserve reward from Allah, and that Allah's grace and bounty are exclusively for them, with no partner in them. Here the Qur'an, refuting their claims, states a principle which is repeated again and again throughout the Qur'anic narratives, sometimes at the beginning and sometimes at their end: that the reality of faith is one, the correct belief is one, provided that through this belief a person bows before Allah, and that faith is such that from it springs forth the fountains of righteous deeds; and that Allah's grace and bounty is not a limited thing, nor is it restricted to any lineage. It is for all believers. All people, whatever time and place they belong to, have been and will be entitled to His grace according to this eternal and everlasting religion of Allah, and finally, in accordance with the last religion (Muhammadan) and the last prophethood, the end of believers will be this.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 2, verse 62:

إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا ........ i.e., the Muslims.

وَالَّذِينَ هَادُوا ............ i.e., those who found the way to Allah, those who are the descendants of "Yahuda" (Judah).

وَالنَّصَارَى........ ........ i.e., the Christians.

وَالصَّابِئِينَ: In my view, the more preferred opinion is that the Sabians (al-Sabi'un) are those among the polytheists who, before the Prophethood (bi'thah), turned away from the hereditary polytheistic religion of their people. Doubt had entered their minds about the reasonableness of worshipping idols, so they sought, through their own reflection, to devise a belief for themselves. As a result of this free contemplation, they arrived at the belief in Tawhid. These people claimed that they were upon the original Din-i-Hanif that Hadrat Ibrahim (peace be upon him) had presented. Accordingly, they abandoned the worship of idols, although they did not call their people to the belief in Tawhid. The polytheists used to say about these people that they had become Sabi', meaning that they had abandoned the religion of their forefathers, just as later the same taunt was used by the polytheists against these Muslims. The statement found in some tafsirs, that these people were star-worshippers, appears less preferred compared to this view.

The purpose of the verse is that whoever among these groups believes in Allah and the Last Day and also does righteous deeds, will deserve a reward from his Lord. No fear or grief will befall them, because in Islam the basis is on belief and conviction, not on nation or lineage. However, this principle of action and recompense relates to the periods before the Prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ). After his Prophethood, it is evident that the final form of faith in Allah (in the form of Islam) has been fixed.

After this, addressing the Muslims and keeping the Jews of Madinah in view, some of the deeds of the Children of Israel are described.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 2, verse 63:

The details of this covenant are mentioned later in other surahs and in this very Surah al-Baqarah as well. The purpose here is only to bring this scene back before their eyes, and to point out that the suspending of Mount Tur over their heads, the taking of the covenant with force, and the command to them to hold fast to the laws of the Torah with full strength, have a psychological and expressive harmony among these matters. They are commanded to adopt resolution (azimah) in matters of belief, because no kind of leniency or compromise can be tolerated in beliefs and ideologies. A policy of "give and take" cannot be adopted in the matter of ideologies. Nor can negligence and laxity be tolerated in this regard. Belief and ideology are a covenant between Allah and the believers: a serious and true agreement. Therefore there is no room in it for falsehood or unseriousness. Immense sacrifices have to be given on this path, because this is the very nature of beliefs and ideologies. Belief is a great thing; in this universe its greatness surpasses everything. Therefore a person should turn to it with great seriousness, understanding it well and keeping its requirements in view, and should face the difficulties that come in the way of the ideology with complete single-mindedness and firm resolve. Whoever adopts a belief in this sense should know that he has now bid farewell to comfort, ease and luxury. When Allah the Exalted called the Prophet ﷺ to discharge the duty of prophethood, he said: "Khadijah! The time of rest and sleep has ended." Likewise, Allah also warned him: ﴿Indeed, We will send down upon you a weighty word﴾ [al-Muzzammil 73:5]. And as was said to the Children of Israel: "Hold fast to the Book which We are giving you, and remember what is in it of commands and guidance." By this means it can be expected that you will attain taqwa (God-consciousness).

But along with taking the covenant with strength, seriousness, single-mindedness and firm resolve, it is also necessary that the Muslims who make this covenant understand the reality of this covenant. They should have a good awareness of the nature of this covenant and pledge, and they should dye their lives in its colour, so that the matter does not remain confined merely to emotions, zeal, power and fervour. For our covenant with Allah is in truth that we will spend our whole life in accordance with this pleasing system of life. This system of life becomes prevalent in the heart and mind as life and living consciousness, and in practical life it appears in the form of a system of life and a way of living. In society it manifests in the form of good character and good conduct, and in the Hereafter it results in taqwa and the consciousness of accountability before Allah.

But alas! The Children of Israel nevertheless remained as they were. Their evil nature overcame them: ﴿Then you turned away after that﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:64]: "Yet after that you turned back from your covenant."

After this, the mercy and compassion of Allah again supported them. The grace and bounty of Allah embraced them, and they were rescued from loss and destruction.

﴿And had it not been for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy, you would have been among the losers﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:64]: "Even then, the grace and mercy of Allah did not leave you, otherwise you would long ago have been destroyed."

Now observe a new scene of their stubbornness, covenant-breaking and trickery, in which they demonstrate that they are not at all fit to keep any covenant. They are simply unable to discharge the responsibilities of this solemn pledge; when their base desires and momentary interests come into view, they become helpless.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 2, verse 65:

In another place the Qur'an has described the details of the violation of the commandments concerning the Sabbath. "And ask them about the town that was by the sea. Remind them that the people of that town transgressed the commandments of Allah on the Sabbath (Saturday), and that the fish would come up to the surface before them on the very day of the Sabbath, and would not come on the other days." (7:163)

The Children of Israel had requested Allah that one day be sanctified for their rest. Accordingly, Allah sanctified the day of the Sabbath and made it unlawful to perform any work for worldly livelihood on that day. After this, they were put to the test: on Saturdays all the fish would come out in great abundance on the surface of the river, and on other days they would disappear. This was a trial before which the Jews could not stand. How could they remain steadfast? Such an excellent catch was right there before them. What more could they have wanted? Would they have let that catch go merely for the sake of a covenant and a pledge? The Jews could not possibly do this; it was against their temperament.

﴿Then We said to them: "Be you apes, despised and cast out."﴾

They had, by breaking the covenant of Allah, become deserving of this punishment. They were deserving of becoming animals, because man is a creature endowed with will, and they had fallen from that station.

It is evident that no animal can think beyond its belly. Thus, as soon as they abandoned the distinctive quality of humanity, namely firm and lofty will and the resolute determination to remain upon the covenant made with the Lord Most Generous, they fell from the station of humanity to the level of bestiality.

It is not necessary that their bodies were also transformed into the bodies of apes. It is possible that in soul, thought, consciousness and disposition they became apes and began to act like apes, because the effect of thought always falls upon the face, form, bearing and movements. The outward state of a person is deeply affected by his thought.

This event was a most instructive lesson for the opponents of truth in that era and in the eras immediately following it, and for the believers it is an excellent admonition in every age. ﴿So We made it an example for those before it and those after it, and an admonition to the God-fearing.﴾ "Thus We made their end a lesson for the people of that time and for the generations that came after, and an admonition for those who fear Allah."

At the end of this lesson, the well-known story of the slaughter of the cow is now related. This story is narrated in considerable detail in the form of a tale. In the earlier part of the surah, the historical events of the Children of Israel that were mentioned were related in brief and concise terms, because all those events had already been narrated in the Meccan surahs revealed before Surat al-Baqarah, whereas this event had not been narrated anywhere else. This story vividly portrays the stubbornness, disobedience, hesitation and evasion in carrying out commands that characterised the Children of Israel, among whom the Jews of Medina were prominent.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 2, verse 67:

And recall the incident when you killed a man, then began to dispute about him and to throw the charge of his killing upon one another, while Allah was to bring forth what you were concealing. So We said: "Strike him with a part of it." Thus Allah gives life to the dead and shows you His signs, so that you may understand."

The Qur'an has related this story in a manner in which many aspects deserve reflection. One of its aspects is that it clearly brings out the national character and the inherited disposition of the Children of Israel. Furthermore, it also manifests the reality of life and death, the nature of being raised after death, and the boundless power of Allah the Exalted. Then, the artistic excellences of expression and style in this narrative are also worthy of consideration. The beginning of the story, its conclusion, and its harmony with the context are all worthy of reflection.

In brief, in this story of the Surah al-Baqarah, the national features of the Children of Israel have been displayed with great clarity. It appears that their connections with guidance, with the pure and transparent spring of Divine Revelation, and with their hearts have been severed. They have been deprived of belief in the unseen, reliance upon Allah, and the affirmation of the guidance revealed through the prophets. They are constantly hesitant and wavering in accepting the commands and directives of Allah. They are always searching for false pretexts, and often, through their glib tongues and boldness of heart, they resort to mocking the symbols of the religion.

Their Prophet conveys to them the clear command of Allah: "Allah commands you to slaughter a cow." It is evident that this command was, in its own words, perfectly clear and plain, and it was possible to act upon it. The prophet who conveyed this command was their beloved leader, under whose leadership Allah had delivered them from the painful punishment of the Pharaohs, and this deliverance had reached its conclusion through a wondrous, miraculous manner, in accordance with Allah's special mercy, care, and directions. Their Prophet clearly told them that this was not his personal opinion or personal command, but the command of the Lord of Majesty, in whose guidance he was leading the Children of Israel. Now consider well! What answer do these people give to this exalted Prophet? With extreme insolence, folly, and shamelessness, they say to their Prophet that he is mocking them. Behold their shamelessness: in their view, it is as if a commoner who knows Allah is not even present, but rather, the exalted Prophet of Allah can mock them publicly and before the people, not in some ordinary matter, but in a matter concerning the name of Allah and the commands of Allah. They say: "Do you make a mockery of us?"

In response to this foolish and senseless accusation, what could Musa (peace be upon him) do other than say, "I seek refuge in Allah"? Accordingly, he gently explains to them, through hints and allusions, how much respect and reverence is necessary in the presence of Allah, Glorified is His Majesty. He explains to them that the accusation they have made can be committed only by one who is acquainted with the etiquette and reverence of the sacred court, and in whose heart there is the greatness and honor of Allah. Thus he said: "Qala a'udhu billahi an akuna minal-jahilin" (Musa said, "I seek refuge in Allah from being among the ignorant.")

This guidance was sufficient for them, so that now they might come to their senses, return to their Lord, and obey the command of their Prophet. But, after all, they were the Children of Israel. How could it be possible that a command should come and they would act upon it?

They said: "Call upon your Lord for us, that He may make clear to us what it is." (Qur'an 2:68)

Pay attention to the words in which they put their question; those very words show that they still doubt whether Musa (peace be upon him) is joking. They are in earnest. First they say, "Call upon your Lord," as though the Lord of Musa is his alone and is not their Lord. Or, as though the matter concerns Musa alone and they have no particular interest in it: this is only between Musa and his Lord.

Then they ask Musa to find out from his Lord and tell them what the cow "is." The real intent was to ask what kind of cow it should be, but, as mockery and denial, they ask, "Cow! What sort of thing is a cow?" As if they were unacquainted with the nature of a cow.

As to what sort of cow it should be, Musa (peace be upon him) had already told them plainly that slaughtering any cow would suffice to carry out the command. Now Musa (peace be upon him) ignores their question, gives them the correct answer, and tries to bring them onto the right path. He does not begin a philosophical debate with them about the nature of the cow by answering their real question; instead he answers them as a reformer and educator would answer such people, for Allah tests fools and wrongdoers by assigning them the difficult task of being guided to the path of guidance. Musa (peace be upon him) tells them about the cow:

﴿He said: Surely He says that it is a cow neither old nor a virgin, but of middle age between that.﴾ (Qur'an 2:68)

That is, neither very old nor entirely young, but of a middle grade. Yet after this general statement, Musa (peace be upon him) again admonishes them and emphatically tells them:

﴿So do what you are commanded.﴾ (Qur'an 2:68)

If Bani Israel had sought to obey the command, this conversation was sufficient and complete. They should have been content with it: twice this exalted Prophet had set them on the straight path, had taught them the manners of asking questions in the presence of the Divine and of benefiting from the answer, and had again told them to proceed and slaughter a cow of middle grade from their herds. Neither old nor very young, but of middle age: thus they would quickly be discharged of this obligation, slaughter it and carry out Allah's command, and would not put themselves into further restrictions, hardship and difficulty... But alas! Bani Israel were, after all, Bani Israel!

They said, "Call upon your Lord for us that He make clear to us what is its color." So he said, "Indeed, He says it is a yellow cow, bright in color, pleasing to the observers." (2:69)

Thus those wretched people reduced their own wide latitude. Previously the command had great scope and room, but now they were obligated not to slaughter just any cow; rather, they had to slaughter a cow that is of middle age, neither old nor a heifer, then its color too must be yellow, and within that a bright-colored cow. Then it should be neither thin nor ugly, but such that seeing it gladdens the heart. And it is obvious that the observer's delight can be complete only when the required cow is very plump and healthy, full of life and vigor, bounding about and shining. For among livestock these qualities are considered desirable by people, and people generally are pleased to see animals that are full of life, of middle age, and beautiful, and they dislike thin, ugly animals.

In short, until now the Children of Israel had been using evasion and hesitation. Probably that was sufficient, even more than necessary. But even now they do not stop. They keep advancing in their wrong course, making the matter even more complicated. They are imposing further hardship upon themselves. Therefore Allah, too, according to their conduct, continues to make His command more stringent. After all these details have been given, they suddenly again begin to ask about the essence and reality of the cow.

"They said: 'Call upon your Lord for us, that He may make clear to us what she is.' He said: 'He says, she is a cow neither too old nor too young, but of middle age between them. So do as you are commanded.'" Wait, that is not the passage given. I'll translate exactly the text provided.

They said, "Call upon your Lord for us, that He may make clear to us what she is." Then they said, "Ask your Lord clearly on our behalf and tell us what sort of cow is required..."

They offer the excuse for this question and evasion that the matter became confusing for them, and identifying the cow has become a great difficulty. ﴿Indeed, the cows have become confused to us﴾. Now they begin to sense somewhat their obstinacy and quarrelsomeness, and these words come from their tongues reluctantly: ﴿And indeed, if Allah wills, we will surely be guided﴾.

The purpose of this endless obstinacy and debate was that there was no alternative but to make the command more complicated and strict. The wide range of choice that had been provided to them was narrowed and confined, and several more attributes were added to the required cow, although such attributes were not needed earlier, and the scope of obeying the command had been kept broader.

قَالَ إِنَّهُ يَقُولُ إِنَّهَا بَقَرَةٌ لا ذَلُولٌ تُثِيرُ الأرْضَ وَلا تَسْقِي الْحَرْثَ مُسَلَّمَةٌ لا شِيَةَ فِيهَا "Musa said: Indeed He says, it is a cow that is not trained to labour, that neither ploughs the earth nor irrigates the tilth, sound and without blemish."

Now that cow was no longer merely a bright, eye-catching yellow cow of middle age, but along with this it had become a cow that does no labour, does not plough the land, does not draw water, is sound, and its colour is pure with no blemish in it.

Here their minds now become correct. After making the matter harder, imposing as many conditions as possible, and narrowing their own sphere of action to the utmost limit, they now cry out: قَالُوا الآنَ جِئْتَ بِالْحَقِّ "They said: Now you have brought the truth."

"Now" implies that what you were saying before was not the truth. It shows that at this very moment they are becoming certain that what Prophet Musa (ع) is presenting is the truth.

فَذَبَحُوهَا وَمَا كَادُوا يَفْعَلُونَ "So they slaughtered it, though they had almost not done so."

When they act upon the command of Allah and fulfil the obligation of Allah, then here, at the end of the whole story, Allah tells them why He had commanded the slaughter of the cow.

Here we arrive at another aspect of the story of the Cow (Surah al-Baqarah). This aspect manifests the boundless power of Allah. From it we learn the reality of life and death and the manner of being raised again after death, and here the style of discourse moves away from narrative and takes the form of address.

Allah opens up the wisdom behind the command to the people of Musa (peace be upon him) to slaughter a cow. The matter was that they had killed a man, and each person, declaring himself free of the charge of this murder, would accuse another, and there was no witness. The will of Allah decreed that the murdered man himself should reveal the truth, and the slaughtering of the cow before this testimony of truth was in fact an apparent means of giving the testimony. The condition was that on striking him with a piece of the slaughtered cow's flesh, he would come back to life. And so it happened: they struck him with a piece of the slaughtered cow, and he came to life, so that he himself might point out his killer and remove all the doubts and suspicions that had spread concerning the matter of his murder, and thus the truth would come forward with the firmest of proofs. Right would become right and falsehood would become falsehood: milk would be milk and water would be water.

The question is: what was the need for this apparent means and cause? Allah could raise the dead even without it, without any means or instrument at all. The question is:

What is the nature of the connection between the slaughtered cow and the murdered man who was brought back to life?

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 2, verse 73:

In keeping with the habit of the Children of Israel, a cow used to be slaughtered among them as a sacrifice and as a means of drawing near to Allah. As for the scene in which a lifeless piece of flesh apparently produces signs of life in a lifeless corpse, its reality is that the piece of flesh is merely an apparent means, demonstrating the perfect power of Allah, the reality of which it is impossible for a human being to reach. People see its effect and result with their own eyes, but the manner of bringing the dead back to life is beyond their understanding. ﴿Thus Allah brings the dead to life﴾: He brings the dead to life in the way that you see with your own eyes, yet despite that you are unaware of its reality. You do not know how it came to life. The purpose is that in just such an effortless and very easy manner, Allah will bring the dead back to life again.

There is a vast distance between the nature of death and the nature of life. This difference makes the head spin, yet before the power of Allah, passing from death to life and from life to death is a simple and easy process. How? This is precisely the matter that is beyond the grasp of every human being. No one can attain it. To know the secret of life and death is to know the real mysteries of Allah, and in this eternal world it is not possible to reach this secret of Allah. However, a human being can derive admonition and lesson from it by reflecting upon this mystery and secret.

﴿And He shows you His signs that you may understand﴾ (2:73).

Now we come to the beauty of its expression and its harmony with the context.

This is a brief story, whose beginning is also expressed in a very concise manner. At the outset we are not even told why Allah commands the Children of Israel to slaughter a cow, just as the Children of Israel themselves did not know why this command was being given to them. Thus their spirit of obedience and their spirit of submission and contentment are being tested.

After this, the actual story begins. A conversation starts between the Children of Israel and Prophet Musa (peace be upon him). This matter keeps growing, and on the other side Allah is also equally a participant in this conversation, but it cannot be known what conversation took place between Musa and Allah, even though they ask him each time to inquire from his Lord and report back, and he too first asks his Lord and then conveys the answer to them. Although the context of the discourse does not state what Musa asked Allah and what answer Allah gave, this silence and this quietness is more fitting to the greatness, supremacy and exalted station of Allah. The manner in which the Children of Israel were accustomed to conversing, and especially the way they were conversing in this incident, was by no means appropriate for the question and answer between Musa and Allah to be mentioned within it.

At the end, suddenly ........ as was wholly unexpected for the Children of Israel at that time. The Children of Israel are commanded to strike the dead and lifeless piece of the slaughtered cow upon the murdered person, and to see how he comes back to life and speaks. Yet there was neither life in the flesh of the cow nor any means of life in it.

In short, like the other brief and excellent stories of the Qur'an, this brief story adopts a wise style of expression that exactly suits its wise subject matter.

At the conclusion of this final scene of the story, and as the result of the admonitory signs and instructive events that came before it, one would have expected that the hearts of the Children of Israel would melt, and that feelings of the fear of Allah and taqwa would well up within them. But our astonishment knows no bounds when we see that the discourse concludes, quite unexpectedly, on these words.

Here the Jews are compared to stones, and when they are set beside stones they turn out to be even harder and drier. Their hearts are likened to stones, as they are being likened to them here. This is known to the Children of Israel. Earlier they had witnessed the scene in which twelve springs gushed forth from a single stone. ........ They had also seen that when a ray of the manifestation of Divine glory fell upon the mountain, it was crushed to pieces and Prophet Musa (peace be upon him) fell unconscious. Yet their hearts are so hard that no softness or freshness arises in them. No trembling of the fear of God is produced in them. Rather, they are extremely hard, dry, barren and stony-hearted. This is because they are admonished with these words: ﴿And Allah is not unaware of what you do.﴾

These words contain criticism of the Children of Israel and of their long history: disbelief, denial of the Prophets, deceit and treachery, wickedness and debauchery, disobedience and rebelliousness, fearlessness and hard-heartedness, and a history full of obstinacy and cunning. Here the first part of the discussion on this history comes to an end.

Lesson 5: At a Glance

In the passage explained earlier, the conclusion of the discourse was a reminder and admonition to the Children of Israel. It was explained how Allah continually showered His favours upon them, and how, in return, they repeatedly and persistently showed ingratitude. In some places the events and observations concerning Allah's favours and the disobediences of the Children of Israel were narrated in detail, and in others in brief. The account concluded with the verdict that the hearts of the Children of Israel, in accepting guidance, have become as hard, dry and barren as solid stones, and indeed, in their hardness and dryness, their hearts have become harder than stones.

Now, in the verses under discussion, the address turns back to the Islamic community, and the Muslims are told their story and informed how cunning and mischief-making a people the Children of Israel are. In light of their nature and their long history, the Islamic community is warned about their guile and deceit, so that the Muslims are not misled and deceived by their mischief, false propaganda and baseless claims. This long account of the cunning of the Children of Israel, and its repetition again and again from different aspects, shows how extensively the Jewish community was plotting against the Muslim ummah (community) and the religion of Islam in that era, and how they were constantly lying in wait to harm this movement. That is why such a detailed discussion was necessary.

In the course of the discussion, the address sometimes turns to the Children of Israel, so that the Muslim ummah may be reminded of the covenants Allah took from them, and of the various ways in which they broke these covenants. It shows how they went astray, how they broke their word, and then how they denied the Prophets. They also killed several Prophets, because they could not follow the Prophets according to their own desires. It also describes how they transgressed against the Shariah of Allah, how they engaged in unjustified argument and contention, and how they distorted the laws of the Shariah that were in their possession.

Here some examples are presented of the debates, disputes and obstinacy that they engaged in with the Muslims. The Prophet (ﷺ) is instructed to expose the reality of these claims, to make clear the weakness of their arguments, and to present the bright and clear truth in the face of their false plots.

For instance, they believed that they would remain in Hell only for a counted number of days, because they were a people beloved and pleasing to Allah, and had a high station with Him. Accordingly, Allah commands the Prophet (ﷺ) to ask them: ﴿Have you taken a covenant from Allah, which He will not break? Or do you say about Allah what you do not know?﴾

When they are invited to Islam, they say: "We believe only in what has been revealed to us." They reject whatever has come beyond that circle, although it is the truth, and it confirms and supports the teaching that was already with them. Accordingly, the Prophet (ﷺ) is given this guidance: "Say to them: If you are indeed believers in the teaching that came to you, then why did you kill the Messengers of Allah before this, who were born among the Children of Israel?" ﴿Moses came to you with clear signs, yet you took the calf as a god after him while you were wrongdoers.﴾ ﴿And remember when We took your covenant and raised the mountain above you: hold firmly to what We have given you and listen.﴾ They said: "We have heard and we disobey." Their false devotion was such that the calf had settled into their hearts. Say: "Evil is that which your faith commands you, if you are believers." (Al-Baqarah 2:93)

Their claim was that the Hereafter belongs exclusively to them, and nothing will be given to other people there. Allah instructed the Prophet (ﷺ) to invite them to mubahala (a mutual invocation in which both parties call down Allah's curse upon the liar) and to gather in some open place, both sides, and to pray to Allah that He destroy whichever of them is lying. ﴿Say: If the abode of the Hereafter with Allah is exclusively for you, to the exclusion of other people, then wish for death, if you are truthful.﴾ After this, Allah Himself tells us that they will never wish for death. And so it happened: they withdrew from the mubahala, because they knew that in the matter they claimed, they were liars.

In short, in the course of the discourse, the Jews are severely criticised, their deceptions are exposed, and the Muslims are instructed to be cautious about them. The purpose of this measure is to break the force of the secret plots through which they were trying to create dissension within the ranks of the Muslim community, and to make the Muslims alert. Even today the Muslim ummah faces this same cunning and deceit of the Jews, which the predecessors of the ummah once faced in Madinah. Yet, with great regret, it must be said that the Muslim ummah is not benefiting from these Qur'anic verses in the way that the predecessors of the ummah benefited from this divine guidance, and as a result of which they prevailed over the cunning and trickery of the Jews in Madinah. Yet at that time the religion of Islam was new, and the Muslim community had only just been formed. From that time until today, the Jews have been striving to turn the Muslim ummah away from the Holy Qur'an, so that Muslims abandon their religion. This is because the Jews are seriously afraid that Muslims may begin to use against them that same Qur'anic weapon, and may not take those measures for their protection which are the true and effective measures against their deceit and plots. For the Jews know well that as long as the Muslim ummah is deprived of those true sources of its power and supremacy, the Jews can live in peace and tranquillity.

Therefore, it is a fact that whoever distances this ummah from the Qur'an and the religion of Islam is an agent of the Jews, whether he does so consciously or unconsciously, deliberately or without intention. For as long as this ummah is distant from and heedless of the reality, that is, the faith-based system of life, the faith-based Shariah and the Islamic law, Judaism poses no threat. The reason is that the existence of the Muslim ummah, its strength and its unique and genuine source of supremacy, is only one: faith and Islam. This is the one path, and these are the signposts which guide, and by following which a Muslim can reach his destination.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 2, verse 75:

At the end of the previous lesson, Allah had drawn a picture of the state of the hearts of the Children of Israel. From it we learned that they were extremely hard-hearted, dry, and unyielding in their hearts and minds. Allah likened their hearts to stones that were extremely solid, from which not a single drop of water could emerge. They were so rough that a person could not pass his hand over them with ease. For anything to grow within them, or for signs of life to appear within them, was simply impossible.

This is a picture which shows that, because of their frozen minds, their base nature, and their inflexible, prejudiced mentality, they had become unfit to come onto the path of guidance. Therefore, after this portrayal and this indication of despair regarding them, the discourse turns to certain Muslims who still thought that perhaps the Children of Israel might come onto the path of guidance. Such people tried to pour faith into the hearts of the Children of Israel, to bring them somehow to the light of faith. The Noble Qur'an, in an interrogative manner, despairs these believers who think in this way, and says that they should remove from their hearts even the last ray of hope in this matter.

﴿Do you then hope that they will believe for you, when a party of them used to hear the words of Allah, then distort them after they had understood them, while they knew?﴾ O Muslims! Further, the group pointed to here (the Jews) is the most educated community, and the one who knows best the truth that Allah revealed to them in their Book. Like the class of Jewish scholars, who used to hear the Torah, the book revealed to their Prophet, and understood it, yet despite this they would alter it and make such interpretations that the meaning would become something else entirely. And they did not do this because they did not know the proper context of the words, but rather they used to do it deliberately, with intent, knowing that they were distorting. Their thoughts and actions were held in the reins of their carnal desires and expediency, and they ran intoxicated behind the melodies of base aims. When they mistreated the Book of Moses (peace be upon him), in which they also believed, then the Noble Qur'an, which was revealed upon Muhammad (ﷺ), they would certainly treat it even worse, because they had not believed in Muhammad (ﷺ) at all. Therefore, they persisted deliberately in this corrupt mentality and false attitude. When we see that their mentality is corrupt and that they persist knowingly in falsehood, or that their opposition to the Islamic call, their conspiracies against the Islamic movement, and their slander are no longer an unexpected matter.

"When they meet those who believe, they say, 'We believe'; but when they are alone with one another, they say, 'Do you tell them what Allah has disclosed to you, so that they may argue with you about it before your Lord? Will you not then use your reason?'"

The passage above is a quotation from the Urdu translation of Sayyid Qutb's commentary, which I have been asked to render faithfully. "When they meet those who believe, they say, 'We believe'; but when they are alone with one another, they say, 'Are you telling them what Allah has opened up to you, so that they can use it as proof against you before your Lord? Do you not understand?'"

Do they expect that those people will accept your word? Whereas they are extremely irresponsible people, who conceal the truth and distort the Word of Allah. Vices such as hypocrisy, deception, duplicity and trickery have entered their very nature. Then among them there were some who, when they met the Muslims, would say, "We too have accepted faith," meaning, they had accepted faith in the prophethood of the Prophet (ﷺ), because in their Torah there were clear good tidings about the Final Prophet, and they were eagerly awaiting the advent of the Final Prophet. They used to pray to Allah that through the Final Prophet He would grant them victory over the disbelievers. Allah says: "They used to seek victory over the disbelievers before this" (Qur'an 2:89). But when they met one another in private, they would strongly rebuke each other for telling the Muslims the things that are mentioned in the Torah confirming the truth of the Prophet's mission. They would say, "Have you gone mad? Are you telling these people what Allah has disclosed to you, so that they may argue with you before your Lord and establish proof against you?" Thus they would establish a proof against themselves. Here their characteristic nature, utterly devoid of knowledge of Allah, overcomes them; they appear entirely bereft of even a true conception of Allah's knowledge and His attributes. They think that if they do not tell these things to the Muslims, Allah will not hold them to account. Accountability arises only if these things are told to the Muslims.

Even more ridiculous is their statement to one another: "Do you not use your reason?" One does not know what kind of reason and wisdom this is, whose non-use they are rebuking one another for.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 2, verse 77:

Before advancing, the Qur'an cannot help but express its wonder at this way of thinking and this conduct of theirs.

﴿Do they not know that Allah knows what they conceal and what they reveal?﴾ "And do they not know that Allah knows what they conceal and what they reveal? Allah has knowledge of all things."

Now the Qur'an presents the condition of the Children of Israel to the Muslims from another angle. It is explained that among them there are two kinds of people. One group is of the ignorant and unlettered who have no knowledge of the Book of Allah that was revealed to them. Their minds are filled only with delusions, superstitions, conjecture, and pleasing wishes. They think that they are a people beloved and chosen by Allah, and that whatever evil deeds they commit, Allah has forgiven all their sins; therefore they sit with the hope, in their minds, of being easily saved.

The second party is the one that profits unlawfully from this ignorance. Without fear, it fabricates verses and texts from its own side. Through interpretations that serve its own purpose, it turns the meaning of Allah's words into something else. It conceals whatever it wishes, and places before the people whatever it wishes. About things written with its own hand, it spreads the claim that they are the word of Allah, and it does all this for the sake of worldly gains that will end and personal interests, or so that its leadership and superiority may remain established.

Now, of these two groups, from which can we expect that they will embrace faith, respond to the call of truth, and remain steadfast upon guidance? And that they will save themselves from distorting the texts of the revealed Book which stood as obstacles in their path? In short, there is no hope that such people will believe; they will not yield to the words of the Muslims. Destruction and ruin are written in their destiny, and this destruction and ruin, which is their written fate, has been appointed for them because they wrote the verses with their own hands and then attributed them to Allah. This destruction and ruin is the earnings of their own hands, for it was with these very hands that they fabricated those verses and attributed them to Allah.

Among their desires and vain hopes was this: that however much immorality they commit and however much they violate the commandments, they will still be among those who are saved. They will remain in the Fire of Hell for a few days and after that they will arrive at Paradise. It is evident that this wish stands in complete contradiction to their system of justice, its enduring sunnah, and the correct concept of reward and punishment. But the question is: what is the basis of this hope of theirs? On what document do they determine this period? As though a formal agreement has taken place between Allah and them, and within it the term of their punishment has been fixed. This notion is nothing but the baseless hope and self-delusion of ignorant people, and on the other hand this idea is a bundle of lies and fabrications of their deceitful scholars. These are the kinds of hopes on which all those people rely who have abandoned sound belief and way of life, after a long time has passed over them, and whose connection with their true religion has ceased. They know nothing of their religion except its name and a few outward rituals. They become unaware of the reality of religion and its essential subject, yet, because they attribute themselves to that religion, they think that this mere verbal attribution will be sufficient for their salvation.

Now, in this regard, a decisive statement is given to them about the reality of their claim. This matter is derived from Islam's universal concept of reward and punishment, and it is stated as a general rule that the reward will be according to the deed. As you sow, so shall you reap.

Here it would not be without interest to pause for a moment and reflect on the miraculous and artistic manner in which the Quran has expressed this particular principle of reward and punishment and this mental concept, and how it has drawn its picture, so as to seek to understand the causes and secrets of Allah's inviolable command and eternal principle.

"Yes, whoever earns evil and remains immersed in sin, it is as if evil were a kind of earning." Here the intended meaning is merely the commission of a fault, but the words by which it is expressed reflect a well-known psychological state. Those who are afflicted with calamity become accustomed to it, they take pleasure in committing it, they derive enjoyment from it, and they come to regard it as their earnings. For if they found it detestable and disliked, they would not commit it. Furthermore, if they thought that it was a kind of loss, they would not commit it with such zeal and fervour. Moreover, they would not allow evil to dominate them in such a way that their whole world falls into its grip and they become completely entangled in its web. For if these people disliked it, and perceived the loss that lay within it, they would flee even from its shadow, although naturally they would be inclined towards committing it. Furthermore, they would seek forgiveness from Allah Most High and, leaving the sphere of influence of this sin, take refuge in the shelter of another, in which case this evil could neither surround them nor overpower them, and the doors of repentance and of making up for what has passed would not be closed to them. ﴿And his sin has encompassed him﴾, and his wrongdoing has surrounded him. This is an expression that presents this condition and meaning in a embodied form. This is an important characteristic among the artistic merits and distinctive qualities of the Quran, and it is an important sign of the Quran's particular manner of expression. This manner of expression has a special effect on the human mind, which purely abstract concepts and meanings do not have. Abstract expressions that are not in a dynamic form cannot produce such an effect. What better expression could there be for the mental condition of persisting in disobedience than that the sinner himself is confined within the realm of sin, lives within its limits, has become wholly devoted to this calamity, and cannot even draw a single breath of life without it.

And when a person becomes so entangled in a sin that he is surrounded from every side and all the doors of repentance are closed to him, then this just and inviolable decision of Allah Most High is issued: ﴿Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein forever.﴾

Following this judgment and outcome, the ruling for the opposite case is also stated here.

﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds - they are the companions of Paradise; therein they will abide forever.﴾ And those who do righteous deeds - they are the people of Paradise, and they will remain in it forever. And those who do righteous deeds.

That is, it is a necessary requirement of faith that it breaks forth from the heart and emerges in the form of righteous action. Those who claim to have faith should reflect carefully upon this reality, and so should all Muslims who call themselves Muslims, and we ourselves are among them; there is a dire need for us to satisfy ourselves thoroughly about this truth. The existence of faith cannot be conceived unless it produces righteous action as its result. As for those who say that they are Muslims, yet spread corruption on the earth and oppose goodness and virtue, who obstruct the establishment of the Islamic system of life on earth and the implementation of the Islamic Shariah and deny it, and who remain in constant opposition to Islamic ethics, for such people there is not even an atom's weight of the wealth of faith; for them there is no reward with Allah, and no one will be able to save them from the punishment of Allah. Even though they hold within their hearts the same pleasing hopes and wishes that the Jews held, which Allah mentioned above, the ruling for all of them is the same.

After this, some further circumstances of the Children of Israel are set before the Muslims: various incidents of their conduct at different times, their disobedience, deviation, misguidance, and breach of covenant and pledge are related, and these black deeds of the Jews are laid open before the Muslims.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 2, verse 83:

In the previous lesson, where the breaches of covenant by the Children of Israel were mentioned, a reference was also made to this covenant (mithaq). Here, a detailed indication of some of the terms of that agreement is given.

From the first verse it becomes clear that the covenant which Allah Almighty mentions with the Children of Israel is the same covenant that was concluded with them after the Mount Sinai (Koh-e-Toor) was lifted over their heads. They were emphatically commanded to hold firmly to it and to remember the instructions given to them within it. It is likely that it contained a statement of the fundamental matters of religion, and these fundamental matters are the very ones that Islam has now presented before them, and which they are rejecting as something strange and new.

Among the matters on which the covenant Allah made with them was based, one important matter was that they should worship Allah alone and not associate anyone with Him; that is, that they adopt the complete belief in tawhid (the Oneness of God). In this covenant there was also the command to treat well parents, relatives, orphans and the needy. It also contained the instruction that they should enjoin people to good, and it is evident that enjoining good and forbidding evil (amr bil-ma'ruf wa nahy 'anil-munkar) is at the head of good deeds. Moreover, in this covenant prayer (salah) was made obligatory and the payment of zakat was commanded. In short, all these things are such that they are regarded as fundamental matters in Islam as well, and all these matters have been made obligatory in Islam.

Several points are established by the study of this covenant.

First, that the religion of Allah has always been one and the same, which is Islam, and that Islam is the final link of this religion, and it has accepted all the fundamental principles of the earlier laws. Second, the reality becomes evident that the Jews had an extreme hatred for the religion of Islam. Islam was calling them only to those very things to which they had bound themselves in a covenant with their Lord, yet despite this they were rejecting it.

Because of this shameful conduct of theirs, the style of speech changes from the third person (ghaibana kalam) to direct address (khitab). Although previously, leaving aside the Children of Israel, the believers were being addressed, and their evil deeds were being described before them, suddenly addressing them while recounting these black deeds is a cause of deep shame for them: "Thumma tawallaytum illa qaliluman minkum wa antum mu'ridun" ("Then you turned away, except for a few of you, and you are persistently turning away").

From this, some of the secrets become known as to why, in narrating events in this wondrous Book of Allah, there is a sudden shift (iltifat) in speech, and what wisdom is hidden within it.

Now the discourse continues with the Children of Israel. The Qur'an addresses them and shows the contradictions in their stance, and the points at which they violate the covenant they made with Allah.

﴿And remember when We took your covenant: That you shall not shed your blood, nor expel yourselves from your homes. Then you acknowledged it, while you were witnesses.﴾ (84)

"Then remember! We took a firm covenant from you that you would not shed each other's blood, nor drive each other out of your homes. You acknowledged this and you are witnesses to it." Then what happened after this acknowledgement, testimony and witnessing?

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 2, verse 85:

"Yet here you are, killing your own people, expelling a group of your own kind from their homes, backing one another against them in sin and aggression; and when they come to you as captives, you arrange their ransom, though their expulsion was itself forbidden to you. Do you then believe in part of the Book and disbelieve in part of it?"

This event, which the Qur'an presents against them, is the same that had taken place in the wars of Aws and Khazraj some time before the victory of Islam. Aws and Khazraj were two polytheist tribes of Yathrib, and there was such intense enmity between them as had no parallel in all of Arabia. In Yathrib there were also three Jewish tribes, some of whom were allies of one tribe and some of the other. When war broke out between these two tribes, their Jewish allies also took part in the fighting. Thus, at times, a Jew who was an ally of one side would kill a Jew who was an ally of the opposing side, and this was entirely contrary to the firm covenant they had made with Allah. When the allies of one tribe prevailed, the Children of Israel would plunder the Children of Israel, expel them from their homes, and enslave their women, although by the explicit terms of the covenant such conduct was forbidden to them. But when the fighting ended, these victorious Jews would then pay the ransom for the defeated Jews of the opposing side, securing their release from captivity and slavery, wherever they were held, whether in their own camp or in the camp of their enemies. And they did this in obedience to the command of the Torah which said: "If a slave of the Children of Israel comes to you, buy him and set him free."

This was the great contradiction of their life, and placing it before them, the Qur'an asks them:

أَفَتُؤْمِنُونَ بِبَعْضِ الْكِتَابِ وَتَكْفُرُونَ بِبَعْضٍ "Do you then believe in part of the Book and disbelieve in part of it?"

Allah says that this is a clear violation of the covenant. Therefore they are warned that for this they will be humiliated and disgraced in this world, and in the Hereafter they will be given a painful punishment for it. Moreover, they are cautioned that Allah is not heedless of them, and He will not overlook such clear transgressions.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 2, verses 86–87:

After this, the believers are addressed in particular, and humanity in general, and it is explained what the reality of these Jews is and what the outcome of their actions is, the actions they are carrying out.

﴿They are the ones who have bought the life of this world at the price of the Hereafter. So their punishment will not be lightened for them, nor will they be helped.﴾

The question is: how did they buy the life of this world at the price of the Hereafter? It is this: they were prepared to break the covenant of Allah solely so that, for the sake of their worldly interests, they could keep the covenant they had made with the polytheists, and this is a covenant whose fulfilment necessarily requires them to violate their religion and the Book of Allah.

It should be remembered that splitting into two factions and concluding agreements with two allies is an old stratagem of the Children of Israel. They always remain in the middle, and out of caution they join each of the opposing blocs, so that whichever bloc succeeds, their share in the gains it obtains is in any case secure; whichever group succeeds, its success is the success of the Jews. The conduct of those who do not trust in Allah and who do not firmly hold the rope of Allah is always of this kind. Such people always resort to cunning and trickery, and they try to keep the help of human beings against Allah. They give more importance to the covenants of human beings than to the covenants of Allah.

But faith prevents a person from joining any covenant or pact that is against the injunctions of the Shariah and that necessarily involves breaking the covenant made with Allah. No such covenant may be made for the sake of some expediency or for the sake of adopting some measure of protection. For protection lies in a person keeping the covenant made with Allah. Moreover, the greatest expediency is that a person carry out the commands of Allah, the Exalted, and follow his religion.

This was the conduct of the Children of Israel towards their reformers and prophets (peace be upon them)! The Qur'an describes this conduct in detail, establishes it in the light of well-known events, and then suddenly takes them to task, and seizes upon their vile conduct regarding the Final Prophet and this new and last message. The Qur'an tells them: it is you who treated the earlier prophets in this way. Read carefully?
