Here the Qur'an's manner of address becomes harsh and forceful, and in some places it seems as though lightning is striking or fire is raining down. The Qur'an places before them their own statements and their historical deeds, and takes them to task in such a way that these poor people are left entirely speechless. They have no argument left, and they can offer no excuse. In truth, out of arrogance (istikbar) they turned away from accepting the truth. Malice against Islam was filled in their hearts; they kept away from the Muslims, considering them contemptible; they found it very pleasing that no one other than themselves should attain this lofty position; and envy was gnawing at their hearts, asking why this grace and bounty of Allah was descending upon the Muslims. Yet, for the sake of showing people, they would state the reasons mentioned above for accepting Islam. Allah the Exalted rejected these outright, because this was the remedy for their defiant and rebellious stance in the face of Allah and His Messenger.

﴿And they say, "Our hearts are wrapped."﴾ Rather, the truth is that Allah has cursed them for their disbelief, so they seldom believe.

They used to say that there are coverings over our hearts. No new call can reach them, nor are they ready to listen to the cry of any new caller. They said this so that they would discourage the Prophet (ﷺ) and the Muslims, and so that they would give up calling them to this new religion. Moreover, they said these things as the reason for not accepting the Prophet's (ﷺ) call. Therefore Allah, the Exalted, refuting these statements of theirs, says: ﴿Rather, Allah has cursed them for their disbelief﴾, meaning: because of their persistent rejection, Allah, as a punishment, deprived them of being blessed with guidance, and veils came between them and that light. ﴿So they seldom believe﴾.

That is, since they have fallen far from the path of truth because of their persistent disbelief and ancient misguidance, and since Allah has also deprived them as a punishment, therefore they seldom believe. Also, the meaning of this verse may be: "Since they have adopted a disbelieving course, therefore they seldom believe," that is, this is their constant way on which they remain. Both meanings are consistent with the context of the discourse.

This is the commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 2, verse 89:

Their adopting this disbelieving attitude was all the more reprehensible because they were denying the very thing they had been waiting for over centuries, and they had been hoping that through it they would gain dominance over all the disbelievers. Their belief was that through this coming Prophet they would attain victory and triumph. And when he came, confirming the Book that was with them, they took the path of disbelief.

وَلَمَّا جَاءَهُمْ كِتَابٌ مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ مُصَدِّقٌ لِمَا مَعَهُمْ وَكَانُوا مِنْ قَبْلُ يَسْتَفْتِحُونَ عَلَى الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا فَلَمَّا جَاءَهُمْ مَا عَرَفُوا كَفَرُوا بِهِ

"And when there came to them a Book from Allah, confirming what was with them, although before this they had been seeking victory over those who disbelieved; but when there came to them that which they recognised, they disbelieved in it."

Now consider their conduct towards this Book that has come to them from Allah. It confirms the Book that was already with them, and before its arrival they used to pray for victory over the disbelievers. Yet when that which they recognised came to them, they refused to accept it.

This was such a vile act that they rightly deserved to be cast away from the path of guidance. For this reason, the curse of Allah descends upon them, and they are described as characterised by disbelief: فَلَعْنَةُ اللَّهِ عَلَى الْكَافِرِينَ "So the curse of Allah be upon the disbelievers." Then Allah explains that the bargain they made is a losing bargain. Moreover, Allah also reveals the real and hidden cause of this detestable stance and disliked conduct of theirs.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 2, verse 90:

{Arabic verse and Urdu rendering as given in the source:}

"Wretched is the price for which they have sold their souls: that they deny what Allah has revealed, out of envy that Allah should send down His bounty (revelation and messengership) upon whomever of His servants He wills. So they have incurred wrath upon wrath, and for the disbelievers there is a humiliating punishment."

They have bought, in exchange for their own souls, disbelief, knowingly; and this is a very losing bargain for them. In effect, they have made disbelief the price of their souls. Every person sets some value upon himself, more or less, and if he sells his self in exchange for disbelief, this will be a severely losing transaction. Yet it is a fact that they did exactly this, although the matter is stated here by way of parable and vivid depiction.

In this world, their loss was that they could not become members of that honoured caravan of faith. And their loss in the Hereafter is that a most humiliating punishment awaits them, watching for them. For their final end was upon disbelief, and throughout their whole lives they earned nothing but disbelief.

What compelled them onto this course was only that their hearts were filled with envy of the Prophet ﷺ. They thought that the final Prophet would be from among them, but Allah chose Muhammad ﷺ from the Children of Ishmael. Unable to bear, with their hearts so narrow, that Allah should bestow His grace, revelation and messengership upon whomever He wills, they... Their conduct was clear injustice and transgression beyond bounds. Because of this injustice, these people returned deserving wrath upon wrath. Thus, as the punishment for this arrogance, envy and blameworthy transgression, there is a humiliating punishment awaiting them.

A particular temperament found among the Jews is the temperament of ingratitude, and those who hold this temperament are accustomed to living a self-centred life within the confined circle of extreme prejudice. Such people constantly feel that the welfare of others besides themselves is, in reality, their own deprivation. Such people are devoid of the consciousness of the broadest concept of human brotherhood. If one studies the history of the Jews, it becomes evident that for years on end the Jews lived in isolation from all of humanity with this same mentality, as though they had no connection with the tree of humanity. Rather, they always plotted against all of humanity. They always kindled within their hearts the fire of hatred and envy against all of humanity, and thus this hatred and envy remained for them a calamity to their lives. The taste of this hatred and rancour they continued to make all of humanity taste: they always incited some nations against others and set them against one another, so that they might gain material profit from those wars, and thereby keep extinguishing the ever-burning fire of hatred and envy in their hearts. They always schemed to bring about such destructions upon various nations that, as a consequence, at times these very people were also destroyed and ruined. This long chain of evil and corruption was always established because the hearts of the Jews were filled with envy and hatred toward humanity, and these people possessed an extremely self-centred mentality?

بَغْيًا أَنْ يُنَزِّلَ اللَّهُ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ عَلَى مَنْ يَشَاءُ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ
"Out of mere obstinacy, that Allah should send down His bounty (revelation and messengership) upon whomever of His servants He wills."

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 2, verse 91:

﴿And when it is said to them, "Believe in what Allah has sent down," they say, "We believe in what was sent down to us," and they reject what is besides it, while it is the truth, confirming what is with them.﴾ "When they are told, 'Believe in what Allah has sent down,' they say, 'We believe in what has been sent down to us' (that is, to the Children of Israel)."

They reject whatever has come beyond that circle, although it is the truth and confirms and supports the teaching that was already with them. They would say this at the time when they were invited to believe in the Qur'an and to accept Islam. They would say, "We have already believed in what has been sent down upon us, and it is sufficient and healing." Apart from this, they rejected all other guidance, whether it was revealed to ʿIsa (peace be upon him) or to the final Prophet, Hazrat Muhammad (ﷺ).

According to the Qur'an, this attitude of theirs, and their rejection of all other guidance besides the Torah, is a strange conduct.

﴿while it is the truth, confirming what is with them⟩ "Because it is the truth and confirms and supports the teaching that is already with them."

That is to say, what concern do the Children of Israel have with the truth? What has happened that the truth should confirm the teachings that they possess, when they have been deprived of it? They are worshippers of their own desires, slaves of their tribal prejudice, and moreover, they follow their whims. For before this, they had already rejected the guidance that was revealed upon their own prophets. Allah taught His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) to attack them on this very point, in order to expose their reality and clarify the weakness of their position:

﴿Say: "Why then did you kill the prophets of Allah before, if you were indeed believers?"﴾

"Say: If you truly believe in the teaching that came to you, then why did you kill the prophets of Allah before this, who were born among the Children of Israel themselves? You claim that you believed in the prophets of the Children of Israel who brought you the teaching and guidance, so if you were truly believers, why did you kill the noble prophets?"

Not so, for Musa (Moses) was your first prophet and your great deliverer. Even the guidance he brought you, you rejected. ﴿And Musa certainly came to you with clear signs; then you took the calf (as a deity) after him while you were wrongdoers.﴾ "Musa came to you with clear signs, yet you were so wrongdoing that after he turned away from you, you made the calf into a deity." Was this the demand of your faith and of divine revelation? Can you, with such conduct, claim that you have believed in the guidance and signs which Musa (peace be upon him) brought you?

Not only that, but Musa (peace be upon him) took from you a firm covenant beneath a rock and a mountain. Do you not remember that you broke even this extraordinary covenant, and fell into rebellion and disobedience?

﴿And when We took your covenant and raised the mount above you, [saying], "Hold firmly to what We have given you and listen." They said, "We have heard and we disobey." And they were made to drink the calf into their hearts because of their disbelief.﴾

Recall, then, the covenant that We took from you by raising Mount Sinai above you. We had emphatically commanded you to adhere firmly to the instructions We were giving you and to listen attentively. Your forefathers said, "We have heard, but we will not comply." And such was the extent of their false worship that the calf had settled in their hearts.

Here the style of address changes into narration and report. First the Children of Israel are addressed and reminded that you did such-and-such. Then the direction of speech turns to the believers and to people in general, and they are told: look, these Children of Israel did such-and-such. The Prophet (ﷺ) is also made to understand that he should suddenly confront them head-on, and question them about how base and despicable their faith is, a faith which, by their own claim, compels them to adopt such an openly disbelieving and objectionable attitude.

﴿Say: "Wretched is what your faith enjoins upon you, if you are believers."﴾

Say: if you are believers, then strange is the faith that commands you to such evil deeds.

The two pictorial expressions of the Qur'an deserve deep reflection. The first is that they said, "We have heard," but did not say, "We will not comply" at the outset. How did they say both things in a single breath? In reality, this is a silent position and a narrative expression of an actual event. With their mouths they said, "We have heard," but through their actions they proved that they "will not comply." For action is what actually gives meaning to spoken utterance, and practical expression is stronger than verbal expression. This interpretation of the factual situation actually reflects the comprehensive principle of Islam that, without action, mere words and verbal claims carry no weight in Islam. In Islam, the real consideration is action. Between physical deeds and the interpretations of words, action is the true link, and decisions are made on the basis of action.

The second expression, that "the calf was made to drink into their hearts," is a very harsh and unique expression. It is said that "they were made to drink," meaning someone has given them something to drink. What has been given to drink? The calf has been given to them to drink. Where? Into their hearts. How harsh an expression is this! The human imagination strives to see or conceive of a calf entering the hearts. That is, as if an embodied calf is entering their hearts, and this calf has overspread the world of their hearts. For the meaning, such a sensory image has been devised that for a moment the actual intended meaning, namely the love and worship of the calf in their hearts, is hidden from the screen of the human mind, and a person thinks that the calf has actually been dissolved and given to them to drink.

When we reflect from a literary standpoint on such passages, we realise the value of the Qur'an's pictorial mode of expression. In comparison with conceptual and intellectual expressions, how clear and detailed is the Qur'an's sensory expression? By words, a picture of the actual reality is drawn and set before us.

The sensory mode of expression of the Qur'an and its distinctive features include this as an important example.

The Jews made the great claim that they were the beloved creatures of God Almighty, that they alone were upon the path of guidance, and that they alone would surely attain salvation in the Hereafter, and that no other nations would receive anything in the Hereafter apart from them. The clear implication of this Jewish claim was that in the Hereafter the community of the last Prophet, Muhammad (ﷺ), would also be deprived of salvation. The purpose of this propaganda by the Jews was to create an atmosphere of distrust in the hearts of ordinary Muslims regarding the teachings of the Qur'an, the sayings of Muhammad (ﷺ), and the religion of Islam. Therefore, Allah Almighty commanded Muhammad (ﷺ) to invite them to mubahalah (a mutual invocation in which both parties stand up and pray for the destruction of whichever of them is lying), so that both sides would stand and each pray for the destruction of the one among them who is false?

After this, the Qur'an itself declares that these people will by no means accept the challenge of mubahala (mutual invocation of curse), and will never wish for death. This is because they know that they are liars, and they feared that if Allah were to accept the prayer of both parties, they would be seized by His grip. Moreover, they also knew that, because of the evil deeds they had committed in this world, they would have no share in the Hereafter. And if they did engage in mubahala, the result would be that, through the death they had asked for, they would be deprived of this world too, and, because of the evil deeds they had done, they would already be deprived in the Hereafter... Therefore the Qur'an declares in a decisive manner that it cannot be expected of them that they will accept this challenge, because they are the most greedy of all for the life of this world; and this is also the condition of all the other polytheists (rather, in this matter they go beyond them). So He says:

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 2, verse 96:

They will not wish for death because of what their hands have sent forward in this world; they have no hope of any reward in the Hereafter for the deeds they have earned in this world. Nor do they hope that by it they will be able to escape the punishment of Allah. Rather, punishment awaits them there. Allah knows the wrongdoers well, and their evil deeds are also before His sight.

Not only this, but the Jews possess another trait. The Qur'an paints such a picture of this trait that their humiliation, contemptibility and baseness drip from it. The Qur'an says: وَلَتَجِدَنَّهُمْ أَحْرَصَ النَّاسِ عَلَى حَيَاةٍ, "You will find them the most eager of people for life." What kind of life? They have no concern with that; let there be life, of whatever sort it may be. In their view it is not necessary that that life be honourable. They simply want life, even if it is a life of humiliation and contemptibility. Life and well-being... this alone has been the reality of the Jews. This is the past of the Jews, this is their present, and this is the goal they aim at for the future. The Jews raise their heads only when the danger has passed. As long as the danger hangs over their heads, they do not lift their heads; their necks remain bowed, because they are utter cowards and they love living to an extreme degree... What kind of life do they want?

وَمِنَ الَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوا يَوَدُّ أَحَدُهُمْ لَوْ يُعَمَّرُ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ وَمَا هُوَ بِمُزَحْزِحِهِ مِنَ الْعَذَابِ أَنْ يُعَمَّرَ وَاللَّهُ بَصِيرٌ بِمَا يَعْمَلُونَ

"When it comes to life, these people surpass even the polytheists. Each one of them wishes that somehow he might live a thousand years. Yet a long life will certainly not push them away from punishment. Allah is watching what they are doing."

Each one of them desires a thousand years of life. Why? Because they have no firm certainty about standing before Allah. They do not think that there is any life other than this one? And when a person believes that there is no other life after his life, his span of life becomes narrow for him. He finds his worldly life very constricted, because he believes that he has been granted only these few hours and breaths.

When this viewpoint is considered, belief in the Hereafter is a great blessing bestowed upon a human being. It is a blessing whose outpouring, through faith, falls upon the heart of a person. Allah grants this blessing to this mortal human being so that, although he has been given a limited time in this world, a world of hopes is nonetheless populated in his heart; therefore he does not feel the narrowness of life. As for those who deprive themselves of this blessing and close for themselves the door of everlasting life, their minds hold a deficient and distorted concept of "life." In short, belief in the Day of Judgment is belief in Allah's justice and in the recompense of deeds in the Hereafter; and secondly, it indicates that the existence of the believing servant is abundantly filled with the bounties of life, and that he has been granted an eternal life which never ends and does not stop at any boundary, but rather passes through all boundaries and reaches the limits of everlasting survival, the end of which is known only to the Being of Allah. This life rises constantly to ever greater heights until it reaches the station of union with the Divine."

Now Allah turns the Prophet ﷺ towards a new aspect. The Jews are given an open challenge, and the reality is announced that?

The Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 2, verse 97:

Through this challenge we come to know a strange new characteristic of the Jews. Merely because a revelation was sent down to a non-Jew, the Jews fell into intense hatred. Rather, they have set a record of envy and jealousy, and in this matter they have gone to the point of foolishness, making contradictory statements that cannot be expected from any intelligent person. When they learned that Hazrat Jibril (peace be upon him) brings revelation down to Hazrat Muhammad (ﷺ), these people burned and seethed with envy and hatred, and they invented a absurd story: that Jibril (peace be upon him) is their old enemy, because he has always brought Allah's punishment upon them, and through him the Children of Israel have always been ruined and destroyed. Since Muhammad (ﷺ) is connected to Hazrat Jibril (peace be upon him), they do not believe in him. Had Hazrat Mika'il brought the revelation, they would surely have believed, because Hazrat Mika'il is the angel of Allah who provides rain, freshness and the means of joy for human beings. What a frivolous argument this is!

On their foolish statement, a person involuntarily laughs. But when a person is afflicted with hatred and envy, it is not far-fetched that even greater follies proceed from him. For Jibril was not a human being who could be an enemy to anyone or who could form any friendship of his own accord. He did not have the power at all to do any work by his own will. Being an angel, Hazrat Jibril could not disobey the commands of Allah; he would only do what he was commanded.

﴿Say: Whoever is an enemy to Jibril — indeed, he has brought it down upon your heart by the permission of Allah.﴾ Say: if anyone has enmity toward Jibril, he should know that Jibril has sent down this Qur'an upon your heart by the leave of Allah itself.

Jibril (peace be upon him) had neither personal inclination, nor did he send the Qur'an down upon your heart by his own will. He was only the one who executed the will of Allah, and the descent of the Qur'an upon your heart was being carried out by him under the commands of Allah. The Qur'an was descending upon the heart. The heart is indeed the seat of perception, and it is what understands meanings after perceiving and preserves what is perceived. The Qur'an expresses the perceptive faculty of man by the term "qalb" (heart); therefore, the "heart" meant here as the perceiving organ is not the well-known physical lump of blood and flesh, but rather the faculty that performs understanding and comprehension.

Jibril sent down the Qur'an upon your heart (ﷺ) in the state that it is ﴿confirming what is before it, and a guidance and good news for the believers﴾: it confirms and corroborates the books that came before, and it has come as guidance and as good news of success for those who believe.

In principle, the Qur'an confirms all previous scriptures, because the fundamental teachings of all heavenly books and all divine religions were one and the same, and it is guidance and a message of joy only for the believers, because only the doors of a believing heart are open to its teachings. It is the believers who respond to its teachings. This is a very important reality which must be explained clearly. The verses of the Qur'an create such intimacy within the believing heart, open such paths of recognition and perception within it, and produce within it such awareness and feeling, from which every heart that lacks faith remains deprived. This is why the heart of the believer finds guidance in the Qur'an, and for it this message becomes joy. The Qur'an has stated this reality in various places: ﴿Guidance for the God-fearing﴾; ﴿Guidance for a people who believe﴾; ﴿Guidance and mercy for a people who have firm conviction﴾. Thus, faith is obtained as a result of God-consciousness (taqwa) and certainty (yaqin). And the Children of Israel were deprived of it for this very reason: they were neither believers, nor God-fearing, nor acquainted with the taste of certainty.

In other words, guidance is obtained as a result of faith, God-consciousness and certainty, and the Children of Israel were deprived for the reason that they were neither believers, nor God-fearing, nor acquainted with the taste of certainty.

It was their habit to distinguish between the messengers sent by Allah and His religions and laws. Likewise, they also distinguished between the angels of Allah, whose names and functions they knew. They would say that their relations with Mika'il were very good, but their relations with Jibril were not good. For this reason, in the next verse Allah the Exalted gathered together Jibril, Mika'il and all the other angels and messengers. The purpose is that they are all one: whoever is an enemy to one of them is an enemy to all of them, indeed he is an enemy to Allah. Therefore, Allah too will be an enemy to him, and they will become disbelievers.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 2, verse 98:

"Whoever is an enemy to Allah and His angels and His messengers and Jibril and Mikail, then indeed Allah is an enemy to the disbelievers." Those who are enemies of Allah's angels, His messengers, Jibril and Mikail, Allah is the enemy of those disbelievers.

After this, the direction of address turns back to the Prophet (ﷺ). He is enjoined to remain firm upon the truth and the clear signs that are being revealed to him. None but the wicked and the corrupt can deny them. And the Children of Israel are warned that they never remain faithful to their covenants, whether the covenant was made with Allah, or with the earlier prophets, or with the Final Prophet (ﷺ). The Holy Qur'an censures them for having cast aside a Book of Allah that confirms all the Books that are in their own possession.

Here Allah has set out the causes for which the Children of Israel were rejecting the clear verses of Allah that had been revealed from Allah Himself. That is, they were immersed in wickedness and corruption (fisq wa fujur). Their nature had become corrupted, for a sound nature had no option but to believe in these verses. If the heart is not crooked, these verses impose themselves and compel acceptance. The Jews' adoption of disbelief is not due to any shortcoming in the proofs in the verses of the Noble Qur'an, nor to their failing to satisfy; rather, the real cause is that their own nature has already been corrupted and they have become immersed in wickedness and corruption.

After this, the address turns back to the Muslims and to all other human beings. The Jews are condemned, and another of their base qualities is mentioned: that they hold divergent desires among themselves. Despite this blameworthy partisanship, they have a common ground between them. They do not even adhere to a single opinion, nor do they abide by the covenants they make. They do not hold firmly to any one rope. Although they are extremely selfish regarding their personal interest and their national interest, and they do not like that anyone other than themselves should receive Allah's grace and bounty, yet despite this national partisanship they are not united. They themselves do not abide by the covenants they make with one another. Whenever they make a firm pledge among themselves, some group among them rises up and breaks it, and openly violates that collective decision.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 2, verse 100:

﴿Is it not so that whenever they make a covenant, a party of them casts it aside? Nay, most of them do not believe.﴾

Was it not always the case that whenever they made a covenant, a group among them would surely cast it aside? Indeed, most of them are such that they do not believe with a sincere heart.

They made a firm covenant with Allah beneath Mount Sinai (Tur), and afterward they broke it. The covenants that they made with the prophets who came before the Prophet ﷺ, they also violated. And after the Prophet ﷺ came to Madinah Tayyibah, the agreement he made with the Jews, they too set aside, although conditions had been fixed with them in that agreement. They took the initiative in aiding the enemies of the Messenger ﷺ, began criticizing the system of life presented by the Prophet ﷺ, and tried to create discord among the Muslims. Yet all these acts were contrary to the Covenant of Madinah (Mithaq al-Madinah).

This was the blameworthy habit of the Children of Israel, whereas the conduct of the Muslims was entirely different from it. The Prophet ﷺ said: "The blood of the Muslims is equal, they are helpers of one another against others, and even the least of them may grant protection on behalf of all of them." And when they make an agreement with anyone, none of them is permitted to break it or violate it.

During the caliphate of Hadrat Umar ؓ, his commander-in-chief Hadrat Abu Ubaydah ؓ wrote that a village-dwelling people of Iraq had been granted protection (aman) by one of our slaves. Now, what should we do with them? Hadrat Umar ؓ replied that Allah the Exalted has made the keeping of covenants a great obligation, and until you fulfil this promise you cannot be called trustworthy. Accordingly, acting upon that covenant, they left the people of that city in their own condition.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 2, verse 101:

This is the description of a noble, upright and principled community. From this it becomes clear how great the difference is between the morals of the wicked Jews and the morals of the upright Muslims.

وَلَمَّا جَاءَهُمْ رَسُولٌ مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ مُصَدِّقٌ لِمَا مَعَهُمْ نَبَذَ فَرِيقٌ مِنَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ كِتَابَ اللَّهِ وَرَاءَ ظُهُورِهِمْ كَأَنَّهُمْ لا يَعْلَمُونَ (101)

"And when there came to them a Messenger from Allah, confirming what was with them, a party of those who were given the Book threw the Book of Allah behind their backs, as if they did not know."

This is an example of breaking a covenant, which one group among them committed. Among the covenant that Allah took from them is this clause: that whatever messengers would be sent in the future, they would believe in them, honour them and help them. When Allah sent His Book (the Qur'an) to them through the Final Prophet, a party among the People of the Book threw it behind their backs. In this way they rejected a divine Book that was already with them, and in which there were prophecies about the Messenger (ﷺ). They cast aside those prophecies, and they also cast aside the new Book that was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

This verse also intends a subtle taunt against the People of the Book. That is, if the polytheists had rejected the Book of Allah, it would not have been surprising from them; but these wretched people rejected it despite being People of the Book. They were well acquainted with prophethood and the Messengers. They always remained attached to the sources of guidance. Light was always before their eyes. Yet, despite being people of guidance and insight, what did they do? They threw the Book of Allah behind their backs, meaning they denied the Book and stopped acting upon it. They removed the Book of Allah from their thought and from their lives. Here the Qur'an has presented the mental meaning of their denial and inaction in a thoroughly sensory manner. The mental meaning now moves out of the realm of abstraction into the realm of perceptible things. Their act is expressed as a perceptible physical movement, and such an ugly and repulsive picture is drawn of it that denial and rejection drip from it. In this image they appear extremely hard-hearted and foolish; they appear as an embodiment of insolence, filth and disgrace. Through this depiction, the human imagination sees an intense motion, as though hands are set in motion and cast the Book of Allah behind their backs.

After rejecting such a Book, what happened? That Book was confirming the revelation that was with them. Then what did they do? Probably they accepted this unshakeable truth, or on the contrary they clung to the very guidance that this Qur'an was also confirming, which they themselves already believed in.

By no means! Not only did they not adopt any one reasonable course, but they cast the Book of Allah behind their backs and pursued incomprehensible, baseless wonders and old-fashioned fables, which had no reality and were not based on any certain foundation.

They abandoned the Book of Allah, though it itself confirmed the guidance that was with them, and began to follow those things which the devils attributed to the time of Solomon (peace be upon him). These devils used to attribute false things to Solomon (peace be upon him), namely that he was a great sorcerer, and that the things he had subjugated, he had subjugated through this black magic. The Qur'an, refuting this false notion, says that Solomon was not a sorcerer: وَمَا كَفَرَ سُلَيْمَانُ ﴿And Solomon did not disbelieve﴾. The Qur'an thus regards sorcery as disbelief (kufr). Therefore, by negating it of Solomon (peace be upon him), it shows that sorcery was not the work of Solomon (peace be upon him) but of the devils. وَلَكِنَّ الشَّيَاطِينَ كَفَرُوا يُعَلِّمُونَ النَّاسَ السِّحْرَ ﴿But the devils disbelieved, teaching people sorcery﴾. It was those devils who committed disbelief, those who taught people sorcery.

After this, the Qur'an refutes the notion that the teaching of sorcery was revealed by Allah Himself to the two angels Harut and Marut at Babylon. وَمَا أُنْزِلَ عَلَى الْمَلَكَيْنِ بِبَابِلَ هَارُوتَ وَمَارُوتَ ﴿And what was sent down at Babylon to the two angels, Harut and Marut﴾. It is not true that sorcery was revealed at Babylon to two angels named Harut and Marut.

It appears that a considerable story about these two angels was current among the Jews, and that the Jews and the devils would say that the two angels possessed the knowledge of magic and used to teach this knowledge to people as well. They also held that this teaching of magic had been revealed to them by Allah. The Qur'an has refuted this fabrication as well, that the teaching of sorcery was sent down by Allah through those two angels at Babylon.

However, here the Qur'an clarifies the reality of this story: that these two angels were among the wise secrets of Allah, and were sent as a trial and a test (fitnah) for the people. Whoever came to them to acquire the teaching of sorcery, they would tell him: وَمَا يُعَلِّمَانِ مِنْ أَحَدٍ حَتَّى يَقُولا إِنَّمَا نَحْنُ فِتْنَةٌ فَلا تَكْفُرْ ﴿And they did not teach anyone until they had said, "We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve"﴾. Whenever those angels taught anyone, they first clearly warned them, saying: "Look, we are merely a trial, so do not fall into disbelief."

Here the Qur'an again describes the teaching of sorcery and magic as kufr, and the proclamation of its being disbelief is made through the two angels Harut and Marut.

The Qur'an says that there were some people who, despite the clear warning of these angels, insisted on learning sorcery from them. Since they insisted on being afflicted by this trial, Allah also opened this door for them: فَيَتَعَلَّمُونَ مِنْهُمَا مَا يُفَرِّقُونَ بِهِ بَيْنَ الْمَرْءِ وَزَوْجِهِ ﴿So they learned from them that by which they separate a man from his wife﴾. Even so, these people would learn from them the thing by which they could cause separation between husband and wife.

Although this was the evil in that black knowledge about which the angels had given warning, the Qur'an, in keeping with the occasion, turns attention here to a fundamental principle of the Islamic worldview: that not a leaf in this universe can move without the will and permission of Allah. وَمَا هُمْ بِضَارِّينَ بِهِ مِنْ أَحَدٍ إِلا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ ﴿And they could not harm anyone with it except by the permission of Allah﴾. It was evident that without the permission of Allah they could not harm anyone through it.

It is the will and permission of Allah by which causes produce their effects and results. This is an extremely fundamental and important principle and belief of the Islamic worldview, and it should be clearly established and firmly rooted in the heart and mind of a believer. The best place to present this belief is indeed such a magical environment. There is no doubt that if you put your hand into fire, it will certainly burn, but this burning is not possible without the command and will of Allah. It is Allah who has placed in fire the capacity to burn and in your hand the capacity to be burned, and when He wills, He can strip both fire and servants of this capacity, as indeed happened in the event of Abraham (peace be upon him). The same is the case with the magic through which sorcerers cause separation between husband and wife: if it is not the will of Allah, it cannot have any effect. If His wisdom and will do not require it, He can at any time suspend this property of the sorcerer.

The same holds for all the means and causes that have come to our knowledge until today. In each of these, Allah has placed a specific property, and this property operates by His permission and will. Just as Allah has granted these means these qualities, in the same way He can also strip these causes of their properties.

Then the Qur'an also explains clearly the reality of what they were learning: the magic through which they caused separation between husband and wife. The Qur'an shows that this black knowledge was not beneficial even to them: وَيَتَعَلَّمُونَ مَا يَضُرُّهُمْ وَلا يَنْفَعُهُمْ ﴿And they learned what would harm them and not benefit them﴾. Yet despite this, they learned that which was harmful to them and not beneficial. The fact that the trial into which they were falling was disbelief was sufficient proof that it was pure evil and had no benefit in it.

وَلَقَدْ عَلِمُوا لَمَنِ اشْتَرَاهُ مَا لَهُ فِي الآخِرَةِ مِنْ خَلاقٍ ﴿And they certainly knew that whoever purchased it would have no share in the Hereafter﴾. And when you know that whatever he is doing will, as its result, deprive him of all the good of the Hereafter, and yet he adopts this course, then he is deliberately ruining his Hereafter and depriving himself of all the good of the coming world.

Why? So that he may enjoy himself in this life of a few days. How evil is the bargain these people are making, while they are well aware of this reality.

وَلَبِئْسَ مَا شَرَوْا بِهِ أَنْفُسَهُمْ لَوْ كَانُوا يَعْلَمُونَ ﴿How wretched is that for which they sold their souls, if only they knew!﴾

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran) on Surah 2, verse 103:

﴿And if they had believed and been mindful of God, the reward from God would have been far better for them, if only they knew.﴾ (2:103)

This statement applies to those who learned sorcery from Harut and Marut in Babylon. It also applies to those who followed what the devils presented in the name of the kingdom of Solomon (peace be upon him). These were the Jews, who cast the Book of God behind their backs and made binding upon themselves those fabrications and blameworthy practices.

Here it seems necessary to shed some light on the reality of that sorcery, which these Jews pursued and through which they created discord between husband and wife, and because of which they set aside even the Book of God.

In our own age it is frequently observed that some people possess such miraculous faculties that science, to this day, cannot offer any scientific explanation for them. For such wonders people have devised various names, yet the reality of these phenomena has still not been determined, and they remain marvels to this day. For example, telepathy, that is, the perception of thoughts from a distance: what is its reality? How is it possible that a person, from a distance where neither his sight nor his voice can reach, calls another person and draws thoughts from him, with no great distance intervening between the two?

Then, the process of magnetic hypnosis also deserves consideration. How does it become possible? One will imposes itself upon another by an incomprehensible method, and one thought conforms itself to another thought in such a way that thoughts keep passing from one to the other, and the second keeps receiving from the first. It appears as though the affected person is reading an open book. To this day, the most that science has been able to do in this area is to acknowledge these realities and assign some names to them, but science has not yet been able to answer the question of what their reality is. Nor does science have an answer to how this process is completed.

Apart from these realities, there are also some things which science still hesitates to accept, either because sufficient observations about them have not yet been gathered that would enable it to conduct experiments in this field. True dreams are also a very strange matter. Freud, who strongly denies every spiritual power, could not deny them either. How does the dream give us an indication of events occurring in the darkness of the future? And before long, that indication takes the form of actual events. The same is the case with those hidden feelings of human beings, for which man has not yet been able to devise any name. Sometimes a person begins to sense that something is about to happen, that someone is about to arrive, and after this, the anticipated matter occurs in one form or another.

Therefore, it is mere obstinacy for a person to deny these unknown realities out of mere carelessness, only because science has not yet reached those means through which it could conduct an experiment in this field.

This does not mean, either, that a person should accept all the fables of the world without question and believe in every tale. Rather, the correct and moderate course is that a person adopt a flexible and balanced position regarding such unknown realities. It is neither right to deny them one hundred percent, nor reasonable to accept them without question. The outcome of this middle course will be that when man's knowledge and the initial means of perception that are available to him now develop further, it will become possible for him to discover such realities. Therefore, man should acknowledge that his knowledge is limited, that there are some realities which lie beyond his range of perception, and he should recognize his limits and show due regard for unknown realities.

The nature of sorcery is also somewhat similar to this. The inspiration which the devils cast upon wicked people is also among the matters beyond perception. One of its many forms is that the sorcerer has the capacity to influence the senses and thoughts of human beings. Sometimes its effect is also upon solid objects and bodies. However, the sorcery mentioned in the Qur'an concerning the sorcerers of Pharaoh was merely illusion and deception of the eye. In reality, no change occurred in the nature of anything through it.

﴿It was made to appear to him, because of their sorcery, that their ropes and staffs were moving.﴾ (Ta-Ha 20:66)

It is possible that these people, by employing such effects of sorcery, caused separation between husband and wife, and between friend and friend, because when a person is affected by something, certain movements proceed from him in conformity with that effect. But, as has been said, the chain of means, causes and their results and effects cannot function except by the permission of God, the Exalted.

Naturally, a question arises here: who were those two angels, Harut and Marut, and in which period of history did they live in Babylon? The Qur'an did not consider it necessary to explain this question, since the story of these angels was commonly known among the Jews. When the Qur'an related this story to them, they raised no objection to it. Many events which were well known among the audience of the Qur'an at that time have been mentioned by the Qur'an in summary form, because the purpose of the Qur'an was fulfilled by mere allusion, and storytelling was not the Qur'an's concern at all.

In Fi Zilal al-Quran, we do not wish to record all the details and the mixture of sound and unsound narrations (ratb wa yabis) that are popular about these angels, because there is material about them in the books of tafsir, and among the narrations that are reasonable, none is reliable (thiqah).

Throughout its longest history, humanity has repeatedly encountered many trials and tribulations. These trials and tribulations have taken different forms in different eras, in accordance with the intellectual level of humanity and the environment of that time. Now, if this trial has come at some time in the form of two angels, or in the form of two humans of angelic character, then this is no astonishing or unprecedented matter. For the trials which have come upon humanity have also been of many strange and extraordinary kinds, especially in that age when humanity was treading the initial stages of progress in the world of thought and perception, and was walking in the dark night of illusion and ignorance, behind the heavenly light.

Furthermore, for us the clear and firm guidance given in these verses is sufficient. And if something is ambiguous (mutashabih) and incomprehensible, there is no need to pursue it, especially now that we have moved very far from the environment in which such events occurred. For us, it is enough to know that the Children of Israel went astray by pursuing sorcery and other baseless and frivolous matters, that they set aside the true and certain guidance of God, and that the practice of sorcery is an act of disbelief (kufr). Those who perform such deeds will have no share in the Hereafter, and they will be deprived of all the goodness and blessings that God has prepared for them there.

Lesson 6 at a Glance

In this lesson, the conspiracies of the Jews and their intrigues against Islam and the Muslims are further unveiled. The Islamic community is warned about the stratagems and tricks which the Jews employed against Islam. It is also explained how much hatred and envy they harbor in their hearts against the Muslims, and how day and night they are busy in causing harm to the Muslim Ummah and devising plots against it. Therefore, Muslims are prohibited from imitating these enemies of Islam, the disbelieving People of the Book, in any way, whether in their speech or their conduct. Muslims are told the real reasons behind the statements, actions and policies of the Jews. The plots, mischief-making and deceptions which they carried out against the unity and solidarity of the Muslims are clearly described. It appears that the Jews raised a storm of malicious propaganda by using the pretext of issues such as the reconstruction of the Islamic society and the modification and abrogation (naskh) of certain Shariah injunctions and obligations in accordance with new circumstances and requirements. Through the deep conspiracies they had devised, they wished to create doubts in the hearts of the Muslims regarding the source of these injunctions and obligations, namely the Divine Being and the revelation of God's Word. They used to say to the Muslims: "If this revelation were from God, there would have been no need for modifications to earlier injunctions and for abrogating them."

The Jews had been spreading such propaganda even before, but when the command to change the qiblah was revealed sixteen months after the Prophet's ﷺ migration (hijrah), they raised a great storm of propaganda against Islam. For a long period after the migration, the Prophet ﷺ continued to pray facing Bayt al-Maqdis, the qiblah of the Jews, and from this the Jews would argue that the true qiblah and the true religion were indeed theirs. Therefore, the heartfelt desire of the Prophet ﷺ was that the qiblah of the Muslims should be changed from Bayt al-Maqdis to Bayt al-Haram. However, the Prophet ﷺ never expressed this wish, but throughout this entire period this desire remained in his heart, and God, in accordance with the wish of the Prophet ﷺ, made the qiblah that was pleasing to him the qiblah of the Muslims, as the details mentioned in the following pages show. Since the Children of Israel were clearly aware that as a result of the change of qiblah, the apparent superiority of their religion over Islam would also end, and they would no longer be able to use it as evidence for the superiority of their religion, at this stage they began a massive propaganda campaign to create disunity in the ranks of Islam and to cast doubts in the beliefs of the believers about the revelation of God's Word from God. Their conspiracy was so deep that in it they attempted to strike at the fundamental belief of the Muslims and at the divine origin of the Qur'an. What they said to the Muslims could be summarized as: "If facing Bayt al-Maqdis in prayer was false and contrary to the truth, then all your prayers for sixteen months were wasted. And if that act was right, then why was it changed?" The aim was that whatever prayers they had offered so far would bring them no reward, and that the leadership of the Prophet ﷺ was not a wise leadership (God forbid).

It appears that some Muslims had begun to be affected by this propaganda. Therefore, with great anguish and restlessness, they began to ask the Prophet ﷺ questions about it, because this incident was so unusual, and such a disturbance had arisen in hearts that, while it persisted, a climate of confidence in Islamic leadership could not remain, nor could complete trust in the source of Islamic beliefs be maintained. Therefore, the Muslims also began to ask about its wisdom and about convincing proofs regarding it. This was the atmosphere in which these verses of the Qur'an were revealed. In them it was explained that abrogation of injunctions is based upon profound wisdom. Through it, God reveals better injunctions for the Muslims, injunctions that are more beneficial for them in new circumstances, because God alone knows which command is best in which circumstances. At the same time, the Muslims are warned that the real aim and endeavour of the Jews is only to make the Muslims, after they have believed, revert to disbelief, because they are consumed by envy that God has bestowed upon the Muslims a grace, kindness and honour as great as divine revelation, and why He has entrusted to them this great responsibility in preference to them. For God has revealed His final Book to the Muslims. The Qur'an here clearly explains what hidden purpose lies behind all these mischievous activities of the Jews. On this occasion, the Qur'an also ridicules their false claim that Paradise is exclusively for them. The Qur'an also records their mutual accusations, that the Jews say: "The Christians have no true religion," and the Christians say: "The Jews have no true religion." And the polytheists go further and claim: "Both are upon falsehood."

The Qur'an unveils the secret of their evil intentions and hidden conspiracies regarding the change of qiblah in this manner: the Ka'bah is the first house of worship on the earth for God, and by preventing people from facing it in prayer, the Jews are committing, in order to defile the mosques and places of worship of God, a crime which, in their own view, is also a very great crime.

In short, the same theme has been presented throughout this entire lesson, and at the end, the aim of the Jews and Christians behind all these activities is clearly placed before the Muslims: namely, to turn the Muslims away from this true religion and bring them over to their own religion. The Qur'an says that the People of the Book will never be pleased with the Prophet ﷺ until he follows their creed. As long as he does not fulfil their desire, they will continue this war of deceit, false propaganda and trickery until the last moment. Behind all their mischief-making, their deceptions and all the hollow arguments they put forward, only this one purpose is at work.

Lesson 6: Explanation of the Verses (104 to 123)

At the beginning of this lesson, the address is directed to "those who have believed." The point is that the quality which distinguishes them from other people is faith. It is this quality that connects them to their Prophet on one side and to their Lord on the other. It is also this quality that, when they are called by it, makes their hearts attentive, and they become ready to respond to every call.

Calling them by this quality, Allah instructs them not to use the word "Ra'ina" when addressing the Prophet ﷺ, but to use "Unzurna" (ﷺ... "Look upon us" / "Please give us consideration"), which has the same meaning. Appealing to them through the quality of faith, the Qur'an commands them to adopt listening and obedience, and warns them of the evil abode and evil end of the disbelievers, namely the painful punishment.

Regarding the reason for the prohibition on using the word "Ra'ina," the commentators have stated that some foolish Jews would pronounce this word in a way that made it appear to be derived from the verbal noun "ru'una" (arrogance) rather than "ri'aya" (consideration). By doing this, these people sought to vent the malice of their hearts by insulting the Prophet ﷺ and showing disrespect to his dignity. They lacked the courage to say openly to the Prophet ﷺ anything directly. Therefore, some base and despicable people among the Jews attempted to abuse him through this verbal trickery. Hence, the believers were commanded not to use at all those words which the Jews were using for this vile purpose, so that the door to their meanness would be closed.

The use of such contemptible stratagems by the Jews to insult the Prophet ﷺ clearly shows how intense their hatred was toward the Prophet ﷺ and his movement. It shows how they were ready to employ every base tactic against him and did not let any opportunity in this regard slip from their hands. Moreover, by prohibiting the use of such words through divine revelation on such an occasion, it also becomes evident that Allah was ever watchful over His Prophet and the Islamic movement, and used to repel the conspiracies and deceptions of their treacherous enemies.

After this, Allah warns the Muslims of how much spite and rancor these people harbor against the believers, and how they are always committed to enmity and harassment of the Muslims. They do all this only because Allah bestowed upon the Muslims this special favor and grace. These details were explained by Allah so that the Muslims would be cautious of their enemies, and remain more firmly steadfast in the faith due to which the hearts of their enemies burn, and that they would give thanks for the special favor Allah has bestowed upon them, and safeguard it.

Allah here includes both the People of the Book and the polytheists in the category of disbelievers, because both groups rejected the prophethood of the Last Prophet. In this respect they stand on the same footing, and both hearts are filled with envy and malice towards the Muslims; neither of them wishes that any good should reach the Muslims. The thing that has made them burn with jealousy over what the Muslims possess is their religion. It galls them that Allah chose the Muslims for this good, leaving them aside. Why was the revelation of the Qur'an sent down to them, why were they honoured with this favour, and why were the Muslims made the guardians of the greatest trust in the universe, namely the Islamic system of life?

Earlier it was explained that these people were by no means willing that Allah, in His grace, should bestow favour upon any other servant. In this regard their narrow-mindedness reached such a point that, because the Prophet ﷺ brought the message of revelation, they became enemies even of Jibril (peace be upon him). Yet ﴿Allah selects for His mercy whom He wills﴾. Moreover, only Allah knows where the best place is for this trust and message of His. Now, if Allah has sent this message down upon Muhammad ﷺ and the believers accept it, then it was present in Allah's knowledge that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the believers were fit to bear this burden of trust. ﴿And Allah is the Lord of great bounty﴾ (105).

There is no greater blessing than the blessing of prophethood and messengership, no greater wealth than the wealth of faith, and no greater honour than the honour of calling to Islam. Here Allah wishes to make the Muslims feel and to awaken within them the awareness that Allah has bestowed upon them a great favour and grace. Earlier, the Muslims were given the understanding that because of these blessings of Allah upon them, the hearts of the disbelievers had burned with rancour and envy, and therefore they should remain watchful of them. The purpose of this was also that the Muslims should be cautious of them and that their awareness should be sharp against the schemes of the Jews. Against the whisperings and doubt-sowing of the Jews, it was necessary to awaken this kind of feeling and awareness among the Muslims, because these people, both at that time and ever since, have been striving to weaken faith in this system of life in the hearts and minds of the Muslims. It was indeed the wealth of faith that made them envious of the Muslims, because through it the Muslims became distinguished and superior to them.

As we have explained above, this Jewish assault began with the abrogation of some verses and rulings of the Noble Qur'an, especially when the command to change the qibla from Bayt al-Maqdis to the Ka'bah was revealed. This event deprived the Jews of an important proof of their claim to superiority, and they intensified this vile propaganda. Therefore Allah said: ﴿Whatever verse We abrogate or cause to be forgotten, We bring forth one better than it or similar to it. Do you not know that Allah has power over all things?﴾ (106)

These verses were revealed on the occasion of the change of the qibla, as is also shown by the context of the verses that follow. Or it may refer to partial changes that were being made in the rulings of the Qur'anic commands and divine instructions under various circumstances for the guidance of the Muslim community. Or it may refer to the overall changes that the Qur'an made in comparison with the Torah and the Gospel, although on the whole the Qur'an had called those books true scriptures. Whichever one of these is meant, or all three, the Jews used them at that time in propaganda against the Islamic movement and to spread doubts among the Muslims, and began attacks on the central beliefs of Islam. Whatever is meant, Allah is not powerless over anything; all the affairs of the heavens and the earth are in His hand of power. It is for this reason that Allah then says:
