The words in which the Muslims are addressed, "You have neither any guardian nor any helper," give the sense that both a warning and a reminder are intended at once. The manner of indirect warning has been adopted because some people had been affected by the misleading propaganda of the Jews, and, overawed by the mischief they had created, had begun to put to the Prophet ﷺ questions that did not accord with complete trust and firm conviction. For this reason Allah the Exalted disapproved of such questions on their part and warned them clearly.

Allah warns the believers not to fall into contentious argument like the people of Musa (peace be upon him), nor to question their Messenger needlessly about proofs, nor to demand extraordinary, miracle-like things. This is just what the Children of Israel did to trouble their prophet. It was their habit that whenever Musa (peace be upon him) gave them a command or conveyed to them a message from Allah, they would engage in contentious disputes, as several incidents earlier in this same surah have already passed.

Allah warns the Muslims of the natural outcome of this attitude, for the natural outcome of this attitude can be nothing but misguidance and, after faith, disbelief. The Children of Israel had earlier reached exactly this end, and now the hearts of these people desire that the Muslims too should reach the same end.

Envy, which is an extremely bad trait and a moral disease, creates within the human soul the desire that all other people be deprived of every kind of good and not find the path of guidance. Not because such envious, mischief-making people are unaware of the reality of the situation; they know the reality of the situation very well, but out of envy alone they hold this desire.

﴿حَسَدًا مِنْ عِنْدِ أَنْفُسِهِمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا تَبَيَّنَ لَهُمُ الْحَقُّ﴾ "Out of envy from their own selves, after the truth has become clear to them." Although the truth has become manifest to them, they act this way because of the envy of their souls.

The black and base feelings of envy against Islam and the Muslims were surging in the hearts of the Jews, and those feelings are still exactly the same today. All of their plots and all of their schemes against Islam were based upon these feelings, and to this day their conduct remains exactly the same. The Holy Qur'an is explaining this very reality in detail before the Muslims so that they may arrive at the truth of the matter, and so that they may understand that behind this continuous struggle of the Jews against Islam and the Muslims, the only motive at work is that they wish to shake the beliefs of the Muslims and drag them back to that state of disbelief in which they themselves were previously afflicted, from which Allah the Exalted delivered them, and they came to faith, and they were blessed with the great favour and the sublime blessing.

When this reality becomes clear and the detestable hatred and envy of the Jews becomes evident, the Holy Qur'an instructs the Muslims to rise above the low level of the Jews and think in a higher manner. They should not answer envy with envy and evil, but should act with pardon and forgiveness, and wait for the time when Allah brings His decree.

In general, this whole paragraph seeks to make the Islamic community understand, and to focus the attention of Muslims on, where the real source of their danger lies and where the plots against them are being hatched. In this way the Islamic consciousness is prepared to confront the evil designs, base conspiracies and blameworthy envious feelings of the Jews. But once this preparation is complete, that Islamic consciousness is turned towards Allah, so that Muslims await His command and place every movement and every action of theirs under Allah's disposal, until the moment of decision arrives. At that time Muslims are commanded to act with forgiveness and pardon, to keep their hearts free from hatred, envy, rancour and enmity, and to await the commands and decision of the One who has authority and the One who wills.

After this, the Qur'an examines the claims that the Jews and Christians generally used to make. For example, they used to say that only they were upon guidance, and that Paradise is for them alone and no one besides them will enter it. This claim was made by both the Jews and the Christians at the same time, and each of them used to say that the other did not possess even an atom's weight of truth. In the course of mentioning these claims, the Qur'an also clarifies its true concept regarding deeds and their recompense.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 2, verse 111:

In Madinah, those who stood opposed to the Muslims were the Jews, because there was no organised Christian group there that was afflicted with hostility to Islam in the way the Jews were. Yet the wording of the verse has been kept general. Here the verses of Allah refute the claims of both groups, and by quoting the statements of the Jews and the Christians about each other, the views of the polytheists of Arabia on both of them are presented in the Hereafter.

﴿وَقَالُوا لَنْ يَدْخُلَ الْجَنَّةَ إِلَّا مَنْ كَانَ هُودًا أَوْ نَصَارَى﴾ "They say: None shall enter Paradise unless he is a Jew or a Christian."

Here the claims of the two sects have been brought together and stated jointly, though each of them was making its claim independently. The Jews said that only the one who is a Jew would enter Paradise, and the Christians said that only the one who is a Christian would enter Paradise. These lengthy claims of both were mere assertions. Neither had any rational or traditional proof behind it. For this reason Allah instructs His Prophet to challenge them to produce their proof.

﴿قُلْ هَاتُوا بُرْهَانَكُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ﴾ "Say: Produce your proof, if you are truthful."

Here Allah, in keeping with the occasion, states an important principle of the Islamic outlook on life concerning recompense. In Allah's dealings in this matter, no nation, no group, and no individual will receive any special favour. What is valued with Allah is righteousness, complete submission to Him, and acceptance and contentment. Here, decisions are not made merely by looking at names and titles.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 2, verse 112:

بَلَى مَنْ أَسْلَمَ وَجْهَهُ لِلَّهِ وَهُوَ مُحْسِنٌ فَلَهُ أَجْرُهُ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِ وَلا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ
"Yes, whoever submits his whole self to Allah while being a doer of good, for him is his reward with his Lord, and there is no fear for them, nor shall they grieve."

حق یہ ہے کہ جو بھی اپنی ہستی کو اللہ کی اطاعت میں سونپ دے اور عملاً نیک روش پر چلے ، اس کے لئے اس کے رب کے پاس اجر ہے اور ایسے لوگوں کے لئے کسی خوف یا رنج کا موقع نہیں ہے۔

اس سے قبل ایک جگہ یہودیوں کے اس دعوے پر کہ " انہیں آگ نہیں چھوئے گی مگر چند دن " کی تردید کرتے ہوئے بھی اللہ تعالیٰ نے اپنے ہاں سزا کا یہ عام اصول بیان کیا تھا۔" ہاں جو بھی برائی کمائے گا اور اس کی برائیاں اسے گھیر لیں گی وہ لوگ جہنمی ہوں گے اور وہ ہمیشہ جہنم میں رہیں گے ۔ "

یعنی خطیئات کے مرتکب لوگوں کو سزا محض اس لئے ہوگی کہ انہوں نے خطیئات کا ارتکاب کیا۔ اس کے علاوہ کوئی نقطہ نظر یا کوئی پہلو اس کا باعث نہ ہوگا کہ انہیں سزا دی جائے۔ غرض نیکی اور بدی میں اللہ کے ہاں جزا و سزا کا یہی ایک اصول ہے۔

بَلَى مَنْ أَسْلَمَ وَجْهَهُ لِلَّهِ وَهُوَ مُحْسِنٌ فَلَهُ جو اپنی ہستی کو اللہ کی اطاعت میں سونپ دے اور عملاً نیک روش پر چلے " یعنی اپنی پوری ذات کو اللہ کے مختص کردے۔ اپنے پورے شعور کے ساتھ اللہ کی طرف متوجہ ہوجائے اور جس طرح پہلا شخص خالصتاً برائی میں گرفتار ہوگیا تھا ۔۔ یہ ہمہ تن اللہ کے لئے ہوجائے۔ "

مَنْ أَسْلَمَ وَجْهَهُ لِلَّهِ "جو اپنی ذات کو پوری طرح اللہ کی اطاعت میں سونپ دے۔" اس فقرے میں اسلام کی اہم ترین خصوصیت اور واضح علامت کو بیان کیا گیا ہے۔ یعنی ایک انسان پوری طرح اللہ کی طرف منہ کرلے۔ یعنی ہمہ تن متوجہ ہوجائے اور مکمل انقیاد اور اطاعت اختیار کرلے یعنی معنوی طور پر اللہ کے آگے جھک جائے اور عملاً بھی اس کا مطیع فرمان ہوجائے اور چونکہ معنوی رضا و تسلیم کے لئے ظاہری دلیل عملاً اطاعت حکم ہوا کرتی ہے، اس لئے کہا گیا اور عملاً نیک روش اختیار کرے۔ اسلام کی اہم ترین خصوصیات اور نشانیوں میں سے ایک یہ امر ہے کہ انسان کا شعور اور روش اس کا عقیدہ اور عمل، اس کا قلبی ایمان اور عملی روش کے درمیان ہم آہنگی پیدا ہوجاتی ہے۔ اور تب ایک بندہ مومن اس عطاءِ الٰہی کا مستحق قرار پاتا ہے۔

فَلَهُ أَجْرُهُ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِ وَلا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ "ان کے لئے ان کے رب کے پاس اجر ہے اور ایسے لوگوں کے لئے کسی خوف یا رنج کا کوئی موقع نہیں۔" ان کا اجر محفوظ اور ان کے رب کے پاس ہے۔ امن و طمانیت کی ایک عظیم دنیا جس میں رنج والم کا شائبہ تک نہیں، ان کے لئے منتظر ہے۔ فرحت و سرور کا ایک عالم ہے جس میں حزن و ملال کا کوئی لمحہ نہیں۔ ان کے لئے تیار ہے۔ جزا کا یہ اصول عامہ ہے اور تمام لوگ اس میں برابر ہیں۔ اللہ کے ہاں کسی کی رو رعایت یا کسی کی کوئی شان محبوبیت نہیں ہے۔

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 2, verse 113:

The Jews and Christians would both keep making grand claims, and each of them would say that the other has nothing. Moreover, the polytheists went one step further than them and would say that neither of these two groups has any reality.

وَقَالَتِ الْيَهُودُ لَيْسَتِ النَّصَارَى عَلَى شَيْءٍ وَقَالَتِ النَّصَارَى لَيْسَتِ الْيَهُودُ عَلَى شَيْءٍ وَهُمْ يَتْلُونَ الْكِتَابَ كَذَلِكَ قَالَ الَّذِينَ لا يَعْلَمُونَ مِثْلَ قَوْلِهِمْ فَاللَّهُ يَحْكُمُ بَيْنَهُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ فِيمَا كَانُوا فِيهِ يَخْتَلِفُونَ (113)

"The Jews say that the Christians have nothing, and the Christians say the Jews have nothing. Yet both of them recite the Book. And those who have no knowledge say the same kind of thing as they say. So Allah will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that wherein they used to differ." 

Those who have no knowledge of the Book, that is, the unlettered Arabs who had no book. Whenever they saw that the Jews and Christians were afflicted with division and differences, how they were hurling abuse at one another and making accusations, or what baseless superstitions and unreal matters they had believed in, they would observe that the beliefs of the people of polytheism and the Arabs' polytheistic notions, such as the idea that the angels are children of Allah, were in no way higher than these. Therefore, considering those beliefs contemptible, they would say of the Jews and Christians that their adherents likewise had no reality.

After the claims of the Jews and Christians regarding ownership of Paradise, the Qur'an relates their mutual accusations and leaves their judgment to Allah, saying: فَاللَّهُ يَحْكُمُ بَيْنَهُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ فِيمَا كَانُوا فِيهِ يَخْتَلِفُونَ "So Allah will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that wherein they used to differ, because He is the just Judge, and ultimately all affairs return to Him." Those who claim that they alone are the people of Paradron and the people of guidance, yet adhere to no logic and whose claims are based on no proof, it seems appropriate to leave the matter of such people to Allah. This is the only way to be free of such people.

The Jews used to strive to create doubts in the hearts of the Muslims about the commands of the Prophet ﷺ and his teachings, especially regarding the change of the qibla. Their propaganda had reached its peak. Now the discourse turns to refuting these blameworthy efforts. Allah says that their striving is in reality the destruction of the mosques of Allah, and their aim is to prevent people from remembering and reflecting upon Allah in the mosques of Allah.

The closest reading to mind is that these two verses relate to the issue of the change of the qiblah. At that stage the Jews were busy trying to keep the Muslims from turning towards the new qiblah in prayer, although the Ka'bah was the first house of worship established for people, and it was the original qiblah. Although there are several other narrations concerning the occasion of revelation of this verse besides this one.

Nevertheless, the generality of the verse indicates that it is a general ruling, and that everyone is forbidden from preventing people from remembering, reflecting upon and worshipping Allah in the mosques of Allah, or from seeking to destroy those mosques. Here the ruling for such people is also stated, along with the recompense that all those who do such deeds deserve. "And the recompense is this: ﴿Such people should not enter them except in fear﴾." ﴿Such people are fit only to enter these places of worship in fear.﴾

That is, they deserve to be constantly pushed away, driven off, and deprived of peace and security, unless they seek refuge out of that fear and unease, entering the mosques fearfully and holding fast to the sanctity of the mosque. (This very situation arose at the conquest of Makkah), when the herald of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called out: "Whoever takes refuge in the Masjid al-Haram will be granted safety." Thereupon even the rebellious individuals of Quraysh took refuge in the mosque, although these were the very people who for a long time had been preventing the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions even from worshipping in the Masjid al-Haram. While describing the end of such people, the Holy Qur'an further explains that such people will be disgraced in this world, and in the Hereafter a great punishment has been prepared for them. ﴿For them in this world is disgrace, and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment.﴾

Some commentators have interpreted the verse ﴿Such people should not enter them except in fear﴾ to mean that it is their duty to enter the mosques, observing the etiquette of the mosque, in fear and with humility and reverence, because respect for the mosques of Allah and the awe and majesty of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, require that one step into His house with due reverence. Nevertheless, this too is one interpretation, and the verse admits of it.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 2, verse 115:

But of these verses, the second, namely "Wa lillahil mashriqu wal maghrib" (And to Allah belong the east and the west), since it was revealed on the occasion of the change of the qibla (tahwil al-qibla), we have therefore also applied the first verse, "Wa man azlamu" (And who is more unjust), to the change of the qibla.

﴿And to Allah belong the east and the west. So wherever you turn, there is the Face of Allah. Indeed, Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing.﴾ The east and the west belong to Allah. Wherever you turn, that is the direction of Allah's Face. Allah is vast in bounty and knows all things.

From this verse it is evident that it was revealed in refutation of the propaganda of the Jews, who were opposing the change of the qibla, saying that if this is the qibla, then it means that the prayers the Muslims offered facing Bayt al-Maqdis were all invalid, all wasted, and that there would be no reckoning for them with Allah. The verse refutes this false notion of the Jews, that wherever one turns is the qibla. When a worshipper turns in any direction, the Face of Allah is in that direction. As for the fact that Allah has commanded us to pray facing a specific direction, that is purely obedience to the command and an act of worship and submission. This command has not been given because, God forbid, the Face of Allah is in that direction and not in another. As for Allah, He does not impose hardship or constraint on His servants in any matter, nor does He diminish their reward, for He knows the secrets of their hearts and also knows the inclinations and tendencies that people have toward turning to a particular direction. With Allah there is great vastness. He is the Master of intentions. ﴿Indeed, Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing.﴾

After this, the Qur'an clarifies that the conception of God among these people has itself become corrupted, and that they have deviated from the foundation of religion, namely the doctrine of Tawhid, which was the basic and correct conception of all messengers and prophethoods, and that their conception of God has become connected with other jahili (ignorant) notions regarding the essence and attributes of Allah.

Accordingly, the Qur'an here clarifies that there is no fundamental difference between the conception of God of the polytheists of Arabia and that of the polytheists among the People of the Book. Their hearts are joined together, and at this occasion the correct faith of Islam is clarified before both groups.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 2, verse 116:

The saying that "Allah has taken a son" is not only the belief of the Christians about Prophet Masih (Jesus), but the Jews too believed in the sonship of Uzair (Ezra). And this same belief the polytheists of Makkah held about the angels of Allah. The Qur'an has not detailed the beliefs of these sects here, because a summary discussion was intended. Here the aim was to allude briefly to the three groups who, at that time in the Arabian Peninsula, were standing in the way of the Islamic movement. It is astonishing that even today in the Islamic world, these same three groups stand in the way of Islam. The Jews, in the form of international Zionism; the Christians, in the form of international Crusaderism; and the Arabs, in the form of international communism. This last, communism, is a greater disbelief (kufr) than the "Arab polytheism" of that time. By stating this common characteristic, the claim of the Jews and Christians that only they are the people of guidance is automatically refuted, because in the fundamental belief of guidance they share the same disposition as the polytheists.

Before describing the second corrupt and false aspect of their concept of the Divinity, Allah Almighty, by means of their aforementioned corrupt concept of Him, declares His purity and freedom from it, and explains what the nature of the relationship is between Allah Almighty and His creation.

﴿Glory be to Him! Rather, to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth; all are obedient to Him. He is the Originator of the heavens and the earth; and when He decrees a matter, He only says to it, "Be," and it is.﴾

In this verse, from the Islamic point of view, the transcendent and pure concept of Allah, the Glorious and Exalted, is described. It is explained what the nature of the relationship is between Allah and His creation, and also how the universe proceeded from the Being of Allah. The concept presented regarding all these matters is higher and more exalted than all other concepts about them. How did this universe proceed from the Being and Attributes of Allah? He simply willed, and it came into existence. The mere saying of "Kun" (Be) was enough, and "Fa-yakun" (and it is) followed. That is, the mere direction of the Divine will towards a thing that is to be is sufficient for the command that it comes into existence immediately, in the very form and shape determined for it. In this process no intermediary and no material force is needed. Now the question is: how does the Divine will become attached to a creature, and how as a result does the creature come into existence? We cannot come to know its reality, because it is a secret that is hidden from human perception, since the human power of perception is not yet capable of bearing this secret. By the nature of human creation, the human power of perception was not made capable of knowing this secret, because for the fulfilment of the purpose for which man was created, he has no need of it. What is the purpose of the creation of man? The discharge of the duty of khilafah (vicegerency) on earth and construction and development within the earth. Allah has revealed to man only as many secrets of the laws of nature in this universe as he needed, and without which he could not discharge his responsibilities, and through which the benefits of the treasures of the earth became possible for man. On the other hand, he has been kept unaware of such secrets as had no connection with the purpose of the creation of humanity, namely the great khilafah. In this matter other philosophies went astray, such that they never saw any ray of light, and they vainly pursued the solving of these mysteries. They established hypotheses which were merely the product of human perception. Yet human perception, by its very creation, is not capable of reflecting upon these metaphysical hypotheses. Allah has not given human perception, from the very beginning, the means through which it could reach these mysteries. Thus, if one reflects, even the highest of all philosophical ideas are so ridiculous that an ordinary person too is astonished on seeing them and begins to wonder how a philosopher and an intelligent person arrived at such conclusions. All this happened because the proponents of these philosophies pushed human perception beyond its natural limits and used it in metaphysical matters in which it had no capacity. Therefore they could not reach any satisfactory conclusion. Rather, the conclusions of these philosophies carry no weight in the eyes of the person who believes in the Islamic view of life and lives under its protective shelter. Islam has safeguarded its adherents from groping about in these darknesses without clear proof. Therefore, it does not basically make the unsuccessful attempt to solve metaphysical problems through the wrong method of thought. Among Muslims in later periods, those philosophers who, influenced by Greek philosophy, began to think according to philosophical hypotheses, fell into great confusion and erroneous discourse, just as their Greek philosophical teachers had fallen before them. These Muslim philosophers introduced into the Islamic system of thought problems which were contrary to its very temperament, and they had not even a remote connection with the reality of the Islamic worldview. In short, whenever man has pushed his intellect and thought beyond its limits and used it against its temperament and nature, the outcome has always been the same.

﴿Rather, to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth; all are obedient to Him.﴾

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 2, verse 117:

He has no need to take any son from among the things that are in the heavens and the earth. Therefore all people are His creation, and they stand on one level and hold one and the same status.

﴿The Originator of the heavens and the earth. When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, "Be," and it is.﴾ (117)

The manner in which this Divine will becomes attached to the thing that comes into being is beyond the grasp and understanding of human perception. Indeed, it lies beyond the reach of human perceptive power. Therefore, to spend the faculties of human perception in comprehending such unimaginable modes would be a futile undertaking, and would amount to wandering without proof or evidence in that intricate and winding valley.

Here the commentary on the claim of the People of the Book regarding filial relation (ibniyyah) concludes. After correcting their false beliefs, the discussion now turns to the statements of the polytheists, which oppose the station of divinity and resemble the beliefs and sayings of the People of the Book.

﴿And those who have no knowledge say: "Why does Allah not speak to us directly, or why does no sign come to us?" Likewise said those before them, the same as their saying.﴾

"Those who have no knowledge" refers to the unlettered people who are deprived of the knowledge of the Book, and they were generally polytheists. They had no knowledge of the Book of Allah. These people repeatedly demanded of the Prophet (ﷺ) that he bring them to speak with Allah, or present before them some miracle. Mention of this unreasonable demand here is made so that it may be shown that the nations before them, the Jews and Christians, also made similar demands of their prophets. The people of Moses (peace be upon him) demanded that they wished to see Allah openly. Moreover, they also went to extreme lengths in demanding material extraordinary events (khawariq al-'adat) and miracles. The intent is that these polytheists and Jews possess one and the same temperament and one and the same mode of thought, and they are afflicted with one and the same kind of deviance: "tashabahat qulubuhum" (their hearts have become alike). Thus the Jews have no superiority over the polytheists. All of them are entirely of one disposition in their mode of thinking, obstinacy and deviance. ﴿Indeed, We have made the signs clear for a people who have certainty.﴾

For one whose heart has the taste of faith, when he studies the signs of Allah, he finds in them the fulfillment of his faith, and in these signs lies the provision for the satisfaction of his conscience. In short, signs and miracles cannot create faith within anyone; rather, it is faith by whose light the signs and miracles of Allah can be understood, and through which tranquility can be attained. In this way the heart and mind of a person can continually receive guidance.

After the conclusion of their sayings, the refutation of their false ideas, and the unveiling of the purposes behind their misleading propaganda, the address now turns back to the Holy Prophet (ﷺ). Allah describes his duties, specifies the objectives for him, and tells him the nature of the struggle that exists between him and the Jews and Christians: how deep the difference is between him and them, and that it can be removed only by paying a heavy price, while he possesses neither that price nor is able to pay it. And if (God forbid) he were to agree to pay this heavy price in order to unite with them, he would make himself the object of the wrath of Allah.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 2, verse 119:

﴿Indeed, We have sent you with the truth﴾ "We have sent you with the knowledge of truth."

These words carry such force that they dissolve the misleading doubts of those who spread deviation, they cut off the root of the conspirators' plots, and they nullify the deception and misguiding instruction of the hypocrites. Moreover, the phonetic rhythm of these words is itself a manifestation of firmness and certainty.

﴿Bashiran wa nadhira﴾ "A bearer of good news and a warner." That is, conveying the message of truth and calling people to it is your fundamental duty. You will give glad tidings to those who obey and warn those who disobey. Upon this, your duty is fulfilled.

﴿And you will not be questioned about the companions of the Blazing Fire﴾ (119) "You are not responsible or accountable for those who have made the Fire their companion." These are people who will enter Hell because of their own misfortune and its consequences.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 2, verse 120:

O Messenger! The Jews and Christians will remain at war against you, and will continue to plot against you. They will never make peace with you, nor will they ever be pleased with you, unless you abandon your mission, give up the truth, cast aside the certainty that you possess, and adopt the crookedness, polytheism and jahili (Days of Ignorance) concepts in which they are immersed. As has already been explained shortly before this.

﴿And the Jews will never be pleased with you, nor the Christians, until you follow their religion.﴾

This is the real reason for their rejection of the truth. It is not that some shortcoming has been left in presenting proof and evidence to them. Nor is it that they are dissatisfied about your being on the path of truth, or that the guidance coming to you is not from Allah. No matter how far you advance towards them, and no matter how much love you show them, none of these things can make them pleased with you. They can be pleased with you only if you adopt their creed and their religion and give up the truth and reality that you possess.

It is this worldview that manifests itself in every time and place. The Jews and Christians, in every age and era, who appear at war against Islam and the Muslim community, are in fact fighting an ideological war against Islam, and this ideological war is being waged between the Islamic bloc and these two Western blocs. Although these Western blocs sometimes fight against one another, this hostility is like that between two sects of one religion, whereas in confronting Islam and the Muslims these two sects (the Jews and Christians) have always remained united.

In its reality and essence this is an ideological war, but the Jewish and Christian world, which is immersed in enmity towards Islam and Muslims, keeps giving it different colours and keeps raising various kinds of flags over it. And they do this with great malice, cunning and deceit. Previously, by waging an ideological war against the Muslims, these people had experienced the passionate love the Muslims have for their religion and their worldview. Therefore, these enemies of Islam, with great cleverness, turned around and changed the title and flag of their struggle. Now they have begun fighting against Islam without declaring an ideological war, because in an ideological war they feared the emotions and zeal of the Muslims. Moreover, these people advanced under the banner of homeland, economics, politics, acquisition of military centres and other such aims, and planted in the hearts of some heedless and deceived Muslims the notion that the war of beliefs and ideologies has now become a thing of the past, having no meaning.

Now it is not permissible to raise the banner of jihad and wage battle on the basis of religion and creed. This reality is a characteristic of these bigoted enemies of Islam who appear outwardly defeated, and they have adopted this approach solely so that they remain safe from the ideological zeal and fury of the Muslims, whereas in their intention and aims the hardline Zionists and international Crusaders (even if they are international communists) are in fact all engaged in removing that heavy stone (the Islamic ideology) from their path. History bears witness that previously they clashed with it for a long period, but Islam defeated them all.

In short, this is an ideological war; it is neither a dispute over a piece of land, nor a conflict of interests, nor a contest over places of military importance. These hollow slogans and flags of wealth and land have no real significance; all these stratagems have been adopted by the enemies of Islam solely so that they may keep the simple-minded Muslims unaware of the reality of this struggle and its true aims and objectives. And we have fallen into their deception. Therefore there is no need to blame these enemies; rather, we should blame ourselves, because we have abandoned the Sunnah of the Prophet (ﷺ) and the guidance of Allah that He gave to the Prophet for the guidance of the Muslim community, whereas Allah is the most truthful and His word is clear on this:

﴿And the Jews will never be pleased with you, nor the Christians, until you follow their religion.﴾

They demand only this one price from the Muslims; anything beyond this they do not accept. But true guidance and the firm decision are this: ﴿Say: Indeed, the guidance of Allah is the (only) guidance.﴾

Guidance is that alone; guidance is confined and limited to it, and apart from it there is no guidance at all. Therefore success cannot be achieved by walking on any path other than the straight path designed by Allah. Hence it is absolutely necessary to adopt it. There is no escape from it. We cannot make any amendment to it, nor can we bargain over any small or large part of it. This guidance must be accepted in its entirety: whoever wishes may accept it, and whoever wishes may reject it. But beware, lest the desire for faith and guidance, or their love and friendship, divert you from this path of truth and the straight path.

﴿And if you were to follow their desires after the knowledge that has come to you, you would have no protector or helper against Allah.﴾ What a frightening warning! What a firm decision and how severe a threat! And against whom is it directed? Against the chief of the prophets and the beloved of the Lord of Glory, the Prophet (ﷺ)!

The point is that the guidance of Allah, besides which there is no guidance, you can deviate from only by beginning to follow the desires of these people; otherwise there is no reason, that is, no shortage or weakness of proof and evidence, to abandon it.

Among the People of the Book, those who become free of base desires also read their Book in the manner it ought to be read. That is why they also believe in the truth that is with you. Those who reject this truth will be the ones who suffer loss; neither you nor the believers are in loss.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 2, verse 121:

الَّذِينَ آتَيْنَاهُمُ الْكِتَابَ يَتْلُونَهُ حَقَّ تِلاوَتِهِ أُولَئِكَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِهِ وَمَنْ يَكْفُرْ بِهِ فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْخَاسِرُونَ

"Those to whom We gave the Book recite it as it ought to be recited; it is they who believe in it. And whoever disbelieves in it, it is they who are the losers." Translation of the Urdu rendering: Those to whom We have given the Book read it in the manner that the right of reading it demands. They truly believe in it with sincere hearts. And those who adopt a posture of disbelief toward it, it is they who are in fact the losers.

Because they have been deprived of faith, and faith in this entire universe is one of the great blessings of Allah among all His favours. Therefore, what greater loss can there be than the loss of faith? After this decisive and forceful discourse, the direction of address turns back toward the Children of Israel. It is as if, after this long contest and debate, and after recounting the long history of their conduct toward Allah and His prophets, they are addressed for one last time. Having left them aside and addressed the Messenger ﷺ and the believers, now they are once again invited for the last time. Yet they have become extremely heedless and careless about the honour of safeguarding the Divine trust, namely the Islamic outlook on life. Although this honour and responsibility had been theirs since ancient times. In sum, in the final part of this discourse too, people are given the same invitation that was given to them at its beginning.

**Lesson 7: At a Glance**

Here the narrative turns to events that belong to the period before Musa (peace be upon him), namely the story of Ibrahim (Abraham, peace be upon him). The way the story of Ibrahim is presented in this context also makes its importance clear. For the Islamic community in Madinah, this story was extremely important for shedding light on the various kinds of disputes that existed between the Muslims and the Jews.

The People of the Book traced their lineage to Ibrahim through Ishaq (Isaac, peace be upon him). They took pride in this descent and in God's promise to Ibrahim and to his descendants after him, a promise of growth and blessing. Because of this, they believed that guidance and remaining upon the correct religion were in some sense their exclusive possession, just as they regard themselves as the sole claimants to Paradise, whatever their deeds may be.

The Quraysh too were descendants of Ibrahim through Isma'il (Ishmael, peace be upon him), and they took pride in this lineage. They had inherited from Ibrahim the custodianship of the House of God (the Ka'bah) and the building of the Sacred Mosque (al-Masjid al-Haram), and they had also inherited from him religious leadership over all of Arabia and the ranks of excellence and honour.

Earlier, while discussing the claims of the Jews and Christians regarding Paradise, the Qur'an had stated: "They say, none will enter Paradise except those who are Jews or Christians." In another place, their statement was quoted as they sought to turn the Muslims into Jews or Christians: "Become Jews or Christians so that you may be guided." It was also pointed out that some of them hinder people from the remembrance of God in the mosques of God and strive to ruin them. There, we said that these statements may relate to the event of the change of the qiblah (tahwil), because at that time the Jews had launched a malicious propaganda campaign against the Islamic community.

Now, here, the discussion concerns Ibrahim, Ishaq and Isma'il (peace be upon them all), the House of God, its construction, and the related Islamic rites. This is the appropriate occasion for it, so that correct facts about the lineage of the prophets and their mutual relationship may become firmly fixed in people's minds, in place of the baseless claims of the Jews, Christians and polytheists. It also settles the question concerning the direction to which the Muslims are to turn. On this occasion, the religion of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), that is, pure monotheism (tawhid), is also clarified, and it is shown that the fabricated beliefs and deviations adopted by the People of the Book and the polytheists have no connection, even remotely, with the Islamic doctrine of tawhid. On the contrary, there is no difference between the beliefs of Ibrahim, Isma'il, Ishaq and Ya'qub (Jacob, peace be upon them all)—Isra'il, from whom these people trace their lineage—and the beliefs of the Muslims and their final religion. It is also made clear that the religion of God has always been one and the same, that it has been the mission of all prophets and messengers, and that it is not restricted to any people or lineage, nor is it the monopoly of anyone. It is a belief that is the wealth of the believer's heart; it has no connection with blind tribalism. It is an inheritance that is not divided by the ties of blood and lineage but is conferred through the bond of faith and belief. Therefore, whoever accepts this religion and safeguards it, to whatever lineage he belongs and whatever people he is a member of, is the most entitled to it, even more than one's full brothers and one's own offspring, because this is the religion of God, and between God and His servants there is no bond of lineage or any other kind of relationship.

These truths, which form an important part of the fundamental outlines of the Islamic worldview, are stated by the Qur'an with a remarkably distinctive style, clearly and in full. Apart from its eloquent and articulate mode of expression, the context here is exceedingly coherent. First, it is stated how God tested Ibrahim, and how he succeeded in that trial, and as a result God raised up the Final Prophet, Muhammad (ﷺ), and established the Muslim Ummah. Therefore, the Muslim Ummah became the rightful heir to this inheritance, and this honour was taken away from the descendants of Ibrahim. This is because those who deserve an ideological inheritance are only those who hold firm faith in prophethood, act upon it well, and maintain a correct conception of prophethood. This is the reason for an ideological inheritance.

Amid the narration of these historical facts, the manner of expression shows that Islam, in its meaning of submitting oneself wholly before God, was the first message at the beginning of the line of messengers, and at the conclusion of that line, this same Islam was the mission of the messengers. It was the doctrine of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), and after him, the belief of Isma'il, Ishaq and the other messengers and righteous movements. These figures entrusted this trust to Musa (Moses) and Isa (Jesus, peace be upon them), and the inheritance of Ibrahim finally reached the Muslim Ummah. Whoever remains steadfast upon this belief and this doctrine will be the spiritual heir of Ibrahim, and will be the rightful holder of God's covenant with Ibrahim and the fulfilment of the good tidings given to him. But whoever turns away from Islam and keeps himself far from the religion of Ibrahim has thereby forfeited the covenant of God, deprived himself of the right of that fidelity, and ceased to be the fulfilment of those good tidings.

At this point, all the claims of the Jews and Christians that they are a chosen and distinguished people collapse at their foundation, merely because they are the grandchildren of Ibrahim and his successors. Since they abandoned the doctrine of tawhid, they have been deprived of the inheritance of Ibrahim.

At this same point, the claims of the tribe of Quraysh also crumble, that they are entitled to the guardianship, care and construction of the House of God, because they have departed from the spiritual inheritance of the first founder of that sacred place. Likewise, the claim of the Jews is also overturned, that they are the people of the qiblah of Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem), and that the Muslims should, as is proper, keep Bayt al-Maqdis as their qiblah. Therefore, the Ka'bah is the qiblah for them, and it was also the qiblah of their forefather Ibrahim (peace be upon him).

All these matters have been expressed in a beautiful and graceful form, containing countless clear indications, and containing stations and points for reflection in which extremely subtle meanings lie hidden, and explanations that are deeply impactful. Now, in the light of the above indications, we shall discuss in detail this eloquent style of expression.

The address is to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Recall the account of Ibrahim's (peace be upon him) trial. He was given certain commands and placed under certain obligations, and he fulfilled those commands and prohibitions with complete faithfulness. In another place, Allah, praising Ibrahim's (peace be upon him) faithfulness, said: ﴿And Ibrahim, who fulfilled [his commands]﴾. This is the lofty station that Ibrahim (peace be upon him) attained: the station where Allah Himself bears witness to the faithfulness and obedience of His servant, even though as a human being he is a weak and deficient creature, for whom complete fulfilment (wafa, that is, full obedience) is not possible.

It was by reaching this station that Ibrahim (peace be upon him) became deserving of this honour and this trust. ﴿He said: "Indeed, I am going to make you a leader (imam) for the people"﴾. An imam who is the qiblah and ka'bah of the people: one who leads them to Allah, who is foremost in doing good, with people following behind him, and who is their beloved leader.

Here, through the person of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), human nature becomes apparent. Within a human being there exists the innate impulse that his lineage should continue through his offspring. This is a deep natural and psychological awareness, which Allah has placed in the depths of human nature. Its wisdom is that the progress of life continues, and human life moves forward along the lines that the Creator has laid down for it, so that the advances begun by earlier generations are carried further by those who come after, and harmony is maintained among all generations. Some people wish to break this awareness and eliminate it, although it is embedded in the very nature of man. Its wisdom is that man may be able to achieve certain far-reaching objectives. Under this same impulse and awareness, Islam has laid down detailed rules of inheritance (qanun-e-miras), so that human beings continue their striving and accelerate it for the welfare of their children and grandchildren. Today, the efforts being made in the world to demolish this natural awareness are in fact a means of destroying human nature. It is certainly true that certain corruptions exist in the collective life of man, but to destroy human nature and the human personality itself in order to eliminate these corruptions is an extremely crude, short-sighted and unnatural method of treatment. Every remedy for these collective corruptions that is carried out through a method contrary to nature can never succeed, can never be beneficial, and can by no means be lasting. There are remedies that will eliminate these corruptions and yet will not conflict with human nature. But to find such methods, faith and guidance are needed, and the healer must have a complete and deep awareness of human nature, and his thinking must reach beyond man's physical creation to its depths, and this thinking and this zeal for reform must be free from class-based hatred and enmity, because on account of such class feelings, instead of any comprehensive reform of man taking place, man falls into comprehensive ruin. So Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said: ﴿And from my offspring?﴾

The answer to this question comes from the Lord of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), who tested him and then chose him. This answer lays the foundation for the important principle we have already mentioned: that leadership and command are the right of those who prove themselves deserving of it through their awareness, conduct, capability and faith. It is not a hereditary or lineal office that passes from father to son. Here, relationship and connection are not based on blood, lineage or nationality; rather, bonds of religion and faith are the basis of connection, and in matters of leadership and authority, slogans of blood, race and nation fall within the category of the claims of jahiliyyah, which stand in clear opposition to the correct human outlook on the life of mankind.

﴿He said: "My covenant does not extend to the wrongdoers."﴾

Wrongdoing (zulm) also has many kinds and many forms. The associating of partners with Allah by the soul is itself a form of wrongdoing. Disobedience to Allah on the part of people is also a wrongdoing. The trust that is here forbidden to wrongdoers refers to general leadership (imamah), which encompasses all its types: prophetic leadership and messengership, the caliphate, leading the prayer (imamat al-salat), and all other offices of leadership and authority. Therefore, justice and fairness, in their broad meaning, are the first condition for the entitlement to every kind of leadership. And if a person commits any kind of wrongdoing, he deprives himself of the entitlement to leadership, whatever that leadership may be.

What was said to Ibrahim (peace be upon him), and this covenant whose wording contains no ambiguity, definitively establishes that the Jews will always remain far from and deprived of the office of leadership, because they committed wrongdoing, fell into immorality and disobedience, disobeyed Allah, and abandoned the beliefs and convictions of their noble forefather.

Furthermore, what was said to Ibrahim (peace be upon him), and this covenant whose wording contains no crookedness or obscurity, also definitively deprives of the office of leadership those who call themselves Muslims, if they have committed wrongdoing, fallen into immorality and transgression, and strayed far from the path of Allah. They have cast the Shari'ah of Allah behind their backs. They claim to be Islam, while they have removed the Shari'ah of Allah and His system of life from their entire lives. The claim of Islam by such people is a mere false claim, which is not in fact founded upon the firm basis of the covenant made with Allah.

The Islamic conception of life cuts off all those ties and relationships that are not established on the basis of a common thought, outlook or unity of action. It recognizes only those ties and relationships that are founded upon unity of ideology and practice. Any other connection has no value in the eyes of Islam. Indeed, Islam even separates two generations of the same ummah when one generation opposes the other in its creed and ideology. And if the bond of creed is broken, Islam even brings separation between father and son and between husband and wife. In short, the Arab world in a state of polytheism and the Arab world in a state of Islam are as different as heaven and earth. Between the two there is, from the Islamic point of view, no relationship, no connection and no tie. Among the People of the Book, those who believed form one ummah, and those who abandoned the religion of Ibrahim, Musa and Isa (peace be upon them all) form another ummah. Between these two there is also no relationship, no connection and no tie. Here, a family is not formed through the relationship of father, grandfather and grandchildren; rather, those become members of one family who gather together upon one creed and one ideology.

From the Islamic point of view, the formation of an ummah is also not based on lineage; rather, the ummah is formed from the believers, even if their colours, their races and their homelands differ. This is the Islamic conception of life, whose springs flow from this divine manner of the Book of Allah.

This is the House of Allah, whose custodians today, the people of Quraysh, are terrorising the believers, inflicting all kinds of torments upon them. They have subjected them to every sort of hardship merely for the crime of religion and faith, to the point that they were compelled to abandon the neighbourhood of this House and its blessings and migrate, even though Allah's decree concerning this House was that it would be a centre for the people, and that all men would turn towards it from every direction. Here no one would frighten them. Here they would have spiritual and physical peace and tranquillity, because this House is in itself a embodiment of security, a source of tranquillity and a place of safety.

The people were commanded to take the place of worship of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), that is the Ka'bah (by "the place of Ibrahim" in my view and preference, the whole of the Ka'bah is meant), as a place of prayer and worship. Therefore it is now entirely logical that this same House should also be the qiblah of the Muslims, and no one has any valid objection to this. For Muslims, this is the proper qiblah, because in terms of faith and monotheism, only the Muslims are the community of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) and his heirs. The Ka'bah is solely the House of Allah, not the house of any human being. Allah, who is its Owner, entrusted this duty to two of His righteous servants, Ibrahim (peace be upon him) and Isma'il (peace be upon him), that they should keep it pure and clean and ready for those who come here to bow and prostrate, or who seek a place of security and take refuge here, or who come here for the purpose of Hajj and visitation, or those who live here and perform i'tikaf in this House, or who arrive from outside for the sake of worship. Moreover, this House was not even the property of Ibrahim and Isma'il (peace be upon them both), so that these rights would have passed by inheritance to Quraysh. Quraysh were appointed as custodians and servants of it only by Allah's permission and command, so that they would keep it ready for the believers who come to it.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 2, verse 126:

Ibrahim's (peace be upon him) prayer once again confirms that this house of Allah is a sanctuary of security. And once again it becomes clear here that in Islam the basis of inheritance and succession (wirathah wa niyabah) rests on moral excellence and righteousness. In the preceding verse, Ibrahim (peace be upon him) had been given the guidance: ﴿My covenant does not include the wrongdoers.﴾

From this, Ibrahim (peace be upon him) understood well that dar în râh falân ibn falân chîze nîst (on this path, the lineage of so-and-so son of so-and-so counts for nothing). Therefore, in his prayer for provision, by saying "whoever among them believes in Allah and the Last Day," he himself excluded the wrongdoers. This is because he had understood well the Sunnah of Allah and the purpose of Allah.

Ibrahim (peace be upon him) was an extremely forbearing and God-fearing prophet. He was most steadfast and firmly held to the straight path. He would immediately adopt the course of action he was commanded to follow, and in his prayers and requests too he kept the will of Allah in view. So at this point Allah, the Exalted, answers his prayer by saying regarding those about whom he had fallen silent, namely the people of disbelief and the people of Hell, ﴿He said: As for him who disbelieves, I will let him enjoy for a little while, then I will drive him to the torment of the Fire, and wretched is the destination.﴾

Observe the style of expression! The discourse begins in narrative mode. A story begins thus: "And [remember] when Abraham (peace be upon him) and Ishmael (peace be upon him) were raising the foundations of the House."

Now the reader waits for the narration to continue, but suddenly a scene appears on the screen of our imagination, as though Abraham and Ishmael stand before us. It feels as if we are not merely imagining them but seeing these two with our own eyes. They are present before us, and it is almost as though we could hear with our own ears this heart-melting supplication of theirs.

This strange atmosphere of a fervent prayer, a melodious plea and a request for what is sought lies right before our eyes, as if all of this is happening at this very moment. A living and moving scene is before us, with its characters standing in clear form. A beautiful and graceful mode of expression is among the important distinctive features of the Qur'an. The Qur'an describes any scene of the earlier ages in such a way that it appears to be moving on the screen before us. This quality of vivid, moving, personal portrayal and scene-painting, full of life, belongs to this eternal Book of God alone, and it is indeed miraculous.

And what is inside this supplication? The humble devotion of prophethood, the firm certainty of prophethood, and the prophetic consciousness of belief and creed in this universe. It is this same devotion, certainty and consciousness that God wishes to teach to the heirs of the prophets. The Qur'an's aim is that through this inspiration, this consciousness becomes deeper in the hearts and minds of the heirs of the prophets.

﴿Our Lord, accept from us. Indeed You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.﴾ (127) "O our Lord, accept [this] from us; indeed You are the Hearing, the Knowing." This is a prayer for acceptance, and this is the ultimate goal, because this deed is purely for God, with humility and submission. Through it, both of them turn towards God. And behind all this activity and action lies only the desire for the pleasure of God and for the acceptance of prayer. The ray of hope is that God hears the call of everyone who calls upon Him, and along with that, He knows the feeling that lies behind that call and the consciousness of the one who calls.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 2, verse 128:

رَبَّنَا وَاجْعَلْنَا مُسْلِمَيْنِ لَكَ وَمِنْ ذُرِّيَّتِنَا أُمَّةً مُسْلِمَةً لَكَ وَأَرِنَا مَنَاسِكَنَا وَتُبْ عَلَيْنَا إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ التَّوَّابُ الرَّحِيمُ

"Our Lord, make us both submissive to You, and from our descendants a nation submissive to You. Show us our rites of worship, and turn to us in forgiveness. Indeed, You are the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful."

Sayyid Qutb: This is a hope for the assistance that these two (Ibrahim and Isma'il, peace be upon them) seek from Allah in the matter of being guided to Islam. In their hearts was the firm awareness that their hearts are in the fingers of Allah the Exalted, and that guidance is only His guidance; no one can be guided without His assistance and His granting of success. Therefore both of them are wholly turned toward Allah, inclined and drawn to Him, and Allah is the best of helpers.

The nature of the Ummah of Muslims is that its members help and support one another. Its individuals, generation after generation, are ideologically bound together, and therefore the supplication is made: وَمِنْ ذُرِّيَّتِنَا أُمَّةً مُسْلِمَةً لَكَ "and from our descendants, a Muslim nation for You."

This is a supplication from which it becomes clear what the first desire of the believer's heart is. Belief and ideology are the beloved and occupation of a believer; it is his first priority. The importance of the wealth that had been given to Ibrahim and Isma'il (peace be upon them) was clear to them, namely the wealth of faith and the treasure of creed. This importance and desire compel them to plead for this wealth on behalf of coming generations too. Therefore they pray to their Lord that He not deprive their progeny of that wealth, the worth of which no thing equals. Earlier they had prayed that He grant their progeny provisions and abundance; therefore they also considered it necessary that their progeny not be deprived of the wealth of faith. They also prayed that He teach their progeny the rites of worship and show them the methods of worship. He is the Forgiving, the Merciful, who pardons them.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 2, verse 129:

After this, they make a further supplication that, even in distant ages, God should make a permanent arrangement for their guidance.

﴿Our Lord, raise up among them a Messenger from among themselves, who will recite Your verses to them, teach them the Book and wisdom, and purify them. Indeed, You are the Mighty, the Wise.﴾ (2:129)

"O Allah! From among these people, raise up a Messenger from their own nation, who will recite Your verses to them, teach them the Book and wisdom, and purify their lives. Indeed, You are the Mighty and the Wise."

In consequence of the acceptance of this supplication of Ibrahim and Isma'il (peace be upon them both), that Noble Messenger (ﷺ) was sent, and after many centuries, and his mission came from the progeny of Ibrahim (peace be upon him). He now recites the verses to them, teaches them the Book and wisdom, and purifies them from every kind of filth and pollution. A sincere supplication with Allah is always accepted, but it becomes manifest at the time that the wisdom of Allah the Exalted has appointed for it. It is the habit of ordinary people to be hasty, and those who do not attain their desired goal become despondent and distressed.

At the time of the revelation of this supplication in Surah al-Baqarah, there was an all-encompassing conflict going on between the Muslims and the Jews. In these circumstances, this supplication contains certain allusions and has particular significance. Ibrahim (peace be upon him) and Isma'il (peace be upon him), who were commanded to build and purify this House and to provide facilities for its worshippers, visitors and residents, were the forefathers of the present custodians, namely the Quraysh, in whose hands today lies the management of the Ka'bah. And their clear declaration is: "Make us submissive to You" and "Raise up from our offspring a Muslim community." Just as they also said: "O our Lord, raise up among them a Messenger from among themselves, who will recite Your verses to them, teach them the Book and wisdom, and purify them." Thus, through this supplication of Ibrahim and Isma'il (peace be upon them both), they establish that the Muslim community is the successor and vicegerent of Ibrahim and Isma'il (peace be upon them both), and that it has the right that the management of the Ka'bah now be in its hands. Thus the Ka'bah is the centre of the Muslim community, and in comparison with the polytheists this community has a greater right to the management and administration of this House of God, and in comparison with the Jews and Christians it is more deserving that the Muslim community should have its own qiblah.

Those who claim that they are upon guidance, link their religion to Ibrahim (peace be upon him), and say that they are the heirs and successors of the millat of Ibrahim, and those of the Quraysh who trace their lineage to Isma'il should listen carefully: when Ibrahim (peace be upon him) asked about this succession, leadership and imamate for his offspring, the answer from Allah was:

﴿My covenant does not include the wrongdoers.﴾ (2:124)

"My promise does not extend to the wrongdoers."

And afterwards, when Ibrahim (peace be upon him) asked for blessing and abundance of provision for the people of Makkah, he said: ﴿Whoever among them believes in Allah and the Last Day﴾ (2:126), "whoever among them believes in Allah and the Last Day."

And when these personalities rose to build the Ka'bah, they supplicated: O Lord! Make us submissive to You, and raise up from our offspring a Muslim community, and raise up among them, from their own offspring, the Final Prophet. Allah accepted the supplications of both of them, sent Hadrat Muhammad ibn Abdullah, and through him re-established the Muslim community, and thus caused this ideological inheritance to continue.

With the conclusion of the story of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), the address now turns toward those people who were challenging the Muslim community's right to leadership and superiority, who were at war with the Prophethood and Messengership of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and who were engaged in argument and dispute with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the question of what the reality of the religion of Islam is, what the true religion is, and what their own assumptions are. Therefore the Qur'an gives the impression about these people as follows.

This is the religion of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), that is, pure and clear Islam and submission. Only one who wrongs himself will turn away from it. Only one who is truly foolish will be far from it, and he will be a ruiner of his own self. Hadrat Ibrahim (peace be upon him) is the one whom the Lord of Majesty chose for the community of the world, and about whom Allah bore witness that in the Hereafter he would be among the righteous. He chose this religion. When his Lord said to him, "Submit," he, without hesitation, without any doubt and without any deviation, immediately bowed in submission and at once said: ﴿I have submitted to the Lord of the worlds.﴾

This is the religion of Ibrahim, pure Islam and clear faith. Ibrahim (peace be upon him) did not confine it to his own person alone, but also chose it for his offspring.

He enjoined his children to hold fast to it. Hadrat Ibrahim (peace be upon him) gave this counsel to his children. Hadrat Ya'qub (peace be upon him) also enjoined it upon his children, and it should be remembered that Hadrat Ya'qub is the Israel to whom these people attribute themselves. Yet they do not accept his counsel, and they do not accept the counsel of their noble forefather. Although both Hadrat Ibrahim and Hadrat Ya'qub (peace be upon them both) reminded their children that Allah had chosen this religion for them: ﴿O my sons! Indeed Allah has chosen this religion for you, so do not die except as Muslims.﴾

This is Allah's choice, so after Allah's choice there is no path for them except to choose it. At the very least, the requirement of this grace, this favour and this special kindness of Allah is that they should give immense thanks to Allah for this choice and this bestowal, and should always strive so that in no age and no era does this land of Allah remain empty of the Muslim community, and this movement of worship of Allah continues to flow at all times on this earth: ﴿So die not except in a state of submission.﴾

This was the counsel of Hadrat Ibrahim (peace be upon him) which he gave to his children, and which Hadrat Ya'qub (peace be upon him) gave to his children. And at the last moments of his life and in the agony of death, Ya'qub (peace be upon him) did not forget this counsel. The Children of Israel should reflect upon this deeply.

The scene of Ya'qub (peace be upon him) and his sons at the time of the agonies of death is a great scene. It is a most admonishing, instructive and impactful scene. A person is caught in the struggle between death and life, and in those moments, what is occupying his mind and heart? What is the concern in which his heart and mind are engaged, although he is in the last moments of life? At that time, in what great matter does he seek to gain satisfaction by speaking? He is leaving a legacy for his children, and he emphasises that they should guard this legacy until their last breath, and in his final gasps he hands it over to his children, and he speaks about it in great detail. This legacy is the legacy of a way of life and belief. This is the wealth that he hands over to his sons, and this is the important matter in which he takes such keen interest. This is that great matter in which he takes such keen interest. This is that great affair which remains in his memory even in his final moments: مَا تَعبُدُونَ مِن بِعدِی (What will you worship after me?).

This is the great matter for which he has called you. And in this important matter, I want you to be satisfied. This is my wealth, my legacy, and the important trust which I am entrusting to you. قَالُوا نَعْبُدُ إِلَهَكَ وَإِلَهَ آبَائِكَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَإِسْمَاعِيلَ وَإِسْحَاقَ إِلَهًا وَاحِدًا وَنَحْنُ لَهُ مُسْلِمُونَ ("They said: We will worship your God and the God of your fathers, Ibrahim, Isma'il and Ishaq, one God; and to Him we are submitting.")

Thus they recognise their religion. They commit it to memory. They accept this inheritance, and they firmly resolve to guard it, and thus they satisfy their revered father, who is in the last moments of his life.

The children of Ya'qub (peace be upon him) continued to observe this charge until later times, and they always acknowledged that they are Muslims. At this point the Qur'an asks the Children of Israel this question: أَمْ كُنْتُمْ شُهَدَاءَ إِذْ حَضَرَ يَعْقُوبَ الْمَوْتُ ("Or were you witnesses when death approached Ya'qub?")

Yes, this event did take place; the Qur'an bears witness to it and confirms it. Thus the Qur'an tears away the veil from the deception of those people and decides that the Children of Israel now have no ideological or spiritual connection with their forefather Isra'il.

"In the light of this account, the distinction that exists between the Muslim community of bygone times and the Children of Israel who opposed the Islamic movement becomes clearly manifest. For between that Muslim community of bygone times and their self-styled successors of today there is no connection, no inheritance, and no spiritual bond of inheritance."

Every person will give an account of their own deeds. Each has their own path, each has their own identity, and each has their own distinguishing characteristics. That was a community of believers, and those who came after, its corrupt successors, have no connection with it. What relation do the unworthy and good-for-nothing later generations have with those pure-hearted people? They were one separate community, and these are another separate community. Their banner was separate, and this banner is distinct. Their outlook on life was a faith-based outlook on life, while the outlook on life of these good-for-nothings is purely jahili (ignorant) outlook. In the jahili outlook on life, one community and another community, and one era and another era, are not distinguished, because according to its concept, if two societies are bound by ties of blood and lineage, then in effect both societies are one and the same. But in the faith-based outlook on life, a believing society and a corrupt society are distinguished. Between them there is no kinship, no connection, and these two societies cannot become one ummah. In the sight of Allah these are two separate ummahs. Therefore, according to the values of life of the believers too, these two are different and opposed. According to the Islamic outlook on life, an ummah is only that which holds faith in one single way of life and one creed, even if, in terms of physical relationship and with regard to race and lineage, its members belong to different regions. The Islamic community is not related to any land, any territory or any race or color; it is that outlook on life which is more suited to the dignity of humanity, whose foundation rests on the lofty spirituality of the higher world, and not on earthly and base relationships.

In the course of this detailed account of the historical events of the era of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), in the course of the explanation of the history of the Sacred House (Bayt al-Haram) and the Ka'bah of the Muslims, and in the course of explaining the reality of the Islamic system of life and the reality of inherited notions, the Qur'an now turns to the hollow claims of the contemporary People of the Book, and refutes their false ideas, baseless arguments and unreasonable disputations. From these it becomes evident that all their beliefs, in terms of evidence and in the arena of debate and contention, are without foundation, and are based merely on stubbornness and hostility, and they have no proof for these assumptions of theirs. Thus the Holy Qur'an establishes that Islamic doctrines and beliefs are in reality reasonable and natural beliefs, and that only one who is purely obstinate and hostile can deviate from them. Allah says:

The Jews said that you would find the right path only by becoming Jews, and the Christians said that you would find guidance only by becoming Christians. Allah combined these two claims and told the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to refute their false claims in these words:

قُلْ بَلْ مِلَّةَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ حَنِيفًا وَمَا كَانَ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ

"Say: Rather, [we follow] the millah (religious community or way of life) of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), a ḥanīf, and he was not among the polytheists."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was told to say to them: Come, let us and you all return to our origin, that is, to the millah of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), who is our father and your forefather, the source and wellspring of Islam. His Lord had made a covenant with him, and he was not a polytheist, whereas you have fallen into polytheism.

After this, Allah commands the Muslims to proclaim this great religious unity and religious harmony, which continued from the religion of Abu al-Anbiya, Ibrahim (peace be upon him), down to Isa (peace be upon him), and whose final link is now Islam. The People of the Book are invited to believe in this united and accepted religion:

قُولُوا آمَنَّا بِاللَّهِ وَمَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْنَا وَمَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَى إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَإِسْمَاعِيلَ وَإِسْحَاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ وَالأسْبَاطِ وَمَا أُوتِيَ مُوسَى وَعِيسَى وَمَا أُوتِيَ النَّبِيُّونَ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ لا نُفَرِّقُ بَيْنَ أَحَدٍ مِنْهُمْ وَنَحْنُ لَهُ مُسْلِمُونَ (136)

"Say: We believe in Allah, and in what has been revealed to us, and in what was revealed to Ibrahim, Isma'il, Ishaq, Ya'qub and the Tribes, and in what was given to Musa and Isa and to the prophets from their Lord. We make no distinction between any of them, and to Him we submit."

فَسَيَكْفِيكَهُمُ اللَّهُ وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ

"So Allah will suffice you against them, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing."

صِبْغَةَ اللَّهِ وَمَنْ أَحْسَنُ مِنَ اللَّهِ صِبْغَةً وَنَحْنُ لَهُ عَابِدُونَ

"The colour of Allah. And who has a better colour than Allah? And we are worshippers of Him."

The Qur'an's compelling argument now reaches its decisive conclusion in this way.

﴿Say: Do you dispute with us concerning Allah, when He is our Lord and your Lord? For us are our deeds, and for you are your deeds; and we are sincerely devoted to Him.﴾ (2:139)

"O Prophet, say to them: Do you dispute with us about Allah, when He is our Lord and your Lord? For us are our deeds, and for you are your deeds. And we have made our worship purely for Allah."

There is no room for disagreement over the oneness of Allah and over the attribute of His lordship (rububiyyah). He is the Lord of us and of you. We will give account for our deeds, and you will be answerable for your deeds. But our condition is that we have become wholly His alone: we do not associate anyone with Him, and we do not attach our hopes to anyone else besides Him. Thus Allah, through the words of the Muslims, clarifies their doctrinal position, and this position is such that there is no scope for debate, contention or dispute in it.

Now the discussion turns away from this indisputable position to another subject, in which there was disagreement; yet it is shown that the disagreement that was raised about it is also unnecessary and unreasonable. He says: ﴿Or do you claim that Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob and the Descendants were all Jews or Christians?﴾

These people lived even before Moses, and before Judaism and Christianity came into existence. Moreover, Allah has already explained the reality of their religion, and has testified that their religion was Islam, as was explained in detail above. Allah says: ﴿Say: Do you know better, or does Allah?﴾

Allah has put to their position only a single question, because their position was clearly wrong at first sight. There was no need to answer it; they were merely admonished by means of questioning looks.

After this, the Children of Israel and the People of the Book are told: you know well that these personalities lived before Judaism and Christianity came into existence. You also know that they adhered to that original religion which is called Hanifiyyah, and that in your scriptures, you have the testimony that Allah is about to send the Last Prophet with the divine religion of Hanif, which is also the religion of Abraham (peace be upon him). But you are concealing this testimony. ﴿And who is more unjust than one who conceals a testimony he has from Allah?﴾

And Allah is well aware that you are concealing the testimony that was deposited with you as a trust of leadership, and on the contrary, you are also employing debate, contention and deception to conceal it. ﴿And Allah is not unaware of what you do.﴾

Now the matter reaches its highest point. A decisive verdict is given on this issue, and it is made clear that between Prophet Ibrahim (peace be upon him), Prophet Isma'il (peace be upon him), Prophet Ishaq (peace be upon him), Prophet Ya'qub (peace be upon him), the children of Ya'qub (peace be upon them), and their so-called followers existing today, there is complete contrast. They were one thing, and these are another.

Therefore, the conclusion of the discussion is placed on the sentence that has already passed: ﴿That was a community that has passed away. For it is what it earned, and for you is what you have earned. And you will not be questioned about what they used to do.﴾ (141)

This is a decisive statement. Now, as it were, the dispute has been ended, and the final word has been said concerning the baseless claims of these people.

﴿And the last of our supplication is that all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds.﴾

**Part Two at a Glance**

From the beginning of this section of Surah al-Baqarah, which is the start of the second part (para), the emphasis is on the Islamic movement being prepared to bear the great trust (amanat-e-kubra). The responsibilities include the Islamic worldview (nazariyah-e-hayat), and then, on the basis of that worldview, the establishment of the system of khilafah (Divine vicegerency) in the world. Although there are passages throughout that deal with debate and dispute with the opponents of the Islamic movement, the chief opponents at that time were the Children of Israel, that is, the Jews. Therefore, here their conspiracies, deceptions, their ideological war against the Islamic worldview, and their struggle against the existence of the Islamic movement are addressed. Throughout, Allah's instructions are given to the Islamic movement, and it is warned about the many-sided battle that its enemies have launched against it. Muslims are made aware of the shortcomings into which the Children of Israel had fallen.

The main theme of this part and of the remainder of the surah is that it grants the Muslim ummah a distinct identity and a separate qiblah, so that it may become a community capable of bearing the office of the Divine khilafah. It is to be given a separate system of law and a separate Shari'ah which confirms and embodies the laws and codes revealed before it. The ummah should possess a comprehensive system and a general method. Most importantly, this ummah should possess a particular view concerning human life and death. It should be conscious of the sacrifices it must make for this worldview, in wealth and possessions, in thought and understanding, in conduct and manners, and in life and honour. It must prepare itself to acknowledge and obey the supreme authority of the Almighty Lord, in accordance with the Qur'an and the Sunnah. In short, it must do all of this with submission, contentment, and the utmost obedience.

This is why the discussion of the change of qiblah (tahwil al-qiblah) begins right from the start. From the command regarding the change of qiblah it becomes clear that this ummah is being declared the "middle ummah" (ummah wasat). It is a witness over mankind, and the Messenger is a witness over the ummah. This ummah is the leader of the entire globe, its guide and its director. Therefore it has been advised that, because of this station, it will face many difficulties, and it must be patient with them. It must remain content with Allah's decree. It must offer sacrifices of wealth and life, and in every condition it must entrust all its affairs to Allah.

Moving a little further, before us are placed some principles of the faith-based view of life. It is explained that "righteousness" (birr) is another name for piety (taqwa) and righteous action (amal-e-salih). The directions of east and west, and turning towards them while worshipping, are not in themselves any solid righteousness. In truth, this is a reply to the uproar the Jews were raising at the time of the change of qiblah. They were distorting the facts or concealing them, and all this argument and dispute was a show. They were doing all this with deliberate planning. Accordingly, in these verses the discussion is mostly about the change of qiblah and other matters related to it.

Now the context returns to the practical organisation of the movement, and at the same time some rulings concerning the basic acts of worship are given. It is explained that collective order and worship are in fact the fundamental principles on which the collective life of the Muslim ummah is founded. The organisation of society is necessary also so that the movement can discharge, in the best manner, the responsibility that has been placed upon it. Accordingly, this section mentions the law of retaliation (qisas), the law of bequest (wasiyyah), the rules of fasting (siyam), the legal struggle concerning the Sacred Mosque and the sacred months, the obligation of the Hajj, the penal laws concerning wine and gambling, and the family laws. All these rulings are founded on the Islamic worldview and the principles of connection with Allah. In the final part of this para, in connection with jihad of the self (jihad bil-nafs) and jihad of wealth (jihad bil-mal), as a lesson and example, after Musa (peace be upon him), the second rise of the Children of Israel is also mentioned, when they said to their prophet of the time: "Appoint for us a king so that we may fight in the way of Allah." (1)

This too is a lesson for the Islamic movement. It contains important experiences and guidance for it, because the Islamic movement is the true heir to the ideas and experiences of these nations.

A deep study of the first para makes clear the nature of the struggle that the Qur'an set in motion. The aim of the Qur'an in the building and shaping of the Muslim ummah becomes clear. This is a great struggle, launched against external conspiracies, hatreds, deceptions, false propaganda and complete lies. It is also waged for the reform of the human self, against its inner and human weaknesses, its moral trials and its misguidance.
