In truth, this is the struggle to build guidance and to establish a correct view of life, upon which a community must be founded that can take up the office of khalifatullah fil-ard (Allah's vicegerent on earth) and give the whole world righteous leadership.

Behold the miracle of the Qur'an! The principles, foundations, guidance and indications for organising a community which it laid down for the first Islamic community are necessary today and tomorrow for every community that wishes to rise along Islamic lines. The battle that Islam fought against its opponents could today be waged against every opponent of Islam. Indeed, the conspiracies, deceptions and hostile plans with which the Qur'an contended against its earliest opponents still exist in exactly the same form, and their trickery, plots and schemes today remain the same. Therefore the Muslim ummah today needs, for its struggle and for its protection, the very same guidance that the first Islamic movement needed. Likewise, today the Islamic movement, for its correct view of life, for determining its station in this universe, and for regulating its relations with people, is seen to be in need of the same guidance and the texts of the Qur'an. In this regard the Qur'an presents clear milestones, whereas all other sources of knowledge, understanding, rectitude and guidance, even the newest systems, remain silent on this matter. The Qur'an today is still the path of action for this ummah throughout its entire life. It is still the guide of this ummah on the path of truth. It is still the complete constitution of the ummah, the source of its system of life, and the point of reference for its collectivity. It is the fountainhead of its international affairs and its moral principles. This is the true miracle of this Book!

**Lesson 8 at a Glance**

The subject of discourse in this lesson is solely the change of qiblah. All discussions relate to it. Throughout this lesson, the conspiracies which the Jews carried out at that occasion, in order to spread disorder among the ranks of the Islamic community, are exposed. The objections that the Jews raised concerning this event, and the effects that resulted from them on the minds of the people of Islam, are addressed.

There is no definitive narration concerning this event, nor does the Qur'an mention anything about its date. The verses in question relate to the change of the qiblah from Bayt al-Maqdis to the Ka'bah. This event occurred sixteen or seventeen months after the Hijrah to Madinah. From an overall look at the narrations concerning it, it is generally understood that in Makkah, after the obligation of prayer (salat), the Muslims used to pray facing the Ka'bah. Although this is not explicitly stated, after the Hijrah to Madinah, by the command of the Lord, the Muslims began to pray facing Bayt al-Maqdis. Although no verse of the Qur'an was revealed about this matter either, only the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was given the command. Finally, in this matter, the following verse of the Qur'an was revealed:

﴿So turn your face towards the Sacred Mosque; and wherever you are, turn your faces towards it.﴾ (al-Baqarah: 144)

The former command was abrogated (naskh). Whatever the reality of the event, since the Muslims were praying facing Bayt al-Maqdis, and Bayt al-Maqdis was the qiblah of the People of the Book, that is, the Jews and Christians, the Jews of Madinah used this as a pretext not to enter Islam. They would say: "Since Muhammad (ﷺ) and his companions pray facing our qiblah, the religion is in fact our religion. Our qiblah is the true qiblah. We are the original and the Muslims are the followers. Therefore it is appropriate for Muhammad (ﷺ) and his companions to enter the religion of the Jews themselves, rather than for them to invite us to their religion."

Apart from this, making Bayt al-Maqdis the qiblah was very burdensome for the Arab Muslims. They were accustomed to the reverence and honour of the Sacred House. It had always been their Ka'bah and their qiblah. Added to this, the Jews had begun to take pride in the fact that the Muslims were turning towards their qiblah in prayer. They were also using this as an argument against the religion of Islam.

In these circumstances the Messenger (ﷺ) would repeatedly lift his face towards the sky and turn his attention towards his Lord, but would say nothing with his tongue. He was waiting for the Almighty to guide him according to His own will.

It was in these circumstances that revelation descended, and the wish of the Messenger (ﷺ) was fulfilled:

﴿We have certainly seen the turning of your face towards the heaven. So We shall surely turn you to a qiblah that you will be pleased with. So turn your face towards the Sacred Mosque; and wherever you are, turn your faces towards it.﴾ (al-Baqarah: 144)

"O Prophet, We are seeing your face repeatedly turning towards the sky. Behold, We turn you towards the qiblah that you desire. Turn your face towards the Sacred Mosque. And wherever you are, turn your faces towards it in prayer."

It is narrated that this event occurred in the sixteenth or seventeenth month after the Hijrah. When the Muslims heard the news of the change of qiblah, some of them were in the state of prayer, and had already completed half of the prayer. In the middle of their prayer they turned their faces towards the Sacred Mosque, and completed the prayer facing the new qiblah. As soon as the qiblah was changed, the Jews raised the whole of Madinah on their heads, and began to clamour. The change of qiblah was grievous to them. Therefore, by engaging in disputes about the qiblah, they were creating doubts in the hearts of the Muslims about their religion. The change of qiblah was ending their argumentation, but now, in a different manner, their uproar began. They also changed direction, and now began to create doubts in the hearts of the Muslims in another way. They say to the Muslims: "If praying facing Bayt al-Maqdis was false, and you prayed facing it for a long time, then all those prayers of yours have been wasted. And if praying facing Bayt al-Maqdis was correct, then the change of qiblah is false, and all your prayers are being wasted. In any case, this change in the rulings and this abrogation of these verses is not a revelation from Allah."

The effects of this hostile Jewish assault were also felt within the Islamic camp. This is evident from the verses of the Qur'an that were revealed on this subject. In the first para the verse "Whatever verse We abrogate or cause to be forgotten..." (﴿مَا نَنسَخْ مِنْ آيَةٍ أَوْ نُنسِهَا﴾) and two full sections were revealed there, and the verses under discussion in the second para also relate to the same matter. In them, emphatic instructions are given concerning this disputation, clarifications are made, and the Muslims are warned. I shall speak about these issues at the time of explaining the texts.

At this appropriate place it seems fitting to say something about the change of qiblah and its wisdom. Why did the Muslims need a specific qiblah to be determined? This was in fact a significant turning point in the history of the Islamic movement. In the life of the movement, its great effects appeared.

The qiblah of the Muslims was initially the Ka'bah. After the Hijrah, for certain educational purposes, it was changed and Bayt al-Maqdis was appointed as the qiblah. This is indicated in this lesson's verse: "And We did not make the qiblah which you used to face except to know who follows the Messenger and who turns back on his heels." (al-Baqarah: 143)

"We appointed the qiblah which you used to face previously only in order to see who follows the Messenger and who turns back."

In truth, from the Age of Ignorance (jahiliyyah) onward, the Arabs had greatly revered the Sacred House, and regarded it as a symbol of their national pride. Since Islam wished to establish pure monotheism (khalis lillahiyyah), it wanted to remove from the hearts of the Muslims all attachments other than their connection with the Holy Lord, and to eradicate every slogan of ignorance and every feeling of partisanship apart from the Islamic worldview. It wished to establish a divine system whose connection is directly with Allah alone, free from all historical and tribal partisanship and from all the impurities of race and colour. Therefore the Muslims were commanded to abandon facing the Ka'bah in prayer, even though this command was for a short period only. They were commanded to turn their faces towards Bayt al-Maqdis, so that all the filth of ignorance might be completely removed from their hearts, and their souls purified of all the impurities of ignorance. This was so that it might become known who unconditionally obeys the Messenger of Allah, who is the very embodiment of submission and contentment, and who, with firm character and without any reservation, is obedient. It was also so that it might become known who, influenced by the concepts of ignorance, by national notions of race and colour, and by the slogans of history and homeland, turns back on his heels. Moreover, it was so that it might become known whether, in the most hidden corners of any Muslim's consciousness, or in the deepest layers of any worker's conscience, there is any admixture of falsehood, directly or indirectly.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 2, verse 142 (part 2 of 3):

When the Muslims submitted to this command, they turned joyfully towards the new qibla to which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had directed them. The Jews sought to take advantage of this situation and began to use it as an argument against the Islamic movement, and then the command of Allah arrived. The Muslims were commanded that they should now face the Masjid al-Haram and offer their prayers. Not only was the argument of the Jews brought to an end, but through this change the hearts of the believers became acquainted with another reality: the reality of Islam, and of Islamic history. The reality that the House of Allah (Bayt Allah) was built by Ibrahim (peace be upon him) exclusively for the worship of Allah, so that it would become the inheritance of the ummah that was to rise as a result of the supplications of Ibrahim (peace be upon him). Ibrahim (peace be upon him) prayed: "O Lord of the worlds, raise up from my offspring a Messenger who is upon this religion which was the religion of him and his sons and grandsons." As was mentioned in the first part: ﴿And when Ibrahim was tested by his Lord with certain words, and he fulfilled them﴾ (al-Baqarah: 124).
"Remember when Ibrahim was tested by his Lord with certain words and he fulfilled them."
Where the subject of discussion was the Masjid al-Haram, its foundation and construction, and the other circumstances and matters connected with these affairs, the discussion was also about Ibrahim (peace be upon him), his religion, his progeny, his qibla, his covenant and his testament, both with the People of the Book and with the polytheists. However, the verses mentioned in the first part were in reality a prelude to the present commands regarding the change of qibla, in which, after only a short interval, the qibla was changed from Bayt al-Maqdis to Bayt Allah. The Masjid al-Haram had been built by Ibrahim and Isma'il (peace be upon them both), and beside it both of them offered a lengthy supplication. Then the ummah of Muslims was raised upon the religion of Hanif, and it became the heir of the Covenant of Ibrahim. In these circumstances, the command to change the qibla from Bayt al-Maqdis to Bayt al-Haram was the natural and logical result of the situation. The command harmonised the outward practices of the Muslims with their historical consciousness, which history had already created in the hearts and minds of the ummah of Muslims.
Allah had emphatically enjoined upon Ibrahim (peace be upon him) that he and his progeny remain Muslims, and Ibrahim (peace be upon him) emphatically enjoined upon his children that they also remain steadfast upon the religion of Islam, just as Ya'qub (peace be upon him) (Israel) also gave the same charge to his children. Moreover, Ibrahim (peace be upon him) knew this reality as well: that the wrongdoers do not attain to the covenant of Allah. Since the command to construct the Bayt al-Haram was given to Ibrahim and Isma'il (peace be upon them both), it was therefore their inheritance. This inheritance was bound to pass only to those who were to inherit the religion of Ibrahim (peace be upon him). And since it was the ummah of Muslims who inherited this covenant and this grace of Allah, the natural outcome is that the House of Allah should also come to them, and that it should be the qibla of this ummah.
Indeed, for a brief period the Muslims offered their prayers facing the Masjid al-Aqsa, which was the qibla of the Jews and Christians, as is indicated by the context and the surrounding circumstances. This happened under a specific wisdom, which we have explained in detail. Now the will of Allah is that this inheritance be handed over to the ummah of Muslims.
By denying the religion of Islam, the People of the Book had themselves deprived themselves of the inheritance of Ibrahim. Therefore, in such circumstances, the command to change the qibla was founded on precise wisdom and was most appropriate. Accordingly, by the command of Allah, the House built by Ibrahim (peace be upon him) now became the qibla, so that the Muslims might inherit the whole of it, both outwardly and consciously: the religious inheritance, the inheritance of the qibla, and the inheritance of the grace and mercy of Allah.
For the Islamic movement it is necessary that it be distinct, singular and set apart: distinct in its concepts and beliefs, and distinct in its qibla and its acts of worship! The distinction of the qibla and of worship is as necessary as the distinction of concepts and ideologies.
The distinction of concepts and ideologies is generally understood, but the distinction of the qibla and of the outward symbols of religion is sometimes not understood, and therefore it is appropriate that something be said about the form and shape of the acts of worship as well.
The person who does not see the outward form of acts of worship in their true background, or who studies only the outward forms in worship apart from human psychology and impressions, when he sees people strictly observing the outward forms of worship, considers this act to be ascetic formalism, narrow-mindedness and dark thinking. But such a notion is not correct. When viewed from a broad perspective and with deep reflection, a different reality comes to light in every respect. For example:
The constitution of the human personality is made of the visible body and the hidden soul. Therefore man, in order to express his spiritual consciousness and hidden emotions, takes on an outward form. Inner feelings are not satisfied until they take on a tangible outward form. Only in this way is a complete expression of inner feelings and inclinations possible; in this way the expression of those inclinations is also fully realised in a perceptible manner, just as those inclinations exist in complete form within the human self. Thus the feelings find satisfaction, man becomes content, and the outward and inward aspects of the human personality come into harmony.
Thus the human self at one and the same time inclines towards the mysteries of the cosmos and the unknown realities, and on the other hand it obeys outward forms. Keeping these natural principles in view, Islam has determined the outward form of the acts of worship and symbols; therefore it is not possible to perform Islamic worship merely through intention, or spiritual attention, or concentration of thought. In Islamic worship, for intention, attention and concentration of thought to be realised, it is necessary that they take place in an outward form. For example: standing in prayer, facing the qibla, saying the takbir, reciting the tasbihat, bowing, and prostrating, and so on.
In Hajj: wearing the ihram from the prescribed days, wearing the prescribed garment, the prescribed movements, sa'i, supplication, talbiyah, sacrifice, and having the hair shaved or trimmed. And in fasting: intention, abstaining from eating and drinking, and abstaining from marital relations, all belong to this category. Behold, in every act of worship there is movement, and in movement there is worship. Thus the outward and inward aspects of human psychology have been brought into harmony. Harmony and order have been established among human faculties, and thus, in exact accordance with the demands of human nature, all the aims of the Islamic view of life have been achieved.
It was within Allah's knowledge that by nature man gives outward form to his inner concepts and feelings. Because of this natural inclination, many nations deviated from the straight path. Some people used outward symbols and signs to express the sense of greatness: stone idols were fashioned, trees and stones were worshipped, they bowed before the sun, the moon and the stars, and animals, birds and beasts were worshipped. When these people did not adopt a suitable method for expressing their inner feelings and beliefs, one that would have been in accordance with human nature, then in these circumstances, in accordance with the will of Allah, the Islamic call arose, and it adopted the natural method for expressing beliefs and feelings, which is seen in the determination of the outward form of Islamic worship. Islam adopted such methods for the worship of Allah and devised such forms for it, in which not even a trace of the notion of corporeality with regard to the Divine Being is present. In it no direction or side of the Divine Being is determined. According to the Islamic method of worship, when a person fully turns towards the Lord, he faces the qibla, but his heart, his senses and his limbs are directed towards Allah alone, even though his outward face is turned in the direction of a building.
The question is: then why was a single place specified? The need arose so that a Muslim might acquire a distinctive form compared with other people, and so that in prayer and other acts of worship he would be recognised by one specific qibla or direction. This determination was in reality a requirement of the intellectual and practical foundation of distinction and individuality. History bears witness that this determination and specification gave the Muslims an identity; otherwise Allah has no relation to any direction or side.
It was this very motive that led to the command that Muslims should not adopt the particular symbols and particular manifestations of other religions and peoples: those symbols which they have devised to express their inner concepts and beliefs, or thoughts and feelings. Muslims have also been told that in their thought and action they should not adopt the manners and customs of non-Muslims. This command was not given merely out of prejudice or narrow-mindedness or asceticism, but rather Islam had in view a profound and wise outlook beyond outward form. Behind outward forms there were hidden certain causes and wisdoms. These were the very reasons on account of which one nation separates from another, one understanding differs from another understanding, one ideology is distinguished from another ideology, one conscience is set apart from another conscience, the morals of one person differ from the morals of another person, and on the roads of life the paths of two individuals diverge in different directions.
Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him) reports: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Jews and the Christians do not dye (their hair), so you should act in opposition to them." (Imam Muslim, Bukhari, Abu Dawud)
Once the Prophet (ﷺ) went to some people who stood up out of respect for him. He (ﷺ) said: "Do not stand up like the non-Arabs, some of whom honour others in this way." (Abu Dawud, Ibn Majah)
On one occasion the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Do not exaggerate my praise as the Christians exaggerated the praise of the son of Maryam. I am only a servant of Allah."
In short, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade resemblance to non-Muslims in outward appearance and dress. Imitation of the non-believers in movements, habits and manners was also forbidden. Imitation in speech and action was forbidden. This is because behind such outward form lie in reality those concepts on the basis of which one way of life differs from another way of life, one system differs from another system, and the emblem of one nation differs from the emblems of other nations.
The Muslim ummah has been raised so that it may establish the Islamic system in the world. Therefore Muslims were strictly forbidden to take guidance from any system other than Allah and the Islamic system of life. They were commanded that they should never accept intellectual defeat before any other nation on the face of the earth. If they do so, then this very defeat will compel them to imitate that nation and its civilisation. The Muslim ummah has been established so that other nations may follow it, and that it may take up leadership.
Therefore it should derive its ideas and its ways only from that source and fountainhead which has granted this ummah the rank of leadership. In the sight of Allah, Muslims alone are exalted and superior; they are the ummah of the middle way; they are the best ummah, raised for the leadership and the good of mankind. Then from what source should their ideology and their practice be drawn? From where should they derive their manners and their principles of discipline? Should they abandon Allah and accept as the fountainhead of guidance and right direction those most abject nations, whom Allah Himself raised the Muslims to lift out of the abyss of degradation?

Islam introduced all of humanity to a lofty conception of life; it gave humankind a lofty system of living. Therefore it calls the whole of humanity to embrace this lofty conception of life and this lofty system of living. If Islam, in comparison with other systems and ideologies, wishes to unite humanity upon the foundation of its presented lofty system of life and sublime view of life, this desire is not based on any prejudice. Rather, Islam is the advocate of the Oneness of Allah. It wishes to establish unity upon a lofty ideology; it wishes to unite the whole of humanity at a lofty station. Therefore it does not take part in any union in which the revealed ideology of life of Islam has been abandoned. It does not take part in any union whose foundation has been laid upon ignorance (jahiliyyah), and certainly this is not prejudice. Is this prejudice? If it is, then it is the prejudice of the struggle made for goodness, truth and the reform of circumstances, and I would sacrifice myself for such prejudice!

The Islamic movement should well fix in its mind this reality: why does it face a particular qibla when it prays? The qibla is not merely a building towards which Muslims turn at the time of prayer. The building and the direction are only a sign. In reality this is a sign of distinction and particularity; and it is a distinction of ideology, a distinction of identity, a distinction of aim, a distinction of priorities, and a distinction of the constituent elements of the ummah.

At this time the world is filled with jahili concepts, and Muslims stand in the midst of this world. There are countless aims based on jahiliyyah that people have adopted. There are countless jahili priorities that have taken possession of human hearts and minds. There are countless banners of jahiliyyah that various people have raised. Therefore the need of today is that the Muslim ummah establish its own separate identity, one that is not confused with the identities currently in vogue. It should determine a distinct ideology and a unique philosophy for its own existence, which differs from jahili concepts and jahili philosophies. It should set for itself such an aim and determine for itself such priorities as are in harmony with its own particular personality and its view of life. It should raise a distinct banner that is founded solely upon devotion to Allah (lillahiyyah). Its hallmark should be that it is the ummah of the middle way, the middle ummah which Allah has raised for the betterment of humankind. Why? Because it is transmitting to people that ideological inheritance of which it is the trustee.

This belief is a complete system of life. This community is its heir and trustee. It holds the office of God's vicegerency (khilafah) on earth, and this is its distinguishing mark. This community will be a witness over people, and among its duties is to lead the whole of humanity. Where? Towards Allah and towards the establishment of the Islamic system. In short, the establishment of Islamic life is its distinctive characteristic, and its identity is formed through it. The constituent elements of its existence, the distinction of its personality, its aims, its priorities, its knowledge and its emblems all depend upon its beliefs. It is this outlook that grants it the station of leadership. It is for the sake of this outlook that it was created. Apart from this outlook, whatever garment it wears, whatever movement it starts, whatever banner it raises, it will not attain distinction; it will be swept away in the flood of jahili (ignorant) movements, and its features will always remain indistinct. Having shed light on the philosophy and wisdom of the Islamic movement, we now turn to the explanation of the verses.

From the context of the Qur'an and the events that took place in Madinah, it is known that the "foolish ones" (al-sufahaa') here refers to the Jews. It was they who raised an uproar at the time of the change of the qiblah. It was they who raised this question: "What has turned them away from the qiblah to which they used to face?" (maa wallahum 'an qiblatihimu allati kanu 'alayha), i.e., why did they suddenly turn away from the qiblah they had previously faced in prayer? The qiblah they used to face was Bayt al-Maqdis.

It is narrated from Hadrat al-Bara' ibn 'Azib (raḍiyallāhu 'anhu), who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to Madinah, he alighted among the Ansar, among his maternal relatives, and he prayed facing Masjid al-Aqsa for sixteen or seventeen months. But in his heart he would like it if the qiblah were to become the Ka'bah. One day, at the time of the 'Asr prayer, the qiblah was changed by Divine revelation, and he prayed the 'Asr prayer facing the Ka'bah. The people also changed the qiblah along with him. Then a man who had prayed and come out saw people in another mosque bowing in ruku', and he said: "I bear witness that I have just prayed behind the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and we faced the Ka'bah." So those people turned towards the Ka'bah in the very state of ruku'. (Narrated by Imam Malik; Muslim, Bukhari and Tirmidhi.)

The Jews were very pleased that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed facing their qiblah, Bayt al-Maqdis, but when the qiblah was changed, they felt it very grievously. Upon this, this verse was revealed: "We see the turning of your face towards the sky" (qad nara taqallaba wajhika fi al-sama'), O Prophet (ﷺ), we observe the repeated lifting of your face towards the sky.

On this, the fools, that is the Jews, said: "What has happened to them that they turned away suddenly from the qiblah towards which they used to face in prayer?"

From looking at the verses that follow, it will be seen that the Qur'an gave detailed answers to the questions and objections of these people, because the effects of their propaganda were also affecting the hearts and minds of the Muslims. This is well understood from the Qur'an's manner of expression.

"The foolish among the people will surely say: What has turned them away from the qiblah to which they used to face?" (sayaqulu al-sufaha' min al-nas ma wallahum 'an qiblatihimu allati kanu 'alayha). "Say: To Allah belong the east and the west; He guides whom He wills to a straight path."

These verses in fact serve as a preface to the verses on the change of the qiblah that follow. The matter is being conducted in the form of question and answer. Allah knew that the hostile people would raise such questions, so by way of forestalling them He answered in advance. Or the actual situation was that the command to change the qiblah was the Prophet's own (as mentioned in the hadith), and the opponents had also begun a barrage of questions, but Allah, by adopting the future tense, indicated that what they were saying was in accordance with their own plan. Their scheme was not a hidden one, so its answer was also prepared in advance. For refutational purposes, this manner of expression is extremely effective. It is said: "People will say such things," although they have already said them.

The Qur'an tells the Prophet (ﷺ) the answers to the opponents' questions in advance, so that whenever they raise them the Muslims may respond, and thus the Islamic movement is given a correct point of view in this matter in advance. "Say: To Allah belong the east and the west; He guides whom He wills to a straight path."

East and west all belong to Allah; wherever I look, there is only Him. No direction or place has any virtue of its own. However, when Allah prescribes a direction or a place, or chooses a place Himself, then it gains virtue through this. It is Allah who puts whom He wills on the straight path. If He selects a direction for His servants, or designates a place as their qiblah, then that place becomes distinguished and honoured, because Allah's command has become attached to it; thus the straight path passes through that direction, and all other directions become crooked.

In this single phrase, the Islamic viewpoint regarding place and direction is presented. The source of guidance for mankind is indicated. Thus a correct point of view emerges: that in every condition, at every turn of life, one should turn one's attention to the Divine Being.

Now the discourse turns to the Muslim Ummah. It is told what lofty station it holds in this universe, what duties it has to fulfil on this earth, what excellence and superiority it has among humanity, and what role it must play in people's lives. This station and rank require that it have a single, distinctive qiblah and that it possess a distinct identity. Set aside other matters and listen to the words of the Great Lord who chose this Ummah for a mighty mission:

﴿Thus We have made you a middle nation, that you may be witnesses over the people, and the Messenger may be a witness over you.﴾

This is the middle Ummah. It is a witness over the people. It is its duty to establish justice and equity among people, to determine for them the standard of truth and the values of life, and to give them an opinion that becomes public opinion, upon which people rely. It should carefully examine the values, beliefs, customs and national symbols of all the peoples of the world and pronounce its judgment: "This is truth, and this is falsehood!" It is not an Ummah that takes its ideas, values and standards of beauty and ugliness from other nations. It is a witness over people and holds the position of a judge and arbiter. Just as it is a witness over people, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is a witness over it. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ will prescribe for this Ummah the values of life and the standard of truth; he will pass judgment on its deeds and customs; and the final decision regarding its actions and words will be his. From this, the reality of this Ummah and its duties become known. It should become thoroughly acquainted with its own reality, know its importance and worth, correctly define its position and role in this world, and fully prepare itself to discharge it—that is, it should be the standard of truth for people, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ should be its standard of truth.

This Ummah is the middle Ummah. In every sense of "middle" it is the middle: if "middle" means the best and most excellent, it is still the middle; if "middle" means moderation and balance, it is still the middle; if "middle" is taken in the material and sensory sense, it is still the middle Ummah.

The "middle Ummah" is moderate in beliefs and ideologies—neither drowned in spiritual asceticism nor captured by materialism, but adhering to the principles of nature. For example, what is the human body? It is matter, and the soul has been embedded in the material body, or the material body has been united with the soul. This Ummah gives full right to this human being composed of these elements—indeed, to each of its constituent elements. It works both for the growth and perfection of spiritual life and, by fulfilling human material needs, also works to sustain this material life. This Ummah establishes a broad sphere for human freedom of thought, freedom of expression, and the satisfaction of personal taste and inclination, without excess or deficiency, with moderation, harmony and balance, and grants the person full freedom within that sphere.

This Ummah is the middle, also in the realm of thought and consciousness. It does not sit content and frozen with the existing store of knowledge, nor does it close the doors of knowledge, insight, experience and research; yet it does not follow every slogan-monger without thinking, nor does it imitate everyone like a monkey. It becomes the guardian of its beliefs, principles and system of thought and action, holding them firmly, yet it keeps a sharp eye on the thoughts and experiences of all humanity. Its settled policy is: "The wisdom of the believer is his lost property; wherever he finds it, he takes it up"—but with steadfastness, consistency and conviction.

It is also the middle Ummah in discipline and order. It does not leave the human being in the arena of life so free that there is no external check other than conscience and consciousness; nor does it leave him entirely at the mercy of rigid legal constraint and compulsory reform. Rather, on the one hand, it awakens conscience and consciousness through guidance and reform and creates the awareness of goodness in society; on the other hand, it also employs the legal system and the means of penal discipline and organizes society. Indeed, it advocates a beautiful blend between guidance and right-guidance and the law of punishment. It neither surrenders the person solely to the coercion of law nor leaves him so free.

This Ummah is the middle Ummah. It is the middle in relationships and connections too. It considers the individual existence of the person to be a reality, and therefore does not ignore it altogether so as to let the personality of the individual be completely lost in the personality of the group or state. Nor does it leave him so free that he suddenly becomes self-willed and nothing remains before him except his own self. It leaves free those personal tendencies and personal powers of the individual through which movement and activity arise in society and it progresses. It grants freedom to those tendencies and qualities by which the individual's self and personality are formed.

After this, it deliberately imposes such restrictions as regulate excess and extremes and deficiency. Generally, it encourages those activities which create the spirit of service to humanity, but then it also adopts legal measures through which the individual becomes the servant of the community, and the state and community become the guardians of the individual; and the middle Ummah carries out this task with great harmony and in the most appropriate manner.

From the standpoint of geography, too, this Ummah is the middle. It dwells in the center of the earth. At the center of the inhabited region of the globe, where this Ummah is settled on the surface of the earth, it lies in the exact middle of north and south and east and west. It is a witness over human beings, and all humanity is a witness over it. Whatever it possesses, it gives to all the inhabitants of the earth, and through this Ummah the material treasures and spiritual treasures of nature reach the whole human population. It rules and holds authority at this lofty and important position, and all the material and spiritual movements of the world appear under its influence.

After place, if we look from the perspective of time, this too is the middle Ummah. By the time humanity's childhood ends, it is this Ummah that comes. From this Ummah begins the era of maturity of intellect and wisdom. Along with humanity's childhood, the pollution of superstitions and myths had been following it. This middle Ummah, standing in the middle of the stages of human history, is shaking it off. And even in that age of maturity, it protects humanity from the trial of arrogance and intellectual deviation. It has created a beautiful harmony between the divine guidance and teachings of the age of the prophets and the scientific discoveries of the modern age of reason and wisdom, and it is seen leading all humanity along the straight path in the very middle, always remaining at the point of balance.

This was the station that Allah, the Exalted, once bestowed upon this Ummah. Can it not regain it? Certainly it can regain it. There is no obstacle in its path. But the matter is that this Ummah has abandoned the system of life that Allah had chosen for it, and in its place has adopted other systems of life that Allah did not choose for it. This Ummah has taken on other colors and hues, none of which is ṣibghat Allah (the color of Allah). Yet Allah's will was that the Ummah should be dyed in the pure color of Allah.

This is the Ummah, this is its mission, and this is its role. It is worthy of undertaking these responsibilities and of making sacrifices on this path. For the station of leadership there are responsibilities and duties; before attaining the station of leadership, trials are necessary, so that it may become evident how sincere and steadfast the Ummah is towards Allah, and to what extent it is ready to bear the responsibilities of a righteous leadership.

The command for the change of qiblah was issued, and at this occasion it was also made clear why the Muslims had been commanded to turn toward Masjid al-Aqsa while praying:

﴿And We did not make the qiblah which you used to face except that We might know who follows the Messenger from who turns back on his heels.﴾

From this verse, the plan that Allah, the Exalted, devised for the religious training of this newly formed community becomes clearly known. Allah's will was that the Islamic community would become the inheritor and trustee of the ideology and would attain the station of vicegerency on earth (khilafat fil-ard). Allah's will was that the Ummah should work purely for this ideology of life, and that it should purify its heart and mind from the influence of all jahili (pre-Islamic ignorance-based) conceptions. It should abandon all ancient customs and national peculiarities; extinguish every smoldering spark of jahiliyyah; cast off every garment of jahiliyyah; and give up every symbol of jahiliyyah. Its consciousness should contain only the Islamic authority—pure Islamic symbols, free from every admixture. The source of its guidance and right-guidance should be one and only one; no other source should share in it.

Regarding turning toward the House of Allah (the Kaaba) in prayer, there were other tendencies besides the ideological inclination. The pure Islamic ideology of Abraham (peace be upon him), the forefather of the Quraysh, had not remained pure among them. Various kinds of shirk had entered it, and tribal fanaticism had also become part of their religion. At that time the House of Allah was regarded only as a sacred place of the Arabs, while Allah's will was that it should be a sacred place of Allah rather than of the Arabs, and that it should have no attribution other than the attribution to Allah; this place should be purely a divine symbol, with no other connection attached to it.

Since the Kaaba was bound up with the historical sentiments of the Arabs and their national inclinations too, Allah the Exalted ordered for a short period that the qiblah of the Muslims would be Masjid al-Aqsa instead of the Kaaba, so that the roots of historical and national inclinations regarding the Kaaba would be cut from the hearts of the Arabs. Then it would also become known who among the Muslims obeys the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and who does not. Those who obey the Messenger ﷺ merely because he is the Messenger of God would be separated from those who obey him because he is an Arab and regard the Kaaba as their qiblah and kaaba, and because the sentiments of respect for their national consciousness and their ancient sacred places are given importance in Islam too, and because the means of satisfying their historical inclinations are also present in Islam—and it is surely for this reason that they are Muslims.

This is an extremely subtle and profound point. The Islamic ideology of life is absolutely unique, and when it settles in a heart, it does not tolerate any other partner in that heart. It eliminates all other symbols and qualities apart from its own symbols and qualities. The Islamic ideology of life uproots all jahili customs and practices, whether great or small. This verse points to this:

﴿And We did not make the qiblah which you used to face except that We might know who follows the Messenger from who turns back on his heels.﴾

Allah already knows future events before they occur, but the will of Allah is that the event which is to happen should become manifest to people, and after that accountability should be taken and punishment given. Out of His mercy, He does not punish merely on the basis of His knowledge of the future; He punishes only for those matters which take place and which are actually committed by the offender.

It was known to Allah that abandoning all historical and national conscious tendencies at once, and giving up qualities and symbols that are deeply attached to heart and soul and are steeped in the mind and consciousness, is an extremely difficult task; the uprooting of them is extremely burdensome. This can happen only when faith has fully overtaken the heart and mind, and then that heart receives divine help and attains nearness to the Divine Being. The Divine Being takes it to Himself and guides it:

﴿And indeed it was difficult, except for those whom Allah has guided.﴾

Since they had received divine guidance, for them it was no difficult task to remove jahili conceptions from their hearts and minds; and upon receiving guidance they cast aside all the traces of jahiliyyah. This Ummah became the Ummah of Allah; obedience and submission became its symbol, and the condition became such that Allah could turn it in whatever direction He wished, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ could lead it wherever he wished.

Now the Muslims are reassured regarding their faith and their prayer, that they are walking on the path of guidance. Therefore their prayers cannot be wasted. Allah never wrongs His servants. Whatever worship they perform, He does not waste it, and He does not impose upon them a burden beyond their capacity—although this capacity becomes stronger through faith, indeed it becomes multiplied:

﴿And Allah would not have let your faith be lost. Indeed, Allah is to the people Kind and Merciful.﴾

He knows well the strength of human beings and their capacity to endure. Therefore He does not issue any command that lies beyond the bounds of their strength. He guides mankind, and if their intention is sound and their resolve firm, He Himself helps them in every trial, so that they emerge successfully from that test. If trials and tests are a manifestation of His wisdom, then succeeding in the trial is His grace and bounty: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Kind and Merciful to mankind﴾ [2:143]. Know well that He is compassionate and merciful towards you.

Thus Allah pours the cup of inner tranquility into the hearts of the Muslims. Their unease is removed, and in their hearts there arises a firm awareness and certainty of the good pleasure of Allah.

Now it is announced that the desire of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) regarding the qiblah has been fulfilled. The change of the qiblah is proclaimed, but at the same time the Muslims are also made aware of the mischief-making of the Jews. The factors and motives that operate behind that mischief and the continuous conspiracies are also unveiled. All of this is presented in a manner that the Islamic movement may gain correct knowledge of this great struggle, which Allah is conducting for its organisation and training, and which is undertaken on its behalf to protect it from the mischief and clamour of its opponents.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 2, verse 144:

For every people there is a direction toward which they turn. So race towards good deeds; wherever you are, Allah will bring you all together. Nothing is beyond His power. Wherever you set out from, turn your face (in prayer) toward the Sacred Mosque, for this is the absolute truth from your Lord. And Allah is not unaware of what you do. And from wherever you set out, turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque, and wherever you are, face it when you pray, so that people will have no argument against you. Only those among them who are wrongdoers will continue their objections, so do not fear them, but fear Me, and so that I may complete My favour upon you and that you may be guided to the right path.

At the beginning of these verses, the state of the Prophet ﷺ was portrayed in these words: "قَدْ نَرَى تَقَلُّبَ وَجْهِكَ فِي السَّمَاءِ" — "O Messenger, We see your face turning repeatedly toward the sky."

This expresses the intense desire that the Prophet ﷺ held regarding the change of the qiblah. Compelled by the Jews, their obstinacy and their disputations, he began to wish that the existing qiblah of the Muslims would be changed. Since the Muslims were praying facing the qiblah of the Jews, and the Jews had attempted to use this through false propaganda, clamour and an effort to mislead the Muslims, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, under his heartfelt desire, would repeatedly lift his face toward the sky; out of respect and reverence, he would not express anything, fearing how he could present a proposal in the presence of the Lord, or bring forward any matter on his own before Allah, lest it be displeasing to Allah. But Allah fulfilled his wish, and the words in which this wish was fulfilled show that Allah desired the pleasure of His beloved.

"فَلَنُوَلِّيَنَّكَ قِبْلَةً تَرْضَاهَا" — "Indeed, We shall turn you to a qiblah that you like."

Now the qiblah is determined, the one which Allah knew his own wish also lay in: "فَوَلِّ وَجْهَكَ شَطْرَ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ" — "Turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque."

Now this is your qiblah, the qiblah of your ummah. For those who are present with you and for those who are yet to come, it is the qiblah until the Day of Resurrection, until the time when the earth and its inhabitants are finally presented before Allah: "وَحَيْثُمَا كُنْتُمْ فَوَلُّوا وُجُوهَكُمْ شَطْرَهُ" — "Wherever you are, turn your faces toward it in prayer."

From every direction, from all corners and sides of the earth, there is now one qiblah, and every individual of the ummah will face toward it wherever he may live, whatever his homeland, however distant his location. Even if their colours differ, their languages are various and their nationalities are separate, there will be one qiblah. Whether the ummah of Muslims is in the east or the west, it faces that same direction. Thus a sense arises in this ummah that it is one body and one soul, striving with one aim before it, for the establishment of one system of life, which grants it one concept, one Messenger ﷺ and one qiblah.

Thus Allah joined this ummah together: one Allah, one Messenger, one religion and one qiblah. Despite differences of nationhood, homelands, languages and colours, one ummah; all principles of race, lineage and homeland were set aside, and the foundation of the unity of the ummah was placed upon the Islamic ideology of life and the unity of the qiblah. The truth is that this unity alone is worthy of the children of Adam, because human beings unite upon creed and ideology; they unite upon one mode of worship and one qiblah of worship, whereas the gathering of animals is based upon fodder, pasture and pen.

Now the topic is: "People of the Book and the new qiblah. وَإِنَّ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ لَيَعْلَمُونَ أَنَّهُ الْحَقُّ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ" — "Those who were given the Book know well that this command for changing the qiblah comes from their Lord and is the truth."

It is precisely within their knowledge that the one who raised the foundations of the House of Allah, that is the Sacred Mosque, was Prophet Ibrahim (peace be upon him), the forefather of this ummah who became the inheritor of this mission, indeed the forefather of all Muslims. They also clearly know that the command of the new qiblah too came from Allah, and there is no doubt about it; yet, in accordance with their hereditary habit, they will adopt an attitude directly contrary to this knowledge and conviction, purely out of enmity and hostility toward the Muslims. But Allah is their protector; He is the Guardian who will destroy every plot of theirs: "وَمَا اللَّهُ بِغَافِلٍ عَمَّا يَعْمَلُونَ" — "And Allah is not unaware of what they do."

They can never be satisfied by any proof. Their understanding of proof is not lacking; what is lacking among them is sincerity. They are slaves of their desires, and despite having knowledge, they lack the capacity to accept truth and reality: "Even if you brought the People of the Book every sign, they would not follow your qiblah" (Q. 2:145). "Whatever proof you present to the People of the Book, they will never follow your qiblah."

Their reins are in the hand of their desires. Worldly interests drive them along, and personal aims serve as their camel-drivers' songs (hida' khwan). Among the sincere, countless people still think that the Jews and Christians do not accept Islam because they lack correct knowledge of Islam, or because Islam has not been presented to them in a satisfactory manner. The reality is that this is merely an illusion. They do not accept Islam precisely because they have correct and full knowledge of it! And they know that Islam is entirely contrary to their interests. They know that in it there is no place for their leadership and dominance. This is the reason they continue, constantly and without cease, to plot against Islam, through various methods and by various means, both directly and indirectly. They are at war against Islam, both openly and behind the scenes. They fight against Islam themselves and also incite and stir others to fight against it. In every form, they do this work. What Allah Ta'ala said to the Prophet (ﷺ) applies to them at all times: "Even if you brought the People of the Book every sign, they would not follow your qiblah" (Q. 2:145).

The condition of the People of the Book is that they continually turn away from the qiblah of the Muslims and the Islamic system of life, the indications of which are clearly visible in that qiblah. But the question is: in contrast to their position, what is the stance of the Prophet (ﷺ) and of those who have embraced Islam? "And you are not one who will follow their qiblah" (Q. 2:145). Naturally, this is the correct position.

That is, it is contrary to the dignity of the Prophet (ﷺ) that he should in any way follow their qiblah. Here the Qur'an has adopted this mode of expression: "And you are not one who will follow their qiblah," that is, a nominal negative sentence (jumlah ismiyyah manfiyyah), and not "You do not follow their qiblah," because through the first phrase the lasting dignity of the Messenger (ﷺ) and his steadfast adherence to his position in this matter are well expressed, and after him the community of Muslims also receives a clear indication that it must never abandon the qiblah adopted by its Messenger. Allah Ta'ala has chosen this decision for you out of regard for His Messenger's desire and consolation. He should not raise any banner other than this divine banner, and should not follow any system other than the Islamic system of life, to which the indications in the change of qiblah point. As long as that community is the community of Muslims, it should adopt this very course of conduct. If it does not do so, then it will have no connection or relationship with Islam; its Islam will remain merely a claim to Islam.

In connection with the change of qiblah, it is explained that even among the People of the Book themselves there was already sharp disagreement concerning the qiblah. They too are not united, because their desires are also divergent: "And no group among them will follow the qiblah of another group" (Q. 2:145).

There is enmity between the Jews and Christians, and various Jewish sects are also opposed to one another. Then the various Christian sects are also at war with one another.

When the People of the Book harbor this enmity toward the Messenger (ﷺ), and truth has already been sent down to him from Allah, then how can it be right for you (ﷺ) to follow their desires after knowledge has come to you from Allah? "And if you were to follow their desires after the knowledge that has come to you, then indeed you would be among the wrongdoers" (Q. 2:145).

Previously the manner of speech was very gentle and compassionate, but here, in address to the Prophet (ﷺ), the divine address suddenly becomes somewhat severe, and a definite seriousness arises in the style. Why? Because now the matter concerns action and steadfastness; the matter is one of acting upon the guidance. Therefore a warning is given in plain words: "Indeed you would then be among the wrongdoers" (Q. 2:145).

The path is clear; the straight way is before you. Knowledge is that which comes from Allah; from other sources, only desire is obtained. It is the duty of the Muslim to acquire certain knowledge, and not to abandon real knowledge in favor of changeable and doubtful sources based on base desires. There is no doubt that knowledge not based on revelation can be nothing but mere desire.

Here it seems necessary to clarify that, as a result of the organized propaganda and misleading whisperings of the Jews, the mental condition of some Muslims in Madinah had become such that they needed this kind of definite expression. It was appropriate to warn them; a manner of reproof and rebuke was appropriate.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 2, verse 146:

After this brief address to the Muslims, the discourse returns once more to its main subject. The point is that the People of the Book certainly know that the truth is what the Qur'an states and what the Messenger ﷺ commands. Yet despite this certain knowledge, they conceal that truth. Why? Because they are not worshippers of Allah but worshippers of their own desires (nafs)!

﴿Those to whom We gave the Book recognise it as they recognise their own sons. But indeed a party of them conceal the truth while they know it.﴾

﴿Those to whom We gave the Book recognise it (the place that has been made the qiblah) just as they recognise their own sons. But a group among them knowingly conceals the truth.﴾

Recognising one's own children is the highest example of knowledge and certain recognition. In Arabic, this comparison is used for a matter or event that is certain, about which there is no doubt or uncertainty in one's knowledge. The condition of the People of the Book is that the certain knowledge of the truth has already reached them. The command regarding the change of qiblah is also a part of this universal truth, and yet they conceal the truth which they hold as certain knowledge. Therefore, the correct course of action for the believers is that they should never be influenced by the lies and fabrications of the Jews. It is by no means fitting for them to accept anything from those Jews who know the reality and yet conceal it. They themselves deny even that part of their own religion which the Messenger of the Muslims, the trustworthy one of revelation, presents in the form of revelation, merely out of prejudice.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 2, verse 147:

After the discussion concerning the People of the Book, the address now turns to the person of the Prophet ﷺ: ﴿The truth is from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters.﴾ This is a decisive truth that comes from your Lord, so do not fall into any doubt about it whatsoever.

Did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ever doubt? No, never. In another verse, when it was said: ﴿If you are in doubt about what We have sent down to you, then ask those who have been reading the Scripture before you.﴾ That is, if you have any doubt about the word We have revealed to you, then ask those who have been reading the Book before you.

On this, the Prophet ﷺ said: "I have no doubt, nor do I ask them."

Then why was the Messenger of Allah ﷺ addressed personally? The purpose was to draw the attention of the Muslims, whether those Muslims who were present with him and were being influenced by the superstitions of the Jews, or those who would come later and could be influenced in religious matters by the falsehoods and lies of the Jews.

I would say that today the Muslims should heed this warning. Today we are afflicted with an ignorance for which there is no parallel. We seek guidance and fatwas in our religious matters from Jews, Christians and atheist Communists. We read our own history from them. We rely on them to speak about our heritage. Whatever doubts they raise about our Qur'an, the Sunnah of our Prophet ﷺ and his biography, we listen to them with complete satisfaction. We send our students to them so that they may acquire Islamic teachings from them, and they return from their universities with their intellect and conscience corrupted, yet are called scholars.

Remember! This Qur'an is for us the Book of Shari'ah. It is the Book of the entire Muslim Ummah. It is the lasting Book of the Ummah, in which it has been shown the path of action and warned against the path of wickedness. In contrast, the People of the Book remain the People of the Book, and the disbelievers remain disbelievers. Their religion is their religion, and our religion is our religion!

The discussion now returns to the main subject. The believers are commanded not to pay any attention to the words of the People of the Book. They should not accept their guidance or direction, and should continue steadfastly along their own way of life and their own outlook. Every group has its own direction of movement. The direction of the Muslims is towards righteousness and goodness. They should not cast their eyes upon anything else, and should keep moving forward. In the end they have to appear before the Lord of the Day of Resurrection, who is fully capable of gathering them together. He is able to give everyone recompense for their deeds there:

﴿And every one has a direction towards which he turns. So compete with one another in good deeds. Wherever you may be, Allah will bring you all together. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.﴾ Each has a direction to which he turns; so race to good deeds. Wherever you are, Allah will bring you all together. Indeed Allah has power over all things. Nothing lies beyond His power.

The mischief that the People of the Book spread, the plots they hatched, and the distortions and misinterpretations they made of the word of Allah are here. The believers are commanded to take no interest at all in these activities of the People of the Book. They should set out on the path of action and vie with one another in the work of goodness. Along with this, they are reminded that in the end they must come before Allah, the Most High. He has power over everything. No task is difficult for Him, and nothing can remain hidden from His sight. This is the truth in comparison with which all sayings and conditions are false, and which have no reality at all.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 2, verse 149:

Then the matter of the change of the qibla is repeated, and a emphatic command is given that people should turn towards the new qibla (qiblah) while praying, the one that Allah has chosen. On this occasion some new definitions are formed and some conclusions are drawn.

﴿And from wherever you set out, turn your face towards the Sacred Mosque; and indeed it is the truth from your Lord. And Allah is not unaware of what you do.﴾ "Wherever you go out from, turn your face in prayer towards the Sacred Mosque. Indeed, it is the truth from your Lord, and Allah is not unaware of what you do."

This emphatic command does not mention the Jews, nor does it mention their position regarding the qibla. It has been said that the Prophet (ﷺ), wherever he is and wherever his travels take him, should turn towards the House of Allah during prayer, because this is the true decision of his Lord. Implicitly, it was also said: lest you turn away from this truth. The words of the Qur'an, "And Allah is not unaware of what you do," clearly point to this. These words reveal the reality that indeed some Muslims had doubts in their hearts, and such a situation existed that Allah had to repeatedly emphasize the command and also issue a severe warning.

The third time, the instruction about the qibla is emphasized again for a fresh purpose. The Muslims were praying facing the qibla of the Jews, and the Jews and others argued from this that their religion was superior to the religion of the Muslims, since their qibla was the original one, and therefore this was proof that their way of life was also the original one. So by further emphasizing the command to change the qibla, this argument was ended forever. (On the other hand, the polytheists of Arabia regarded the Sacred House (Bayt al-Haram) as a holy place and showed it great reverence. They too objected to Bayt al-Maqdis being the qibla, saying that the Muslims were followers of the Jews: they had abandoned their own sacred place and were praying facing the qibla of the Children of Israel.

﴿And from wherever you go out, turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque; and wherever you are, turn your faces toward it, so that people will have no argument against you, except those of them who are wrongdoers. So do not fear them, but fear Me, and that I may complete My favor upon you and that you may be guided.﴾ "And wherever you go out, turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque, and wherever you are, turn your face toward it in prayer, so that people will have no argument against you. Except for those among them who are wrongdoers; so do not fear them, but fear Me, so that I may complete My favor upon you and that you may be guided to the path of guidance and success."

The Messenger ﷺ was commanded that wherever he went, he should face the Sacred Mosque in prayer, and the Muslims were commanded that wherever they were, they should turn their faces toward the House of Allah in prayer.

It was said: ﴿لِئَلا يَكُونَ لِلنَّاسِ عَلَيْكُمْ حُجَّةٌ﴾ "So that people will not have an argument against you." The wrongdoers will keep on making their claims; they do not yield to any proof or argument. The instruction is that such people be disregarded. These people are obstinate and afflicted with enmity. Such people cannot be satisfied in any way; they will continue their wrangling. The Muslims should ﴿فَلا تَخْشَوْهُمْ وَاخْشَوْنِي﴾ "not fear them, but fear Me."

They have no authority over you; the reins of your affairs are not in their hands. It does not befit you that out of fear of them you abandon the commands sent down to you from Me. Only I am worthy of fear and awe, because all the affairs of your world and the Hereafter are in My hands.

The wrongdoers are disregarded. The Muslims are warned of Allah's seizure, and the Muslims are reminded of Allah's blessings and favors. It is said that if you maintain a correct attitude and obey the commands of Allah, the result will be a rain of further blessings: ﴿وَلأتِمَّ نِعْمَتِي عَلَيْكُمْ وَلَعَلَّكُمْ تَهْتَدُونَ﴾ "So that I may complete My favor upon you, and that you may be guided to the right path."

In short, this is a reminder containing a particular hint, an increasing encouragement, and a repeated pointing to Allah's grace and kindness.

What is that blessing? It lies in their own hands; their own hearts and minds bear witness to what it is. It is present throughout their whole lives. They find it in their stance and in their society. They also find this blessing in the position they have assigned for themselves in this universe.

They had lived in the ignorance and darkness of jahiliyyah; they had seen the darkness of jahiliyyah with their own eyes. After that, they themselves embraced the light of faith, adopted purity and cleanliness, and adopted knowledge and recognition. Therefore they find the effect of this blessing in their hearts and minds at all times: fresh, deep, and clear.

They had lived a shortsighted tribal life, and for base aims they had spent years in bloodshed and slaughter. Then, of their own will, they gathered under the banner of a worldview and became a force and a power. Their aims became lofty and their priorities broadened. Their outlook rose above the narrow circle of families and tribes and came to rest on the foundations of all humanity, and it expanded. Therefore they hold a broad awareness of the blessings of Allah within themselves and in their surroundings.

Where did they stand before Islam? A degraded, filthy society, disturbed ideas, and unsettled values of life, that is, in comparison with the jahili society. Having considered it thoroughly, they adopted the pure and elevated society of Islam, whose ideas and beliefs were clear as glass and whose values were balanced. Therefore Islam was for them a blessing beyond expectation. Looking at their own position, they felt that they were immersed from head to toe in the blessings and bounties of Islam.

Therefore, Allah's saying ﴿وَلأتِمَّ نِعْمَتِي﴾ "so that I may complete My favor upon you" is, in fact, a hidden hint from Allah in this phrase; it was and is a kind of encouragement toward those blessings and favors, the awareness of which the Muslims themselves had.

Here the command concerning the change of qibla is repeated, but in each repetition a new meaning is given. The first time it was said that the Messenger ﷺ, since he desired the change of qibla, expressed this desire in respectful silence; he would repeatedly look up at the sky. So Allah granted the change of qibla. The second time it was said that although the Messenger's ﷺ request and desire existed, the command comes from Allah and is the very truth. The third time, the command given informed the Muslims of the wisdom behind the change of qibla: that the enemies of Islam used it to argue for the superiority of their religion, and therefore the command of change was issued. The purpose was that those who do not support the truth and do not accept proofs and arguments deserve that they have no honor and are light in every matter.

Along with these reasons, at that time in the ranks of this newly emerging Islamic movement in Medina, there existed circumstances that required this repetition, emphasis, argument and explanation. The effect of the misleading propaganda and false arguments of the opponents was found in the hearts of some Muslims, as is shown by the fact that Allah repeatedly addresses the Muslims with emphasis on this matter, and to remove this effect the Qur'an adopted this forceful manner of expression. And these temporary instructions concerning the change of qibla were made a part of the Qur'an forever, so that in such circumstances Muslims would adopt the same conduct, because they had entered a struggle that would continue until the Day of Resurrection, which would never cool, never soften: the struggle of the Islamic revolution.

In this connection the Qur'an again reminds the Muslims that Allah has blessed them with His favor. He, accepting the supplication of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), sent to you His Messenger, and Ibrahim (peace be upon him) was the first builder of the Bayt al-Haram, the qibla of the Muslims. Thus the Qur'an declares the Muslims to be the spiritual heirs of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), and a direct connection between the Muslims and Ibrahim (peace be upon him) is established.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 2, verse 151:

If we reflect on the content of this verse, it becomes clear that it repeats the same matters to which Ibrahim (peace be upon him) called in the same passage. At that time Ibrahim and Isma'il (peace be upon them both) were raising the walls of the Ka'bah. The beloved friend of Allah (Khalil Allah) had prayed: "O Allah, from among my progeny, those who dwell in the vicinity of this House, raise up for them a Messenger who will recite Your verses to them, teach them the Book and wisdom, and purify them."

In this way, the Muslims are reminded that the sending of Rasulullah (ﷺ) among them, and their own existence as Muslims, is in truth the direct granting of their father Ibrahim's (peace be upon him) prayer. There is also an indication in this that their movement is not a new movement; it is an ancient one. Their qibla is not a new qibla, but the qibla of their forefather Ibrahim (peace be upon him). And the generosity that Islam has bestowed upon them is the same generosity that Allah promised to His friend.

He has given you your ancient qibla, and granted you a distinct identity. This is but one example of the blessings that He continuously bestows upon you. And the first of His blessings is that He sent among you His Messenger (ﷺ) from among yourselves: كَمَا أَرْسَلْنَا فِيكُمْ رَسُولا مِنْكُمْ "Just as We sent among you a Messenger from among yourselves."

He established prophethood among you. Is this not a great honour for you? The Jews had for a long time been waiting for the last Messenger, and they thought that he would be from among them, and that under his leadership they would triumph over the Quraysh. But Allah chose the Seal of the Messengers from among you: يَتْلُو عَلَيْكُمْ آيَاتِنَا "He recites to you Our verses."

What he recites to you by way of reading is the truth. In this phrase there is a kingly encouragement. The speech of Allah is being revealed upon Rasulullah (ﷺ), yet the address is directed to His servants. When one reflects on this manner of speech, it appears as a great honour. The heart rejoices with delight. What a status these people have! Who are they, and what are they? The Lord of Holiness is addressing them. They are being spoken to in His very own words. What a great mark of favour is this! Had Allah not bestowed His grace and generosity upon them, from where would they have obtained such a station? This is purely the result of the rain of mercy from Allah. At the beginning of creation, Allah fashioned the framework of man and breathed a soul into it. He continued his lineage so that from among them would arise people who deserve the blessings of Allah, people who would welcome those blessings.

وَيُزَكِّيكُمْ "And He purifies you." Had Allah not existed, not one of the polytheist Arabs or the Muslims would have been purified. They would neither have been purified nor attained elevated rank. Allah sent a Messenger from among them so that he might purify them, purify their hearts from the filth of shirk and the defilement of jahiliyyah, and purify their souls from all those notions under whose burden the human soul had lain buried for centuries.

He also purifies them from the defilements of sensual desire, so that their souls do not fall into the pit of sexual licentiousness. Those whom Islam does not purify, whether the people of ancient times or of modern times, quench their sexual thirst, as it were, from a spring of filthy water, which the nature abhors and by which human humanity is destroyed. An animal that is bound only by its animal nature is elevated above such a human being; those who are deprived of faith are, by comparison, far purer than that animal. Likewise, Allah purifies their society from plunder, exploitation, usury and profiteering. All these things are also a kind of filth. They corrupt human consciousness and the human soul, and collective life becomes polluted by them. He purifies their lives from oppression and injustice and grants them a system of justice and benevolence, a justice which humanity had neither seen nor heard of before the Islamic way of life and the Islamic system of government. In short, He cleanses them from all the filths and defilements which are the ugly stain on the face of the jahiliyyah spread around them, and which are found in every society that has not been purified by the Islamic spirit, in which the pure and clean system of Islam has not been implemented.

وَيُعَلِّمُكُمُ الْكِتَابَ وَالْحِكْمَةَ "He teaches you the Book and wisdom." What was said earlier, that it is the Messenger who recites the verses to you, also means that the Messenger teaches you the Book. But here, along with the teaching of the Book, the teaching of wisdom (hikmah) is included. Wisdom is in truth the outcome of teaching the Book. Wisdom is the skill by which a person gives every thing its true and proper place, weighs every matter and every problem on a correct standard, and is able to understand the real purpose and objective of commands and guidance. History bears witness that those people whom Rasulullah (ﷺ) trained, and whom he purified through the verses of the Book of Allah, became so complete in wisdom and understanding that they were like a fruit fully ripened upon the tree.

وَيُعَلِّمُكُمْ مَا لَمْ تَكُونُوا تَعْلَمُونَ (151) "And He teaches you what you did not know." The history of the Islamic community bears witness that this is a great truth. Islam chose this community from Arab society, which had no store of knowledge beyond a few scattered pieces of information, only that knowledge which was necessary for the life of a tribe in the desert, or which sufficed for the needs of the small towns surrounded by the desert. Islam transformed this desert community into an ummah that began to provide wise and just leadership to all of humanity. Within a short period, this ummah reached a state where it kept a keen watch, was aware of the affairs of the world, and was adorned with the ornament of knowledge. The Qur'an and wisdom, the guidance based on the Qur'an and the sayings of the Messenger (ﷺ), became for this ummah a path of guidance and a fountainhead of knowledge.

The Prophet's Mosque in Madinah, where the Noble Qur'an and the sayings of the Messenger based on the Qur'an were recited and taught, became a great university for the ummah. Those who graduated from this university went forth and provided wise guidance to all of humanity, and offered such leadership as has no parallel in the whole of human history before it, nor has any been found after it to this day.

The Islamic system of life, which provided this leadership and produced this standard group of human beings, still has the capacity today to provide humanity with the same kind of leadership, provided that this ummah truly believes in this Noble Qur'an, rightly accepts it as the source of its life, and does not use it merely for the gratification of the ear through beautiful recitation, but makes it the constitution of its life.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 2, verse 152:

﴿So remember Me, and I will remember you.﴾ "You remember Me, and I will remember you." This is a generosity that can come only from Allah, whose treasures never diminish, whose treasures have no guardian, and whose giving has no reckoning or accountant. From His treasures, requests are answered and gifts are bestowed without any cause. This is not because He is in need, but because He is the Giver, the Bountiful.

A hadith reports: "Whoever remembers Me in his heart, I will remember him in My heart; and whoever remembers Me in a gathering, I will remember him in a gathering better than theirs." (Hadith sahih)

Another hadith with a similar meaning: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said that Allah the Exalted said: "O son of Adam! If you remember Me in your heart, I will remember you in My heart; and if you remember Me among people, I will remember you among the angels."

Some narrations add: "among those who are better than them. If you draw one span closer to Me, I will draw one cubit closer to you; if you draw one cubit closer to Me, I will draw two cubits closer to you; and if you come to Me walking, I will come to you running."

This is the grace and generosity whose description cannot be expressed in words. Gratitude for it cannot be rendered except by the heart prostrating itself with all its depths.

How is Allah to be remembered? Words are not essential; it is the attention of the heart. It is the heart turning towards Allah, whether or not words accompany it. Remembrance is an inner awareness and an impression, and its lesser effects are that a person becomes ready to obey Allah, and its higher effects are that a person is granted the vision of Allah. Those who are blessed with the bounty of reaching Allah, and who have tasted the delight of His vision, have nothing before them but this: only the vision of the Beloved.

﴿And be grateful to Me, and do not be ungrateful.﴾ Gratitude also has many levels. The first is that a person acknowledges Allah's blessings; then he feels shame before disobeying Him. The final level is that a person becomes embodied gratitude: every movement of the body, every word of the tongue, every beat of the heart and every thought of the mind becomes a pattern of gratitude. Ungratefulness is forbidden. The reference is to that final station, to which an ungrateful person eventually arrives. Through "do not be ungrateful" the final point is indicated, where the line of ingratitude reaches its end. We seek refuge in Allah.

On the occasion of the change of the qibla, the guidance is entirely clear and appropriate. The remembrance of Allah is the point at which the heart of the believer becomes prepared for the worship of Allah. Then he becomes purely Allah's, and is ascribed to that relationship, that is, he becomes a servant through servitude.

On the occasion of warning against Jewish conspiracies, it is also fitting to give guidance regarding thought and gratitude. We have said that the ultimate aim of the Jews was to return the believers to disbelief. They wanted this blessing, which Allah had specially given to them, to be taken away from the Muslims. What blessing? The blessing of faith: the highest blessing that can be given to any individual or community. Especially for the Arabs, it was a blessing greater even than a great blessing. It was through it that the existence of the Arabs was established. In the history of humanity, the Arabs played a great role; their name became linked with the outlook on life they bore and which they were to convey to all of humankind.

Without this blessing the Arabs were nothing. They were obscure, they are still obscure, and if they do not embrace it, they will remain obscure in the future.
