What did they have other than the Islamic outlook on life through which they could make a name for themselves in the world? Can any nation attain a position of leadership in the world without an outlook on life?

Leadership requires a vision that leads the whole of life and shows the path of progress to human life. The Islamic outlook on life is in truth a complete system of life. It is not merely a slogan without positive action behind it, but a practice that supports this outlook. Along with the good word of the Kalima of Islam, a good deed that corresponds to the Kalima is also necessary.

It is necessary, indeed an obligation, for the ummah to remember this truth so that Allah remembers it. And Allah should not cause it to be forgotten completely; whoever Allah has forgotten, understand that he has drowned. On earth his good mention will not remain; in the heavens he will have no well-wisher. Whoever remembers Allah, Allah will remember him: he will be mentioned in the heavens, and his good mention will resound throughout the vast and wide universe.

There was a time when the Muslims remembered Allah, and then Allah also remembered them. Then what happened? Their name was raised high throughout the entire universe, and the leadership of the world, righteous leadership, was entrusted to them. But then there came a time when they forgot the Lord, the Possessor of Majesty, and He also forgot them. Before long they became insignificant and were lost. They fell to the humiliating status of a subordinate in the community of nations. The remedy still exists. Allah the Exalted calls: "Remember Me, and I will remember you. Be grateful to Me, and do not adopt ingratitude."

Lesson 9 at a glance

After the change of the qibla, and after giving the Muslim ummah a distinct and separate status and an identity suited to the distinctive outlook on life of this ummah, the first guidance given to the Muslims was that they should seek help through patience and prayer, because they had been entrusted with a great responsibility. This office demands great sacrifices. They must offer blood as martyrs; they must bear loss of life, loss of wealth, and loss of goods and produce. They will see days of hunger and be confronted with frightening nights. Beyond this, they will have to give countless sacrifices. For all these sacrifices they must prepare themselves.

They must strive, against their own selves and against this entire world, for the establishment of the Islamic system. They must confront the terrors of this great struggle, and such confrontation and preparation can happen only if the believers seek help through patience and prayer. They must join the heart of this ummah to Allah, purify their hearts for Allah, and turn to Allah and His Messenger in all their affairs. For what is all this done? For what reward is it undertaken? For the attainment of Allah's pleasure? For seeking His mercy and guidance? How great is this reward! Ask the heart of the believer about its worth!

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 2, verse 153:

The Quran mentions patience (sabr) repeatedly, because the Islamic movement was to face the most severe opposition and hardships. Allah knew that patience and steadfastness would be needed on this path. Since the Islamic movement would have to confront constant difficulties and unceasing struggles, it was necessary that the believers act with patience and that their souls remain alert in both internal and external affairs. The strength of the believers had to stay organised and their nerves had to stay firm. In such circumstances, what other course is there but patience and steadfastness? Thus patience is needed in worship, patience is needed in keeping away from sins, and, in short, patience against these many-sided conspiracies; patience over the delay of Allah's help; patience over the long struggle; patience over the power of falsehood; patience over the scarcity of supporters of the religion; patience under the burden of hatred and enmity, and patience over the bitterness of self-interested people.

When patience becomes prolonged and difficulties increase, the power of patience weakens. Sometimes it also happens that, if outside help is not available, the cup of patience overflows. Therefore, alongside prayer (salah), the command to be patient is also given. Prayer is a spring that never dries up. It is a provision for the journey that never runs out. It is a means of renewing strength, and it is the sustenance of the heart. Through it the full power of patience is obtained, and with patience there arises contentment, cheerful forbearance and firm certainty.

Man is mortal, weak, and the possessor of limited strength. Therefore it is necessary that he turn towards the Supreme Power. When he faces the outward and inward powers of evil, and the matter exceeds his limited strength and endurance, he should seek help from that "great power". On this path there come stages where the force of desire becomes strong, where the pull of greed and avarice is intense, where the struggle to remain steadfast on the path of truth becomes heavy, where the forces of wickedness, depravity, oppression and aggression gain strength and confrontation becomes difficult, where the road grows long, hardship increases, and the days and nights of life appear dark.

Man reflects and sees that he has not yet reached any goal, yet death is near; he has gained nothing, and the sun of his life is near setting. He sees that evil has swelled like carded cotton, while truth has shrunk. The destination is far, the last ray of hope has disappeared from the horizon, and there is no sign of the way on the road. In such circumstances, patience and prayer alone are the springs of strength.

It is at such points and such stages that the worth of prayer is known. Between mortal man and the eternal Lord, prayer establishes the one direct connection. It is the meeting point where a single drop joins the eternal spring. It is the key to the treasures of Allah that make a person independent, fill his lap, and send down a rain of mercy. It is a leap through which a person breaks the limits of this small, confined world and enters the boundaries of a greater universe. In intense heat and scorching sun, it is cool shade, the morning breeze and pleasant dew. For a weary heart, it is a pleasant feeling.

It is related in a hadith that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was distressed, or faced hard circumstances, he would say: "O Bilal, give us rest through it." Whenever he (ﷺ) was in the crowd of troubles, he would begin to pray abundantly.

The Islamic system is in essence a system of worship and servitude. Its worship is also wise, and its greatest wisdom is that it is a provision for the journey, a source of spiritual aid, and a cleansing of the heart. Whenever a person is afflicted by calamity and his heart is constricted, this worship becomes a means of expansion, and the person bears that calamity with ease, cheerful forbearance and contentment.

When Allah chose Hazrat Muhammad (ﷺ) for this great mission and heavy responsibility, He commanded him:

﴿O you who wraps himself (in garments), stand (in prayer) through the night, except a little, half of it, or reduce it a little, or add to it, and recite the Quran in measured tones. Indeed, We are about to send down to you a weighty word.﴾ (al-Muzzammil 73:1-5)

What were this standing in the night and this prostration and bowing by day? They were the preparation and training for this heavy speech and this great responsibility, a path full of afflictions and hardships. This was the worship from which springs of tranquillity gush forth, mutual bonds are strengthened, tasks become easy, eyes are brightened, and a shower of consolation, reassurance, comfort and peace begins to fall upon the believing heart.

This is why, when the Muslims reach the threshold of these afflictions and hardships, Allah turns them towards patience and prayer. And as to what the outcome will be, He says: ﴿Indeed, Allah is with those who are patient.﴾

Allah is with them: He helps them, grants them strength and firmness, holds affection and love for them, and on this arduous journey He does not leave them alone. He does not withdraw from them and their limited might and power to one side. Whenever their provision runs out, supplies come from Him; whenever they become exhausted and worn out, He grants them fresh strength. He begins the verse with the sweet voice of "O you who believe," and concludes it with these encouraging words: "Indeed, Allah is with those who are patient."

Countless hadiths have been transmitted concerning patience and forbearance. Here, in keeping with the context of the Quran and to prepare the Muslim community for the responsibility for which it has been raised, it is appropriate to mention some of these hadiths:

Hazrat Khabbab ibn al-Aratt (رضي الله عنه) narrates: We complained to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), while he was reclining against the wall of the Kaaba. We said: "O Messenger of Allah, will you not seek help for us? Will you not supplicate for us?" He (ﷺ) said: "Among those before you, a man would be seized, a pit would be dug for him in the ground, he would be placed in it, then a saw would be brought and placed on his head and he would be split in two; and iron combs would be used to tear the flesh from his bones, yet none of these hardships could turn him from his religion. And by Allah, Allah will surely complete this affair, until a rider travels from Sanaa to Hadramawt fearing none but Allah, and the wolf guards the sheep, but you are hasty." (Bukhari, Abu Dawud, Nasai)

Ibn Masud (رضي الله عنه) says: Once the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) related the story of a prophet, as if I am still seeing him now: his people struck him and made him bleed. He was wiping the blood from his face and saying: "O Allah, forgive my people, for they do not know." (Bukhari and Muslim)

Yahya ibn Wathhab narrates from an elderly companion of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: A believer who mixes with people and endures their harm is better than a believer who keeps apart from people and does not endure their harm. (Tirmidhi)

And now, the Islamic movement is in Madinah Taiyyibah. On the surface of the earth, it is advancing towards the establishment of the Islamic system. Why should it not advance! This was its destiny from the very first day. It has raised the banner of truth and is setting out with that banner on a long and difficult journey. The Quran is preparing it spiritually. In the course of this great movement of jihad there will be tugging and pulling, afflictions will stand in the way, and these mujahideen will have to sacrifice their lives and wealth. Therefore the Quran here grants them a correct perspective and a correct outlook on life. The Quran grants the Islamic movement a standard, a touchstone, and a balance, by which it can weigh all its affairs and all its values on this long and arduous journey.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 2, verse 154:

In the battle between truth and falsehood, some will fall and lay down their lives in the path of truth. Some beloved and dear ones will be killed, and some noble and religious people will also be martyred. Those who go forth in the way of Allah and who offer their lives as a sacrifice in the battle between good and evil are generally people of pure intention, a clean heart and a polished soul. If such people are killed in the way of Allah, they are not dead. In reality they are alive. It is not permissible to call them dead; neither should you consider them dead in your feeling and awareness, nor call them dead with your tongue. They are alive, and Allah is witness to this. They are alive, indeed, certainly alive!

The apparent eye sees that they have apparently died. Can this superficial view decide the reality of life and death? The reality is that life is the name of action, progress and continuity. Death is associated with uselessness, stagnation and cessation. Those who are killed in the way of Allah, their action continues; their martyrdom affects society. Their blood reaches this ideology of life, and through it the ideology of life grows. Other individuals keep being influenced by this martyrdom, and this influence remains continuously established. Even after martyrdom, the martyrs remain active and effective. Their blood keeps creating a colour in the life of the whole society. And this continuity remains until the Day of Resurrection. This is life, rather, everlasting life. In this sense, they are alive even in this world among people.

But they are also alive with their Lord, and there too they are alive in the same way as they are alive here. What is the condition of their life with their Lord? It is as it is here, or it may be that we do not have full awareness of this condition. Allah the Exalted says: "Rather they are alive, but you do not perceive" (bal ahya'un wa lakin la tash'urun). In reality they are alive, but you are not aware of their life. Our sphere of knowledge is limited, and this is a life that we cannot comprehend. But in any case, they are alive!

They are alive. That is why, unlike ordinary dead people, they are not given ghusl (ritual bath). They are buried in the same clothes in which they attain martyrdom. The purpose of ghusl is that the body of the deceased becomes pure, but martyrs are already pure, because there is a soul in their body. The clothes they wore in the world, they will wear in the grave as well, because in any case they are alive.

They are alive. Their family does not mourn this killing. Their friends and companions do not find this separation burdensome. They are alive in such a way that they participate in the affairs of life of their family and relatives. They are alive. That is why the separation from them does not weigh heavily on those left behind. This great event, this great sacrifice, neither frightens them nor becomes a burden for them. If they are alive, then what? They are living honourably with their Lord. They are given the highest honour, and the full recompense of their sacrifice is repaid to them, rather, a bounty beyond that is added upon it.

In Sahih Muslim there is a narration: "The souls of the martyrs are in the form of green birds, they fly about in Paradise wherever they wish, then they come and take up residence in lanterns suspended beneath the Throne." This information certainly reaches the Lord, the Lord of Majesty. Allah the Exalted says: "What do you desire?" They say: "O our Lord, what more could we want? You have given us what You have not given to any of Your creation?" Allah the Exalted again asks the same question. When they realise that unless they ask for something, their release will not come, then they say: "We wish that You return us to the world, that we may fight in Your way and be killed once more," because they themselves already see the reward of martyrdom. Allah, glorified is His majesty, says: "I have decreed that the martyrs shall not be returned to the world."

Anas (may Allah be pleased with him) said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No one enters Paradise and then wishes to leave it, even if the whole world were given to him, except the martyr, who wishes to be returned to the world and to be killed once more in the way of Allah, because he sees how great the value of martyrdom is." (Muslim, Bukhari)

Who are these martyrs? They are those who fight in the way of Allah. Only in the way of Allah. No other slogan, no other aim and no other ideology should share in it; they should be fighting only for that truth which Allah has revealed, only for that system of life which He has laid down, only in the path of that religion which Allah has made obligatory. Only in His way, not in any other way, not under any other banner, nor in partnership with any other symbol or aim. The Qur'an and Sunnah have laid great emphasis on this sincerity of intention, to the extent that there should remain no doubt in the mujahid's self, and no trace of other than Allah, so that he belongs to Allah alone.

It is narrated from Musa (may Allah be pleased with him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about a person who fights for display of bravery, or for the expression of zeal, or for show, which of them is in the way of Allah? The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Only he is in the way of Allah who fights purely so that the word of Allah becomes supreme." 

It is narrated from Abu Musa (may Allah be pleased with him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about a person who repeatedly fights for display of bravery or for the expression of zeal, which of them is in the way of Allah? The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Only he is in the way of Allah who fights purely so that the word of Allah becomes supreme." (Malik, Imam Bukhari, Imam Muslim)

Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated that a man said: "O Messenger of Allah, a man intends jihad in the way of Allah, but along with it his worldly purpose is also attached?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "He will have no reward." The man repeated this question three times, and each time the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "He will have no reward." (Abu Dawud)

Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever goes out for jihad in the way of Allah, and goes out for that jihad only because he has believed in Allah and affirmed the messengers, Allah has guaranteed for such a person that He will admit him into Paradise, or will return him to the dwelling from which he went out for jihad, taking with him reward and a full share of spoils. By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, whatever wound he receives in the way of Allah, on the Day of Resurrection this mujahid will be raised in that same wounded state; the colour of the wound will be the colour of blood and its smell will be like musk. By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, if it were not a hardship for the Muslims, I would never stay behind from a detachment that goes out to fight in the way of Allah. But I do not have enough means to provide mounts for all the people, nor do they have the strength to follow me, and it would be unbearable for them that I should go and they remain behind. By Him in whose hand is my soul, I wish that I be killed in the way of Allah, then fight and be killed, then fight and be killed." (Malik, Bukhari, Muslim)

These are the martyrs, the people who go forth for jihad in the way of Allah. But apart from their believing in Allah, apart from their affirming all the messengers, and apart from their wishing to strive in the way of Allah as a result of faith, there should be no other motive in their hearts.

On one occasion the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade a Persian mujahid from mentioning his Persian origin during jihad or from showing any kind of pride in his nationality. Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf (may Allah be pleased with him) narrates from Ibn Abi Uqbah, who narrates from his father (he was a freed slave of the people of Persia), who said: "I took part in the Battle of Uhud with the Messenger of Allah. I struck a man among the polytheists and said: 'Take this, and I am a Persian-born freed slave.'" Upon this, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) turned towards me and said: "Why did you not say: 'And I am an Ansari freed slave; I am the son of their sister and their freed slave.'" (Abu Dawud)

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not like that he should take pride in any quality other than his support of the Messenger, or that he should fight for any banner or any slogan other than the support and aid of this religion.

This is Islamic jihad, and only through this jihad does a person attain the rank of martyrdom, and he is granted that life upon which the martyrs are established.

**Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah al-Baqarah, verses 155–156:**

Now, in this lesson, the Islamic movement is prepared to face new events and new circumstances. A correct outlook is given to it regarding the events that are to come:

For training, a person is passed through the furnace of trials. By placing him in fear and danger, by inflicting loss of life and property, and by subjecting him to hardships and losses in income, Allah tests the resolve of the sincere seeker. These trials are necessary so that the believers may be able to fulfil the responsibilities of the Islamic way of life well, and that, the more they are afflicted in the path of the Islamic way of life, the more dear that way of life becomes to them.

Those ideologies for which these fighters have not undergone any hardship or endured any calamity are not lasting. Such people bid them farewell at the very first stage of calamity. Trials are in reality a psychological examination, which a worker passes for his way of life, and as a result of which this way of life becomes dearer to that worker than his own life, before it does to other people. When workers suffer pain and spend wealth for the sake of the ideology, then they will value it and also protect it.

Other people too will value this ideology only when they see that its adherents give their lives for it and bear all the calamities that come because of it with willingness. Seeing those who endure hardship for their ideas, even ordinary onlookers will say: "The way of life for which these people struggle is something very precious; if it were not precious, these people would never make such great sacrifices and would not endure such great trials and hardships."

In such circumstances, the opponents of this way of life also become speechless, begin to investigate it, begin to value it, and are drawn towards it of their own accord. This is the stage after reaching which the help and victory of Allah arrive, and people enter the religion of Allah in multitudes.

Trial is very necessary; through it the strength of the people of ideology increases, their backbone becomes firm. Through hardships and difficulties their hidden powers awaken. Springs burst forth for the stored-up powers, about which the believer did not even have an idea before these trials and hardships.

Islamic values and Islamic concepts cannot become firm and straight until they are passed through the furnace of hardships and difficulties. It is the result of trials that the eyes of workers become bright and the rust is removed from their hearts.

More important than anything else, and the most fundamental point, is that in a state of trials and hardships all worldly connections are cut off. Various illusions and desires disappear, the heart becomes empty for Allah, rather only the support of Allah remains. This is the stage where all veils are lifted, the doors of insight are opened, the horizon is clear and transparent far and wide, nothing is seen except Allah, no power is seen in the eyes except the power of Allah, no authority of anyone is seen except that of Allah, refuge is only with Allah, and no one else's refuge exists. On reaching this stage, the human soul becomes united with this reality. This is the stage where this verse of the Holy Qur'an becomes a part of the human soul.

﴿And give good news to the patient, who, when a calamity befalls them, say: "Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we shall return."﴾

"And give good news to those who are patient, who when calamity strikes them say, 'Indeed we belong to Allah, and to Him we shall return.'" Truly, we belong to Allah, all of us belong to Allah. The powers within our bodies, rather our entire existence and our whole personality, belong to Allah and to Allah alone. To Allah alone we shall return. The final reference of all matters is to Him. Our heads are bowed in submission. In every matter our heads are bowed in submission!

Thus we stand, with a correct conception and a correct belief, before the one truth and reality of the universe, the Lord of majesty, and we are with hands raised in supplication.

These are the patient ones whom the exalted Messenger (ﷺ) is given glad tidings of rewards and honours. The status and rank of this are proclaimed by the Lord of Majesty Himself.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 2, verse 157:

...Blessings will come from Allah. Here, by using the word ṣalawāt (blessings) for those who are patient, the patient are, as it were, made partners in those ṣalawāt (blessings) which Allah and His angels send upon the prophets. What a lofty station! What an outpouring of mercy, that Allah Himself bears witness that those who are patient in afflictions are indeed the ones who truly possess correct recognition (ma'rifah) and are walking upon the right path. In short, every matter here is magnificent and beyond the ordinary grasp of the mind.

We have reached the end of this lesson on the preparation and training of the Islamic movement. Pause and take stock! Afflictions and hardships, killing and martyrdom, loss of life and property, hunger and poverty, fear and peril, and other difficulties: this is the great preparation and training for them, for the tumultuous, perilous, and extremely arduous long battle between truth and falsehood. All these matters deserve deep reflection.

Look! Allah places all these afflictions and difficulties in one pan of the scale, while in the other pan there is only one thing: that these people deserve blessings and mercy from Allah, and the declaration that in this world it is they who are upon guidance. At this juncture, Allah does not promise victory and triumph to the believing patient ones, nor is any special assistance announced here. Nor is the lure of spoils of war offered. Nothing at all! There is only the promise of Allah's mercy and blessings, and the testimony that they are assuredly upon truth and righteousness... Allah was training the patient ones for a task more precious than their own selves and lives... Therefore Allah wishes to purify this community of every desire and inclination connected with the world, to the extent that they are instructed to remove from their hearts even the desire for the ascendancy of the objective for which they work, the way of life for which they strive and are ready to give up their lives. They are to make only the good pleasure of Allah and obedience to Him their charter. They are to be bound only by the command of Allah. They should keep advancing, and nothing should be before them except Allah's pleasure, the attainment of Allah's mercy, and the assurance that they have set out for the truth and are on the right path. This is the correct objective. This is the correct purpose and goal, and this, and only this, is the sweet fruit for which they run eagerly. As for the hope that through this struggle they will attain victory and success, and that they will be granted dominion and power over the earth, that authority, power, and command are not for them personally; they will be the ascendancy of the Islamic call which they carry.

As for the believing mujahidin, they have been given a great reward: Allah's blessings and mercy will be upon them, and they have been given the certificate that they alone are upon truth. And for what was this reward given? It was given in return for the sacrifice of life and property, and for their earnings. It was given for killing and martyrdom in the way of Allah. Yet even so, the scale of Allah's grace and favour is heavier. This favour is heavier than all other favours. Compared with victory, aid, and establishment in the land, this favour is heavier in every respect. Moreover, it is more delightful than the joy that is attained when, after victory, aid, and Islamic revolution, the heart's longing is fulfilled.

This is the sequence through which Allah took the Islamic front. Whoever among the children of Adam wishes to purify his self, his call, and his religion should adopt this manner of training.

Lesson 10 at a glance

In this lesson, the correction of certain fundamental principles on which the edifice of the Islamic worldview rests is intended. Regarding these fundamental principles of Islam, the Jews of Madinah used to practise deception, mix truth with falsehood, knowingly conceal the truth, and create agitation in the hearts of the Muslims and confusion in their minds. Therefore it was necessary to give clear rulings on these principles. However, the style of expression is general: the matter was stated on a principled basis rather than directed specifically at the Jews and other opponents, and the Muslims were warned of the dangers that are generally likely to confront them on this path.

The question of sa'y (running) between Safa and Marwah has also been taken up. Since in the Age of Ignorance certain non-Islamic and polytheistic notions were attached to this sa'y, it was clarified that these are among the symbols of Allah (sha'a'ir Allah), and therefore the sa'y is permissible. Its appropriateness is also clear from the change of qiblah. Furthermore, since the Islamic system has preserved the Hajj to the House of Allah and other symbols, it was appropriate that the Islamic system clarify its policy regarding these matters.

The Jews concealed the teachings and guidance of Allah. Here they are severely condemned. However, it is stated that the door of repentance is open: "Even if you repent a hundred times, return." But if they persist in their course and insist upon it, then curses will rain upon them and a painful punishment awaits them. There is an explanation of Allah's oneness and cosmic proofs for it, and it is shown that there is severe warning for those who associate partners with Allah. In this connection, a scene is also presented of the relationship between the followers and those who were followed, which will appear on the Day of Resurrection when they see the punishment of Allah. They will then disown one another, but to no avail.

Those who conceal the commands revealed by Allah for merely worldly aims and positions are severely warned. They are told that disgrace, humiliation, and the severe wrath of Allah are prepared for them in the Hereafter.

At the end, the Islamic criterion of good and evil is explained. It is stated that faith and righteous action are the principles through which the Islamic worldview is set right. Goodness does not mean any outward form; merely turning the face towards east or west in prayer is not among the principles of piety. Goodness is the name of firm connection with Allah in consciousness and action, and in the consciousness of action. This statement is in fact linked with the discussions on the change of qiblah.

On carefully reading this entire discussion, it becomes clear that the whole matter revolves around one theme: the struggle between truth and falsehood. In the human mind there is a conflict between truth and falsehood; Islamic values are being determined, the worldview is being clarified, and the objections and propaganda of external conspiracies, deceit, and opponents who create mental confusion are being answered.

The occasion of revelation for this verse has several narrations. Given the nature of the living concept of life that Islam had instilled in the hearts of the foremost Emigrants and Helpers, the narration that the books of hadith report, and that is the most fabricated and the most in line with the psychological logic of the time, is the one that says: "Some Muslims disliked performing the sa'y (going back and forth) between Safa and Marwa during Hajj and Umrah, because in the age of jahiliyyah (the pre-Islamic age of ignorance) they used to perform sa'y between these hills because these places were the shrines of two idols, Asaf and Na'ila. So after Islam came, Muslims began to feel aversion to this sa'y and considered it an act of the jahiliyyah era."

Imam Bukhari (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated through the chain of Muhammad ibn Yusuf, Sufyan, and Asim ibn Sulayman. Sulayman says: "I asked Hadrat Anas (may Allah be pleased with him) about Safa and Marwa, and he said: 'We used to think that these were rites of the age of jahiliyyah. When Islam appeared, we stopped performing sa'y between Safa and Marwa.' Then Allah revealed this verse of the Qur'an: ﴿Indeed, Safa and Marwa are among the symbols of Allah.﴾"

Imam Sha'bi (may Allah have mercy on him) said: "Asaf was an idol on Safa and Na'ila was on Marwa, and they used to kiss them. Therefore, after Islam, the Muslims felt aversion to performing sa'y between them, and this verse was revealed concerning that."

The narrations do not fix the date of revelation of this verse. However, the more preferred view is that it was revealed after the verses concerning the change of the qiblah. Although at that time Makkah had become Dar al-Harb (the abode of war), some Muslims could still perform Hajj and Umrah individually. It is likely that such people considered sa'y between Safa and Marwa to be a custom of the jahiliyyah. In their hearts, through long education and training, the faith-based concept of life had become firmly established, and by its blessing they viewed every act and custom of the jahiliyyah with suspicion and aversion. They had become so sensitive about everything of the jahiliyyah that they feared performing any act that belonged to the jahiliyyah era, lest Islam had ordered it to be abandoned. The Muslims displayed this sentiment of theirs fully on various occasions.

The call of Islam had thoroughly shaken the hearts of these people. This call had penetrated to the depths of their hearts, and it had brought about a great psychological and conscious revolution in them. They regarded all their former conduct with aversion; indeed, they had abandoned their past. They believed that the age of jahiliyyah was a chapter of their life that they had closed forever. Their past now had no connection with them, nor did they have any association with their past. In their view, their past was a kind of impurity and filth, which it was not even permissible to touch.

If one carefully reads the final phase of the life of this chosen people, one perceives how strange the effect of this Islamic worldview had become upon those pure souls. It appears that these people were seized and shaken, and every kind of pollution was shaken off them, and the particles of their existence were reorganized in a new form, just as, when a jolt of electricity is given, the components of a substance change their former chemical form and take on a completely new form.

This is Islam, that is, to come out completely from jahiliyyah, and to consider all the affairs of jahiliyyah completely forbidden and objectionable. It is to come out of every objectionable action that was characteristic of jahiliyyah, and to remove from the heart and mind every consciousness that used to dominate minds in the age of jahiliyyah, until the cup of the believer is emptied for a new concept of life and all its requirements.

The history of the Islamic movement bears witness that when this consciousness settled deeply in the hearts and minds of the Muslims, and they became thoroughly mature, then Islam announced the retention of some suitable rites from among the symbols (shi'ar) of the age of jahiliyyah. Before this, it had severed the connection of these rites with the jahiliyyah and fixed them into the system of Islam in the same way that a gem is fixed in a ring. Now a Muslim did not act upon these select rites because he had practised them in the age of jahiliyyah; rather, he considered them a new symbol of Islam, whose origin lay in Islam, and whose roots drew nourishment from the Islamic system of life.

An example of the solid and profound system of Islamic training is that the Qur'an, concerning this very matter, begins its statement in this way: that Safa and Marwa are among the symbols of Allah. ﴿Indeed, Safa and Marwa are among the symbols of Allah.﴾ Although it is indicated that whoever performs sa'y between them will be performing one of the obligations among the symbols of Allah, the purpose of the sa'y between them is obedience to the command of Allah. Now there remains no connection between this sa'y and the sa'y of the age of jahiliyyah. Now it has no tie or devotion to Asaf, Na'ila, or the other idols of jahiliyyah; rather, its connection is only with Allah and His Messenger.

Therefore, now there is no harm in this circumambulation and sa'y. It is not a sinful matter. The matter is no longer that old matter, and the viewpoint is no longer that old viewpoint. ﴿So whoever makes Hajj to the House or performs Umrah, there is no blame upon him for going back and forth between them.﴾

Of the rites that the Arabs used to practise in Hajj, Islam retained most of them in their original form. It only abolished those things that were connected with idols or were based on the superstitions of jahiliyyah and had no reality. The connection of the rites that were retained was also established by Islam's new concept of life, and it declared that these are the rites that Hadrat Ibrahim (peace be upon him) practised (for details, see the later discussion of Hajj).

The rites of Hajj and Umrah are one and the same. The only difference is that in Umrah, standing at Arafah is not obligatory. Also, the miqat (the places beyond which one may not proceed without intention) fixed for Hajj do not apply to Umrah. But in both Hajj and Umrah, sa'y between Safa and Marwa is essential, and it is among the symbols of Allah.

The verse concludes with the statement that whoever voluntarily and willingly does any good deed at all, it is pleasing to Allah. ﴿And whoever volunteers good, indeed Allah is Appreciative and Knowing.﴾

In this there is an indication that this sa'y is also in reality a goodness. Through this indication, the inner aversion is removed, the heart becomes ready to perform it, and it is satisfied that Allah will count this sa'y as a good deed.

Then He also gives a good reward for this good deed, and He is the Owner of intentions and is aware of every conscious movement of the heart.

Now pause, and cast another glance at this wise style of expression: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Appreciative.﴾ The purpose is that Allah is pleased with goodness, gives its reward, and grants its recompense. The word "Shakir" (Appreciative) not only conveys a particular meaning, but also points to a particular shelter of compassion. This word is a reflection of complete pleasure. As if the Divine Being appreciates the righteous deeds of the servant, then what is the duty of the servant? It is his duty to render further thanks in response to Allah's kindness, and to praise Him greatly. This is a particular style of the Qur'anic mode of expression, which gives human consciousness and feeling freshness, beauty, and gentleness like fresh drops of dew.

After the obligation of sa'y between Safa and Marwa, the next statement is a condemnation of those who conceal the teachings and guidance sent down by Allah. These are the Jews, about whom a lengthy discussion has already taken place earlier in this surah. Their being brought up again here shows that in connection with the change of the qiblah and the obligation of Hajj, they had started debate and disputation, and it has not yet ended.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 2, verse 159:

The People of the Book, through their own Book, knew that the prophethood of the Messenger (ﷺ) was true. They also knew that the commands which he (ﷺ) conveys are true and come from Allah. Despite this, they concealed the commands which Allah had sent down for them in their Book. Thus, the conduct of these people, and of those like them in every age, has been to conceal the truth and reality revealed by Allah, even when there is no reasonable justification for this concealment of truth.

Such people are found in different eras and in different places, who possess knowledge of truth and righteousness but still remain silent at the time of declaring the truth. They know with certainty those statements and verses in which the verdict on this truth has already been given, yet from several verses of the Book of Allah they turn aside: they do not express them, they adopt silence regarding them, and by concealing them they evade the reality that those verses carry. They keep these verses away from the hearing and perception of people, whatever the reason for which they do so. This is a situation that we encounter at various stages of life, and this situation arises in many and countless matters of the realities of religion.

﴿Surely Allah curses them, and all those who curse also curse them.﴾ أُولَئِكَ يَلْعَنُهُمُ اللَّهُ وَيَلْعَنُهُمُ اللاعِنُونَ (159)

It is as though they stand at the place of cursing, and a rain of curses is falling upon them from every direction, and after Allah, every one who curses is pouring curses upon them.

The concept of la'nah (curse) is to drive away with wrath and anger. The curse of Allah means that He will expel them from His mercy, and then those who curse will be pursuing them from every side. Thus they will be rejected from the court of Allah and also be cast out by the Muslims.

﴿Except those who repent, reform, and make clear (what they concealed). Those — I will accept their repentance, and I am the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful.﴾

Despite this warning and threat, the door of repentance remains open in the Noble Qur'an. Through it they find light, and the bond of hope is not broken. In this way the heart is drawn toward the fountainhead of light, and they do not despair of the mercy of Allah. The hope of Allah's forgiveness and pardon remains alive. Therefore, whoever wishes, at whatever time he wishes, with sincerity of intention, may enter this abode of security.

What will be the sign of true repentance? A change and reform in conduct, speaking plainly, acknowledging the truth, and fulfilling the demands of the truth. And those who repent will certainly partake of the mercy of Allah, and their repentance will be accepted. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And I am the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful.﴾ Certainly this will happen, because among those who speak, Allah the Exalted is the most truthful in speech.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 2, verses 161–162:

And those who persist in their wrong course, and do not regard respite and leisure as an opportunity, will certainly reach the end that Allah warned them of before. And now it is said, with greater detail and emphasis: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve and die while they are disbelievers, upon them is the curse of Allah, and of the angels, and of all mankind, combined.﴾ (161) ﴿Abiding therein; their punishment will not be lightened for them, nor will they be reprieved.﴾ (162)

"And those who adopted the attitude of disbelief and gave up their lives in a state of disbelief, upon them is the curse of Allah, and of the angels, and of all people. In that state of being cursed they will remain forever. Neither will their punishment be lightened, nor will they be given any further respite."

Why? Because they closed, by their own hands, the open door that was before them. They did not regard the opportunity as a gift, the chance slipped out of their hands, and they persisted in concealing the truth and in disbelief and misguidance: ﴿Upon them is the curse of Allah, and of the angels, and of all mankind, combined.﴾ This is an all-encompassing curse; in no way will they be able to escape it. Nor will any heart hold mercy for them.

The Qur'an has mentioned no punishment for them other than the all-encompassing curse, and has said that this punishment will not be lightened. There will be no delay, and they will be granted no respite of any kind. This is a punishment such that all other punishments will seem lesser by comparison: the punishment of being rejected, cast away, and disowned. No one will have mercy on them. No eye will accept them, and no tongue will even offer them a greeting of peace. From every direction there will be curse, rejection and severance, from people and also from Allah the Exalted, on the earth and also in the heavens, in every place and from every side. This is the painful and humiliating punishment.

After this, the discourse turns back to Tawhid. The ideological conception of life of faith is founded on the belief in the Oneness of Allah. Observations from the universe are presented that offer irrefutable proofs for the doctrine of Tawhid, and criticism is directed at those who take others besides Allah as deities. It is explained how humiliated and disgraced these people will be on the Day of Resurrection, when the punishment of Allah is before them, the followers from those they followed. Those who were followed will disown their followers, yet no excuse will benefit them at all. Their remorse will not profit them, nor will it save them from the Fire of Hell.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 2, verses 161–162:

And those who persist in their wrong course, and do not regard respite and leisure as an opportunity, will certainly reach the end that Allah warned them of before. And now it is said, with greater detail and emphasis: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve and die while they are disbelievers, upon them is the curse of Allah, and of the angels, and of all mankind, combined.﴾ (161) ﴿Abiding therein; their punishment will not be lightened for them, nor will they be reprieved.﴾ (162)

"And those who adopted the attitude of disbelief and gave up their lives in a state of disbelief, upon them is the curse of Allah, and of the angels, and of all people. In that state of being cursed they will remain forever. Neither will their punishment be lightened, nor will they be given any further respite."

Why? Because they closed, by their own hands, the open door that was before them. They did not regard the opportunity as a gift, the chance slipped out of their hands, and they persisted in concealing the truth and in disbelief and misguidance: ﴿Upon them is the curse of Allah, and of the angels, and of all mankind, combined.﴾ This is an all-encompassing curse; in no way will they be able to escape it. Nor will any heart hold mercy for them.

The Qur'an has mentioned no punishment for them other than the all-encompassing curse, and has said that this punishment will not be lightened. There will be no delay, and they will be granted no respite of any kind. This is a punishment such that all other punishments will seem lesser by comparison: the punishment of being rejected, cast away, and disowned. No one will have mercy on them. No eye will accept them, and no tongue will even offer them a greeting of peace. From every direction there will be curse, rejection and severance, from people and also from Allah the Exalted, on the earth and also in the heavens, in every place and from every side. This is the painful and humiliating punishment.

After this, the discourse turns back to Tawhid. The ideological conception of life of faith is founded on the belief in the Oneness of Allah. Observations from the universe are presented that offer irrefutable proofs for the doctrine of Tawhid, and criticism is directed at those who take others besides Allah as deities. It is explained how humiliated and disgraced these people will be on the Day of Resurrection, when the punishment of Allah is before them, the followers from those they followed. Those who were followed will disown their followers, yet no excuse will benefit them at all. Their remorse will not profit them, nor will it save them from the Fire of Hell.

(And if a sign and indication is needed to recognise this truth.) For those who use their reason, there are signs in the creation of the heavens and the earth, in the continuous succession of night and day, in the ships that sail through rivers and seas carrying what benefits mankind, in the water that Allah sends down from above and by which He then gives life to the earth, and by this same arrangement of His spreads across the earth every kind of living creature, in the circulation of the winds and in the clouds that are made subservient, suspended between heaven and earth. There are countless signs in these. Yet (despite these clear traces that point to the oneness of Allah) there are some people who set up others as equals and rivals to Allah, and who are devoted to them in the way that devotion is due only to Allah. But those who believe love Allah more than anything else. If only those wrongdoers could realise now what they will realise when they see the punishment before them, that all power and all authority belong to Allah alone, and that Allah is severe in punishment. When He punishes, the situation will be that the very leaders and guides who were followed in the world will disown their followers, but they will still receive their punishment. All their means and resources will be cut off, and those who followed them in the world will say: "If only we were given another chance, we would disown them just as they are now disowning us." In this way Allah will show them the deeds they did in the world, presenting them in such a way that they will remain wringing their hands in regret and remorse, yet they will find no way out of the Fire.

The faith-based conception of life is founded upon the principle of the oneness of divinity (wahdat al-uluhiyyah). In the time of the Messenger (ﷺ) there was no dispute about the existence of Allah. There was, however, indeed a difference of opinion regarding the Essence of Allah, His attributes, and the relationship between the Creator and creation. No one disputed the existence of Allah. Never did human nature forget the existence of the Divine, or did mankind ever cease to believe in some god. This is a disease of this modern age, when ideas have sprouted in minds that have no connection with the blessed tree of life, that are entirely contrary to human nature, and as a result of which people have denied even the existence of Allah altogether. Certainly these are superficial ideas, and they have no root in existence and the cosmos. A time will surely come when these ideas will be completely eradicated, and not even their name or trace will remain. The formation, design and structure of the universe cannot bear these ideas. Such people are rejected by the nature of the cosmos, and they are intolerable because the roots of their ideas are not in the nature of the cosmos.

The doctrine of Tawhid is a necessary correction in man's outlook on life, and for the Islamic system of life it is the first brick. Therefore the Holy Qur'an repeatedly states the doctrine of Tawhid in various forms. This is the foundation and basis upon which Islam's moral system and its social organisation have been established. That is, the concept of the oneness of lordship in this universe: "Your God is One God" (wa-ilahukum ilahun wahid), and "There is no god but He, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful."

Emphasis, and repeated emphasis: the result of this emphasis on the oneness of divinity is that the object of worship becomes one, to whom all creation renders servitude and before whom it submits. A definite direction is fixed from which the whole of creation derives its morals and the principles and methods of its conduct, and that source and fountainhead is also fixed from which man derives the principles of law and legislation. And the single system of life is also fixed, which governs all the principles of human life.

As the context shows, here the Muslim ummah is being prepared for the great role it has to perform on the earth. In this connection, this truth is mentioned again here, the truth that is repeatedly mentioned in the Qur'an, which is that blessed tree of the Qur'an whose roots extend far into the earth and whose branches spread far across the sky of reason and consciousness, indeed encompassing this entire universe. The mention of this truth here is fixed so that it may be kept in view in all the legislation and codification of the Islamic society. What is that truth? It is the Divine Oneness (Tawhid al-Ilahi). Then here the attributes of Allah, Ar-Rahman and Ar-Rahim, are mentioned. The source and wellspring of all legislation and codification is this profound and all-encompassing attribute of Allah, the attribute of mercy.

This is the same way the whole cosmos and each of its passing scenes bear witness to Allah's mercy and His oneness.

This is a wholly new approach to awakening feeling and consciousness. Through contemplation of the world's wonders and a deep study of the universe, the doors of heart and vision are opened. Because we have grown accustomed to the wonders of this universe and see them day and night, their novelty and strangeness no longer affect our feeling and consciousness. The universe has become an ordinary thing for man. Therefore man has been told to return and look at this universe once more, with open eyes, keen feeling and a living heart, as though he were seeing it for the first time, and then to keep observing it again and again. In this way he will be able to make wondrous observations in this universe. Here there are countless scenes which, when man first cast his gaze upon them, dazzled his eyes and left his heart astonished. But then what happened? Those scenes became routine for heart and vision. He kept seeing this strange fair of the world every day, and became familiar with it. The turning of the days ceased to be a matter of wonder. Its uniqueness suddenly vanished, and these hair-raising natural scenes no longer attracted his gaze.

These heavens and earth, these fearful distances, these astonishing celestial bodies, these bewildering horizons, and then these countless known and unknown worlds, the movement of those worlds in this space, their orbits and courses, all these are things at the mere thought of which the head begins to spin. These mysteries of the universe that lie hidden behind the veil of the unseen, which peep into the human soul from behind the curtains of the cosmos: this great universe comprising heavens and earth. And yet man is unaware of these dimensions and distances, unaware of their size and magnificence, and incapable of grasping their secrets. Yes, when human perception advances and modern sciences and discoveries become its helpers and supporters, Allah Almighty will inform him of some hidden secrets. (In exact accordance with the prophecy of Sayyid Qutb the Martyr, this process is proceeding very rapidly. Translator.)

The alternation of night and day, the light and darkness chasing each other, the turning of morning and evening, this rising and that setting. The first glance would pinch the eye from the very beginning of creation, hearts would throb, and all these scenes were astonishing beyond measure for man. Then what happened? Man kept observing them again and again, and all this became a routine for him. Its novelty was gone, its attraction ended, and man became heedless. But the heart of the believer always remains awake. In his feeling these observations remain fresh and exactly as they are, renewed moment by moment. He always sees Allah in them, remembers Him, and he beholds these sights and wonders each time in such a way that it is as though a new world and a new creation have just been shown to him.

Look, a ship is passing carrying the needs of people (and I myself have felt a portion of this scene). What a sight it is! In a vast sea there is a black dot on which we are riding, which carries us along. On every side there are the blows of surging waves, and as far as the eye can see there is the expanse of the boundless blue ocean. The ship is moving, tilting this way, falling that way. There is no power here that can prevail except the power and protection of Allah. Here the law made by Allah reigns. It is a small dot, upon the fading lines of the waves, on the breast of a fearful boundless sea.

It is Allah alone who sends down water from the heights of the heavens. Gardens and orchards had been ruined, autumn held sway, the earth had died. Suddenly it becomes green and flourishing again. After death it lives again. Animals of every kind run about upon it, birds of every variety fly and chirp. Winds blow in which trees sway, and between heaven and earth clouds drift, yet they are held in captivity. What scenes these are! If man reflects upon them in the direction of the Qur'anic indications and from the Qur'anic viewpoint, then on seeing the great power of Allah and His vast attribute of mercy, his hair will stand on end. This life, whose perception is beyond us, whose subtle essence lies beyond the limits of perception, which appears on the earth with great delight, then suddenly unfolds before us and becomes powerful. A seed becomes a tree. Where did it come from? If life was hidden within the seed and the kernel, then where did the seed and the kernel come from? And how did this life enter them? What is its origin? What is its first source? You will not be able to escape.

Wait! Human nature insists that you answer this question. The atheists have always fled from answering this question. Indeed it is a very difficult question. Its answer is only this: there exists an absolutely Powerful Creator.

He is the One who gives life to the dead. The atheists of the West give people the impression that they are researching how to give life to dead matter, so that there would be no need to acknowledge Allah. But after striving continually, despite their disbelief and atheism, they were ultimately compelled to admit that they have failed in this matter. The creation of life is impossible. Today, in Russia, atheist biologists have been forced to announce that they are incapable of comprehending this secret. Even earlier, Darwin, a well-known scholar of biology, avoided answering this question.

And then these winds, now moving this way, now that way, carrying clouds upon their shoulders. The clouds are confined between heaven and earth. According to the laws that Allah has appointed on the earth, what is their reality? None knows except Allah. It is not enough merely to enumerate the causes of the blowing of the winds, to recite the theories of materialists, or to state that clouds form in such-and-such a way and rain falls in such-and-such a way. The secret lies elsewhere. The question is: what is the reality of these causes? Power, its source, its present balance, and its present laws, which provide life with this convenience. What is the head of the circle of the causes of life: clouds, rain and dew? These conveniences, which we have been able to discover, are thousands, and if even one of them were absent, life would suddenly cease to exist or would not proceed with such pleasant harmony as it does now. This intricate harmony of the elements of nature shows that life is not an accidental thing. Certainly behind it there is a will at work, an authority operating. This will is one. There is no duality in it. Why? Because there is no contradiction in it, and it is most compassionate, so each of its movements is supportive of life. (There are countless signs for those people who use their reason.) Worldly love and heedlessness have dulled man. If he were to strip away these veils of love and heedlessness from his mind, he would certainly be able to see these observations of nature with a fresh feeling and to see them with mature insight. He would be able to reflect with a heart filled with the light of faith. If he were to cast his gaze upon this earth like a newcomer who has descended upon this earth for the first time from some other world, then he would turn toward every gleam, his ears would attend to every sound, his feeling would note every movement, his heart, vision and consciousness would be struck by fresh experiences, and he would tremble with wonder and amazement.

This is the fruit of faith and its blessings: breadth of vision, depth of perception, beauty, harmony and perfect appreciation. The truth is that faith is a new way of perceiving this universe, and a new awareness of beauty and grace. Faith is, in essence, a joyful participation in the colourful festival of Allah's laws, in which from morning to evening a newer and newer spectacle of divine power is displayed.

Yet, despite these varied scenes of the workshop of life, there are also people who are bereft of the perception of reason. Their vision is short, and they overlook the such unity of the laws of nature and the single, orderly system by which this universe is run, which clearly points to the doctrine of Tawhid (the Oneness of Allah). They pass over all these things as if they were nothing, or they seek different gods and different causes for them.

﴿And among mankind are those who take, besides Allah, rivals (andad) whom they love as they should love Allah.﴾ 

Yes, there are some people who associate partners with Allah besides Him. Among the society to which the Qur'an was addressed, these rival gods were trees, stones, stars, angels and devils. In the various periods of ignorance (jahiliyyah), sometimes common things, sometimes individuals and persons, and sometimes signs and considerations have been rivals to Allah. At times this rivalry falls under the definition of hidden shirk (shirk khafi), and at other times it takes the form of manifest and open shirk (shirk zahir wa jali). When these things are mentioned alongside Allah and the heart holds for them the same greatness and love that should be held for Allah, this is hidden shirk. And if the state of affairs is that the love of Allah wholly departs from the heart and the love and greatness of something else takes its place, this is open shirk.

The attribute of the believers is that they do not hold any other thing in the same greatness as the love and greatness of Allah, nor do they acknowledge such greatness for anything: not for their own selves, nor for the lives of others, nor for any personality, nor for any sign or consideration, nor for any slogan or ideology, and not for any one of those modern values behind which God's creatures run today. In short, they maintain no bond or relationship with any one of these. ﴿But those who believe are stronger in their love for Allah.﴾ In the hearts of the believers there is intense love for Allah, pure love for Allah alone, without condition or measure, above all the other loves that they hold in their hearts for other things. The love of Allah is more intense and dominates every cause.

The relationship between the servant and Allah has been described in terms of love, and this is a very fine description. Between a true believer and the Exalted Lord there is a relationship of love: a relationship of heartfelt love, a bond of spiritual attraction, a relationship of nearness and friendship, and a relationship of a sincere and luminous feeling of love. This is not a official, governmental relationship of superior and subordinate.

These are the people who made others equal to Allah; they have truly wronged themselves. Would that they opened their eyes and reflected upon that scene, that one day they must stand before Allah, the One without partner. Would that they could see with the eye of insight the punishment that awaits the wrongdoers. Indeed, had they opened their eyes they would surely have seen that ﴿all power belongs to Allah entirely﴾. Therefore they should not associate anyone with Allah, nor make anyone His equal, and they would have come to know that ﴿Allah is severe in punishment.﴾

Oh, that they could see the scene in which the leaders disown their followers! They have already witnessed the punishment. The ties and friendships among them have been cut. The leaders and the followers are both in a state of every-man-for-himself. That leadership and that authority, on account of which the followers used to run after them, have collapsed. The leaders are concerned only with themselves. How can they pay heed to the honour of their followers, or how can they save them? Now the reality and power of the One God has become manifest. Now there is only one power before them. The falsehood of the misguided leaderships, their weakness, their helplessness before Allah, and their confusion and impotence before the punishment of Allah have all been exposed.

﴿And those who followed will say: "If only we had another chance, we would disown them just as they have disowned us."﴾ [2:167]

There, these deceived followers will express intense anger at their misguided leaders. They will wish that they might be given one more opportunity, and be returned to the earth, so that they could show their detachment from their weak, useless and deceitful leadership. How terrible is that scene: leaders and followers cursing one another, become enemies of each other, and friends of yesterday are today bitter foes. After this sorrowful end of theirs, the outcome is stated:

﴿Thus Allah will show them their deeds as regrets upon them, and they will never emerge from the Fire.﴾ [2:167]

That is, Allah will present their deeds, which they did in the world, before them in such a way that they will keep wringing their hands in regret and remorse, yet they will find no way to escape the Fire.

Now it is declared: enjoy the pure things of life, and keep away from the impure and wicked things. Beware! Do not obey Satan, for he constantly calls towards impure things. Satan declares some things lawful and some things unlawful in the name of Allah, whereas Allah has never given him the authority of legislating, making lawful and unlawful, and lawgiving. (Muslims are warned that in matters of their beliefs and ideologies they should seek guidance from no source other than Allah the Exalted.) Those who, leaving Allah, call upon things that neither hear nor understand, are warned about this foolish act. Thus the connection of meaning between these verses and the preceding verses also becomes clear.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 2, verses 168–169:

In the earlier verses, Allah informed us that He alone is the one God (Allah), that He alone is the Creator, and that a severe punishment awaits those who set up equals to Allah. Here it is stated that He is also the Provider of His servants, and that the authority to legislate regarding what is lawful (halal) and unlawful (haram) also belongs to Him alone. As we have explained, this is the natural fruit of the Oneness of Divinity (wahdat al-uluhiyyah). The One who created and then sustained is the only one entitled to legislate concerning what is lawful and unlawful, and legislation must be in harmony with the beliefs and principles of faith.

In this sentence, Allah proclaims that people should eat of what is lawful and pure on the earth, except for those things that have been made unlawful. In determining what is lawful and unlawful, seek guidance from Allah alone, and do not follow Satan in any of these matters. He is your enemy. He can never command you to do good. He only gives you false notions and encourages wrong deeds. He wishes that a person, of his own accord, should declare some things lawful and some unlawful, even though he has no proof or authority from Allah. Moreover, such a person may also believe that whatever he is doing is fully in accordance with the Shariah. This is what the Jews of Madinah and the polytheists of Makkah used to do regarding their beliefs, ideas, and actions.

(The command that all things on earth are permissible for you, except those that Allah has declared unlawful, shows that the Islamic way of life is a simple and comprehensive system. It is fully in harmony with the nature of this universe and with the nature of those who dwell in it. Allah created everything in the heavens and the earth for the benefit of mankind, and He has made their use lawful for them. Whether there is a specific prohibition regarding a thing, or no specific ruling at all, there remains the general principle that the use of anything should not exceed the bounds of moderation. But the fundamental policy is that benefiting from all pure things in the world is permissible, in accordance with the demands of human nature, without narrowness, harshness, or unjustified restrictions. There is only one condition: the decision about what is lawful and unlawful for people must rest with Allah alone, since it is Allah who created these good things. Therefore, the rulings of lawful and unlawful should not be taken from Satan, who is their clear enemy. He only commands them to evil and indecency. And without any evidence or certainty, Satan fabricates lies against Allah, and by attributing disbelief to Allah, he insults Him.)

And without any evidence or certainty, Satan fabricates lies against Allah, and by attributing disbelief to Allah, he insults Him.)

Who were these people? They may have been polytheists who kept repeating this argument: whenever they were invited to Islam and told to accept Islam as the source of their values and their law, and to abandon those practices of jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance before Islam) which Islam had not retained, they would give this very reply. The Jews may also be meant, for they held firmly to their traditions and were unwilling to accept any teaching of the religion of Islam. Whether the reference is to the polytheists or to the Jews, Islam strongly forbids its followers to take any element of belief or practice from these people. Muslims must not imitate them, nor import anything from them without thought and consideration.

﴿And when it is said to them, "Follow what Allah has revealed," they say, "Rather we follow what we found our fathers upon." Even though their fathers understood nothing and were not guided?﴾ "Even though their fathers understood nothing and were not guided": if their fathers had no understanding and found no right path, would they still insist on following them? What a vile example of blind imitation and rigidity this is. It is because of this blind imitation and rigidity that the Qur'an draws a repugnant picture of them. They are likened to an animal that understands nothing. If it is a herd animal, it hears only a voice and does not grasp what was said. Their condition is in fact worse than that of such an animal. The animal at least sees, hears and makes sounds, whereas these people are utterly blind, dumb and deaf.

Deaf, dumb and blind, they are. Although they have ears, eyes and tongues, why should they not be such, since despite these faculties they do not benefit from them, and do not find the path of guidance? Whoever has eyes but does not see is blind; whoever has ears but does not hear is deaf; whoever has a tongue but does not speak the truth is dumb.

Whoever abandons reflection and closes upon himself the doors of knowledge, insight, right conduct and guidance, and makes as the source and fountainhead of his outlook on life and his path of action that which is not truly a source or fountainhead and does not deserve to be one, then it is not possible to draw a more repugnant picture of such a person than this.

Now the address turns back to the believers. For them, the pure things of food and drink are declared lawful. They are commanded to give thanks to their Benefactor. Among impure things, some are expressly declared forbidden. The Jews used to create needless confusion for the Muslims regarding these good things and prohibited things. They are criticised, and it is pointed out that these commandments and principles of lawful and unlawful were in fact explicitly present among them as well.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 2, verse 172:

Here the Muslims are addressed with the words "O you who believe," because faith is the strong bond among the people of Islam. It is made known that I am the source of legislation, so take law from Me. Take the rulings of what is lawful and unlawful from Me. It is made known that you should remember the favours I have bestowed upon you. I am your Provider, and it is I who have declared the foods and drinks lawful for you. Not one of the good things has been declared unlawful. Those things that have been declared unlawful are not unlawful because Allah wishes to put you in hardship, but because, by their very nature, they are not pure and wholesome. It is He who has been providing you with sustenance since the beginning of creation. Then the admonition comes that if they desire to worship Allah alone, without partner, then they should give thanks to Him. Gratitude is also a form of worship and servitude. And Allah is greatly pleased when thanks are given. All these instructions have been given in this verse, which consists of a few words.

﴿O you who believe, eat of the good things that We have provided for you, and give thanks to Allah, if it is indeed Him whom you worship.﴾ "O believers, if you truly are those who worship Allah alone, then eat without hesitation of the pure things We have bestowed upon you, and give thanks to Allah."

Afterwards, certain specific items that have been declared forbidden are mentioned in particular. Using the exclusive particle "innama" (indeed only), the circle of prohibited things is restricted: ﴿Indeed, He has forbidden you only carrion, blood, the flesh of swine, and that over which other than Allah has been invoked.﴾ The meaning is: if there is any restriction upon you from Allah, it is this: do not eat the forbidden things. Abstain from blood and from the flesh of swine, and do not eat anything over which a name other than Allah's has been pronounced.

Every sound-natured person, by his disposition, dislikes carrion, and the same is true of blood. Yet beyond the aversion of nature, modern medicine too, a long time after the prohibition stated in the Qur'an and before it in the Torah, has made some valuable discoveries in this regard. For example, that blood and carrion gather many kinds of harmful substances and microbes (Microses). However, we have no certain knowledge that modern medicine has identified all the harms and impurities, and that no other reason for prohibition remains. It is possible that there are other reasons for the prohibition of these things that have not yet been known to us.

As for swine, some people still hold a favourable opinion of it. But sound human nature is even more intensely repulsed by it, and divine laws have prohibited it for a long time. Only recently has it become known that in its blood, flesh and intestines there is a dangerous worm. This worm is in the form of a long thread (Tapeworm), and its eggs are enclosed. Some apologists for pork say: the means of health and hygiene have advanced greatly, so these worms and their eggs are no longer harmful, because by high heat these eggs and worms are completely destroyed; and under modern means of health and hygiene these facilities are available everywhere. But these people do not consider that after long ages their scientific struggle discovered only one harmful worm. What proof is there that the flesh of swine does not contain some other harmful substance that has not been revealed? The divine Shari'ah, which prohibited this harmful thing thousands of years ago, long before human knowledge and awareness, deserves that complete trust be placed in it, that its judgment be regarded as the final word, and that what it has made lawful be deemed lawful and what it has made unlawful be deemed unlawful. This is because this Shari'ah has been revealed from Allah, the All-Wise, the All-Aware.

Those things over which a name other than Allah's has been pronounced, or whose owners have directed them towards other than Allah, are also forbidden. This is because there is no reason in the very nature of these things for their prohibition; it is merely because their orientation has been turned towards other than Allah. The focus of attention has changed, the conscience is no longer pure, the soul is no longer clean, the heart is no longer whole for Allah, and belief and outlook are no longer pure. This is the spiritual cause for which the use of these things has been made forbidden, and it becomes impure in the same way that material impurity is impure. Therefore this is also not wholesome (tayyib), and that is also not wholesome. Since Islam emphasises that the Muslim should turn, with reverence and honour, only towards the Divine Court, and should not associate anyone else with it, these things have also been declared impure and placed alongside the impure-in-essence items, because these things are impure in terms of belief.

Purity of heart and outlook, and of body and liver, is the common factor among the causes of all these forbidden things. Since the preceding verses expounded the doctrine of Tawhid, the meaning was that your Creator and Provider is one; here it is said that the Legislator and Lawgiver is also He. The source of provision and creation and the origin of law and Shari'ah are one. In these verses this concept creates a deep connection.

Despite this prohibition, Islam also takes account of certain circumstances and necessity. In such circumstances it permits these prohibited things in a limited way, to the minimum extent of necessity, but it guides that the limit of necessity must in no way be exceeded: ﴿Whoever is compelled, neither desiring nor transgressing, then there is no sin upon him. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ This principle of exception is general in itself, but here it is connected with the prohibitions mentioned above. However, this principle may also apply to other prohibitions besides these: where there is such necessity, where life is in danger and nothing other than these prohibited things is at hand, then the forbidden thing may be used there too, to the minimum extent needed to meet the necessity. Regarding the places of necessity, there are juristic differences among the jurists: for instance, will analogy (qiyas) apply in the matter of necessity, or will benefit be confined only to what is explicitly stated? Further, what is the measure for meeting the necessity? Is it the minimum use, or is it eating to satiety? I do not wish to go into the details of these differences here. What has been said is sufficient for Fi Zilal al-Quran.

Regarding the things that were declared lawful or unlawful, the Jews had begun to raise a clamour, as the Qur'an has clarified elsewhere. Some things were forbidden only to the Jews: ﴿And upon those who became Jews, We forbade every animal with claws; and of cattle and sheep We forbade them their fats, except what their backs carry or the entrails or what is mixed with bone.﴾ These things were permissible for Muslims. Presumably they were strongly objecting to this permissibility. Some narrations also mention that they objected even to the prohibition of those things which are forbidden here, although these things had been stated in their own Torah to be forbidden to them as well. Their aim was only to somehow cast doubt upon the Qur'anic injunctions and to place in the hearts of the Muslims the doubt of whether revelation from Allah comes to the Messenger (ﷺ) or not.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 2, verse 174:

The verses address, in the strongest terms, those who conceal the commands of Allah revealed in the divine scriptures.

Who were those who concealed the commands of Allah? First and foremost, they are the People of the Book (Ahl al-Kitab).
