The believers are addressed with the title of faith, which is very dear to them, which grants them distinction, and which sets them apart from others. It is the sole bond between them and the one who calls them, and between them and their Lord. The believers are called and invited with the summons: enter fully into Islam!

The first and initial meaning of this call is that the believers should completely surrender before Allah, and that their whole being, in every matter great and small, should become for Allah. Not a single part of their thoughts and their consciousness, their intention and their action, their desire and their contentment, should remain free. They should enter fully into Islam. They should become entirely subject to Allah, belong to Allah in every matter, and be pleased with Allah's decree. They should hand over the reins of their lives, with complete certainty and tranquility, to the hand that is leading them. They should be fully assured that their leader wants nothing but goodness, sincere counsel and right guidance. They should be satisfied that the path on which they are travelling, and the destination toward which they are heading, is the truth, and that in it lies the success of this world and the Hereafter.

At this stage, the call to complete submission shows that until now there were people in the ranks of the Muslims whose hearts harboured hesitation and doubt, who were not yet convinced that they must obey fully, outwardly and inwardly, in every way. And this is no cause for surprise. In movements, on one side there are satisfied, mature and obedient people, while alongside them there are also people who have weaknesses. This call and this summons is one that will continue to be given to the believers at all times, that they should become sincere and single-minded. The beats of their hearts, their consciousness and their inclinations should align with Allah's command and Allah's will. They should belong to Allah, who leads them to their Prophet and to their own system, without any hesitation, without any doubt, and with complete single-mindedness.

When a believer accepts this call, with an open and content heart and fully, he steps into a world that is a world of peace, a world of safety. He enters a realm that is a realm of tranquility, a realm of pleasure and calm. He arrives in a world in which there is neither bewilderment nor anxiety, in which there is neither corruption nor misguidance, where he is in harmony with every person and every living being. Where there is harmony with existence and with all that exists. Where there is calm in the most hidden and secret corners of the human soul, and calm in the outer and collective life of man. A world in which the earth is at peace and in whose faith there is also certainty and tranquility.

The first effect of this peace upon the believing heart is that he receives a correct conception of his Allah and his Lord. This conception is both pure and clean: that He is the one God, that the believer turns only to Him, and that He is his qiblah. Then the believer becomes firmly settled in this, and his heart becomes at rest. Now there are no more different paths and no more different qiblahs. He no longer has that condition; he turns with the utmost tranquility, the utmost certainty, the utmost correctness and the utmost clarity.

He is a God who is Mighty and powerful, who is dominant and capable. When the believer turns to Him, he turns to a tremendous power of truth, which is the sole power in this universe. Now he will live a life of tranquility and rest, and he will have no fear of any false power. He will fear nothing; he will worship a God who is mighty and powerful, dominant and possessed of power. Therefore he will no longer have any fear of being deprived of anything. He will neither fear such powers nor hope from such powers as have neither the power to give nor the power to deprive.

He is a just and wise God. His power and His might are themselves a guarantee against oppression, a guarantee against base desires, a guarantee against deceit. He is not a god like the idols of ignorance, whose conception is bound up with the conception of base impulses and lusts. This is why, when a person enters Islam, he leaves false gods behind and takes refuge in a firm Being, from whom he receives justice, receives peace, and receives special favour and honour.

He is a Lord who is most merciful, most compassionate, the Bestower of blessings. He is the Giver, the Forgiver of sins, the Acceptor of repentance. He hears the call of the afflicted and responds to it. He removes their affliction. Therefore a Muslim lives within the shelter of His kindness, feeling at ease and secure, in safety and in enjoyment. If he becomes weak, he is shown mercy; if he repents, he is forgiven.

After entering Islam, the believer is first introduced by Islam to the attributes of this Lord of his. The believer continues to study these attributes. In each attribute he finds a meaning with which his heart grows familiar. His soul becomes progressively more tranquil, and he receives from his worshipped Lord support, protection, kindness, mercy, honour, nobility, peace and a guarantee of security.

Within the system of peace into which this believer enters, he receives a correct conception of the relationship between the servant and God. It also gives him correct thinking about the relationship between Allah and the servant, and between man and this universe. For example, that it is Allah who created this universe with truth. Then in this universe He created everything in perfect measure with wisdom. Then He created man in this universe in accordance with a wisdom. Therefore he will not be left to roam freely. Allah has made the entire cosmic environment such that all of it, and every part of it, is a means of life for human beings. Then He established man's dominion over whatever is in the earth. Before Allah, too, man is a highly honoured creature. On this earth he is Allah's khalifah and deputy. In carrying out this office of khilafah, Allah Himself is his helper. And then this universe spread around this man is also his companion, intimate with him. The spirit of the universe is in harmony with the spirit of man. This universe also glorifies Allah, and man too extols Him. What is the universe? Rather, it is a fair spread across the heavens and the earth, which the Omnipotent has established for the delight of this man and has invited him to take part in this fair, to fill its emptiness and to become familiar with it. He has been told to love every thing in this vast universe, to show affection for each of its aspects. In this universe there are countless companions, and they too have arrived at this fair by special invitation. In short, all things in the universe, whether lifeless or living, are all members of this festival of spring and deserve affection.

This system of peace gives the Muslim a vision of life. With this vision, if he looks at a humble plant that needs water, and then waters it, helps it grow, and removes the difficulties in its way, then according to this vision of life he will be rewarded for this act alone. What a beautiful vision! What a precious vision! It fills the soul of one who believes with peace. He becomes a companion of this whole universe and embraces every existing thing. He becomes like a lamp that continually radiates peace, safety, gentleness and love on every side.

Then within this system there is the belief in the Hereafter. This belief plays a very important role in the soul of the believer and in the believer's world. Peace descends upon him. Every kind of restlessness, anxiety, despair and irritation is removed from his life. Because the reckoning does not end in this world; it is not necessary that everything be settled in full in this world. The real reckoning will take place in the court of the Absolute Just One. Therefore, if he does good, strives in the way of Allah, and is not successful in this world and receives no reward for it, he feels no remorse. He does not become troubled that in this world, by the standards of worldly people, he has received no reward. If he has not received it, let it be. Soon he will receive it according to Allah's measure, and in full. When rights are distributed unjustly in this world, and are distributed contrary to his wishes, he does not lose hope regarding justice, for a court will certainly be set up, whose officer is the Lord of the worlds, who does not even intend oppression against His servants, let alone commit it.

In this world a frenzied struggle is underway. In this struggle, noble values are generally being trampled, honours are being plundered. Rights are trampled with shamelessness and immodesty, but the believer who has entered this system of life of peace and harmony stays far from it. It is this belief in the Hereafter that keeps him away from filth; he keeps his gaze fixed on the Hereafter. There is generosity and reward there; there is making up for what was lost there; there is bounty and sufficiency there. This world is a field of mutual competition, a battleground of mutual envy and hypocrisy.

This vision of life showers the believing heart with peace, safety, patience and contentment. When he observes the movements of those who take part in this race, these do not seem good to him. Man naturally has the awareness that life is brief and that the moments of leisure are few. In this race of life, this awareness then grows more and more intense. But the belief in the Hereafter in the Islamic vision of life reduces the intensity of this thirst.

Then in this system of peace and harmony, the purpose and goal for which man was brought into existence, and the aim of his creation, is declared to be the worship and servitude of Allah. He was created only so that he might serve Allah. The truth is that in this way he becomes a high and bright star on a lofty horizon. His character and his consciousness become elevated. His deeds and his activities become elevated. His means and his resources become pure. In all his deeds and all his activities he becomes a servant of Allah. His earning and his spending also become acts of worship. When he attains the office of khilafah on earth and establishes here the Islamic system of life, he is still engaged in worship. As a result of this conception of worship, servitude and slavery, a Muslim is neither a traitor nor a wrongdoer; he is neither a deceiver nor a cheat, neither an oppressor nor a tyrant. He does not employ impure means to achieve his goal, nor does he resort to base methods. He does not even become impatient to reach his destination. He does not act in haste or hurry, and he does not entangle himself in worldly difficulties. With pure intention, with continuous action, within the limits of his capacity, he keeps advancing toward his objective. The result of all these things is that no fear and no greed can influence his self. At no stage of this journey of life does he become restless, because at every step he is in the worship of Allah. Therefore he confronts every danger, because that is his purpose of creation. In short, he keeps advancing toward heights in every activity and every field, toward Allah, the Lord of the worlds, and his Creator. The believer's consciousness that he is a companion of Allah's destiny, that he is travelling on the highway of destiny, that he is in the worship of Allah, and that he is a manifestation of the Divine will, showers his soul with tranquility. His vessel of the heart is filled with calm and rest. Without any bewilderment, without any restlessness, without any irritation, and without taking hardships and difficulties into account, he proceeds toward the destination of his goal. He does not despair of the help and support of Allah. Nor does he fear that his objective will vanish from his sight or that his reward will be lost. For this reason, he is also in a state of battle with his enemies, the enemies of Allah, yet his spirit possesses steadiness and tranquility, because he is fighting neither for position and rank, nor for wealth and spoils, nor for any of the worldly aims.

The believing heart carries the awareness that in this whole universe he is a companion of the Sunnah of Allah. Its law is the law of nature. Its direction is the same direction as the nature of the universe. Therefore there is no conflict between him and the forces of nature; there is no war between him and the realities of nature. Thus the natural powers of the believer and the powers of this universe come into harmony. They are not scattered or dispersed as a result of clashing with each other. Rather, all the powers of this universe join with the powers of a Muslim. These powers too seek their destination by the same light by which the believing man seeks it. In short, all the powers of the universe are moving toward Allah, and the believing man too is moving in that same direction.

Islam's obligations for Muslims are natural. They are meant to correct human nature. All of them lie within the limits of human capacity, and they take full account of man's temperament and his created constitution. Islam leaves none of man's faculties idle. Every faculty is engaged in work and plays its part in growth, development and progress. It neglects none of man's spiritual or physical needs. Rather, it fulfils all the natural impulses of man with great ease, great gentleness and great generosity. Therefore, in acting upon these acts of worship, the person faces no difficulty and does not have to struggle against restlessness. He acts upon these acts of worship and obligations according to his strength and ability, and with great tranquillity of heart and great spiritual peace he continually travels his path to its destination. Where to? To his Creator and Lord.

Islam, that is, the divine system of life, gives birth to a society that is also a beacon of peace and security. This beacon continually sheds the light of peace and tranquillity from a lofty place. This society arises as a result of this system, whose buds sprout from the precious and beautiful tree of the worldview that is firmly established in the heart of the believer. This society grows under the divine guarantees of the protection of life, the protection of honour and the protection of property (guarantees).

It is a society whose members are brothers, who love one another, are bound to one another, support one another, and collectively stand as guarantors (social sureties) for one another, and in which every part is in harmony with the other parts. History records that Islam once actually brought such a society into existence, in a very elevated and refined form, in its developed state. Even in the later periods of Islamic history, such societies continued to emerge. Though, by their standards, some were weaker and some were better, nevertheless, despite their weaknesses, they remained higher than all those societies that ever came into existence, whether in the era of ancient Jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance before Islam) or in the era of modern Jahiliyyah, and even higher than those societies which, though not ignorant, have become mixed with Jahiliyyah, which have become polluted by it, and in whose thought and collective order only worldly concepts prevail.

Such an Islamic society has only one bond among its individuals and components, namely the bond of the worldview. It is a very broad ideological society. All nationalisms, all national boundaries, all languages and all colours melt and vanish in comparison with it. In short, all false notions of nationalism, linguism, patriotism, and the intellectual tribulations of colour and race, which have no connection with man's humanity, all melt and are absorbed into this broadly based Islamic society.

Listen! Here are God's instructions concerning this society: "Indeed, the believers are but brothers" (Surah al-Hujurat: 10). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) drew the best picture of this society in a well-known hadith: "In terms of mutual love, mutual compassion and mutual kindness, the believers are like a single body. If one organ of the body is in pain, the whole body becomes restless. The whole body wakes up and a state of fever arises in the whole body." (Narrated by Imam Ahmad)

Look how beautiful the general etiquettes of this society are: "And when someone greets you with a greeting, respond with a better greeting, or at least return it" (Surah an-Nisa: 86). Similarly: "And do not turn your face away from people in contempt, nor walk in the earth arrogantly. Indeed, Allah does not like everyone self-conceited and boastful" (Surah Luqman: 8). "Repel evil with that which is better, and then the one between whom and you there is enmity will become as though he were a close friend" (Surah Fussilat: 34). "O you who have believed, let not a people ridicule [another] people; perhaps they may be better than them; nor let women ridicule [other] women; perhaps they may be better than them. And do not defame one another, nor call each other by [offensive] nicknames. Wretched is the name of disobedience after faith. And whoever does not repent, it is those who are the wrongdoers" (Surah al-Hujurat: 11). "And let not some of you backbite others. Would one of you like to eat the flesh of his brother when dead? You would detest it. And fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Accepting of repentance and Merciful" (Surah al-Hujurat: 12).

This society is one that gives itself these guarantees (securities): "O you who have believed, if a deviator brings you a report, verify it, lest you harm a people out of ignorance and then become regretful for what you have done" (Surah al-Hujurat: 6). "O you who have believed, avoid much suspicion, for indeed some suspicion is sin, and do not spy" (Surah al-Hujurat: 12). "O you who have believed, do not enter houses other than your own until you have asked permission and greeted their occupants" (Surah an-Nur: 27).

"Every Muslim is inviolable to another Muslim: his blood, his honour and his property."

This pure society is such that indecency cannot spread within it. Immodesty is not approved in it. Tribulation is not customary in it. Nakedness does not spread in it. Eyes do not even turn towards hidden parts of the body. In it, people's chastity is protected from free sexual indulgence. In it, sexual desires and the union of blood and flesh are not left free in the manner they are in the system of Jahiliyyah, whether ancient or modern. In this matter, the Islamic society is governed by divine instructions and it constantly listens to the words of its Lord. You too listen: "Indeed, those who like that immorality should spread among the believers will have a painful punishment in this world and the Hereafter. And Allah knows, while you know not" (Surah an-Nur: 19). "The adulteress and the adulterer, flog each one of them with a hundred lashes. And let not pity for them prevent you from [applying] the law of Allah, if you should believe in Allah and the Last Day. And let a group of the believers witness their punishment" (Surah an-Nur: 2). "And those who accuse chaste women and then do not produce four witnesses, lash them with eighty lashes and never accept their testimony, and they are the defiantly disobedient" (Surah an-Nur: 4). "O Prophet, tell the believing men to lower their gaze and guard their private parts; that is purer for them. Indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what they do. And tell the believing women to lower their gaze and guard their private parts and not expose their adornment except that which appears thereof, and to wrap their headcoverings over their chests, and not expose their adornment except to their husbands, their fathers, their husbands' fathers, their sons, their husbands' sons, their brothers, their brothers' sons, their sisters' sons, their women, those their right hands possess, or those male attendants having no physical desire, or children who are not yet aware of the private aspects of women. And let them not stamp their feet to make known what they conceal of their adornment. And turn to Allah in repentance, all of you, O believers, that you might be successful" (Surah al-Ahzab: 59 and Surah an-Nur: 31).

Then the Qur'an itself addresses the wives of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who were the purest women on the surface of the earth, in the purest home, in the purest family, and in the purest era: "O wives of the Prophet, you are not like anyone among the women. If you fear Allah, then do not be soft in speech, lest one in whose heart is disease should covet; but speak with appropriate speech. And abide in your houses and do not display yourselves as in the display of the former time of ignorance. And establish prayer, give zakah, and obey Allah and His Messenger. Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you with [complete] purification" (Surah al-Ahzab: 32–33).

In such a society, the wife has confidence in her husband, and the husband has confidence in his wife. Parents and guardians are content regarding their honour and chastity. People have confidence in their hearts and their nerves. Temptations are hidden from sight, so they cannot pull hearts towards what is forbidden. By contrast, the present state of Western countries is that furtive glances are exchanged at all times. The members of that society must constantly suppress their desires, and as a result they fall victim to many kinds of psychological illnesses. Tension is constantly present in their nerves, whereas the pure and chaste society of Islam remains composed at all times. Over this society, the broad veils of peace, purity and security always cast their shade.

And finally, this society guarantees lawful livelihood and employment to everyone who has the ability to work. This society guarantees a dignified life and suitable necessities of life to every disabled person. For the one who wishes to live a life of chastity and purity, this society provides facilities for lawful marriage. He receives a righteous life companion. It is such a society that if someone in one of its neighbourhoods dies of hunger, it holds the entire neighbourhood legally responsible for the death and imposes penal conditions upon them. Some jurists and legal experts have written that the residents of the neighbourhood must pay the blood money (diyah) of that person as compensation.

Then, looking from another angle, this society guarantees its members civil liberties. In it, people's nobility, their honour, and their lives and property are protected by law. This guarantee is given by the Absolute Legislator Himself, the Lord of Majesty, who is obeyed, and in this society His every word is law. Therefore, in this society no one will be seized merely on the basis of suspicion. No one can snatch another's right to privacy by scaling his wall. No one can spy against another. In this society, if someone's blood is shed, it will not go unavenged, rather retaliation (qisas) will be enforced. Someone's property will not be lost through theft or robbery, because the legal punishments (hudud) are enforced in it.

Then the political system of this society is founded on consultation (shura), cooperation, freedom of opinion, and the guarantee of the right of criticism (nasihah, sincere counsel). In this society all people are equal in the eyes of justice and law. Every member of it is aware that every legal judgment concerning him is from Allah. It is the judgment of Allah's law; in it there is no interference from the ruler of the time, nor from any of his courtiers, nor from the officials of the government or their relatives.

In short, among all human societies, this is the only society in which man is not subject to man, rather all people, whether rulers or ruled, in every case are subject to Allah and His Shari'ah. Both rulers and ruled implement the Shari'ah of Allah, and therefore all of them, with equality and parity, with full faith, full conviction and full certainty, stand step by step before Allah, Lord of the worlds and the Most Wise of judges.

All these meanings fall within the concept of al-Muslim (the one who submits), which is used in the verse, and in which the believers are invited to enter fully, so that they may surrender their selves to Allah, in such a way that no part of their selves remains for themselves, but all of it becomes Allah's, in obedience, submission, acceptance and contentment.

A correct understanding of this concept of peace and security can be attained only when we study those societies which are unfamiliar with Islam, or which are familiar with Islam but have nevertheless become estranged from it and have returned to the system of Jahiliyyah, and which at different times have adopted for themselves various names and titles. The condition of these societies is that they are afflicted with uncertainty. They are devoid of faith. Their members are beset by psychological and nervous troubles and restlessness. These societies have reached the high standard of civilizational progress. In them all facilities have reached their extreme, and all those amenities are abundant which any misguided Jahili civilization considers necessary for progress.

Study this example. Sweden is the most developed of all countries in the world, where five hundred pounds per year is spent from national wealth on each individual. Where healthcare is guaranteed for every person. Where cash is paid for treatment, and treatment in hospitals is free. Where education at every stage is completely free, where every student is given a clothing allowance, and deserving students are also given loans. Where the government gives a marriage allowance of three hundred pounds so that household goods can be purchased. In short, there are many other facilities and conveniences available to the public there. But what are the results of this material progress and civilizational comforts, when the hearts of these children of civilization are empty of faith?

The condition of this nation is that, because of free sexual intermingling, the whole nation is continuously declining physically. Because of free sexual intermingling, tempting nakedness and free sexual misconduct, every sixth marriage ends in divorce. The modern generation has become badly addicted to narcotics. By using these narcotics, these people fill that spiritual void and seek a substitute for the dissatisfaction that arises from uncertainty. Psychological diseases, nervous diseases and sexual diseases, like an epidemic, attack their minds, their nerves and their souls, and thousands of people are badly afflicted by them. This restlessness reaches its extreme when a person, exhausted, decides to commit suicide.

The condition of America is similar, rather worse than this. And the conditions of Russia are even worse than this.

This bitterness and misfortune is destined for every person whose heart is empty of the joy of faith, empty of the cheerfulness of belief. Such a person can never enjoy peace and security, into which entry in its entirety is being called upon the Muslims, so that they may live happily under its shade in peace, comfort, tranquility and contentment.

O you who believe! Enter into Islam (al-silm) wholly, and do not follow the footsteps of Satan. Indeed, he is a clear enemy to you. (2:208)

Along with the call to enter wholly into this peace and security (Islam), the Muslims are being warned: you must never follow Satan. For there are only two paths: one is the path of Islam, the path of safety, and the other is the path of Satan's footsteps. On one side is the way of guidance, on the other the way of misguidance. On one side is Islam, and on the other is Jahiliyyah (the state of ignorance before divine guidance). It is either the path of Allah or the path of Satan, either the guidance of Allah or the misguidance (ghawayah) of Satan. The Muslims should understand well the decisive nature of their stance; therefore they should not allow any hesitation or confusion to approach them in this matter, and they should not become bewildered for a single moment upon seeing the various paths.

The truth is that a believer has not been given the freedom to choose for himself one system of life out of many, or to combine parts of one or two systems and fashion a third system. There are only two paths: truth or falsehood, guidance or error, Islam or Jahiliyyah; it is either the system of life of Allah or the misguidance of Satan. Here in this verse, Allah calls upon the Muslims to enter wholly into this system of peace, and secondly He forbids them from following Satan. Here their conscience and consciousness are being awakened. They are being alerted by reminding them of Satan's age-old enmity. It is made known that the enmity Satan holds towards you is not a hidden or concealed enmity; it is perfectly clear and manifest. Only the one who is heedless can forget it, and heedlessness and faith cannot be gathered in one place.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 2, verse 209:

Now it is explained that if, even after these instructions and clear guidance, you stumble, then your end will not be good. ﴿Then if you slip after clear proofs have come to you, then know that Allah is Mighty and Wise.﴾ That is: if, after the clear guidance has come to you, you slip after having received it, then know well that Allah is Dominant and the Ruler over all.

"He is Mighty (ʿAziz) and Dominant (Ghalib)." The allusion here is that He possesses power and dominance. If they oppose the commands of Allah, they will have to face the overpowering might of Allah. And "He is Wise (Hakim), the Possessor of wisdom." The allusion here is that the system of life He has prescribed for you is good, and that which He has forbidden you is in truth bad for you. And if they do not follow the commands of Allah and do not refrain from the things He has forbidden, they will suffer severe loss. Therefore, both parts of this conclusion and summary are in fact a severe warning and a threat.

Now, from this point, a new style is adopted for warning and intimidation. It is explained what the consequences can be of not living up to Islam and of following Satan. Now the mode of address is abandoned and third-person forms are used.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah al-Baqarah, verse 210:

The particle "hal" (هل) in Arabic introduces a question that also carries an expression of disapproval. The reasons are explained in answer to it, for which some opponents hesitate to accept Islam and do not enter fully into Islam. What is the reason that they do not accept this call of Islam? What are they waiting for? Will they keep waiting in this manner without any reason, and will Allah come down in a canopy of clouds, with the angels also arriving? In other words, are these people waiting for that terrifying Day about which Allah has said that Allah will come in a canopy of clouds, with the angels arrayed in rows, and no one will speak except the one whom Allah permits, and he will speak what is right.

Suddenly ........ While we were still pondering this threatening question, suddenly we see that the Day has indeed arrived and the matter has indeed been decided. The affair is over. Before the people suddenly appears the scene with which they were being warned, to which a reference was being made. "Qudiya al-amr" ("and the matter has been decided"): the record of time has been rolled up and put away. The opportunities of leisure have ended. Salvation has become difficult. Now it is as if people are standing before Allah, before Allah to whom all affairs must be presented: "wa ila Allahi turja'u al-umur" ("all affairs will be returned to Allah").

This is the unique style of the Qur'an. In contrast to all other speeches and writings, this style gives it a distinctive status. Its method is that the Qur'an, within a few moments, presents any scene in a living and moving form. A person feels as though he is standing before that scene; he sees, he hears, and with his own eyes he seems to inspect that scene.

How long will these people remain behind and not enter into that peace? The terrifying Day awaits them. Rather, it is about to come upon them suddenly. And peace is near to them: the peace of this world and the peace of the Hereafter, on the Day when the heavens will be split open with clouds and the angels will be descending. On the Day when the Spirit and the angels stand in ranks, no one will speak except the one whom the Most Merciful permits, and who speaks what is right; that is the Day when Allah will decide. Behold, as if He has settled the matters, and all matters must ultimately be returned to Allah. "Wa ila Allahi turja'u al-umur."

Now in this style of speech there comes another sudden shift. The address turns to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He is told to ask the Children of Israel. The Children of Israel were the leaders of those who hesitated and held back from accepting the call of Islam. In this context it is said about them: "Allah showed them countless clear signs, yet even then they did not accept the call. Rather, they chose disbelief over the blessing of faith and peace, although these blessings had been sent to them by Allah through a Messenger."

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 2, verse 211:

The discourse turns back again to the Children of Israel, and this is a natural matter. A warning is given: do not adopt the stance of the Children of Israel, for in it lies destruction. It is the stance of hesitation and the denial of truth, the stance of rebellion and of fleeing from peace, the stance of obstinacy and of repeatedly demanding miracles, and the stance of continuing to harbour hostility and denial even after seeing miracles. These are the places where the feet may slip and the foot of steadfastness may stumble. Therefore Allah, the Exalted, forewarns the Muslims in advance, so that the Muslims do not reach a bitter end like the Children of Israel.

﴿Ask the Children of Israel how many clear signs We gave them.﴾ And (ask them as well) how severely Allah punishes the people who exchange the blessing of Allah after it has come to them, with wickedness.

The question is not meant to be that the Messenger ﷺ should go and ask the Children of Israel and that they should give some answer. This is one of the styles of the Qur'an. The purpose is to remind that many miracles were presented before the Children of Israel. Countless clear signs kept coming before them. Some signs were shown at their insistence and demand, and some miracles were manifested by Allah Himself for some wisdom of that time. Yet despite the abundance of miracles, what was their conduct? Hesitation and breaking of promises, obstinacy and wavering. Yet they continually remained far from the shade of peace and security which is cast only over the enclosure of faith......

Upon this there follows a general admonition: ﴿And whoever exchanges the blessing of Allah after it has come to him, indeed Allah is severe in punishment.﴾ The advice mentioned here is either Islam, or by it is meant the blessing of faith; the two are nearly synonymous. The supreme example of exchanging the blessing of Allah for wickedness will be found in the history of the Children of Israel. When they exchanged the blessing for wickedness, they were deprived of tranquillity, peace and calm. They refused to submit with acceptance and contentment. They did not bow before the guidance of Allah. They always adopted the attitude of doubt and hesitation. At every step they kept demanding miracles, and at every stage they kept asking for proofs, yet neither were they satisfied by miracles nor were they convinced by clear proofs. They did not benefit from the light and guidance of Allah. And the supreme example of ﴿fear the severe punishment of Allah﴾ is also the history of the Children of Israel. And all those people, in every age and every place, who choose wickedness and misfortune over the blessing of Islam, and then take pride in it, await its evil end (history bears witness that such people met the same end as the Children of Israel).

Whenever humanity has exchanged this supreme blessing for wickedness and misfortune, it has been given punishment, severe beyond measure, even before the Hereafter, in this worldly life. Just cast a glance at the wretched state of humanity spread across the earth! Is it not suffering a severe punishment? Do you not see that everywhere it finds only misfortune and bitterness? Everywhere it is afflicted with bewilderment and restlessness. Man is devouring man, rather man is devouring his own soul and his own nerves. The individual runs in search of humanity, and humanity is in search of the individual. Yet both are running after an empty mirage. In short, in the world of humanity at present there is a deadly void. Some so-called sons of the civilisation of the West try to fill this void, but sometimes through the use of intoxicants and sometimes through excessive use of narcotics. At times such people commit acts that leave a person astonished. It seems that they are running away and some dreadful herd is chasing them.

Just study the outward appearance of the sons of Western civilisation. They make strange shapes and then display them. A woman has her head bowed. Someone has his chest entirely bare. Someone wears a mini skirt. Someone has made a hat that looks like an animal placed on the head. Some have tied ties bearing the picture of an elephant, and worn shirts bearing the picture of a lion or a bear.

Indeed, take one look! Their frenzied dancing, provocative songs, artificial lifestyle, colourful clothing at gatherings and assemblies, making unusual and eye-catching shapes to draw people's attention, and satisfying their emotions by distinguishing themselves in strange ways.

Take a look also at the changing desires of these people. Desires change, husbands change, friends change, clothes change, in every season, indeed every morning and evening.

All these things show that this society is afflicted with anguish, restlessness, bewilderment and turmoil, in which there is no tranquillity and no security. It appears that the condition of these nations has fallen to a frightful degree. Therefore these people are fleeing from their society and their civilisation. But alas, they find no path. It seems as though the soul of the sons of civilisation is empty. They are running away from their own shadows, as if jinn and ghouls are pursuing them.

Is this not the punishment of Allah? Certainly it is a punishment, and it is for every person who does not adopt the Islamic system of life, who does not heed the call of Allah: ﴿O you who believe, enter into peace completely.﴾

In short, firm conviction in Allah's favours is not changed by anything, except that if someone is seized by this punishment of the Lord, then firm faith certainly perishes. Allah forbid.

Earlier it was explained that those who hesitate to accept the call of Islam, and take wickedness and misfortune in exchange for the blessing, await a severe punishment. Now it is shown what the paradise of the Muslims is, what their end will be, what the condition of the disbelievers is and what their end will be. It is shown what the scale of the Muslims is for determining the worth of individuals and for weighing conditions and values of life, and what the scale of the disbelievers is.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 2, verse 212:

The worldly life, its base and temporary things and its small necessities, has been made appealing and adorned for the disbelievers. These things pleased them so much that they became wholly absorbed in them and did not advance. Their gaze became fixed upon them, and they could not reach the realities beyond them. Such people know nothing of lofty values apart from these base things, and whoever becomes entangled in the world reaches only the furthest limit of the world. It is not possible that their intellect and thought can attain those lofty goals which are the focus of the attention of the true believer, and which the lofty vision of the believer has found far off, on the highest horizons.

Sometimes it happens that a believer completely disregards basic provisions. This is not because he is lacking in resolve, nor because he has no capacity for acquiring worldly things, nor because he is negative in outlook and has no interest in the progress and development of the world. It happens merely because he casts a dismissive glance upon this temporary world from a very lofty station, although he is the vicegerent of Allah on this earth, and its care is his responsibility. He takes part in its construction and progress; he improves its civilisation and its productive capacity; yet from among all the varied colours of that station he selects for himself that supreme purpose which is very exalted, sublime and precious. His choosing gaze falls upon the need for a system of life for this world. Humanity wanders searching for potsherds and clay, whereas its guidance should reach the mine where there are pearls and nothing but pearls. The banner of Allah should be raised over the heads of people and on the peaks of the earth, so that humanity may progress to that lofty station. Humanity should lift its eyes from the base and degraded things of this world and look beyond, to what lies beyond this palace of the world.

The truth is that those in whose hearts there is no spark of faith are deprived of great purposes, lofty aims and breadth of thought and vision, and such people are slaves of the world and are called servants of the world.

These short-sighted and dwarf-statured people, entangled in the defilements of the earth, these servants of worldly ends and self-interested people, look upon the believers with great contempt. They see that these people have left all the pollutions, all the impurities and all the base provisions of the world open for these disbelievers, while they carry in their breasts pure and lofty aspirations; and these aspirations are not related to their own selves alone, but are aspirations of all humanity. These desires are related not merely to their own selves, but are desires of their way of life. Indeed, they are the aspirations of all humanity. These desires are related not merely to their own selves, but are desires of their way of life. Indeed, they are the aspirations of all humanity. These desires are related not merely to their own selves, but are desires of their way of life. Now these disbelievers look with a deeper eye and greater seriousness, and see that these people, in pursuit of these aspirations, have not only renounced the world but have become exhausted and worn out in that struggle; they confront the greatest difficulties for their sake, and the worldly pleasures which those dwarf people regard as the spirit of life and their highest goal, these resolute people have spurned. In such circumstances, when these dwarfs and second-rate people survey the lives of those who are truly believers, they cannot reach their lofty aims and cannot grasp the secret of their lives. Then what happens? They involuntarily mock them, they laugh at their condition, then they ridicule their beliefs and sneer at the conduct they have adopted:

﴿Zuyyina lilladhina kafaru al-hayatu al-dunya wa yaskharuna mina alladhina amanu﴾ "The life of this world has been made attractive to those who disbelieve, and they mock those who believe."

Those who have adopted the path of disbelief have been made to find the worldly life very dear and pleasing. Such people mock those who adopt the path of faith.

But the scale by which these disbelievers weigh the values of life is not a true scale. The scale of truth is in the hand of Allah, and what weight and worth the believers have in the scale of Allah:

﴿Wa alladhina ittaqaw fawqahum yawma al-qiyamah﴾ "But on the Day of Resurrection, the God-fearing will be exalted above them."

This is the scale of truth, and moreover it is in the hand of divine power. The believers should determine their worth by this scale. They should move towards the goal and pay no heed to the folly of those fools, not give attention to the mockery of the scoffers, and not take the base values of the disbelievers into account. For the believers will be exalted above these disbelievers in the Hereafter. When the final reckoning takes place, the account of the believers will be the greater, and Allah, who is the Most Just of judges, is witness to this.

Allah has kept good for them; He is more expansive than provision, that is, He is the nourishment of the soul. He will grant them this wealth in this world and in the Hereafter, or in both the world and the Hereafter as He deems fit, for He is free to choose and wise; He alone knows where their good lies. What is the importance of worldly provision?

﴿Wallahu yarzuqu man yasha'u bi-ghayri hisab﴾ "Allah provides whom He wills without reckoning."

Provision in this world is in Allah's power; He gives without measure to whomever He wills.

He is the Bestower, He gives to whom He wills, and rains down gifts upon whom He wills. Sometimes He grants the disbelievers worldly splendour, and this is part of His wisdom; it is not a sign of any merit in them. He also gives His chosen servants both the world and the Hereafter. The source of every kind of generosity is He alone, yet for the elect His choice alone is lofty and enduring.

In human life, both of these patterns are found at all times. Some people derive their worth, and the value of their thought and action, from Allah, the Lord of Majesty. As a result, they rise above the attributes of life and the temporary things of the earth and small aims. The humanity of such people is a solid reality. These people become rulers of life, not slaves of life. In contrast to such people are others for whom the worldly life has been made beloved. They have been made slaves of the temporary provisions of the world. They are slaves of basic values. These people are caught in the snare of the necessities of life and are so entangled in the filthy quagmire of the world that they can no longer extricate themselves from it.

But whatever possessions this fallen creature of God may have, the true believer looks upon them from a very lofty station. Although these people, in their own view, consider themselves fortunate, bounteous and favoured, and consider the believers deprived, at times they sympathise with the believers and at other times they mock them. Yet they themselves are deserving of sympathy; they are themselves worthy of pity and compassion.

After the statement of the lofty values of life, the clarification of the disbelievers' stance regarding the believers, and the determination by Allah Himself of the weight and station of these disbelievers, the following verses now narrate the real story: how disagreement arose among people over concepts, beliefs, values and purposes; and then the principle is stated by which those who differ can end such disputes, and the balance of justice is described which, in the end, will issue a decision among them concerning their differences.

This is the story. At first all people were one community (ummah), with one outlook on life and one way of conduct. This refers to the small human family made up of the descendants of Adam (peace be upon him) and Hawwa (Eve), and at that time no difference of ideas and beliefs had yet arisen among the children of Adam. It should be kept in mind here that Allah began human life on this earth with a small family for the sole reason that the family system holds the place of the first brick in human life. In the beginning there was a period in human history in which all people were on one level, had one direction and one belief. They existed only in the form of a single family. Gradually their numbers increased, and humanity grew. Then they spread out in different directions and settled apart, and their ways of living began to differ. The qualities that Allah had placed within them began to appear. Allah had placed these qualities within them at the time of their creation. Some had less of them and some had more. The wisdom behind this is known only to Allah, and for the variety of life it was deemed necessary that some should have certain capacities and others certain inclinations.

In accordance with the scheme of nature, a difference of viewpoint arose among people, so humanity stepped into the next stage, and Allah sent prophets to guide them, who were bearers of good news and warners. "And He sent down with them the Book in truth, that it might judge between the people concerning that over which they differed" [2:213]. Here this great truth becomes clear: that difference of opinion among people is a natural matter, because difference is one of the principles of their creation. It is as a result of this difference that the scheme for which Allah created man comes into operation. That is, in carrying forward the divine vicegerency on earth and the office of caliphate, man had to perform various kinds of duties, and for these there was a need for different kinds of people and for those possessing diverse abilities, so that all these individuals together might bring the system of the caliphate to completion in full harmony, and implement the scheme that Allah has prepared for the development and construction of this earth, and that each person should play the role determined for him in it. Therefore it is necessary that the abilities of people for the performance of various duties should also be different, and just as human needs are varied, so human capacities should also be varied: "And they will continue to differ, except those upon whom your Lord has mercy; and for that He created them" [11:118–119].

As a result of this natural difference in abilities and duties, a difference of ideas arises among people, their priorities change, their methods change, and eventually their way of life changes. It is Allah's intention that these natural differences should exist to the desired extent. However, these differences should remain within a broad framework, and they should be constructive and upright. What is this broad framework within which they are to be confined? It is the framework of the faith-based outlook on life, and it is so broad that people of varying capacities, people possessing different powers, and people with different abilities can work within it in complete harmony. The faith-based outlook on life neither suppresses these differences, that is, the natural differences, nor completely massacres them; rather, it organizes them, brings them into harmony, and turns the direction of all of them onto the highway of reform and progress.

In these circumstances, the existence of a standard became necessary to which people might turn in cases of mutual conflict: a just judge, before whom the parties appear, whose word is decisive, after which there is no more argument or dispute, one through whom all people present their conviction and certainty. "So Allah sent the prophets as bearers of good news and warners, and He sent down with them the Book in truth, that it might judge between the people concerning that over which they differed" [2:213]. Then Allah sent prophets who gave good news to those on the right path and warned of the consequences of deviation, and He sent down with them the Book of truth so that it might judge between people concerning the matters over which they had differed.

We should reflect upon the word "bil-haqq" (in truth). This is in fact a decisive statement on the matter that truth is precisely that which is in the Book of Allah. This truth has been revealed for the reason that it serves, for people's various ideas, their methods of working and their values, as an honest arbiter, and is the final point of decision in all differences. Apart from it, truth will not be found anywhere; it has no parallel arbiter; after its word there is no further word. Without this Truth, which is one and has no partner, the vehicle of this life cannot travel on the straight track, without making it the judge in all differences and ideas, and without accepting its judgement as the final judgement, without any further litigation and without any objection. It certainly cannot. The intense differences existing among people cannot end, peace cannot be established on earth, and in no way can man enter into security and safety without these measures.

From where should people take their concepts and laws of life? The answer is that, to determine the source of the laws of life and the system of life, it is first necessary to acknowledge the status of the Book of Allah, that all final decisions on differences will be made by the Book of Allah. Moreover, this does not accept duality. Allah, the Blessed, sent down this Book and sent it down with truth. Its source is one; multiplicity in it is not possible, and this is the very source from which the Book of Allah was revealed, and it was revealed so that it might have the power of decision in matters of difference, and be the criterion of truth.

That Book is one in its essence. All messengers have come bringing this one Book; therefore all heavenly scriptures are in fact one book, all religious communities are in fact one community, and the concepts of life of these books and messengers are in fact one. One God, one object of worship, one lawgiver for all humanity; however, in the detailed and particular rulings there was a slight difference, according to different periods, different communities and sects, different styles of life and different kinds of eras. And after all the deletion and addition, the final, stable and complete form is the Quranic teachings, and through these teachings life was freely set on the path of progress without any obstacle, so that human life, in its wide domain, under the guidance and direction of Allah, in accordance with the Sharia of Allah and the living system of life, may progress within its broad limits.

This decision of the Quran regarding the Book of Allah is in fact the correct Islamic viewpoint regarding all ideas and all beliefs. The summary is that in reality every prophet brought this same religion, which consisted of a few fundamental beliefs, namely the belief in Tawhid (the oneness of Allah) and so on, but what happens is that every community, after its messenger departed, gradually deviated from its original religion, and such a heap of wrong traditions and stories accumulated that the foundations of the religion were buried beneath it. People went far away from the original religion. Thus the need arises for a new message to be sent through a new prophet.

New prophets did continue to come, but in reality it was the renewal (tajdid) of the religion of Islam that kept taking place. That messenger would negate the heap of superstitions that had entered the religion, and according to the conditions of that age, a system and a law would be given to the people; it would lay the foundation of a social system, until the Quran was revealed, and now, regarding religious ideas and beliefs, the Holy Quran alone is worthy of being followed and is the truth.

When some non-Muslim scholars discuss the history of religions and beliefs, their method of discussion is to prove that the teachings of each prophet differ from those of the prophet before him, and thus they effectively prove a theory of doctrinal evolution. Some Muslim researchers too are influenced by this method of discussion and, unconsciously, they too seek change and alteration in the original ideas and beliefs of the religions. This style of discussion is adopted by the orientalists and by the researchers of the West themselves regarding religions.

This doctrine of continuity and stability in the original concept of faith is precisely the purpose of the revelation of this Book, which has been sent down with truth and was revealed so that it might judge between people concerning their matters of difference. In every age, through every messenger and prophet, and regarding all matters from the earliest times until today, it does so.

There was a need for a balance by which all people could ascertain the value of their ideas and beliefs. There must be a decisive word after which the discussion ends. Furthermore, there was an absolute need that the source of this balance and this decisive word should not be human. The balance and the decisive word should belong to the Being who is not affected by human desires, who is free from human defects, and in whose source there is no ignorance as there is in man. Then, to establish such a balance, unlimited knowledge is needed. Knowledge of every event is necessary, whether it has already happened, is happening, or is yet to happen. This knowledge must also be absolute, that is, it should not be confined by the limits of time, such that one and the same thing becomes separated by time into past, present and future. A thing is called certain, speculative or unknown. One and the same thing is sometimes present and sometimes absent, sometimes observable and sometimes hidden. Then, by the limits of place, one and the same thing is near and then becomes distant; sometimes it is within the field of vision and sometimes behind a veil, or sometimes perceptible and sometimes imperceptible. In short, the knowledge of a God and object of worship is needed who knows what He created and who created it, and who knows what is beneficial and what is beneficial for all.

To establish a balance of this kind, it is also necessary that the one who establishes the balance be free from needs, free from defect, free from annihilation, that nothing can escape him, and that death does not overtake him; that he be free from greed, that he have no desire for anything and no fear of anyone. He must dominate this whole universe, and his rule must extend over every thing and every person. In short, the balance belongs to that Allah and God who is free from desires, free from needs, and in whom there is no fault or deficiency.

As for human intellect and wisdom, it is sufficient for it that it keeps watch over changing conditions, that its eye is on the changing environment, that new needs are before it, and then it brings about harmony within these conditions at a specified time and in a particular situation. But this is only so when man possesses some standard of truth through which he can gauge his error and his correctness, recognize his right course and his wrong course, and assess whether he stands on truth or falsehood, and all these judgements conform to that standard. This alone is the way by which life can proceed on the right path, and by which people can be satisfied that their affairs of politics and leadership are in the hands of the Lord and Master.

This Book was not sent down with truth so that it would abolish the distinctions of natural abilities among people, eliminate the diverse resources of life, and erase the difference and distinction of various customs and different capacities. Rather, the purpose of this Book has always been that if people differ on any matter, it should decide according to truth.

If this reality is properly understood, then as its logical consequence the historical viewpoint of Islam can be well understood. That is, Islam gives this Book, which Allah sent down with truth, the status of an indispensable sovereignty in matters of difference among people. It regards this Book as the fundamental principle of human life.

Now the caravan of life will be observed: if it agrees with this principle, moves in accordance with it, and stands upon this principle, then it is on the path of truth. If the caravan departs from the system of life and sets out on other principles, it will become known that this caravan has now set out on the path of falsehood.

Even if, at some period of human history, all human beings were to agree to this false system, they still could not transform falsehood into truth. Falsehood would remain falsehood, because people are not the standard by which truth and falsehood, genuine and counterfeit, are determined. They are not the judge. If people decide some matter themselves, it does not become truth, nor does it follow that if the entire human population were to issue some decision, it would become religion.

Islam's position is that if people act upon something, if people have come to believe in something, or if all people have built their lives upon some wrong principle, even then that saying, that action and that principle do not turn into truth. If it is contrary to the Book of Allah, the agreement of people does not make that falsehood a part of the fundamentals of religion, nor does the practice of people turn it into an interpretation or explanation of the religion. Even if such matters have been practised for centuries, this does not mean that they have now become permissible.

This is a reality and it is of great importance. People have introduced many new things into the fundamentals of religion, and only in the case where we accept the Book of Allah as the judge can we separate these things from religion. The history of Islam itself bears witness that at various stages people deviated from the fundamentals of religion, and this deviation has been growing gradually. But it cannot be said that, since for a long time the collective system of people's lives has been founded upon this deviation, this deviation is now the real and practical form of the Islamic system. Never; this cannot happen.

If history records a deviation from Islam that became a common practice, Islam is not responsible for it. That deviation would still be considered an error. It cannot be treated as evidence, and it cannot be established as a precedent. Therefore, those who want to establish the Islamic way of life afresh should uproot all these deviations and declare them null and void. All people should return to this Book, which was revealed precisely so that it might judge between people with truth concerning their disputes and rule among them.

When this Book came, people were surrounded on all sides by their desires. Their desires dominated them. Fear, greed, worldly attractions and deviation kept people away from the sovereignty of this Book of Allah. People had stopped returning to the truth. Out of mere carnal desires, ﴿And none differed concerning it except those who had been given it, after clear proofs had come to them, out of mutual envy among themselves﴾. They devised various methods, abandoning the truth after clear guidance had reached them, only because they wanted to oppress one another.

"Baghy" means envy. Greed is rivalry, and covetousness is competition, and carnal desire is envy. In short, it is this envy and rivalry that induced people to stir up disagreement about the Islamic worldview and the Islamic way of life. People remained engaged in factionalism, enmity, and debate and contention.

If the history of religious disputes is studied according to this principle, it will be found that when a disagreement arose between two people concerning the fundamentals of religion, one of the two certainly had envy in his heart, or both were victims of envy. But if the parties possess faith, then there is no option except unity and harmony. ﴿So Allah guided those who believed to the truth concerning which they had differed, by His permission﴾.

Those who believed in the prophets were guided by Allah, by His leave, to the path of truth about which those people had differed. The believers were granted guidance because their hearts were clean, their souls were single-minded, and their hearts had the yearning to reach the truth. When conditions are like this, reaching the truth and remaining steadfast upon it becomes very easy. ﴿And Allah guides whom He wills to a straight path﴾.

What is the path to which this Book guides? It is a system that is established upon truth, moves upon truth, and remains firm upon truth. It does not shift here and there according to people's desires, and it does not become a plaything in the hands of human inclinations and tendencies.

Allah chooses from among His servants whom He wills for the straight path, because He knows who among people has the capacity to accept the truth and then remain steadfast upon it. These are the people who attain the way of safety, and indeed enter the realm of peace. These are the people who will prevail, even though in the eyes of the worldly they may have no value and are regarded as deprived. Even though these worldly people mock them, just as the disbelievers mock the believers.

The guidance given so far had this aim: that the Muslim community should develop a complete, clear and comprehensive worldview in its heart. Here these instructions conclude. Now the Muslim community is directed to observe carefully the circumstances of those believers who had differences of opinion with their opponents, the enemies of Islam, the polytheists and the People of the Book, and how, because of these ideological differences, they faced countless calamities. Great wars were fought because of these differences, and mountains of afflictions fell upon people, and they were crushed to pieces.

The Muslim community is made aware that this is the sunnat Allah (the established way of Allah), which has continued since ancient times. In this way, believers are separated from ordinary people, and they are prepared to enter Paradise, so that they may enter it and become deserving of it. The sunnat Allah is that ideological people defend their ideologies. They endure difficulties, hardships, pain and suffering for their beliefs and convictions. Sometimes they will attain victory and sometimes defeat, but in every condition they will remain firm upon their ideologies, and no hardship will be able to shake them. No power will be able to frighten them. Amid the successive assaults of difficulties and trials, they should not lose courage. If they do this, they become deserving of Allah's help, because they have become trustees of Allah's religion, and they are trustworthy in the trust that has been entrusted to them. They have the ability to preserve it, and for this they are also deserving of Paradise. Their souls have been freed from fear, and they have been freed from humiliation. They are no longer greedy for comfort and luxury. Rather, they no longer care even for their own lives. In such circumstances, these soldiers of Allah become far removed from this world of clay and water, and draw nearer to Paradise and to Allah.

This was Allah's address to the first Islamic community. He says: it is My established way (sunnah) that I place My knowledge in the hands of whichever of My servants I choose, those whom I make My trustees in this world, through whom I establish the Islamic order and enforce the Shariah. I first train them by putting them in the furnace of trials. This is My historical sunnah.

Go and study the history of Islamic movements in human history. This address was not restricted to the first Islamic movement of Madinah Tayyibah alone; rather, it is addressed to every movement that Allah chooses in this universe to play this great role, those who are the callers to the Islamic system.

This is a great, far-reaching and terrifying experience: the Messengers crying out, the believers crying out along with the Messengers, all of them crying out in one voice, "When will Allah's help come?" From this question one can gauge the trials and hardships that shook these God-fearing people to the core. Surely those hardships were unbearable, for they affected even these hearts filled with faith, and this anguished cry escaped their lips too: "When will Allah's help come?"

It is Allah's sunnah that when these hearts filled with faith endure those soul-shaking trials, then Allah's word is fulfilled and His help arrives: "Surely Allah's help is near" (﴿أَلا إِنَّ نَصْرَ اللَّهِ قَرِيبٌ﴾), "Yes, Allah's help is near."

Yes, Allah's help is preserved for those who deserve it, and those who deserve it are those who remain steadfast until the last moment: those who stay firm in hardship and distress, who stand against calamities, who do not bow before the storms of adversity, and who believe that it is Allah alone who can give aid and support (and when He wills, He will grant it). The situation reaches a point where trials touch their limit and the believers have no other support left; there remains no other means of help and aid but Allah. Only Allah's help remains, and the believers too raise their eyes only towards Allah.

This is the state which makes the believers deserving of entry into Paradise. They enter Paradise after trial and examination, after patience and firmness, after becoming wholly devoted to Allah alone, after dedicating their consciousness purely to Allah, and after forgetting everything and every cause other than Allah.

Through the Islamic struggle and patience upon hardships and trials in its course, a person is granted a great strength. A person gains mastery over his own self. In the furnace of suffering and calamity, the elements of the human soul become pure and clear. Depth, life and strength are born into the Islamic worldview. The ideology becomes alive and radiant, so much so that the eyes of its opponents are dazzled, and this is the stage where even the eternal enemies of the religion begin to enter Allah's religion in multitudes.

This is what happens in every matter of truth. At the beginning of the journey, the bearers of truth face difficulties; but when they show steadfastness, the result is that their enemies and opponents also incline towards them, and even the fiercest adversaries of this worldview and its most powerful opponents lay down their arms and begin to support and assist its call. But even if this result does not come, still greater outcomes emerge than this.

The spirit of the bearers of the Islamic call prevails over all worldly tribulations and all worldly corruptions. This spirit is freed from the slavery of greed, avarice, and luxury and comfort. Ultimately, the true believer reaches a point where he no longer even has attachment to his own life. When the human soul reaches that station, it conquers the whole universe; it conquers all the hearts that reach that station by overcoming difficulties. This is the gain which outweighs all trials and all hardships. The believers who endure to reach this station are those who are the trustees of Allah's knowledge: those who bear the religion of Allah, His Shariah and His trust.

It is this freedom which makes the believers worthy of entry into Paradise in this world. This is the true path. It is the path which Allah showed to the Islamic movement on the very first day, and for every Islamic movement that arises in every age, this is the same path.

This is the path of faith and jihad, the path of trial and affliction, the path of patience and steadfastness, turning towards Allah alone, without partner. Then see how help comes; then see how a rain of blessings pours down.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 2, verse 215 (part 1 of 2):

As is evident, this section of the surah has the atmosphere of questions and answers about rulings. As we explained in the commentary on the verse "They ask you about the new moons" (yas'alunaka 'anil-ahilla), this is a scene that shows how alert the Islamic way of life was, how it had taken hold of the hearts of the members of the community, and how eager the Muslims were, in every matter of their daily life, to learn the ruling of their creed so that their conduct would conform to their way of life. It is a firm sign of a true Muslim that he seeks to learn Islam's ruling in every small and great matter of his life, and that he does not take a practical step until he has found out what Islam says about it. Whatever Islam upholds becomes its constitution and law, and whatever Islam abandons becomes forbidden and unlawful for them. This sensitivity is in truth a sign of firm faith in this way of life.

The Jews, the hypocrites and the polytheists had begun objections against some of Islam's reforms, and in this regard they were launching attacks as a conspiracy. Influenced by them, or in order to discover the true reality and wisdom behind them, some Muslims were also raising questions. The Jews carried out a severely poisonous propaganda against these reforms, and some Muslims would be influenced by it. On such occasions, a portion of the Holy Quran would be revealed and would decide the matter under discussion. The Muslims would attain certainty, the conspiracies would end, the mischiefs would die their own death, and the plot of the conspirators would fall back upon their own necks.

From these questions it becomes clear that in that era the Holy Quran was fighting a many-sided intellectual battle. Sometimes this battle was being waged within the hearts and minds of the Muslims themselves, sometimes within the ranks of the Muslims, and sometimes against those enemies of Islam who were at war with it and busy with plots against it.

This lesson too is part of that intellectual battle, and in it answers are given to certain questions: for example, the questions about spending (infaq), its amount, its recipients, and the kind of property from which one should spend; the question about fighting in the sacred months; the question about wine and gambling; and the question about orphans. The causes of all these questions were the same ones we have mentioned above, and the details will be presented, God willing, at the time of discussing the verses!

Before this question, several verses had already been revealed concerning spending in the way of God (infaq fi sabilillah). In the circumstances in which the Islamic movement began, spending in the way of God is extremely necessary, so that the Islamic community may be able to face hardships and the military battles that lay ahead of it, and the enemies confronting it. The importance of spending had increased in that era for another reason as well: the Islamic movement urgently needed the establishment of collective mutual support (takaful) among its companions. There was a need to eliminate outward distinctions among the members of the community, so that every individual would understand that he is a limb of one body, that nothing is hidden from him, and that nothing is withheld from him. For the consciously intended establishment of a community, a system of collective mutual support and spending is very necessary. To increase the effectiveness of the members of the community, it is necessary that their needs be taken into account.

In such circumstances, some Muslims asked what they should spend. The question was: what should they spend? What should the nature of spending be? In reply, the quality of spending and its recipients were stated:

"Whatever wealth you spend [qul ma anfaqtum min khayr]" — this expression contains two indications. One is that whatever you spend should be good (khayr): good for the giver, good for the receiver, good for the society in which this exchange is taking place, and good in itself. It should be such that the deed is pure, the gift is pure, and the thing is pure.

The second indication is that the one who spends should, after careful thought, spend from his property something of the finest quality. He should spend the best things he has, and share them with others. Spending purifies the heart, cleanses the self, and benefits others; their needs are met. Then, seeking out and spending the better part of one's property is a step by which purity comes into the heart. The human self becomes clean and pure, and the lofty meaning of adopting spending comes to the fore.

But this is only an indication, and it has not been made obligatory or required. Another verse clarifies this: in this regard, it is appropriate that wealth of medium quality be given in the way of God, neither very precious nor utterly worthless. However, the verse contains the hint that in order to bring the self under control, better wealth should be spent, and the people of faith have been encouraged to be ready for this. This is the Holy Quran's method of education, that is, reform is brought about through encouragement and willingness.

What is the manner and recipient of spending? The answer to this question is: "fa lil-walidayni wal-aqrabina wal-yatama wal-masakini wabnis-sabil" — "Spend on your parents, relatives, orphans, the needy and the wayfarer."

Between the one who spends and these people there are particular ties. Some individuals have a relationship of kinship with the one spending; some are bound by ties of blood; some have only a bond of mercy and compassion; and with some there is merely a relationship of human sympathy within the broad bounds of ideology. And all have been gathered into one verse. Parents, relatives, orphans, the needy, the wayfarer — all of them, within the broad sphere of the Islamic way of life, have the guarantee of their needs being met and of support when there is need.

The order of recipients is the same as that stated in this verse. Moreover, it is clarified in some other verses, and in some hadiths there is mention of further detail and explanation. In Sahih Muslim there is a narration in which the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to a man: "First begin with yourself and give charity to it. If there is more, spend on your family; if something remains beyond that, on your relatives; and if something still remains beyond them ......"

From this order of recipients it becomes clear what wise and simple method Islam has adopted for the training of the human self, and for its leadership and guidance. Islam deals with the human being in accordance with his reality — exactly in accordance with his nature, his inclinations and his tendencies. Islam moves with a person in the way a child is born, then stands up and reaches a fixed stage; Islam holds his hand and walks with him step by step. Gradually his progress conforms to the demands of his nature, his tendencies and his capacity. Gradually he develops and advances his whole life along with himself. He is moving toward height, yet he does not even feel constriction or fatigue.

The way of Islam's progress is not to take someone up to heights by putting shackles and handcuffs on him and dragging him. Nor are his natural powers and natural tendencies suppressed so that he is caged like a bird and flutters helplessly; nor is he led on the path of progress in such a way that progress ceases and becomes oppression; nor is he made to fly over mounds and hills. Rather, he is led upward with gentleness and softness. His feet are on the earth, his eyes are on the sky, and his heart is suspended at the horizon, while his soul is joined to God in the heights of the Throne.

God knew well that man has a drive of self-love. Therefore God commanded that first one should provide for one's own self sufficiently, and only after the self is given the command to spend on other relatives. God made the pure things of food and drink lawful for man, encouraged him to enjoy those lawful things, and yet imposed the restriction that he should keep away from indulgence and arrogance.
