It is forbidden to give any nazr or offering for anyone other than Allah, in the path of anyone other than Allah, or on account of anyone other than Allah. To vow to anyone among Allah's servants, other than Allah, is a kind of shirk (associating partners with Allah). This is like the polytheists who used to slaughter various animals at the shrines of their deities and idols, a practice that continued in various periods of jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance).

﴿And whatever expenditure you spend or whatever vow you vow, indeed Allah knows it................﴾ "Whatever you have spent or whatever vow you have vowed, Allah has knowledge of it." The believer's belief that the Essence of the Lord has complete knowledge of his intention, that He is aware of the hidden desires of his conscience, and that all his secret movements are before Him, causes various living sensations to arise in his consciousness. He guards against any kind of hypocrisy or ostentation appearing in his thought and his action. He comes to abhor miserliness and stinginess. No fear of scarcity of resources or of poverty and destitution arises in his heart. His conviction is firmly established that he will receive full recompense from Allah. He begins to live a life of contentment, tranquility and comfort, accepting the decree. He comes before Allah's court, giving thanks for His bounties.

But, on the contrary, the one who does not render the due of blessing does not render the rights of Allah and of His servants. If he does not give khairat and sadaqat from what Allah has given him, then that person commits zulm (wrongdoing). He wrongs his covenant, wrongs the common people, and wrongs his own soul. ﴿And for the wrongdoers there are no helpers.................﴾ "And the wrongdoers have no helpers."

Sadaqah given voluntarily is, in that case, more pleasing to Allah when it is given in secret, and it is most fitting when it is free of any trace of showing off or ostentation. However, if the sadaqah is one of the obligatory charities and duties, then it also carries the aspect of obedience and the carrying out of a command, and the display and publicizing of that aspect is more desirable. For this reason Allah says:

﴿If you give your charities openly, that is good; but if you conceal them and give them to the poor, that is better for you.﴾

This verse mentions both situations. Each form is therefore chosen according to the circumstances of the time, and each act is judged good or bad in practice according to the present condition. In any case, whatever form the believers adopt in spending in the way of Allah (infaq fi sabil Allah, spending for the cause of Allah), they are promised that it will be an expiation for their sins. Allah says:

﴿And He will remove from you some of your evil deeds.﴾

On the one hand, the hearts of the believers become fervent and alert in the fear of God and against evil; on the other hand, they receive the reward of peace and tranquility. And in every stage of intention and action, and in every state, they maintain their connection with Allah. Allah says:

﴿And Allah is well-acquainted with what you do.﴾

It is appropriate here to reflect briefly on these lengthy instructions concerning spending in the way of Allah. These instructions employ encouragement and warning in various ways. Such reflection yields two lessons. The first is that the Islamic system has fully taken into account the temperament and nature of human beings. Stinginess and miserliness are part of human disposition, and a person loves wealth intensely. Therefore there is a need to repeatedly urge him toward spending in the way of Allah, and to keep stirring him so that he may rise above this miserliness and greed, think beyond them, be freed from the bonds of parsimony, and attain the lofty station that Allah has chosen for human beings.

The second point is that although generosity was a common quality in Arab society, those who were generous merely so that they might gain widespread fame, so that their liberality would be proclaimed, and so that they would be spoken of in cities and marketplaces, were many. For Islam, it was not easy at the very beginning of its work to demand that people spend in the way of Allah without waiting for any of these things, and without giving any consideration to them, keeping only Allah in view and not regarding the people at all. This station can be attained only through a long process of teaching and training, and even then only after a long struggle. It will be achieved only when people are continuously called to attain this lofty station, and when they are given training in purification (tazkiyah) and sincerity. Accordingly, the Islamic movement (Tahrik-i-Islami) continued this work without interruption.

For this reason, the address now turns away from the believers and is directed to the Messenger (ﷺ). The direction of address is changed so that all the realities which contribute greatly to the growth of the Islamic conception of life may be firmly fixed in the mind here, and because they have a great effect in establishing Islamic conduct in relation to the Islamic system of life and in correcting human conduct.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 2, verse 272:

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated through Hazrat Ibn Abbas (رضي الله عنه) from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to order that charity be given only to the people of Islam, until this verse was revealed: "The guidance of them is not your responsibility..." Then he (ﷺ) ordered that charity be given to whoever among the followers of any religion asked from you.

The hearts are in the hand of Allah. It is not within the power of any of Allah's creation to guide someone or to lead someone astray, even if that person were the Messenger (ﷺ) himself. Guiding and misguiding is the sole function of Allah, because He is the Creator of hearts. Over hearts there is only the sovereignty of Allah. Only Allah can turn hearts, and it is He who can direct the hearts. The duty of the Messenger is only to convey the message clearly. As for guidance, it is solely the work of Allah. He grants guidance to whomever He wills, because He alone is worthy of granting guidance. Granting guidance is solely the prerogative of Allah. Removing this prerogative from humans is only so that a believer, seeking guidance, turns only to Allah and derives evidence only from Allah. Its second benefit is that, after declaring this prerogative to be exclusively the right of God, a caller (da'i) no longer has any justification to harbor hatred toward misguided people or to feel distress at their obstinacy. For he will continue to invite them continually, will treat them with compassion, and will wait to see when Allah permits their hearts to come onto the right path, when He grants them the ability to take steps in that direction and to recognize their Lord.

﴿It is not your responsibility to guide them, but Allah guides whom He wills...﴾ "The guidance of them is not your responsibility. Guidance belongs to Allah alone; He bestows it upon whom He wills." Therefore, invite them with an open heart and open your breast to them. Pour upon them your mercy and good conduct. Continue to do good to them, and be a helper to them wherever they need your assistance. Keep instructing them to return to Allah, and the reward for this assistance is safeguarded with Allah.

Here we arrive at the heights whose horizons are vast and luminous. Allah Almighty brings the minds and hearts of the believers to those heights and firmly establishes their hearts upon them. Islam not only establishes the principle of religious freedom, and not only eradicates compulsion and violence in religious matters, but goes further still by establishing an atmosphere of religious tolerance based on guidance from Allah. It lays down the principle that, without distinction of religion or creed, the doors of economic cooperation and economic assistance are open to all people, provided they are not in a state of war with the Muslim community. It assures that the reward of those who spend on non-Muslims in such circumstances is also safeguarded with Allah, provided that this spending is purely for the sake of Allah's pleasure. This is such an elevation of humanity that, in a single leap, it reaches that lofty station, and this station can be attained only through Islam, and only those who are truly Muslims can grasp the reality of this lofty station.

﴿And whatever good you spend, it is for yourselves, and you spend only seeking the Face of Allah. And whatever good you spend will be paid back to you in full, and you will not be wronged.﴾

In this verse Allah has shown a glimpse of the dignity of the believers, which must remain before our eyes. Allah Almighty says that when believers spend, they spend ﴿only seeking the Face of Allah﴾ — "You spend only so that you may attain the pleasure of Allah." This is the sole attribute of a believer, nothing else. It is that he spends solely for the pleasure of Allah. He does not spend for carnal desires or for any selfish purpose or gain. He does not give charity in such a way that, having given, he sits waiting with his ears open to hear what people say. He does not spend in order to ride upon the necks of people through his giving, to establish his superiority over them or to prove himself great in comparison to them. Nor does he spend so that those in authority will be pleased with him or will reward him in return. He spends only for the pleasure of Allah, purely for Allah. Therefore, the believer's heart is content that Allah will certainly accept this charity. He also has complete assurance that Allah will bless his wealth. He is also confident that Allah will not only give him his full reward but will bestow additional favour upon him. He is fully assured that, as a result of his kindness and spending upon Allah's creation, he is deserving of kindness and goodness from Allah. Thus, through this generosity, his soul is purified, his character becomes pure, and his personality is elevated. As long as he lives in this world, and the reward of the Hereafter, it is in any case superior and most excellent.

After this, Allah Almighty mentions especially one of the avenues of expenditure in charity. A picture is presented of a group among the believers who are pure and clear, dignified and self-respecting. Upon seeing this picture, a tumult arises in human consciousness. Upon seeing this picture, the heart of the believer is stirred, and the human self perceives such personalities who do not like to receive any kind of help from anyone. So that their self-respect is not hurt in any way, they do not seek need, lest they be regarded as lowly. Therefore they are unable to bring themselves to stretch out their hand in begging, nor do they express their need in this regard.

Allah Almighty says:

This description of quality fits precisely a group of the Muhajirun. They had left behind their wealth and families, they were residing in Madinah, and they had dedicated themselves to jihad fi sabilillah. These people were constantly the bodyguards of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). For example, the Ahl al-Suffah, who were also the guardians of the residences of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). No enemy could reach the residences of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) without being seen. Besides this, they were devoted to jihad fi sabilillah and could not go here and there for earning a livelihood or for commercial purposes. Despite this situation, they did not ask anyone for anything. They adopted such a self-respecting attitude that a person who was not acquainted with their circumstances would think that these were very prosperous and well-off people. They neither asked anyone for anything nor did any business. Only people of understanding and wisdom could grasp their real condition.

However, despite this initial application, this verse is general. Its application extends to people of every age and every era who are of noble lineage, who are confined in such circumstances that they cannot seek livelihood within them, and whose nobility of soul prevents them from asking anyone. They outwardly maintain such an attitude that their real condition cannot be gauged, and behind this outward condition lies a situation which an unaware person cannot correctly assess because of their self-respect. Only a sensitive and wise person can come to know their real condition. Therefore, the inner intense feelings of any person do appear on the face, even though that person may try hard to conceal them out of modesty and self-respect.

This is a picture that manifests profound indications. This brief verse creates such a picture of these noble people. It is a complete picture, woven with the colours of self-respect and modesty. Every phrase of this verse is, as it were, the pen-tip of a painter, transferring the features of these people onto paper, and through this picture their impressions and feelings are fully expressed. As soon as a person recites these verses, the images of these personalities are imprinted upon the tablet of his mind, such that those figures seem to stand before his eyes. Those faces are clearly visible. This is the manner of the Holy Quran in depicting various examples of humanity. Different kinds of people appear as though they are living and moving personalities.

The condition of these noble and needy people is that they conceal their needs in the same way that a person conceals his private parts. If something is to be given to such people, it should be given only in privacy, so that their self-respect and dignity are not hurt. For this reason, at the end of the verse, a kind of indication is given that the assistance to such people should also be rendered in a most secret manner. Accordingly, the one who spends is assured that Allah knows well. And He is the one who gives full reward. "And whatever good you spend, indeed Allah knows it" (2:273). "Whatever wealth you spend in aid of such people will not remain hidden from Allah." It is only Allah who knows hidden secrets, and with Him no good deed is lost without its reward.

At the very end, this discipline of spending in the way of Allah concludes with a general and universal verse that encompasses every kind of spending and charity. Its command is also general and includes everything that is given for the sake of Allah.

This concluding passage of the verse shows a remarkable generality and harmony. The beginning and the end of the verse, like the balanced refrain of a melody, are repeated in a balanced way, in the form of a general principle. And with great fitness, الَّذِينَ يُنْفِقُونَ أَمْوَالَهُمْ ("Those who spend their wealth") means every kind of wealth and property that they spend; there is no restriction in it. بِاللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ سِرًّا وَعَلانِيَةً ("by night and by day, secretly and openly") means that in whatever times and circumstances they spend in the way of Allah, فَلَهُمْ أَجْرُهُمْ ("they have their reward") ﴿with their Lord﴾. Their every kind of reward is secure. It will also be increased, and there will be blessing in their lifespan. In the Hereafter too they will receive full recompense, and Allah's pleasure will be added to it. عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ وَلا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ ("with their Lord, and no fear shall come upon them, nor shall they grieve"). From no direction will they have any fear; from no direction will there be any apprehension of anyone. It will be so neither in this world nor in the Hereafter. Thus this is the fitting and proportionate conclusion to the rule of spending in the way of Allah, in which there are indications that spending in the way of Allah, in its general form, is rewarded, whatever its kind, whenever it is done, and for whatever purpose it is made.

It is worth noting here that Islam does not base the economy of the lives of its adherents solely on spending in the way of Allah. In the Islamic system, the economy depended on providing employment opportunities for every person who had the capacity. Besides this, Islam based its economy, among the Muslims, on the just distribution of wealth, and the principle of this distribution of wealth is based on good performance and entitlement. But sometimes exceptional circumstances arise in which the general principles of the economy are not useful, and in those circumstances the difficulties that arise are not resolved by them. Islam resolves such circumstances through spending in the way of Allah. This spending is sometimes in the form of a compulsory tax, which is imposed by the Islamic government that implements the Islamic Shariah. Only an Islamic government can impose this kind of compulsory tax. Zakah and obligatory charities (ṣadaqāt wājibah) are among the important revenues of the Islamic government. And sometimes this distribution of wealth takes the form of voluntary charities (ṣadaqāt nafliyyah), whose amount is not fixed, and these voluntary charities are given by the wealthy to the deserving, which are given to them personally. And when giving this kind of gift, it is necessary to observe the etiquettes and conditions mentioned above. And it is because of these etiquettes that the recipients display self-respect. This self-respect is what is expressed in this verse. Islam promoted this self-respect in the Islamic society to such an extent that a person might have nothing at all, and be in need even of the basic necessities of life, yet he would not stretch out his hand to ask anyone.

Bukhari narrated from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAmrah, who said: We heard from Abū Hurayrah, who said that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The poor man is not the one whom one date or two dates turn away, or one morsel or two morsels, so that he goes about begging. The poor man is the one who is self-respecting." If you wish, recite this verse: لا يَسْأَلُونَ النَّاسَ إِلْحَافًا ("They do not ask people insistently").

Imam Ahmad narrated, through Abū Bakr and ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn Jaʿfar, through his father, a report from a man of the tribe of Muzaynah. His mother advised him: "Why do you not go to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and ask, as other people do?" He said: "I should ask the Messenger of Allah for something?" He went and found him delivering a sermon: "Whoever shows self-respect, Allah will grant him; and whoever seeks independence, Allah will make him independent. Whoever asks people while he has property equal to five awqiyah, has indeed asked insistently (ilḥāfan)." I said to myself: "I have a she-camel which is certainly worth more than five awqiyah, and my servant has another she-camel which is also worth more than five awqiyah." So I turned back and did not make the request.

Ḥāfiẓ Ṭabarānī narrated with his chain from Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn: Ḥārith (a man of Quraysh who lived in Syria) was informed that the financial condition of Ḥaḍrat Abū Dharr (raḍiyallāhu ʿanhu) was not good, so he sent him three hundred dīnārs. Abū Dharr replied: "Does ʿAbdullāh not find anyone poorer than me? I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Whoever asks while he has forty dirhams has asked insistently.'" Abū Dharr's family has forty dirhams, one goat and two servants. Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh said: they are servants on monthly wages.

In short, Islam is a complete system of life. Its texts, its guidance and its laws all function together simultaneously, and the provisions of these texts, guidance and laws should not be considered separately. The principles and rules of Islam operate simultaneously, and therefore there is coherence and proportion among them. As a result, there comes into being a society whose like is not found among human societies on this earth. It is a unique society of its own kind.

**Lesson 20: An Overview**

In the previous lesson, the method and manner of spending in the way of Allah (*infaq fi sabilillah*) and charity (*sadaqah*) within the Islamic system of life were explained. Here, the page of spending and charity is placed directly opposite and reversed: that is, the system of *riba* (usury, interest) and its oppressive and deceitful consequences. In charity there is generosity, kindness, purity, cleanliness and nobility, along with mutual cooperation and *takaful* (mutual social guarantee). In usury-taking, on the other hand, there is stinginess and miserliness, filth and impurity, selfishness and personal gain.

The essence of charity is that in it one gives up wealth in this world, and apparently no return or compensation is taken for it. The essence of *riba* is that along with recovering the loaned money, the usurer also takes something extra. This extra wealth is extracted from the debtor's labour or from his flesh and blood. It is extracted through labour in the following manner: when the debtor took the money, worked with it, and gained profit as a result of his labour, in that case the extra wealth is a share of his labour. But if he gains no profit, or suffers a loss, then in that case the extra wealth is a share of his sweat and blood. Or, for example, if he took the loan for personal expenses or for the essential expenses of his family, and did not put it into a profitable business at all, then in that case too the interest amount is, as it were, recovered from that person's very self.

This is why, if charity is a bright page, then *riba* is a dark page set in opposition to it. If the face of the one who spends is radiant, the face of the usurer is dark and black. This is because, immediately after describing that beautiful, graceful, pure, merciful and generous face, the ugly face of the usurer has also been presented. This face has been presented in such a manner that all the inner evils and vices of the usurious business become evident through it: the merciless conduct of individuals, the ruin of the needy, and all the evils and corruptions that arise in society from this usurious system.

Islam eliminated all the evils of the age of ignorance (*jahiliyyah*). Yet the condemnation Islam has directed at usury is greater than the condemnation it has directed at any other evil. Moreover, the verbal and substantive threat Islam has issued against the practice of usury is not issued against the perpetrator of any other evil, both in these verses and at other places as well. And Allah's Being is certainly encompassing of far-reaching wisdoms. There is no doubt that the usurious system that prevailed in the age of ignorance had its own corruptions and vices. But in our present age of capitalism, the way its consequences and corruptions have openly come to light, and the way its ugly face has been unveiled and brought into view with such clarity, was never the case in the age of ignorance. In that age, this repugnant face was not as ugly, hideous and frowning as it is today. And in this modern age of ours, it has come fully into the open.

The grave assault that these verses launch against the then-dominant usurious economy: its true wisdom and benefit is still clearly apparent today, compared to the age of ignorance, while all of humanity today is being ground under the millstone of this system. Whoever wishes to reflect and ponder well upon the real wisdom of the Islamic system of life, its true greatness, its comprehensiveness and its meticulous precision, can, by reflecting on these verses and texts, attain what was not possible for those who first studied these verses. This is because today the whole human economy directly confirms each and every ruling of these texts. The whole of humanity today, which feeds on usury and is fed upon by it, has been struck by such mountains of calamity and hardship that they have broken its back and crushed it. This system has corrupted its morals, lowered the standard of its health, shattered its economic order, and, above all, it has destroyed and ruined its religion. Today the world is at war with its true Creator, and because of this it is afflicted with the punishment of Allah. If it is an individual, he too is caught in this punishment. If it is a nation or a community, it too is caught in this calamity. Yet neither does this punishment diminish, nor does any nation or community take warning.

The principle of spending in the way of Allah, which the Qur'an established in the previous lesson, was in fact the fundamental principle of Islam's social and economic system. The objective was that the economic system of an Islamic society should be founded upon mutual goodwill, charity and spending, and that under its shade people should live as compassionate and sympathetic toward one another. Whereas the jahili system, in contrast, is founded upon the oppressive and base morality of usury, in which there is no room for kindness and mercy.

These two systems are in fact systems opposed to one another. One is the Islamic system and the other is the usurious system. By their foundational thought, they can never come together in one place. They cannot unite on any single foundation. Nor can they, in terms of their effects and consequences, be alike. Each operates in view of its own particular conception of life and its own goals and objectives, and these two systems are entirely contradictory to one another. The results they produce are also different from one another. This is why, right from the outset, this terrifying attack was launched upon this system, and those who are the cogs of the usurious system were threatened with dreadful consequences.

Islam bases its economic system, indeed its entire system, upon the truth that exists in this universe. This truth is the Divine Being. He is the Creator of this universe. He is the Creator of this earth. He is the Creator of this human being. It is He who adorned every existent with the light of existence. It is He who is the owner of every existent, because He is the originator of every existent. In this universe He has made the human race, every member of it, His successor. The powers and necessities that He placed in this universe, He gave into the disposal of the human race. But these powers were conditioned upon a promise and a stipulation. This vast universe was not handed over to this human being, Adam's child, to be disposed of without restriction or condition, so that he might do whatever he pleased within it. For living here, He defined for humanity certain clear limits and bounds. He granted him vicegerency on the earth on the condition that he would live his life here in accordance with the Divine system of life. He would be a follower of Allah's Shariah. Therefore, all his decisions, actions, morals and worship here, which conform to that covenant, will be enforced and valid. And those of his deeds that oppose that covenant and contradict the Shariah will be null, void and suspended. And if he forcibly imposes here any principle or morality contrary to the Shariah, that will be oppression and aggression, and neither will Muslims accept them as legitimate, nor will Allah accept them. Therefore sovereignty over this earth belongs exclusively to Allah, just as sovereignty over this universe is in operation for Allah alone. As for human beings, whether they are rulers or ruled, the source and fountainhead of their authority is the Islamic system of life and the enforcement of the Islamic Shariah. Even if the whole of humanity were to decide, it would still have no right to decide that it is now free from following the Shariah. This is because man, as ruler and possessor of authority here, is Allah's deputy and agent, and this agency has been granted to him under a charter, the observance of which is obligatory upon him. Man is not himself the owner of the wealth that is in his disposal.

Among the important clauses of this covenant and charter is this: that all those people on this earth who believe in their Creator should live together through mutual cooperation and *takaful*. They should be each other's allies and friends, and all of them should benefit from the means of sustenance that Allah has given them. This is on the basis of mutual cooperation and *takaful*, and not on the basis that all these means are absolutely common property, as is the concept of modern Marxism. This *takaful* and cooperation rests upon the foundation of limited individual ownership. On this foundation of limited ownership, if someone's labour bears fruit and abundant wealth accumulates with him, then it is his duty to spend from what Allah has given him upon those who are needy and whose means are limited. But alongside spending, it has been made obligatory for all members of society to earn and work according to their strength and capacity. Within whatever means are available to him, no one has been permitted to become a burden upon others, or, despite being capable of earning and working, to seek communal support from society. As we have already explained earlier, for this communal support system of the Islamic order, every Shariah has made *zakat* obligatory, while *sadaqah* and spending in the way of Allah have been made voluntary aid, which has no limit and no boundary.

In establishing the principles of its economic system, Islam has kept moderation and balance in view. Within this system, even in spending in the way of Allah, extravagance, oppression and transgression of limits have been forbidden. Likewise, in the enjoyment and use of the pure things that have been made lawful for human beings here, extravagance has also been forbidden. This is because the sphere of expenditure on the essential needs of human life has been restricted, and confined within the bounds of moderation. Whatever remains beyond the restricted needs remains always at the disposal of *zakat* and voluntary charity. Especially in circumstances in which a believer is also commanded to put his wealth into profitable enterprise and to keep increasing it.

In business life, Muslims have been placed under this restriction: that in their commercial struggle they should not become a cause of harm or injury to anyone, and should not engage in any business that would create any kind of obstruction in the supply of people's necessities. Nor should they engage in any business as a result of which wealth becomes confined, quite apart from the rest, to a few hands and its circulation becomes limited. ﴿So that it does not become a circulating commodity only among the rich among you﴾ (Qur'an 59:7).

Islam has made the purity of thought and action obligatory in economic struggle as well. It has placed great emphasis on the purity of means and results in business. It has laid down principles and rules concerning the growth of commerce and the increase of wealth, which ensure that human conscience and human morals are not adversely affected, and that the collective existence and collective life of society are not harmed by these activities. (For details, see my book *al-'Adalah al-Ijtima'iyyah fi al-Islam*.)

All these principles and activities are based upon the truth that runs through this entire universe. That is, the conception of divinity, and then within the framework of that covenant which was agreed between the human being and the reality of existence, which governs all the dispositions and activities of the human being who has become the vicegerent, who is carrying out the duties of the caliphate upon the land that belongs to Allah.

These are the reasons on account of which usury becomes an act which, at its foundation, is entirely in conflict with the faith-based conception of life. This is because the usurious system is based upon an entirely separate conception of life, a conception in which there is no room for the creed of monotheism and the existence of the Divine Being. It is a godless conception of life. Therefore, in the usurious system there is no room for principles and morality, whereas Allah, the Exalted, desires the organization of human life on the basis of those principles and morality.

The fundamental concept of the usurious system is that there is no connection between human life and the will of Allah. Man has been the owner of the earth from the very beginning. He has no responsibility toward Allah in the form of any covenant or agreement. Therefore he is not bound at all by the commands issued by Allah, the Exalted.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 2, verse 275 (part 2 of 3):

In accordance with this conception of life, man is free to use all the means by which he can accumulate wealth. He is not bound by any principle in increasing and developing wealth. Similarly, he is not bound by any limit or restriction in spending wealth. In this regard he is not bound by any covenant or pledge with Allah. Nor is he bound to take into consideration the interests of other people. Therefore, it has no effect upon him, even if his hoarding and his enormous increase in capital cause suffering to millions of people. Sometimes the laws made by man try to curb the unlimited concentration of wealth by imposing some partial restrictions on the freedom of such a person. For example, a ceiling is placed on the rate of interest. Sometimes the laws made by man impose restrictions on certain financial manipulations, oppression and injustice, deception and financial harm to humanity. But these restrictions become a routine, and people return to their original habits. Therefore they begin to do the very things whose desire is deeply rooted in their hearts. These human laws cannot establish and make firm in society those principles which the laws revealed by the Lord, the Holy One, produce in the heart of man. In short, the foundation of the interest-based system is laid upon a wrong and corrupt basis, namely that the supreme purpose of man in this world is only that he should go on gathering wealth and property, whatever disgraceful means he has to adopt for it, and then he should benefit from that wealth and spend it as he pleases. This is why greed arises so strongly in the heart of a materialistic person that he pounces upon wealth like dogs, and wants to acquire everything and derive every kind of benefit from it. Thus, trampling all principles and sacrificing all the interests of the world, he persists in gathering wealth.

One consequence of the usury system is that it grinds all of humanity to dust. In it, the life of individuals and of society becomes difficult. As a result, nations and communities are destroyed. And this destruction takes place only for the benefit of that handful of people who supply money within this system. The nations that come within the grip of this system also fall morally, psychologically and nervously; their financial system is ruined, and proper growth does not take place in human economics. The result is that real and practical power over all humanity passes into the hands of a few people who are the most despicable of all of Allah's creatures. Along with this, they are utter corrupters. This is a class which holds no regard for friendship, sympathy or responsibility toward humanity on this earth. As in our modern age, humanity is confronted with exactly such a group. This group supplies money to governments and nations just as it supplies money to individuals. In those countries where this group resides, it conducts its business within them and also carries out this work in the outside world. And the fruit of human labour keeps coming to them. The earnings of people's blood and sweat are imperceptibly flowing into their coffers. And this benefit keeps reaching them merely because of their usurious business, in which their own toil and effort have no part.

Not only is the wealth of the people in the hands of this group, but this group also enjoys complete influence and power in that society. This group has no principles before it, nor is it bound by any moral system, nor does it believe in any religion or faith; rather, they use their influence, which they acquire in this usurious society, in mocking religion, morality, principles and character. And as a result of this terrifying influence, they create such circumstances, implement such schemes and create such an intellectual atmosphere that, living within it, they further exploit the common people because of this usurious system. In these circumstances, their meanness and detestable greed face no obstacle, and all their aims are fulfilled. In this regard, the best and easiest method for such people is that they make the masses addicted to sexuality and hedonism, destroy human morality and chastity, and drop humanity into the filthy sewer of lusts and pleasures. And they become so accustomed to it that they spend even their last penny on it. Thus their wealth keeps getting trapped in their economic net. This work is carried out in such a way that these usurious traders run the entire global economic system in accordance with their limited interests, even if, as a result of their measures, global economic production becomes confined to the interest of a few capitalists, who supply capital and into whose hands the reins of global capital pass, instead of serving the interest of the common people and the whole human society; and they pull all the strings for their own benefit.

This tragic event came to completion in our modern age in a way that, even in the age of ignorance, it had not taken such a terrifying form. This is because the usurers of the early centuries, whether existing as an individual or as an institution, were not as effective as the banks and financial institutions of the modern age function. These modern financial institutions enjoy influence within the great governments of the whole world. They affect the foreign and trade policies of governments. Moreover, they have taken control of the international institutions of journalism and publication. They get books written according to their temperament and ideas. Teachers and universities are under their control, and they exert complete influence over the media. Through these means and channels they create in the general public a mentality such that the masses, whose flesh and bones they are eating, whose blood they are sucking, and whose labour's pleasures they are plundering through this usurious system, have their minds so captured that this usurious system appears to them as a reasonable and necessary system, which seems completely sensible. They think that without this usurious system the world would be deprived of economic progress, that the economic development of the Western world is solely due to this usurious system, and that those who are struggling for the abolition of the usurious system are not practical people but merely gallop imaginary horses. They also say that the foundation of their ideas and conceptions rests merely on moral theories or merely on theoretical principles for which there is no practical model in the real world, and no path to their implementation. And if an attempt were made to devise such a system, the economic system of the entire world would be destroyed as a result. Then these usurers make mockery the target of those who criticise the existing usurious economic system. And this mockery is carried out through those people who are themselves bitten by this usurious system and are destitute solely because of it, just as today the entire global economic system has been shattered and ruined because of this usurious system. These global organisations of usurers run this economic system merely according to their own designs and their own will, and when it goes against their will, they deliver such jolts to it and create such financial crises that the minds of economic experts are set right, and they re-establish this entire global financial system afresh in accordance with the interests of a handful of usurers.

From a purely economic point of view too, this usurious system is a defective system. Some Western economic experts have also come to realise its harms, although these people grew up within this usurious system. And because of the propaganda of Western financial institutions, the concept of interest was deeply ingrained in Western knowledge and culture, morality and conceptions. Among those economic experts who oppose interest purely from the viewpoint of the economic system, the foremost is Dr Schacht of Germany. He was a former director of the German bank "Reichsbank". In the lectures he delivered in Damascus in 1953, one striking and important conclusion emerges from a deep and continuous statistical process: that the wealth of the entire world eventually appears to flow towards a handful of usurious financial institutions. This is because in this system the lender keeps profiting, whereas the borrower always suffers loss. Therefore, in the end, the result of the statistical process is simply that wealth continually flows back to the usurers who lend money. In our age, Schacht's theory has been fully proven. This is because at present the true owners of the entire wealth of the globe are a few thousand individuals and institutions. As for the others who are considered owners, or the owners of factories who take loans from banks, or those who work in those factories, all these people are in fact employees and servants of these financial institutions and work for their interests. These few thousand individuals and institutions receive the fruits of the labour of the workers of the entire world.

This is only one weakness of the interest-based economic system. Any system that is based on interest transactions will always have a relationship of hostility and conflict between those who pay money and those who work in the fields of industry and commerce, and they deal with one another like gamblers and constantly oppose one another. The lender always seeks to derive the maximum benefit. Therefore he tries to keep wealth hoarded, so that trade and industry come to feel a dire need for it, and thus a trader and an industrialist become ready to give him the maximum profit. He keeps raising the rate of interest until the borrowing traders and industrialists feel that there is no benefit for them in this business. So the results of their work go into loans and interest, and nothing remains for them. At such a time the expansion of money contracts and shrinks. Factories stop production. Workers become unemployed. People's purchasing power decreases. And when the economic crisis reaches that point, the usurer now perceives that the demand for wealth has ended and capital lies idle, so he compelled, reluctantly, reduces the rate of interest again, or rather is forced to reduce it. Then industrialists and traders turn towards it again, and prosperity returns to life once more. Thus the world keeps falling victim to global economic crises, and the common man keeps being crushed in this mill, remaining unaware like livestock.

In this system every consumer indirectly pays the usurers their share of the tax. Therefore the traders and industrialists do not pay from their own pockets the profit they give to the usurers. They recover this profit from the consumer. They raise the prices of consumer goods, and thus this usurious amount is distributed over all of humanity, and having been collected from them, it ultimately accumulates with the usurer. As for the loans which governments take from these financial institutions, namely for reforms and development projects, their burden too ultimately falls upon the common man, because the government imposes further taxes on the people in order to pay the interest on these loans, and the common man bears this burden too. In short, in the end every person bears his share of the burden of paying the rate of interest to the usurers. But this matter does not stop even at this limit. This imperialism does not stop merely at usurious dealings. For the sake of this exploitation, wars are begun.

Here, in Fi Zilal al-Quran, it is not possible for us to enumerate the harms of the usurious system. That requires a separate discussion (for valuable discussions on this subject, see those which the great Muslim Sayyid Abul A'la Maududi has written under the title Islam aur Jadid Iqtisadi Nazariyat. Sayyid Qutb). Therefore we present here only this summary, so that those who wish to become true Muslims may know what the fundamental facts are on account of which Islam has prohibited this detestable usurious system:

1. The first point is that we should clear our hearts and minds on this matter: that the usurious system can never coexist with Islam anywhere. Whatever scholar or mufti says anything else is deception, and clear fraud. This is because the Islamic conception of life is fundamentally in conflict with the usurious system. The consequences of the usurious system which arise in the thought and action of the masses, or the morality that arises as a result of it, are against Islam.

2. The usurious system is a calamity for all of humanity. Not only in the realm of faith, morality and conception of life, but also in the very depths of purely economic life, it is a torment. This system robs human prosperity and welfare, and is the greatest obstacle in the path of the balanced development of humanity. Yet outwardly this system has been given the false label that it has been devised for the economic progress of all humanity.

3. Islam presents a practical system and a moral system that are inseparably bound together. In Islam, the concept is that in all his affairs and dealings, man is bound by the covenant that he is the vicegerent and successor (khalifah) of Allah on this earth, and that all his dealings are conditional upon the condition of this vicegerency. Here his entire life is a testing ground; he has been sent as a trial, and he will have to give an account of his entire life one day. The Islamic system of life is neither merely a moral system consisting only of a few moral instructions, nor merely a practical system; it is a system of life comprising moral and practical guidance at the same time. If he adopts this system well, he will be rewarded for his whole life in the same way, as though he had worshipped. And if he abandons it, he will be punished in the Hereafter for both these aspects in exactly the same way. Thus, the economic system of Islam is not complete without its moral aspect, and the economic ethics of Islam are not an optional element but an essential part of Islam's economic system. Without them, Islam's practical economic system cannot function at all.

4. The fourth point: as a result of usurious dealings, the human conscience inevitably becomes dead and corrupt. Human morals become corrupted. Towards other members of humankind, the attitude and feelings of a usurer do not remain good. The life of human society becomes difficult, and the arrangement for the collective sustenance (kafalah) of society is damaged. Because of the usurious system, feelings of greed, avarice, selfishness, deceit and gambling arise among the masses. Modern experts in economics consider usury to be a major reason why capital flows into base, unproductive channels, so that a certain return on investment is obtained. And so that after paying the interest, something may remain for the one who takes the loan as well. It is this same impulse that leads to capital being invested in base and filthy films, filthy journalism, dance halls, dens of debauchery, wine houses, and all those expenditures which are destructive to morals, and through which the process of moral destruction continues. Under the usurious system, capital is not invested in things that are beneficial to humanity; rather, the aim is that capital be placed in projects from which the maximum possible profit is obtained. In today's global economy, this is a daily observation, and its primary cause is the present system of usurious dealing.

5. The fifth point is that the Islamic system is a complete system of life, all of whose parts are interconnected. When it declares usurious dealing to be forbidden, it also creates a system in which there is no need whatsoever for such usurious dealing. It organizes the structure and arrangement of economic life in such a way that in no sector does the need for it arise at all. And no aspect of man's economic progress is affected by this; collective economic development continues.

6. The sixth point is that when the Islamic system of life gets the opportunity to implement its system, its policy will not be to abolish outright the institutions of collective development; rather, its policy will be to purify those institutions from usury. Accordingly, the usurious impurities will be removed from these institutions. These institutions will be organized on certain other principles and will continue to work for collective development. Among these institutions are banks, companies, and all modern economic institutions.

7. This is an extremely important point. A Muslim should firmly believe that it is utterly impossible for Allah to forbid usurious dealing and yet for the collective life of man to be unable to function without non-usurious dealing. Likewise, it is impossible that something impure, defiling and harmful should be such that human life cannot be established without it. Therefore, Allah alone is the Creator of human life on this earth. It is He who has appointed man as His vicegerent on this earth, and it is the command of the Divine Being Himself that human life on this earth be advanced and that facilities be provided to man. Every affair is accomplished only by the will of Allah. It is He who grants man the ability to do good in this world. For this reason, from the standpoint of principle, it is impossible that something should be forbidden by Allah and yet at the same time be necessary for the progress and growth of life, such that progress cannot be achieved without it. Whoever holds the view that there is no other way to advance life in this world, or that there is some filthy and wicked thing without which life cannot survive or without which life in this world cannot be advanced, is certainly mistaken in this thinking; his claim is poisonous and this notion is false. It is a notion that has been spread generation after generation, namely that the usurious system is a milestone for the progress and growth of the world, and that the usurious system is a natural system. This notion has in fact been introduced, through an organized conspiracy, into the springs of education and culture, and into the sources of knowledge and training in East and West alike. Then, in the modern age, the foundation of life was built upon this system. And this was done by the individuals and agencies that provide capital to this system. The difficulty that arises is that to everyone, establishing a system of life on any foundation other than interest seems difficult. This difficulty takes on a terrifying form when a person is deprived of the wealth of faith. Furthermore, because of enslaved thinking and the failure to think freely, this task also appears difficult. For the agencies providing capital have implanted this illusion in the hearts and minds of people in the form of conviction, because they have complete control over the sources of knowledge and recognition. They have complete control over international institutions and governments. These usurers have complete control over the institutions of general and specialized publication and dissemination.

8. The eighth point is that those who maintain that in the modern age no economic system can be founded on any system other than the usurious one are, in fact, following a baseless illusion. This is in reality a great lie, and this lie prevails only because certain powerful international institutions keep it alive for the sake of their own interests. Whenever the intentions of international financial institutions become sound, whenever all of humanity resolves to change this system, or at least the Muslim Ummah resolves to bring about its change and determines that it now wishes to be free from the grip of international financial institutions, and manages its own welfare, and founds its system of prosperity and progress upon morality and purity, then at that very moment a completely new financial system will emerge before the world. It will be the Islamic system, which Allah has chosen for all humanity, and which has already been implemented in practice, under whose shade life has displayed its full flourishing. Even now this system is capable of implementation, and under it an economic system can be organized, but the condition is that people understand and find the path of guidance.

Here we cannot give the details that would allow a full discussion of the complete particulars and minutiae of this system. For us these general indications are sufficient. (In this regard, Maulana Abul A'la Mawdudi has presented some practical proposals, to which I have referred earlier. They may be considered. Sayyid Qutb.) From these it becomes clear that this evil of usury is not among the necessities of economic life. In the history of humanity, usurious systems had prevailed before as well, and Islam freed humanity from its grip. Today too, humanity has adopted economic misguidance, and only the firm, merciful and sound-natured system of Islam can deliver it from this misguidance.

Now let us look in some detail at how Islam attacks the bitter economic system of usury. This system has subjected humanity to bitterness, greater than which humanity has never experienced.

This is a frightening sentence and a dreadful portrayal. Those who devour usury will not rise except as one rises whom Satan has driven mad by his touch... "Their state is like that of a person whom Satan has struck and driven insane."

The manner in which the Qur'an has depicted the usurer, presenting the usurer in a living and moving form, possesses an impact and admonition that cannot be produced by the most beautiful meaningful or theoretical phrasing. It is a depiction whereby the image of the usurer appears vivid, perceptible and striking. Through this image, familiar characters who are commonly experienced have been displayed. The Qur'an refreshes in people's sight this character they have seen, so that this character creates fear in the human sensibility, and the human feelings of the usurers who invest capital are awakened and stirred. They are shaken and jolted out of the usurious economic system to which they are accustomed and which they practice, and they are extracted from the atmosphere of greed and selfishness in which they see many benefits. This method of instruction is very effective in its own place, especially since this manner of expression is also realistic and factual.

Most exegetes have explained the meaning of "they will not rise" (la yaqumuna) as referring to the rising and resurrection on the Day of Judgment. But my view is that in our life on this earth too, this frightening image is actually realized. Moreover, the meaning that the state of the usurer in the world is like this is also consistent with the following sentence: that those who do not abandon the usurious system are in fact declaring war upon Allah. We observe that in the world of economics this war is being waged continuously, and it is imposed upon humanity that has lost its way, and within this system a usurer is engaged in frenzied striving just as a person touched by Satan is frenzied. Before we seek the madness of the usurer in the practical system of life, it seems appropriate to portray briefly the state of the economic system of usury in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), at the time of the revelation of the Qur'an, and what the notions of the economic experts of the Age of Ignorance (jahiliyyah) were regarding this usurious system.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 2, verse 276:

يَمْحَقُ اللَّهُ الرِّبَا وَيُرْبِي الصَّدَقَاتِ وَاللَّهُ لا يُحِبُّ كُلَّ كَفَّارٍ أَثِيمٍ ... "Allah deprives usury of blessing and causes charity to grow, and Allah does not love any ungrateful, sinful person."

Allah's promise is true and His warning is certain. In our own age we are seeing with our own eyes that in today's modern world, the societies that engage in interest-based dealings do not have peace and tranquillity in the hearts of their members. Blessing has departed from these societies, and prosperity and contentment of heart have vanished.

Allah wishes to eliminate riba, so He does not send down His bounties and blessings upon a society in which the filth of riba is found. He afflicts such societies with famine and misfortune. Outwardly it appears that there is prosperity everywhere in the society. Abundant production is seen everywhere. Income is coming in abundant quantity from every side, but despite how much income is coming in, the blessing is not seen in proportion to it, in that a person could benefit from this abundant income in a pure manner, with peace and security. We have already pointed to the deprivation and misfortune that drips from the faces of people in the wealthy, high-income countries of the West, and we have also already described the spiritual anguish and anxiety in which, despite the increase in great wealth, there is no decrease. The anguish, restlessness, deprivation and misery of these countries are spreading throughout the world, because in these countries humanity is engaged in a continual and perpetually deadly war. The people there spend their lives morning and evening in a cold war. After day and night, the burden of life is becoming heavier on these nerves, whether or not they are aware of it. Because of this mental and nervous conflict, there is no blessing in their wealth, no blessing in their lifespan, their health is not enviable, and their hearts are not at rest.

On the contrary, the society that is founded upon collective cooperation and mutual support, whether this cooperation is through obligatory charity (sadaqat wajibah) or voluntary charity (sadaqat nafilah), and in which the spirit of mutual love, mutual kindness and mutual consent is at work, and in which every individual strives solely so that he may attain Allah's pleasure and become deserving of His reward, and who is always assured that Allah is his helper and that He will give him many times over the reward of charity and kindness, upon all such societies Allah sends down His blessing. Blessings descend upon the individuals of the society and also upon the groups of such a society. Blessing comes into their wealth, abundance comes into their sustenance, blessing comes into their health, blessing comes into their strength, and their hearts are filled with tranquillity and remain steadfast.

Those who do not see these realities in the present condition of humanity are the kind of people who in fact do not want to see these realities, because their carnal desires demand that they not see them. These are people upon whose eyes veils have fallen, and these veils they have deliberately placed. And these are the usurers, whose personal interest lies in this interest-based system remaining permanent and established, and therefore they cannot see these realities.

وَاللَّهُ لا يُحِبُّ كُلَّ كَفَّارٍ أَثِيمٍ ... "And Allah does not love any ungrateful, sinful person." From this sequel and this conclusion it becomes definitively clear that after the prohibition of the interest-based economic system, if some people insist on continuing it, they are sinners and disbelievers. Allah does not love them, and there is no doubt that whoever declares lawful what Allah has made unlawful is characterised by disbelief and sinfulness, even if he keeps repeating لَا إِلٰهَ إِلَّا اللّٰهُ مُحَمَّدٌ رَّسُولُ اللّٰهِ a thousand times with his tongue, because Islam is not merely a matter of verbal utterances; it is a complete system of life and a way of conduct, and the denial of any single part of it entails the denial of the whole. There is certainly no doubt about the prohibition of riba and the consumption of usury, and a person who considers it lawful and builds his economy upon its foundation is undoubtedly sinful and commits kufr. We seek refuge in Allah from that.

In contrast to this disbelieving and unrighteous system of life, and against this contemptuous warning to the holders and supporters of the interest-based economy, the Qur'an begins the chapter on righteous deeds and charity, which are the important characteristics of the Muslim community in this matter, and the central point of the righteous Islamic system that stands against this oppressive interest-based system is stated here, namely, the system of zakat against the system of riba.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 2, verse 277:

The fundamental element opposite the system of riba is zakah, and the nature of zakah is that it is a form of expenditure and spending for which there is no return in this world; nor does anything come back as a result of that expenditure. In the context of the discourse, the purpose of mentioning zakah is to describe this important attribute of the believers, and also this important attribute of the Islamic society, and to show what sights of inner contentment, peace and security, the pleasure of Allah and the blessings of God there are in this faith-based society as opposed to the usury-based society, and how exquisite a scene this society is.

Zakah is in fact the fundamental principle of a society that is based on mutual solidarity and mutual sustenance, and in such a society there is neither the existence of usurious economics in any sector or any aspect, nor does it seek any guarantee from usurious economics.

In the feeling of the Islamic Ummah, and in our own feelings, the true form of zakah has become confused and lost. The wretched generations of the Muslim Ummah have passed centuries without seeing the Islamic economic system functioning in practice. They have not observed in practice the Islamic system of life, established on a purely faith-based conception of life, purely ideological training and ideological morality, and shaping humanity and human psychology along a particular course; and this system itself being such that its correct conceptions are alive, a pure system of morality is in force, lofty values of life are established, and in it the central point of the Islamic economic system is zakah, while in contrast all other systems are practically founded on riba; and then the Ummah sees human life flourishing, and the economic system founded on individual effort and struggle, and if there is any collective form of mutual cooperation, it is free of riba.

The true form and appearance of zakah has become doubtful in the hearts and minds of the wretched generations of our age, who have been deprived of guidance, because these generations have never seen that lofty, superior and beautiful picture of humanity which emerges as a result of the system of zakah. The present generations were born within the modern material system and grew up in its shadow, and this modern system is founded on a purely usurious conception. These generations have seen only miserliness and stinginess, greed and avarice, individualism and selfishness, which rule over the hearts of everyone in the modern age. In this age, wealth reaches the needy and the poor only through the detestable usurious system. People live without any collective system of sustenance. They receive security only when they themselves possess capital, or when they have spent a substantial portion of their wealth and insured themselves under the present usurious system. Today, industry and commerce obtain capital only when they take it through the usurious system; therefore the idea has overwhelmed the hearts and minds of modern generations that apart from the usurious economic system there is no economic system at all, and that life can be conducted only under this system.

The true conception of zakah has so vanished from the minds of modern people that they have come to regard it merely as an individual kindness and virtue, and believe that no collective system can be built upon it. Yet these people cannot even imagine the great scale of the proceeds of zakah, that two and a half percent is obligatory upon both capital and profit, and that those whom Islam has trained, in its own particular manner, pay this rate with great joy. Through admonition and guidance, through legislation, and through a system of life whose conception dominates their hearts and minds, and which an Islamic government collects this rate of zakah as a necessary right, not that something is paid as charity; and from this great fund all those are sustained whose personal resources have become insufficient, and the state of affairs is that every member of society obtains the guarantee that his life and the life of his children is secure, and secure in every condition. From this fund the debts of those who are crushed under the burden of debts are also paid, whether these are commercial debts or non-commercial debts.

In Islam, importance is not given to the outward form and appearance of a system. Importance is given to the spirit of a system. The kind of society that Islam seeks to bring into existence through its training and guidance, its legal system and codification, and its whole system, that society is perfectly proportionate and harmonious with the form of its system, its components, its institutions, and its strategy. That society is the complement of its law. From the depths of the conscience of the members of that society there comes into existence a collective system of sustenance. All its institutions and strategies bring into being a collective sustenance. In this system, individual and institution are mutual helpers and mutual guarantors. This is a reality that is far beyond the understanding and perception of those who have grown up in the modern material system of life; yet it is a reality that we Muslims know well, and our faith-based taste perceives its sweetness, while the people of the modern age, because of their wretchedness and lack of taste, do not sense this sweetness. The modern person is afflicted with this deprivation and wretchedness because the reins of his life are in the hands of this modern material system. May God grant that they remain thus deprived and remain far from that good whose glad tidings Allah gives in these words: ﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds, establish prayer and give zakah, their reward is with their Lord, and there shall be no fear for them, nor shall they grieve.﴾ Those who are deprived of these heavenly guidances will also be deprived of inner contentment and peace, while they are already deprived of reward and recompense, because of their ignorance, their jahiliyyah, their misguidance and their obstinacy.

Allah makes a firm covenant with those who will establish their lives upon faith and righteous action, and who will set their economy right through mutual economic cooperation: their reward is secure with Allah; they will live in peace, they will not be afflicted by any fear or danger. They are fortunate, not deprived. Therefore they will be safe from every kind of anxiety: ﴿For them is their reward with their Lord, and there is no fear for them, nor shall they grieve.﴾

In circumstances where a society whose economy is based on usurious economics becomes deserving of the wrath and anger of Allah, its members become bewildered and go astray, and as a consequence they fall victim to spiritual fear, grief and sorrow.

In human history, humanity has witnessed with its own eyes this system of peace and tranquility in a true Islamic society, and it is witnessing in the modern usurious society the general atmosphere of grief, fear and restlessness. Would that we could seize every sensitive heart and shake it hard, so that it would awaken from the sleep of heedlessness and grasp this truth. Would that, if it were possible, we could awaken the sleeping eye, open it, and that it would grasp this great truth.

Alas, we do not have that power. If we had it, we would do it... We can only point to the truth. It is possible that Allah may turn this lost and unfortunate humanity toward it, for hearts are between two fingers of Allah the Most High, He turns them however He wills, and guidance is in the hand of Allah, who grants it to whom He wills. In such circumstances, the peace and abundance which Allah promises to an Islamic society that removes riba from its life; thus it casts out disbelief and disobedience from its life, and establishes its life upon faith, righteous action, the worship of Allah, and the system of zakah. In short, in such circumstances, amid peace and abundance, Allah calls out to those who have believed; and this call is in fact a final warning. They are commanded to purify their entire lives from the defiled and bankrupt usurious economic system, and if they are not prepared for this task, then this is in effect a declaration of war from them against Allah and His Messenger ﷺ, without any leniency, without any respite, and without any dilatory tactic.

In this verse, those who have believed are addressed and told to give up the interest that remains outstanding. They cannot be true believers unless they fear Allah and abandon the remaining sums of interest. Those who do not do so are not true believers, even if they proclaim their faith far and wide. For what meaning does faith have without obedience to and submission to the commands and injunctions of Allah? The verse does not leave them under any illusion, nor does it leave any person who hides behind the proclamation of faith, concealing his true reality, in doubt. The reality is that such a person is neither obedient to the command nor content with the Shari'ah. He does not implement the Shari'ah in his life. He does not make the Shari'ah the arbiter in his affairs. The truth is that those who distinguish between beliefs and actions in the religion of Islam are not true believers, even if they make lengthy and broad claims of faith, proclaim their faith with the tongue, and even if they are punctilious in observing fasting and prayer and other acts of worship. For Allah the Exalted says: "O you who have believed, fear Allah and give up what remains of interest, if you are indeed believers." ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَذَرُوا مَا بَقِيَ مِنَ الرِّبَا إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾

Islam forgave the interest that those people had already consumed. It did not decide that the usury already consumed should be returned from them. Nor did Islam order the confiscation of all or part of their property, on the ground that usury was part of their business. This is because nothing in Islam is declared forbidden unless Allah Almighty declares it forbidden, and no ruling can be issued without legislation. The nature of law is that its effects appear after its enforcement. What has passed has passed; past matters are left to Allah, and legal rulings are not applied to them. In this way Islam saved society from a great explosive economic and social crisis. Had this law been given retrospective effect, a very great crisis would have arisen. This is the principle which modern legal systems have recently adopted. This is because legislation in Islam is enacted so that the reality and life of a human being may be reformed: that he be set on the right path, be purified of filth, and be freed from unjust bonds, so that he may progress and his standard be raised. Along with this, Islam made the faith of the believers depend upon their acceptance of this legislation: they are true believers only when they accept it, and upon its revelation and upon its reaching their knowledge, they must immediately implement it in their lives. Along with this, Islam also creates in their hearts the fear of Allah and taqwa (God-consciousness). The consciousness of taqwa is the guarantee through which Islam enforces its laws. It is the guarantee that arises within the souls of the believers themselves. It is the inner watchman, and in Islam its rank is higher than the guarantees and watchmen that a law traditionally receives. Therefore Islamic laws receive for their enforcement the guarantee and supervision which the man-made laws of the modern age do not receive, because those laws are enforced only through external pressure. And it is no secret how easily the external supervisor can be outwitted, in circumstances where no watchman sits within the conscience of a person, that is, a supervisor of the fear of Allah and the pleasure of Allah.

This was the encouragement to abandon riba, but along with it comes a warning and a threat. And this threat is so severe that hearts tremble from it. ﴿Then if you do not do it, then be informed of war from Allah and His Messenger﴾ ... "If you did not do so, then be warned that there is a declaration of war against you from Allah and His Messenger."

Refuge in Allah! And a declaration of war from His Messenger! This is a war that confronts the human soul. It is a frightful war whose outcome is entirely in view, in which mankind is certainly to be defeated. Man is mortal and weak; what can he do against the overpowering might of Allah Almighty, who in a single moment will reduce everything to ashes and wipe out its very name and trace?

After the revelation of these verses, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) instructed the ruler of Makkah to fight the Al-Mughirah of Makkah, because even after the revelation of these verses they did not refrain from their usurious dealings. On the day of the conquest of Makkah, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), in his sermon, abolished all the usurious debts of the Age of Ignorance (jahiliyyah). He said: "The first I remit is the interest of my uncle Abbas ؓ." This burden remained upon debtors for a period after Islam came. But when the Islamic society became mature, its foundations became strong, and the time came to rebuild the economic system of the region away from the principle of riba and upon correct Islamic principles, then Islam took this step. On this occasion the Messenger (ﷺ) said:

"All the usury of the Age of Ignorance is under these two feet of mine, and the first usurious debt that I remit is the usury of Abbas."

Along with this, he would also instruct the people to return the usury they had taken during the Age of Ignorance. This shows that it is the duty of the Islamic state to fight those who insist on continuing usurious economics and who disobey Allah's command, even if such people declare that they are Muslims. Abu Bakr ؓ waged war against those who withheld zakat on this very principle, although they recited "La ilaha illa Allah, Muhammad Rasul Allah," and performed prayer. Therefore, whoever refuses obedience to the Shariah and does not implement it in his life no longer remains a Muslim.

It should be kept in view here that the declaration of war from Allah and His Messenger against usurers is more general than a war of guns and weapons which a ruler wages against some power. This declaration of war, as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, is against every society whose economic system is founded upon usury. This war is all-encompassing and frightful. It is a war upon the nerves, a war upon hearts. It is the war of riba against goodness, blessing and prosperity. It is a war by the usurious system against human happiness, prosperity and tranquility. It is a war of human conflict and of pursuing one another. Ultimately, it is a war of armies and weapons between nations and peoples. It is an all-encompassing and destructive war which breaks out on this earth whenever its system is based upon the principle of riba, and because of which blessing vanishes from this earth and prosperity disappears. All these wars and conflicts are launched by the capitalists who control the wealth of the whole world, and they kindle the flames of these wars. Sometimes they do this directly and sometimes indirectly. They ensnare companies and corporations in their deceptive net. After that, nations and governments fall prey to their net. Then these governments pounce upon their prey, and thus war begins between them. Sometimes these governments rush to protect their interests and their capital, bring their military power into the field, and thus the flames of the battlefield blaze up. Sometimes it happens that the common people become unable to pay taxes and official dues. Poverty becomes widespread among the masses. Labourers and toilers, distressed, join movements whose mission is sabotage and spreading destruction. And thus a popular war begins in some region. And the conflicts that arise under this usurious system produce the general results, easily apparent, that people's souls become corrupted, moral ruin spreads, debauchery arises among people, and the framework of humanity is destroyed. The spiritual world of man suffers a ruin such that no atomic war can inflict a similar destruction upon the human body.

This war, whose declaration has been made against those who engage in usurious dealings, has its flames rising at every moment. Even today it rages everywhere. The lost humanity's wealth is being offered as a sacrifice to it. But humanity is unable to comprehend this. Humanity thinks that it is earning wealth and progressing. It is producing material results in great abundance; diverse products are being manufactured. But this very production is ruin for it. If this same production came from a pure, non-usurious system, it would be a cause of blessing and prosperity for humanity. But this production comes forth from the impure and polluted system of usury. Therefore it is a burden upon humanity, under which humanity is suffocating, while the scholarly group of usurers lives in comfort and ease, and feels no concern at all for the troubles and grief of all of humanity.

Islam invited the first Islamic community to this, and today it is inviting all of humanity to this: that they adopt a pure and clean means of livelihood, and, repenting from the pestilential usurious system, take the straight path. ﴿And if you repent, then you have the principal of your wealth; you shall neither wrong nor be wronged.﴾ "Even now, if you repent, you have the right to take your principal. You shall neither do injustice nor be subjected to injustice." This is repentance from a sin, a return from the error prevalent in the days of ignorance. And jahiliyyah is not confined to a particular era, nor is the term jahiliyyah applied only to a particular system. The reality of jahiliyyah is this: whenever and wherever a human being deviates from the divine system of life, that will be jahiliyyah. Riba is an error whose effects overwhelm a person's conception of life, his morals and his consciousness. Then its effects fall upon society and upon the collective relations of society. It impacts the whole of human life. It impacts economic growth and development, even though those people who have fallen for the deception of usurious dealers think that the usurious economic system is the only system capable of, and the cause of, growth and economic development.

Merely granting the right to the return of the principal is a rule under which neither the creditor suffers loss nor the debtor is wronged. As for how wealth will then be increased, its means and resources are separate, and they are free of riba. The first of these means is the personal struggle of an individual.
